# Changelog

Tracks what's been built and what's next, phase by phase per `docs/archive/spine-prd.md` §12. Update this file as work lands — newest entry on top within each section. This is the progress log; `CLAUDE.md` is the architecture/rules reference.

## Status

**Phase 4 · Money Out & Books is now fully complete** (Tax → Purchases & Expenses → Reports) — this closes the entire v1 core-product scope. See the Phase 4 Stage 3 Completed entry below for the Reports/FEAT-09 breakdown. **Phase 5 (Mobile) — the API-prerequisite stage, the `apps/mobile` scaffold, `packages/ui-native`'s foundational components, and Auth (S-11.1) are all complete.** Job crew assignment, on-site quote acceptance, OpenAPI/Swagger setup, an explicit Better Auth session lifetime, a real booting `apps/mobile` Expo app, `packages/ui-native` (Button/TextField/Card/Badge, NativeWind theming with light/dark/system, a11y test coverage), and now a real login/session/sign-out flow (with a genuine mid-build correction to the mobile auth mechanism — Bearer-sent session token via Better Auth's `bearer()` plugin, not a minted JWT as originally planned) all landed 2026-08-30 (six Completed entries below). **`packages/ui-native` has since been reworked onto `@expo/ui` (real native SwiftUI/Jetpack Compose components) with a new native-only `apps/showcase-native` doc app on `expo-router`** — see the 2026-09-04 Completed entry; `apps/mobile` itself is unaffected (still consumes `packages/ui-native`'s public API unchanged) and remains the next thing to build screens against. Next per the Phase 5 plan: build the read screens (Home/Job detail/Profile) online-only against the now-working auth + API client, before layering in offline caching.

**FEAT-08's one remaining deferred gap is closed: the job variation-order line editor now has the tax rate/group picker.** The Phase 4 Tax entry below deliberately left `variation-order-line-editor.tsx` on the legacy flat-percentage `Input` since a variation order is really just a quote under the hood (`VariationOrdersService.create` delegates straight into `QuotesService.create`) — the backend/schema/DTO already fully supported `taxRateId`/`taxGroupId`/`isTaxInclusive` via `quoteLineInputSchema`, so this was purely a frontend gap. `EditableVariationLine` gained the same three fields as `EditableQuoteLine`; the raw "Tax %" `Input` is replaced with the `Combobox` (rate/group picker) + "Price includes tax" `Checkbox` pair, mirroring `quote-line-editor.tsx` exactly (fetches `/tax-rates`/`/tax-groups`, a local `resolveLineTaxRates` mirroring `TaxResolverService.resolve` for instant client-side preview, catalog-item prefill now copies `defaultTaxRateId`/`defaultTaxGroupId` instead of only the flat percentage). New local `TaxRateOption`/`TaxGroupOption`/`VariationOrderCatalogItemOption` types added to `jobs/types.ts`, following this codebase's existing per-module duplication precedent rather than extracting a shared component. `variation-orders-section.tsx`'s create-payload mapping now sends the three new fields instead of only `taxRatePercentage`. New `variation-order-tax.integration.test.ts` asserts a variation order created with a tax group containing a compound rate produces the correct `taxAmount`/`totalAmount` on the underlying quote ($100 line, GST 15% + compound State Tax 6.5% → $22.48 tax, same worked example as the original Tax stage entry, now verified through the variation-order path specifically). `docs/qa-script.md`'s Jobs → Variation Orders section gained a regression check for tax group selection. No DB migration, backend, or DTO change was needed.

**Current phase:** Phase 0 · Foundation is functionally complete (monorepo scaffold, Docker Compose shape, the money/tax core in `@spine/shared`, the full Postgres/Drizzle schema with a working DB-enforced ledger, a documented local dev workflow, a project README, auth (Better Auth: email/password + organizations + JWT), the design system (`docs/DESIGN.md` + `apps/design-system`), the full PRD §F0 `@spine/ui` set plus the complete Radix Primitives + shadcn/ui component union, a hand-rolled Outlook-style `Calendar` component, full `apps/design-system` documentation coverage, the first-run onboarding wizard, a real Settings UI, a shared `AppShell`, a real S3/MinIO-backed Files module, a GitHub Actions CI pipeline, a formal WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility audit-and-fix pass across all 69 `@spine/ui` components, and automated axe-core accessibility regression testing across all 78 `@spine/ui` components, enforced on every future component via a coverage-check script).

**Phase 1 · Sales Spine is fully complete**, per the PRD's own story list (`docs/archive/spine-prd.md` §12: S-01.1→S-01.8, S-02.1→S-02.4, S-03.1→S-03.9 + S-03.11, S-10.4, S-10.11, S-10.12, S-12.9): Contacts & CRM (F1, all 8 stories including CSV import, the leads pipeline kanban board, and the per-contact Timeline tab), Catalogue (F2), and Quotes (F3, including the public accept/reject link and owner notifications) are all complete; the in-app notification centre and browser push notifications are both built; and the dashboard setup checklist is wired to real completion state. Only **S-03.12 (mobile)** remains unbuilt among F3's stories — deferred until `apps/mobile` exists (Phase 5). **Post-Phase-1 addition:** S-01.9 (meeting scheduling on a calendar) was added to FEAT-01 and built after Phase 1 closed, followed by S-01.10 → S-01.12 (private/org meeting visibility, invites, accept/decline/tentative) and S-10.20 → S-10.22 (invite/response notifications, a "starting soon" reminder, and its org-default/per-user lead-time settings) — see the 2026-08-12 Completed entry.

**Phase 2 · Money In is now fully complete.** Invoicing (draft CRUD, issue/void with real §7.2 ledger postings including S-02.3's per-catalog-item revenue split, PDF, email, overdue flagging, one-click reminders, advance/deposit invoices) and Payments (record, multi-invoice allocation with DB-enforced limits, oldest-first suggestion, unallocated customer credit, apply sitting credit to a later invoice, receipt PDF/email) are both fully built with real web UIs (`/invoices`, `/payments`, `/receivables`). Credit notes (S-05.6) and quote→invoice conversion (S-03.10) are both built too. Demo data (S-12.8/F12) covers Invoices + Payments with real seeded totals and postings. Every FEAT-05/FEAT-06/FEAT-09 story in Phase 2's own scope is now built.

**Phase 3 · Jobs & Construction Billing is now fully complete**, built in 5 staged commits per explicit user instruction (no scope deferred). Stage 1: `jobs`/`milestones`/`job_photos`/`job_notes`/`job_variation_orders` schema, real FKs wired from `invoices.jobId`/`invoices.milestoneId`/`journal_lines.jobId` (both existed as placeholder columns since Phase 2/earlier, now pointing at real tables), `JobsService`/`MilestonesService`/`JobsController` covering S-04.1 (create a job from an accepted quote, contract value carried over as a snapshot) and S-04.2/S-04.3 (define milestones as fixed/percent amounts with server-side "percentages must total 100%" validation before any write lands). Stage 2: S-04.4 (mark a milestone complete with photos, field-reachable via `jobs.update_milestones`), S-04.5/S-05.1's milestone path (raise a progress invoice directly from a completed milestone via `InvoicesService.createFromMilestone`), S-04.6 (retention held automatically — `issue()` now splits the AR debit into net-AR + `Retention Receivable` per §7.2 whenever `retentionAmount > 0`), S-04.7 (release retention as a new `retention_release`-type invoice via `InvoicesService.releaseRetention`). Every balance computation across Invoices/Payments/Reports (`balanceDue`, `suggestAllocation`, allocation-limit checks, AR aging) now subtracts `retentionAmount` alongside `amountPaid`/`creditedAmount`, so held-back retention never shows as a collectible or overdue receivable. Stage 3: S-04.9 (variation orders — a new `VariationOrdersService` wraps ordinary `QuotesService` CRUD/send/accept, linking each supplementary quote to a job via `job_variation_orders`; an explicit `apply()` action folds an accepted variation's total into the job's `contractValueAmount` and recomputes every percent-type milestone's `resolvedAmount` against the new base), S-04.10 (general job photos/notes, web upload, field-reachable), S-04.8 revenue side (new `JobCostingService` reads `journal_lines` filtered by `jobId` — never a shadow costing table — summing `income`-account credits as revenue and `expense`-account debits as cost; cost is always 0 today since Purchases/Expenses don't exist until Phase 4, but the query needs no rework once they do). Stage 4 (web UI): `/jobs` list page and `/jobs/[id]` detail page (header, tabbed Milestones/Variation Orders/Photos/Notes/Costing sections, edit dialog, release-retention action), a "Convert to job" action on an accepted quote's detail page (completes S-03.10 alongside Phase 2's invoice-conversion half), and its own top-level "Jobs" sidebar section between Sales and Billing. S-12.3's construction-template effect is presentational only: retention % lives behind a collapsible "Advanced" disclosure in the job edit dialog, defaulting open for orgs on the Construction industry template or any job that already has a nonzero `retentionPct` — Jobs itself stays fully usable for every org regardless of template, per CLAUDE.md's onboarding-is-never-a-gate rule. **Stage 5 (final)**: demo data now seeds 3 jobs at different S-04.1→S-04.7 lifecycle stages (one just started, one with 2 of 3 milestones invoiced and retention accumulating, one fully complete with retention released) via the real `JobsService`/`MilestonesService`/`InvoicesService` methods, exactly like every other demo document type in this codebase; `DemoDataService.deleteAll` now also removes demo jobs (skipping any blocked by `journal_lines.jobId`'s own immutability, matching the existing demo-contact precedent) and its own `jobsDeleted` count reports the real number removed, not the total found; `docs/qa-script.md` gained a full §5 Jobs section plus retention regression checks on the Invoices/Payments/Receivables sections it touches. Verified end-to-end against a live local instance (seed → milestone completion → progress invoicing → retention hold → retention release → deleteAll), not just by reading the code.

**The permission model (§2.1) has been substantially rewritten and built** (S-10.13→S-10.18, S-10.17), cutting across every phase rather than belonging to one: multiple Owners with one DB-protected Primary Owner, Teams subdividing the Staff tier with a configurable capability-based privilege matrix enforced by a `CapabilityGuard` layered on `@OrgRoles`, an Owner-only `/team/*` web area, a real invitation-email/accept flow, and a Profile & Preferences page for every role. See the 2026-08-09/2026-08-10 Completed entries for the full breakdown.

**New: a repeat-quote-conversion safeguard (user-reported, post-Phase-3).** Neither `InvoicesService.convertFromQuote` nor `JobsService.createFromQuote` has ever had a one-shot restriction — a deliberate second conversion is a real use case (staged billing, splitting one quote across two jobs) — but with no total anywhere cross-checking a job's/invoice's amount against the source quote, an ACCIDENTAL repeat click silently doubles the billed/tracked amount. New org preference `quote_conversion_guard` (Settings → "Repeat quote conversion", default **warn**) — `off` (no check), `warn` (a 409 with the existing job(s)/invoice(s) listed, requiring the caller to retry with `confirm: true`), or `block` (rejected outright, no override). One shared `QuoteConversionGuardService` (`apps/api/src/modules/org`) enforces this identically for both conversion paths, checked BEFORE either service does its own work. The web UI's `apiClient` gained an `ApiError` class (extends `Error`, backward-compatible with every existing `catch` site) so the quote detail page can read the 409's structured body and show a real confirmation dialog naming what already exists, rather than a generic error toast. Verified end-to-end against a live instance: off/warn/block all behave correctly, and the guard is quote-scoped across BOTH job and invoice conversions together (converting to a job when 3 invoices already exist correctly warns about all of them).

**Phase 4 · Money Out & Books — Tax (FEAT-08) stage is complete**, first of three planned stages (Tax → Purchases & Expenses → Reports, per the user's own explicit sequencing). Real `tax_rates`/`tax_groups`/`tax_group_rates` tables (S-08.1, S-08.3) replace the earlier Phase 0/1 single-flat-percentage placeholder that only backed onboarding's quick-start step (`GET/PUT /org/tax/default-rate`, kept unchanged for that one purpose). `TaxResolverService` centralizes "resolve a line's `taxRateId` XOR `taxGroupId` into `computeLineTax`'s input shape" and is now injected into Quotes/Invoices/Catalog — every quote/invoice line and catalog item's default tax gained `taxRateId`/`taxGroupId` FK columns (snapshot-on-write, never re-read after) alongside the legacy `taxRatePercentage` (now a computed blended fallback, not user-editable when a real rate/group is set). `isTaxInclusive` (S-08.2) is a new per-line snapshot column, backed by an org-level `prices_include_tax` default setting; `computeLineTax`'s existing `inclusive` parameter (previously always hardcoded `false`) is finally wired through end-to-end. A new `ReportsService.taxSummary` (S-08.4, Owner-only, `GET /org/tax/summary?from&to`) sums `journal_lines` against the two system tax accounts the chart of accounts already seeds (`2100 Output Tax Payable`, `1200 Input Tax Receivable`) — no shadow ledger, matching CLAUDE.md's "derive from journal lines" rule exactly; `taxPaid` is always 0 until Purchases (this phase's next stage) posts to `1200`, needing no rework once it does, same forward-compatible shape `JobCostingService` already established for its own cost side. Web: a fully rebuilt Settings → Tax pane (rate/group CRUD with archive/restore/delete-if-unreferenced, the inclusive-pricing toggle) replaces the old single-rate quick-start form; Quotes' and Invoices' line editors both gained a named-rate/group `Combobox` picker (prefilling from a catalog item's own default) plus a "Price includes tax" checkbox, replacing the old raw percentage `Input`; Catalogue's item form gained the same picker. Demo data now seeds one real "Sales Tax" `tax_rates` row via the real `TaxRatesService` (not hand-inserted) and wires every demo catalog item/quote/invoice line to reference it; `DemoDataService.deleteAll` cleans it up by name once nothing references it. Verified end-to-end against a live local instance: created two rates (one compound) and a group combining them via curl, confirmed `computeLineTax`'s compound math on a real quote/invoice line matched hand-calculated numbers exactly ($100 line, GST 15% + compound State Tax 6.5% → $22.48 tax, not the wrong non-compound $21.50), issued the invoice and confirmed `taxSummary` reported the exact same $22.48 as tax collected with $0 tax paid, confirmed archive/restore and the delete-blocked-when-referenced-by-a-group guard, and confirmed seed → deleteAll leaves manually-created tax rates untouched while removing only the demo-seeded one. `docs/qa-script.md` gained a full §10 Tax section (renumbering old §10-12 to §11-13) with regression checks on Catalogue/Quotes/Invoices totals. The job **variation order** line editor (a third, independently-owned quote-line editor per its own doc comment) was deliberately left on the legacy flat-percentage path at the time — since retrofitted, see the entry above this one.

**Tax summary gained a per-rate breakdown + a real web surface (user-requested follow-up to the Tax stage above).** `ReportsService.taxSummary` now also returns `collectedByRate` — tax collected grouped by named rate/group (or "X% tax" for a pre-FEAT-08 flat-percentage line), largest first, exactly what a real VAT/GST return needs ("how much at 20% vs. at 5%") that a single blended `taxCollected` figure can't show. Deliberately reads `invoice_lines` (which carries the per-line `taxRateId`/`taxGroupId`/`taxRatePercentage`) rather than `journal_lines` (which only has one blended ledger posting per document) — the two sources can legitimately diverge when an invoice's ledger history outlives its own document row (e.g. `DemoDataService.deleteAll` removes the invoice but never touches its already-posted, permanent journal entry, per CLAUDE.md's immutability rule), discovered live when a stale local dev org's ledger total ($2,406.73) didn't match its current invoices' combined tax ($22.48) after an earlier demo-data cycle. Rather than silently under-totaling, the breakdown now always sums exactly to `taxCollected` by appending a trailing "Other / from removed invoices" row for the unattributed remainder — both figures stay independently correct and the mismatch is explained, not hidden. Web: a new "Tax summary" section at the bottom of Settings → Tax (From/To `DatePicker`s, Refresh button, Collected/Paid/Net figures, the per-rate list) — renders unconditionally like every other pane (no client-side capability check, matching this codebase's documented gap) and surfaces the API's real Owner-only 403 as a legible message rather than a silent failure. Verified end-to-end against the live local instance described above: the breakdown's one real rate row ($22.48) plus its "Other" row ($2,384.25) sum to exactly the ledger's $2,406.73.

**Phase 4 Stage 2 (Purchases & Expenses, FEAT-07) is complete** — vendor bills, expenses with an approval-gated posting trigger, vendor payments allocated across bills, and a payables aging view, closing out the "Money Out" half of Phase 4 · Money Out & Books. New tables `vendor_bills`/`vendor_bill_lines` (structurally mirroring `invoices`/`invoice_lines` exactly — snapshot-on-write lines, draft-is-mutable/recorded-is-immutable, the same FEAT-08 `taxRateId`/`taxGroupId`/`isTaxInclusive` shape, one deliberate difference: `billNumber` is plain vendor-supplied text, never allocated via `NumberingService`, per that module's own doc comment), `expense_categories`/`expenses` (S-07.2/S-07.3's web-submission half, S-07.4's approval gate — the PRD's own acceptance highlight, "an unapproved expense does not post to the ledger, approval is the posting trigger," is enforced by `ExpensesService.approve` flipping `status -> approved` AND posting the §7.2 "Expense paid directly" journal entry in the SAME transaction, so there is no reachable approved-but-unposted state), and `vendor_payments`/`vendor_payment_allocations` (an exact mirror of `payments`/`payment_allocations` including a new hand-written migration, `0029_vendor_payment_allocation_limits.sql`, replicating `0020`'s deferred-constraint-trigger allocation-limit enforcement for the vendor side — flagged as the intended path in Phase 2's own CHANGELOG note, now built; unlike the customer side, vendor payment allocations must sum to EXACTLY the payment amount, since FEAT-07 has no "vendor credit" concept). `VendorBillsService.record()` and `ExpensesService.approve()` both post through the shared `LedgerService` exactly like `InvoicesService.issue()` (row-lock, status re-check, numbering, `postEntry`, audit log, all one transaction) — §7.2's "Vendor bill recorded" (debit Expense/COGS + Input Tax Receivable, credit Accounts Payable) and "Expense paid directly" (debit Expense, credit Bank/Cash) postings are both new. S-04.8 (job costing's cost side) is now genuinely complete — `JobCostingService`'s query already read `journal_lines.jobId` for `expense`-type debits since Phase 3, and needed zero changes once this stage started posting them for real. A new `purchases.manage` capability (Owner/Staff, Team-configurable) gates vendor bill/vendor payment mutation; `expenses.submit`/`expenses.approve` (already existing since an earlier phase) cover the expense side. **Real bug found and fixed while wiring Field access to `expenses.submit`**: `CapabilityGuard` unconditionally rejected any non-owner/non-staff role, including `field`, even on routes that explicitly listed `"field"` in their own `@OrgRoles` — meaning `jobs.controller.ts`'s `completeMilestone` route (S-04.4, `jobs.update_milestones`) has been silently unreachable by Field users since Phase 3 despite its own doc comment claiming otherwise. Fixed: `CapabilityGuard` now passes unconditionally for `field` (trusting that Better Auth's `AuthGuard` already evaluated `@OrgRoles` and would have 403'd first if `field` weren't allowed on that specific route) — verified via the existing `capability.guard.integration.test.ts` suite (updated its "Field is always rejected" test to "Field always passes", all 38 integration tests green) and confirms both the new expense-submission path AND the pre-existing milestone-completion path now work correctly for Field. Web: full `/vendor-bills` (list/detail/builder with a vendor-only contact picker and a job/tax/account line-level picker), `/expenses` (list/detail-drawer with Approve/Reject — reject requires a comment, mirroring void-invoice's required-reason pattern), `/vendor-payments` (list/detail-drawer, a "New vendor payment" dialog that disables submit until allocations sum to exactly the amount), and `/payables` (aging buckets, mirrors `/receivables` exactly) — plus a new "Purchases" top-level nav section (money-out mirror of "Billing", ordered directly after it) and a Settings → Purchases pane for expense-category CRUD (mirrors the Tax pane's own rate/group CRUD-list pattern). Demo data seeds 4 vendor bills across every lifecycle outcome (draft/recorded/paid/voided) and 5 expenses across the full approval-gate lifecycle (submitted/approved/rejected), via the real services exactly like every other demo document type; `DemoDataService.deleteAll` cleans up vendor payments before vendor bills (allocation FK ordering, same precedent `payment_allocations` already established) and cleans up the three demo expense categories by name (same "no isDemo column, clean up by name" convention already used for the demo "Sales Tax" rate). Verified end-to-end against a live local instance via curl: submitted and approved an expense (confirmed the exact debit/credit ledger posting), rejected a second one (confirmed zero ledger impact), recorded a vendor bill with compound tax (confirmed the three-line Expense+Input-Tax/Accounts-Payable posting balanced exactly), paid it off via a vendor payment (confirmed `VPY-0001` allocation, bill balance dropped to zero, excluded from Payables), tested the allocation-limit rejection and the DB trigger backing it, voided a bill with a reversing entry, and ran the full demo seed → deleteAll cycle confirming exact counts both directions. `docs/qa-script.md` gained a full §11 Purchases & Expenses section (renumbering old §11-13 to §12-14) with regression checks on Jobs' Costing tab and the Tax summary's now-real `taxPaid` figure. One story, S-07.6 (bill a customer for a billable expense), has a real working API (`POST /expenses/:id/mark-billed`) but no web UI action yet — flagged as a known gap, not silently left unmentioned.

**Phase 4 Stage 3 (Reports, FEAT-09) is complete — this closes out Phase 4 · Money Out & Books and the entire v1 core-product scope before Phase 5 (Mobile).** All eight stories built in one pass: P&L for any date range (S-09.2, `ReportsService.profitAndLoss`, sums `journal_lines` grouped by income/expense account — never computed from documents directly, per FEAT-09's own acceptance highlight); Balance Sheet as-of a date (S-09.3, `balanceSheet`, assets/liabilities/equity from lifetime account balances, with current-period net income folded in as a computed "Retained Earnings (current period)" equity line rather than posted to the seeded `3200` system account, since no formal period-close posting exists yet — the statement still balances exactly, verified live: $4,306,525 assets = $448,725 liabilities + $3,857,800 equity); click-through drill-down behind any P&L/Balance Sheet figure (S-09.4, `accountDrilldown` — given an account + date range, returns every journal entry with its `sourceType`/`sourceId`, which the web client resolves into a real link via a small `SOURCE_TYPE_ROUTES` map); all-jobs profitability summary (S-09.6, `jobProfitability` — one query grouped by `jobId`, the all-jobs counterpart to Phase 3's existing per-job `JobCostingService.report`, same "derive from journal_lines, never a shadow costing table" rule); CSV export on every new report plus receivables/payables/job-profitability (S-09.7, a tiny shared `toCsv` RFC-4180 writer in `apps/api/src/common/csv.ts`, one `/export.csv` route per report with its own explicit column mapping rather than a generic dispatcher, since each report's row shape genuinely differs); period close (S-09.8, new `PeriodsService`/`PeriodsController` under the `ledger` module managing `fiscal_periods` rows — CRUD + close/reopen — with the actual enforcement living in `LedgerService.postEntry` itself, which now rejects any posting whose date falls inside a closed period, checked inside the same transaction as the posting via `tx` so a concurrent close can't race the write); a custom chart-of-accounts entry (S-09.9, `AccountsService.create` — always `isSystem: false`, rejects a duplicate `code`); and a real dashboard (S-09.10, `ReportsService.dashboardSummary` — cash position from the `1000`/`1010` seeded cash/bank accounts' lifetime net movement, total receivables reusing `receivables()` directly rather than a second balance computation, overdue invoice count, and month-to-date revenue from `income`-account journal_lines credits).

`dashboard.view` (existing capability, whose own description already said "P&L/balance sheet stay Owner-only regardless of this grant") now literally enforces that: `ReportsController`'s new P&L/Balance-Sheet/drilldown routes carry `@OrgRoles(["owner"])` with no capability escape hatch, while dashboard-summary/job-profitability/CSV-export-of-those stay `@RequireCapability("dashboard.view")` like receivables/payables already did — no new capability needed, matching CLAUDE.md's "single source of truth" rule since nothing new needed gating. Web: a new top-level "Reports" nav section (`/reports`, three tabs — Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, Job Profitability — each independently loaded so a Staff user with `dashboard.view` but not Owner sees Job Profitability load fine while P&L/Balance Sheet show the server's real 403 inline, matching every other pane's "no client-side capability check" convention); period close and "Add account" are folded into the existing Settings → Chart of accounts pane rather than given their own tabs; the dashboard page gained a real 4-card KPI row (`DashboardSummary`) replacing the placeholder note that used to explain why no stat cards existed yet.

**Real bug found and fixed while first live-testing period close**: initial testing tried to close a period covering a *document's own* `issueDate`/`date` field and close-then-issue appeared to silently do nothing — turned out every domain service posts with `date: new Date()` (issue/record/approve time), not the document's own user-editable date field, so backdating a document's `issueDate` was never actually going to produce a backdated ledger posting in this codebase to begin with. The guard is correct as built (confirmed live: closing a period covering *today* correctly rejects a same-day invoice issue with "falls within a closed fiscal period," and reopening immediately un-blocks it) — `LedgerService.postEntry`'s own doc comment now calls this out explicitly so a future reader doesn't rediscover the same confusion.

**Demo data**: the "active" demo job ("Marina office fit-out") now has one vendor bill and one expense tagged to it (`seedJobs` returns `costingJobId`, threaded into `seedPurchases`) — without this, every demo job showed `cost: 0` and a misleading flat 100% margin on the new Job Profitability report, even though the underlying posting already carried `jobId` correctly whenever a real bill/expense had one set. No new tables landed this stage (`fiscal_periods` already existed in schema since Phase 0, `accounts.create` reuses the existing table), so `apps/api/src/db/reset.ts`'s `TABLES` list needed no changes — re-verified exhaustively against the schema (zero missing, zero extra) as a matter of course.

Verified end-to-end against a live local instance: seeded demo data, confirmed P&L totals (net profit $3,857,800), confirmed the Balance Sheet balances exactly, drilled into the AR account and confirmed every listed journal entry linked to its correct real invoice/payment, confirmed Job Profitability showed the job-tagged demo job's real nonzero cost while every other demo job correctly showed cost 0, downloaded and inspected a P&L CSV export, created and closed a fiscal period and confirmed a same-day invoice issue was correctly rejected then correctly un-blocked on reopen, and created a custom account via the new Settings UI. `pnpm --filter @spine/api typecheck`/`test:integration` (38 tests, unchanged) and `pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck`/`build` all pass. `docs/qa-script.md` gained a full §15 Reports & Dashboard section and closed out its own stale "No P&L/Balance Sheet report exists yet" known-gap note.

**`AlertDialog` vs. `Dialog` audit (user-reported).** Per `AlertDialogContent`'s own doc comment (`packages/ui/src/components/alert-dialog.tsx`), `AlertDialog` is specifically for a pure yes/no confirmation before an action that can't be undone; `Dialog` is for everything else (forms, pickers, viewers). Two new confirmations built this session (release-retention on a job, the repeat-quote-conversion warning above) were built with plain `Dialog` and are now `AlertDialog`. Audited every other `Dialog`/`AlertDialog` usage across `apps/web` — every remaining plain `Dialog` genuinely contains a form control (void-invoice's required reason field, transfer-primary-ownership's owner picker, add/edit forms) so those are correctly left as-is; everything that's a pure confirmation already used `AlertDialog` (contacts, quotes, catalogue, teams, demo-data deletion) with one exception: **deleting a meeting from the calendar had no confirmation at all** — `Calendar`'s (`@spine/ui`) `onEventDelete` fired the API call immediately with zero prompt. `MeetingsCalendar` now intercepts it with its own `AlertDialog` before calling the API, rather than teaching the shared `Calendar` component a confirmation flow every consumer might want shaped differently.

**Variation order acceptance now sends a proactive notification (user-reported known gap, closed).** Applying an accepted variation order to its job was always a deliberate, explicit staff action (`VariationOrdersService.apply`, unchanged), but nothing ever told anyone the acceptance had happened — the only way to notice was manually checking a job's Variation Orders tab. `PublicQuotesService.respond()` now looks up `job_variation_orders` by `quoteId` right after its existing `quote_accepted`/`quote_rejected` notification fires; when the accepted quote is a variation order's underlying quote, it fires a second, distinct in-app+email notification (`variation_order_accepted`, `recipientRoles: ["owner", "staff"]` — same recipient set as every other quote-response notification, since VOs have no per-job manager/owner field to narrow to) linking to `/jobs/:jobId?tab=variations`. No notification fires on reject (there's nothing to apply), and ordinary non-VO quote acceptances are unaffected — verified by a dedicated negative test. This required teaching the job detail page (`apps/web/src/app/(app)/jobs/job-detail.tsx`) real URL-driven tab state for the first time (previously an uncontrolled `Tabs defaultValue="milestones"` with no deep-link support) — same `useSearchParams` + `<Suspense>`-wrapping-the-page pattern already established by the meetings-calendar notification deep link (S-10.20/S-10.21). New tests in `public-quotes-respond-notifications.integration.test.ts`: VO-quote acceptance fires both `quote_accepted` and `variation_order_accepted` with the correct job-scoped link, VO-quote rejection fires neither variation notification, and a plain non-VO quote acceptance still fires zero `variation_order_accepted` rows (all passing alongside the file's 2 pre-existing tests, 5/5). `pnpm --filter @spine/api typecheck`/`pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck` both pass.

**Dashboard v2 follow-up: the KPI summary row is now pinned, never movable (user-reported).** After the card-drag customization redesign above, the user pointed out the top KPI row (Cash/Receivables/Overdue/Revenue) shouldn't be part of the customizable set at all. `kpi-summary` is now removed entirely from `DASHBOARD_WIDGETS` (`packages/shared`) rather than flagged with a "locked" property — keeping the pinned set and the customizable set structurally distinct so there's no code path that could accidentally make it draggable. `DashboardShell` renders `DashboardSummary` directly as a header above the `ReorderableList`, outside it entirely; `widget-registry.tsx`'s `WIDGET_LABELS`/`WIDGET_COMPONENTS` maps no longer reference it. Backward compatible with any user who already saved a layout containing a stale `kpi-summary` entry — `mergeDashboardLayout` already drops any saved key not in the current registry, verified live by PUTting a layout with a stale `kpi-summary` entry and confirming both the dashboard rendered cleanly and the merge function's real output correctly omitted it. `docs/qa-script.md`'s widget-customization section updated to match (renamed "Customize dashboard" → "Edit layout" per the earlier redesign, replaced the stale "grid replaced by a reorderable list" description with the actual in-place card-overlay behavior, and added an explicit check that the KPI row never shows a drag handle or hide toggle).

Revisit only if a real crash-window data integrity issue shows up in practice.

- Quotes Stage 3's own known gaps/rough edges, left as-is because nothing in the task brief called for going further:
  - ~~**Repeat-view notifications aren't de-duplicated.**~~ — **done**, see the 2026-08-29 Completed entry.
  - ~~**A rejection does not trigger an owner notification**~~ — **done**, see the 2026-08-29 Completed entry.
  - **Rate limiting (20 req/min/IP, `@nestjs/throttler`, in-memory) is a first pass, not tuned against real traffic.** It's per-IP only — a customer and their whole office behind one NAT'd IP share the same bucket, which could be too tight for legitimate shared use (e.g. several people at a company opening the same link) or too loose against a determined attacker rotating source IPs. In-memory (no Redis, per CLAUDE.md's single-host stance) also means the limit resets on every API process restart, which is a fine tradeoff for a single-host deployment but wouldn't survive a future multi-instance one without swapping storage.
  - **Token TTL is a flat 30 days**, not configurable per-org or tied to the quote's own `validUntil`. A quote valid for only 7 days still gets a 30-day link — not incorrect (the public page/accept/reject flow independently checks `status === "sent"`, so an expired-by-`validUntil` quote can still technically be viewed/accepted via a live token, matching how the authenticated app treats "expired" as informational, not a hard block — see `QuotesService`'s own `isExpired` comment), but worth a second look if the PRD's "expire" semantics are meant to be a hard cutoff on the public side too.
  - **No public "resend my link" self-service** — if a customer loses the email, only staff re-sending (or revising) the quote mints a fresh token. This wasn't asked for and would need its own rate-limiting/abuse consideration (an anonymous "resend to this email" endpoint is a classic enumeration/spam vector) so it's deliberately not built.
  - **The public web page's actual rendered UI was not visually verified** — no browser-automation tooling exists in this environment (same limitation noted in every prior Quotes session). What *was* verified live: the underlying `GET/POST /public/quotes/:token` calls the page's client component makes (directly, with curl, using a token minted the same way the real send flow mints one), that the Next.js route resolves and server-renders without error, and that `pnpm --filter @spine/web build` successfully compiles `/quote/[token]` as a route. The actual on-screen layout, mobile responsiveness, and dark/light theming were reviewed by reading the component's Tailwind classes against `@spine/ui`'s existing conventions, not by looking at a rendered browser.
- Quotes Stage 2's remaining known gaps (still open, unrelated to Stage 3): no dead-letter queue configured (a permanently-failed job just sits in pg-boss's `failed` state, retained per its default retention window, not routed anywhere for manual triage beyond the `/quotes/email-queue` view, which only shows not-yet-resolved jobs); no Resend (or other) email driver — only Nodemailer/SMTP, per the task's explicit scope; orphaned `files` rows aren't cleaned up when a demo quote (or its PDF) is deleted (`quotes.pdfFileId` is `onDelete: set null`, so the `files` row and its S3/MinIO object simply become unreferenced — the same pre-existing gap as any other upload in this codebase).
- **Quotes mobile (S-03.12)** — fully out of scope until `apps/mobile` exists; PRD explicitly schedules this for Phase 5. The public-link/token design has no web-only assumption baked in that would need revisiting for a mobile "capture acceptance on site" flow, though that story most likely wants a distinct in-app authenticated capture path rather than reusing the public customer-facing link — a decision left for Phase 5.
- Quotes' own smaller loose ends within Stage 1's scope: no drag-and-drop line reordering (up/down buttons only — a deliberate simplification noted in `quote-line-editor.tsx`'s own comment, since a bounded per-quote line list doesn't need a drag library and buttons keep it fully keyboard-operable); no CSV/bulk quote import. ~~No quote-level audit history *view*~~ — **done**, see the 2026-08-29 "History for Catalogue and Quotes" Completed entry.

All of FEAT-01 · Contacts & CRM's 8 stories are now complete. S-01.3's timeline currently merges quotes + activities only (invoices/payments don't exist until Phase 2) — see the Timeline entry below for how it's structured to grow without a rework once those land.

Quotes/invoices should also grow their own attachments via the new `files` table/endpoints once they exist (Files was deliberately built generic — a plain nullable FK per consumer, not polymorphic — precisely for this).

Worth building if a real need for one surfaces.

A "block delete if referenced" guard would actually be *wrong* here, unlike Contacts (where `journal_lines.contactId` genuinely matters for AR aging/reporting). Verified live: deleted a catalog item referenced by a real quote line — the delete succeeded, the quote line's `catalogItemId` went to `null`, and its snapshotted name/quantity/price were untouched. The web UI's delete confirmation already warns "Prefer Archive if this item may be referenced by a quote or invoice later," which is the correct/sufficient safeguard for what is deliberately a non-blocking relationship.

### 2026-10-11 — Every action says when it's done (US-OPS-38, US-CAT-16, D-223)

- **One toast host (US-OPS-38):** `apps/web/src/components/toast-host.tsx` — `ToastHost` in the app layout and `useToast()` anywhere under it. The layout stays mounted across pages, so a toast shown just before `router.push` shows on the page that opens. Toasts stack newest on top, 3 at most by default (2 at phone width), a new one over the maximum closing the oldest at once; each closes after 5 seconds by default, paused while the stack is hovered or a toast focused. The maximum and the interval are props on the host; a toast can set its own interval. Replaces the ten `entity-toast.tsx` copies (each page had its own provider and viewport, so a toast died with its page and a second one replaced the first), the contacts `sessionStorage` hand-off and the payments `?deleted=` and new job's `?created=` hand-offs. The permission toast (US-OPS-12) shows through the same host.
- **The toasts that were missing:** deleting a lead and marking it lost (with its reason, or where to add one); deleting a meeting or one occurrence; deleting a quote or an invoice from its page; revising, converting to an invoice or a job and duplicating a quote (from its page or a row); issuing a credit note from the list; recording a payment from the list ("RCP-0032 recorded" with the credit left or what it paid); completing and invoicing a milestone, applying a variation and removing someone from a job's crew; deleting a refund; removing an attachment.
- **`@spine/ui` Toast:** the viewport lays toasts out newest on top (`flex-col-reverse`) and spans the bottom of the screen below `sm`; a toast slides in from the right (not with Reduce Motion), its close sits at the top, and in dark mode it has a thin outline. The Toast doc page shows a stack.
- **Errors stay where the action was:** a toast no longer carries an error in the refined modules. Deleting a payment, Retry now and Cancel on the email log, the invoices list's row and bulk actions, the quotes list's revise, duplicate and customer link, the catalogue's bulk changes and pausing or resuming a recurring invoice or bill now show what went wrong above the list or page (`components/action-error.tsx`, with a close); a failed bulk change keeps the selection. Banking and expenses keep theirs until they're refined.
- **Bulk changes ask first (US-CAT-16):** the catalogue's bulk Set tax asks "Change the tax on 12 items?" with the new tax and that issued quotes and invoices keep theirs; Set category asks "Move 12 items to “Labour”?"; Set income account asks "Change the income account on 12 items?". Go back keeps the selection. Archive and Restore still don't ask.
- **Docs:** D-223, `09-design-system.md`, the Toast component doc and CLAUDE.md carry the rule; screens `ToastAfterNavigate`, `ToastStack`, `ToastStackDark`, `ToastStackPhone`, `CatalogBulkConfirm`.
- **Tests:** web unit `us-ops-38` (the maximum, phone width, the interval and ×, no host, the toast copy, the error message); UI a11y `toast` (a stack of three); E2E `us-ops-38` (record from the list, lead deleted and lost, the stack, deletes from a record's page, a failed delete shown on the page) and `us-cat-16`, with `us-cat-12` confirming its Set tax. QA script section 215.

- **The list (US-PAY-21, US-PAY-22):** cards for Received this month, Credit to use (a filter) and Refunded this month; rows show the reference, the account, what each payment was applied to and the credit left; newest first (it was oldest first); contact, method and date range filters, search, card, sort and page in the address, with Refresh; a row menu that opens the page's dialogs. `GET /payments` rows gain `appliedTo`, `refundedAmount` and `moneyAccountName`.
- **One Record payment dialog (US-PAY-23, US-PAY-24):** `components/record-payment-dialog.tsx` replaces the payments page's and the invoice page's copies (and the bank statement line's). The customer's open invoices are a checklist oldest due first with how late each is; ticking fills the amount, a typed amount is spread oldest first, and what goes on the invoices and what becomes credit is said before the button. "Email a receipt to …" is a switch (`POST /payments` `sendReceipt`). A payment from the same customer for the same amount within 3 days, or with the same reference, is flagged with a link to it (`GET /payments/possible-duplicates`).
- **Search (US-PAY-25):** a Payments group, by receipt number, reference or customer.
- **Move off an invoice (US-PAY-26):** from the payment's "Applied to" or the invoice's Payments, "Move off …" asks first with an optional reason, removes the allocation, posts P30 (Dr 1100 AR / Cr 2200 Customer Advances, dated today) and audits it on both; the money becomes the payment's credit. Not for deposit or void invoices. `POST /payments/:id/allocations/:allocationId/unapply`.
- **Demo:** demo payments no longer email a receipt to the demo customer, and a payment dated on its own day has its "Recorded" audit entry moved there too, so its page's Activity reads in order with names (checked for every demo in `us-onb-24-28`). The mobile app doesn't use any of these routes; its typecheck and tests pass unchanged.
- **Tests:** API integration `us-pay-19-26`; web unit `us-pay-20` to `us-pay-23`; E2E `us-pay-19-26`, with US-PAY-17, US-PAY-18, US-BANK-02, US-BANK-03, US-BANK-10, US-INV-32 and the quote-to-payment flow moved to the page and the new dialog. QA script section 213.

### 2026-10-11 — The email log (US-SET-27 to US-SET-29, US-DASH-30, D-220)

- **Every email, recorded (US-SET-27):** a new `email_log` table (migration 0114) holds every email Spine sends — when, to whom, the subject, the kind, the record it's about, the status, attempts and the last error; no bodies. Queued emails (quote, invoice, reminder, notification) go through `EmailLogService.enqueue`, and their workers wrap each try in `attempt`, which moves the row through Sending to Sent, Retrying or Failed. Emails sent straight away or by their own job (credit note, receipt, refund, statement, invitation, password reset, test, daily digest, data export) pass `log` to `EmailService.send`. A nightly `email-log-cleanup` job removes rows older than 180 days.
- **The page (US-SET-27):** `/emails`, Owner-only, from Settings › Emails ("Email log") and from a quote's or invoice's "Email failed" message ("See it in the email log", filtered to the record). Cards for Waiting, Failed in the last 7 days (filters) and Sent today; status, kind, range and search; the list in the address with Refresh (D-210).
- **Retry and cancel (US-SET-28):** "Retry now" on a failed or retrying queued email re-queues it with its stored job (attempts start over); "Cancel" stops a queued or retrying one before it sends, and the quote or invoice says "Email not sent — cancelled". Each asks first (D-218) and is audited. `POST /emails/:id/retry`, `POST /emails/:id/cancel`.
- **Not set up (US-SET-29):** with no SMTP server, the log and Settings › Emails say so and how many emails are waiting; a queued email isn't tried meanwhile (no attempts used) and goes out when Spine starts with SMTP set. When the last 3 queued emails in a row failed, the warning gives the error. `GET /emails/status`.
- **Dashboard (US-DASH-30):** an Owner's Needs your attention lists "<n> emails failed", naming the first; Review opens the log filtered to Failed. The digest's table names it "Emails that failed".
- **Retired (US-QUO-07):** the quotes list's "Email queue" dialog, `GET /quotes/email-queue` and `QueueService.listPendingJobs`.
- **Tests:** API integration `us-set-27-29` (with US-DASH-30); web unit `us-set-27`, `us-set-28`, `us-set-29`, `us-dash-30`; E2E `us-set-27-28`. Tests that build services by hand pass the email log. QA script section 212.

### 2026-10-11 — The meeting quick view opens in place (US-MTG-14 fix)

A late meeting's quick view opened without its attendees, which load a moment later; when they arrived it grew past the bottom of the window for a frame, then jumped up to fit. It now shows the Attendees heading with a placeholder row while they load, so it opens at its full height and is placed once. This is what made "a late meeting's quick view stays inside the window" fail about half the time. The test now records the quick view's edges on every frame from the click, so a jump past the window fails it every time. QA script section 204 notes the check.

### 2026-10-11 — Credit notes you can work from (US-INV-36 to US-INV-41, US-ONB-29, D-219)

- **Credit with the tax (US-INV-36):** the issue dialog credits the invoice's own lines — ticked lines and how many, or an amount spread over the lines by what's left on each (`spreadCreditAmount`) — and works each credit line out from its invoice line's figures in proportion, so tax (by component), discounts and tax-inclusive prices come back exactly as invoiced. Before, the dialog made one untaxed free-text line, so a credit note never reduced the tax owed. The totals, tax by name and the split show before the button (`POST /credit-notes/preview`); a line or invoice can't be credited past what's left (`GET /credit-notes/creditable`). `credit_note_lines` gains `invoice_line_id`, `tax_rate_id` and `tax_group_id` (migration 0113).
- **New credit note (US-INV-37):** from the list, pick the invoice (`leftToCredit` on `GET /invoices`), then the same dialog; the new credit note's page opens.
- **A credit note page (US-INV-38, US-INV-39):** `/credit-notes/:id` replaces the drawer — one next step (Apply credit, Email, Download PDF), a strip of Credited, Off the invoice, Applied, Refunded and Credit left, the lines with tax by name, refunds, attachments and Activity (`GET /credit-notes/:id/activity`). Apply credit spreads the credit over the customer's open invoices. Invoices, their Activity, ledger drill-downs and search (a new Credit notes group) link to it.
- **The list (US-INV-40, US-INV-41):** cards for Credited this month, Credit to use (a filter) and Refunded this month; rows show the reason and where each credit went, with a row menu; search, filters, card, sort and page in the address, with Refresh. `use-credit-note-stats.ts` and `credit-note-detail-drawer.tsx` are gone.
- **Invoice page:** the Paid bar counts payments only; "Issue credit note" shows only while something's left to credit.
- **Fix:** the invoice page's "Issue anyway" (the HSN/SAC question) had its handler written as `() => void …`, which US-OPS-10's check for red delete/void buttons read as "void" and failed on; it passed earlier only because Turborepo served the API tests from cache (they read the web app's files, which aren't in the API's cache inputs). The handler is now named.
- **Demo (US-ONB-29):** each demo has three credit notes crediting lines with tax — off the invoice, applied (industry demos) or kept to use, and refunded — dated on their own days this month. A refund of a demo credit note's credit is flagged demo and deleted with the demo, with any applied credit.
- **Tests:** API integration `us-inv-36-41`, demo `us-onb-24-28` (US-ONB-29 added), US-PAY-16's helper and US-ONB-17's numbers; shared `us-onb-24-28` (all demos); web unit `us-inv-36`, `us-inv-39` to `us-inv-41`; E2E `us-inv-36` to `us-inv-41`, `us-onb-29`, with US-PAY-16 and the route smoke test updated. QA script section 211.

### 2026-10-11 — A major action asks first (D-218)

Anything that can't be taken back, changes the books, emails a customer or acts on many records asks before it happens, with `useConfirm()` — a new hook in `@spine/ui` (AlertDialog doc page and a11y test). Newly confirmed: Record and Delete draft on vendor bills (page and row menu); Record, Remove from bill and Delete refund on vendor credits; bulk Approve on expenses; Revise (page and row menu), Convert to invoice, Convert to job and Approve discount on quotes; removing someone from a job's crew and applying a variation to the contract; removing opening invoices, bills and credits; deleting tax payments and customer refunds; finishing a bank reconciliation; cancelling an invitation. Each question says what happens to the data; delete, void and remove are red (D-058). Invoices' own confirmations are in the entry below (D-217). CLAUDE.md and the design-system rules carry the rule. Tests: `useConfirm` a11y and behaviour (`@spine/ui`); E2E `d-218` (Go back changes nothing, the verb acts); the quote, banking, purchases, payments and tax specs answer the new questions. QA script section 210.

The invoices list, the invoice page and the builder are brought up to the refined quotes and jobs screens.

- **Cards (US-INV-27):** Outstanding, Overdue and Due in 7 days show balance totals with counts, in the business's currency ("+ other currencies" when some aren't), and filter the list; Paid this month adds up the payments dated this month that paid invoices. `use-invoice-stats.ts` is gone; the cards read the list. "Received since 1 Oct" is the first of the month in the business's locale, shown once payments load (it had been built from the browser's locale on the server too, so a day-first browser hit a hydration error).
- **The list (US-INV-28, US-INV-29):** search, statuses, contact, card, sort and page live in the address (D-210), with Refresh and a quiet refresh after 30 s away; search covers numbers, customers, line names and jobs. Each row has one status (Draft, Due, Part paid, Paid, Overdue, Void), what kind of invoice it is under the number ("Progress claim 2 · JOB-002", "Deposit"), the issue date, a due countdown or "Paid 2 Oct", and the balance with a bar of what's paid; the row menu offers Issue, Record payment, Email invoice, Send reminder, Download PDF, Duplicate and Void, opening the invoice with `?action=`. `GET /invoices` rows gain `lineNames`, `job` and `lastPaidAt`.

One primary button is the next step (Issue invoice, Send reminder, Record payment, else Download PDF), the rest beside it or under More; a strip reads Total, Paid (last date and bar), Retention held or Credited, and Balance due. An Activity panel (`GET /invoices/:id/activity`) tells the invoice's story — created, from a quote or milestone, duplicated, edited, issued, emailed, reminded, paid (with method and receipt link), credited, voided — newest first. Preview PDF (`POST /invoices/preview-pdf`) renders the invoice on screen with a "Preview only — not a valid invoice" watermark and saves nothing; a draft's PDF carries the watermark too.
- **Confirm before acting (D-217):** Issue invoice asks "Issue this invoice?" (who will owe what, when it's due, and that it can then only be voided or credited) unless the HSN/SAC or credit question already asks; Delete draft asks; the bulk "Send reminders" asks "Send N payment reminders?". The row menu's Send reminder and the dashboard's one-overdue-invoice "Send reminder" (US-DASH-13) now open the invoice with the reminder email to check and send, instead of emailing the customer in one click.
- **Duplicate (US-INV-35):** `POST /invoices/:id/duplicate` makes a new draft with the same customer, currency, lines, notes and terms (a deposit stays a deposit; other types become standard); the builder opens it dated today, due on the terms, with "Duplicated from INV-…".
- **Demo (US-ONB-28):** every demo has an invoice due this week and one overdue (Riverstone's deposit is due in 5 days); some invoices were emailed on their issue day and reminded once late, recorded as the app records them (no real email is queued); invoices, milestone invoices and payments carry their own days in Activity.
- **StatCard:** a `critical` tone (red value), with its docs page and a11y test.
- **Tests:** API integration `us-inv-27-35`, `us-onb-24-28`; web unit `us-inv-27` to `us-inv-29`, `us-inv-32`, `us-inv-33`; shared `us-onb-24-28` (all demos); E2E `us-inv-27` to `us-inv-35`, `us-onb-28`, with the invoice and quote specs updated for the moved actions; US-OPS-21 opens the list filtered to void invoices, US-PAY-10 waits for the receivables rather than the loading rows, US-QUO-31 matches the toast's text exactly, and US-OPS-22 searches for an overdue invoice it looks up rather than "INV-0002", which the job specs now create (all four were order-dependent on the shared demo org). Missing tax counts taxable items with no tax; for a GST business zero-rated items don't count, elsewhere any untaxed item that isn't exempt or non-taxable does.

One save through `POST /catalog-items/bulk` changes every item or none, checking each item's own/others rights first. For a GST business a GST group brings the matching IGST rate as the inter-state tax. Duplicate opens Add item filled from the row. Export downloads `catalogue-<date>.csv` with the list as filtered, in Import's columns plus Category, which Import now reads.

Bundles has an empty state with "Choose items".

In a production build each `router.replace` went to the server, so an earlier keystroke could land after a later one and leave a stale search in the address (US-CRM-28's Back check failed against the production build); the spec's address check is now exact.

### 2026-10-10 — A pipeline that works (US-CRM-24 to US-CRM-28, D-211)

- **The board (US-CRM-24):**
  - Open stages share the width (six fit at 1280 px) and every column, Won and Lost included, runs the full height of the page; a long column scrolls on its own. When the stages don't fit, a shadow at the edge says there's more.
  - Won and Lost are slim columns with the last 30 days' count and total; pressing one opens it (newest first) and "Hide" closes it. Older closed leads show by choosing that stage in the stage filter.
  - A summary strip: open pipeline (per currency), won this month, win rate (won ÷ won and lost, closed in the last 90 days) and overdue follow-ups, which filters the board. An empty open column says "No leads in this stage".
- **Cards (US-CRM-25):** owner initials (name on hover; "—" when unassigned), "12 days in stage", the next follow-up ("Call · Tomorrow 10:00", in the overdue colour when past due), "No activity for N days" after 14 quiet days, the lost reason on lost cards and "Won 2 Oct" on won ones. A card is one button (Tab, Enter); its "⋯" menu (or the menu key) has Open, Move to… and Delete, and a move is announced ("Moved to Proposal").
- **Won and lost (US-CRM-26):** moving to Lost (drag, menu or drawer) asks why: Price, Timing, Went with a competitor, No response, Other, and a note; "Skip" moves it without one, and leaving Lost clears it. Moving to Won offers "Create quote" to people who can create quotes: the new quote takes the lead's contact and currency, says which lead it's for, and is linked to it (`quotes.lead_id`, kept on revisions).
- **The lead drawer (US-CRM-27):** replaces the lead dialog on the board, with owner (any active member or Unassigned) and expected close date, the lead's follow-ups (log an activity, add a follow-up, tick one done), its quotes and its history (created and each stage change, from the audit log). "Add lead" opens it at the column's stage.
- **Filters and refresh (US-CRM-28):** owner ("My leads", each member, "Unassigned") and source filters join search, stage, sort and View; they all live in the address (`/leads?owner=me&source=Referral`). Refresh and "Updated … ago" work as on Contacts, including a refresh after 30 seconds away.
- **API and data:** migration `0111` adds `leads.stage_changed_at` (backfilled from `updated_at`), `expected_close_date`, `lost_reason`, `lost_note` and `quotes.lead_id`. `GET /leads` adds `stageChangedAt`, `lastActivityAt` and `nextFollowUp`; `PUT /leads/:id` takes `ownerUserId` (an active member), `expectedCloseDate`, `lostReason` and `lostNote`; `GET /leads/:id/history`; `POST /quotes` takes `leadId` (same contact) and `GET /quotes?leadId=` lists a lead's quotes. Removing a stage that still has leads also restarts their days in stage.
- **Components:** `KanbanColumn` takes `collapsed` / `onExpand` / `expandLabel` (a slim column), `accent` and `headerAction`; `KanbanCard` takes `onOpen` / `label` (the card is one focusable button), `menu` and `onMenuKey`; `KanbanBoard` shows edge shadows. Cards no longer widen a column with long text. `ActivitiesSection` takes `leadId`, `heading` and `followUps`.
- **Tests:**
  - New: `us-crm-25`, `us-crm-26` and `us-crm-27` API integration; `us-crm-24`, `us-crm-25` and `us-crm-28` web unit; `us-crm-24` to `us-crm-28` E2E; Kanban a11y and keyboard tests.
  - `us-crm-19` and `us-crm-20` read the board's stage names from the columns, since Won and Lost no longer have headings.
  - Native drag and drop still can't be driven in Playwright, so the E2E tests move cards with the menu, which runs the same code as a drop. Cold-lead nudges need 14 days to pass, so the unit tests cover them.
  - QA script section 203.
- **Design:** canvas "06 Pipeline"; six artboards.

### 2026-10-09 — CI confirms instead of discovering: `pnpm verify` and a faster, cheaper pipeline (D-205)

- **`pnpm verify`** runs what CI runs, locally and in CI's order: lint → typecheck → unit → integration → E2E.
  - It creates and migrates `spine_test` and `spine_e2e` when they're missing.
  - It stops at the first failure and says `pnpm verify --from <step>`; `--skip e2e` leaves a step out.
  - Run it before opening a PR or marking it ready.
- **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):**
  - "Lint, typecheck and unit" runs first, with no services (about 5 min). Integration and E2E then run side by side instead of one after the other.
  - Each suite runs only when the code it covers changed: a mobile-only change skips both.
  - The first of integration and E2E to fail cancels the other. Integration stops at five failing tests (`--bail=5`); E2E after five failing specs (`maxFailures`) and now keeps an HTML report for the failure artifact.
  - The required checks keep their names ("Unit and integration" is now a gate over the static and integration jobs), so `main`'s branch protection is unchanged.
- Expected: a full run goes from about 45 minutes of wall time to about 25, and a failure stops within minutes instead of running to the end.

  - "Present" on a job's quote opens it full-screen, read live from the server. It shows "Hand the phone to your customer", the business and address, "QUOTE <number>", "Prepared for", "Valid until", the lines with quantity × price, Subtotal, each tax by name ("Sales Tax (15%)", or CGST and SGST in India), Total and Notes.
  - At the bottom are "Decline" and "Accept quote".
  - Decline is a sheet: "<customer> is declining <number> for <total>. <Business>'s office is told straight away.", "Reason (optional)" and a red "Decline quote". Offline it says "Needs a connection — declining can't be saved offline." and the button stays off.
  - New `POST /quotes/:id/reject-in-person`, which notifies "Quote <number> was declined in person."
- **Accept (US-MOB-17):**
  - The customer types their name and signs in the box. The statement names the total, the customer, the business and the staff member present.
  - "Accept and sign" stays off with a hint ("Type the customer's name to continue." / "Sign in the box to continue.") until both are there.
  - "Quote accepted" then shows who signed and when, that the office was told and the quote is locked, the witness, and "In person, on this phone".
  - The quote leaves the job's "Quotes to present" straight away.
  - The signature is drawn and encoded as a PNG on the phone, with no new native module (D-202). The accept screen turns off the swipe-back gesture so a signature isn't taken as "back".
- **Needs a connection (US-MOB-18):** offline, "Present" shows "Quotes need a connection" with why, "Photos, expenses and milestone updates still work offline.", "Try again" and "Back to job". On Android this is an alert over the job.
- **Signature stored (US-QUO-19):**
  - `quotes.signature_file_id` and `accepted_signer_name` (migration `0110`).
  - `signerName` is required.
  - The signature must be an image the caller uploaded in the organisation.
  - The signature file is read by Owners and Staff with the quote, never by Field.
  - Accepting in person now also sends the variation-order "apply it to the job" nudge, as the link does.
- **Field reaches only quotes to present:** `GET /quotes/:id`, accept and decline in person, for Field, only reach a sent variation order or source quote on a job they're on (404 otherwise, before the status check). Before, Field could accept any sent quote in the organisation by id.
- **`GET /quotes/:id`** also returns `business`, `taxLines` (tax by named rate, summing to the tax) and `acceptedByName`.
- **How it was accepted (US-QUO-20):**
  - The quote page shows "Accepted on site — Signed by <name> on <date> at <time>, witnessed by <name>" with the signature and "View signature full size", or "Accepted online by the customer on <date>".
  - Declines show the same way, with the reason.
  - History reads "The customer accepted this quote online" / "<person> recorded the customer's acceptance of this quote on site, signed by <name>".
- The temporary "arrives in the next update" message for "Present" is gone.

### 2026-10-09 — Phase 5 Group 3: offline, the outbox, Sync and Fix (US-MOB-07, US-MOB-08, US-MOB-09)

- **The outbox:** photos, expenses and milestone completions made on the phone wait in a SQLite outbox, with compressed copies of their photos (long edge 2048 px, JPEG 70%, D-053) in the app's documents folder, until the server has them.
  - Each item's id is its `Idempotency-Key`, and each step uses a key derived from it. Progress is saved after every step, so a retry resumes and never duplicates.
  - It sends oldest first: when something is queued, when the phone reconnects or returns to the foreground, and on "Try sending now".
  - Network errors, 5xx, 408, 409 and 429 retry with back-off (5 s doubling to 5 min) and stay "Waiting". Other refusals become "Didn't send: <reason>" with Fix. A 426 or an ended session pauses sending and keeps everything. Photos over 10 MB, or no longer on the phone, need fixing before anything is sent.
  - The outbox belongs to one person on one server. Signing out or losing access deletes it; an expired session keeps it; someone else signing in never sends it.
  - Group 4's screens add items with `outbox.addPhotos/addExpense/addCompletion`.
- **Offline (US-MOB-07):**
  - Today says "You're offline" and what still works, with "Showing jobs as of <time>", following the phone's own connection (expo-network).
  - Jobs seen before open from the phone.
  - Job cards show "2 photos waiting" / "Completion waiting"; a job shows "Completion waiting" on the milestone and "Waiting" on its photos; Search lists waiting expenses.
  - Back online, the banner goes, every screen refetches and the outbox sends.
- **Sync (US-MOB-08):**
  - The pill reads "<n> waiting to sync" in amber and opens Sync (also from Profile's Sync row and the sign-out warning's "Send them first").
  - Sync shows "<n> items waiting" and why, "Try sending now", NEEDS FIXING, WAITING and SENT TODAY ("Already completed by <name>").
  - A page sheet on iOS, a page on Android.
- **Fix (US-MOB-09):**
  - The reason in red and the item's details.
  - For an expense: the receipt with its size ("14.2 MB · over the 10 MB limit"), "Retake photo", "Choose a different photo" (expo-image-picker, offering Settings if access is refused), "Remove photo", "Send again" and "Delete this expense" (the bin in the top bar on Android).
  - Photos and milestone updates can lose a photo, be sent again or be deleted.
- **API — completing a milestone that's already completed** (first write wins, 02-architecture; built for US-MOB-15):
  - Answers 201 with `alreadyCompleted` and `completedBy`, and changes nothing about the milestone (previously 400).
  - The photos sent with it are still attached.
  - History records `milestone_completion_ignored`.
- **Tests:**
  - Phone: us-mob-07, 08 and 09 (124 Jest tests in total).
  - API: us-mob-09 (each step replayed with the same key creates nothing twice; the late completion; the 10 MB limit).
  - Maestro: `e2e/us-mob-07-offline.yaml` (airplane mode on Android) and the earlier flows pass on both phones. Sync and Fix checked on both against `MobSyncQueue` and `MobSyncFix`.
- **Docs:** 02-architecture §Offline (keys, retries, ownership), 05-api, 07-security, the story notes, native notes, and QA section 193.

### 2026-10-08 — Field app loading states: skeletons per section (D-201)

- **Skeletons while data loads:** a section with nothing saved on the phone and its first request still out shows blocks in its own shape. Headings and quick actions don't wait. This covers:
  - Today: the gauge (an arc), the KPI cards, the job cards and the next meeting.
  - The Jobs list.
  - A job: the heading, milestones, photos and quotes.
  - Photos, Notifications, Search, an expense and a meeting.
  - An empty state ("No jobs…", "You're all caught up", "No results") never shows while loading.
- **Today's period switch:** switching shows skeletons for the gauge and KPI cards only; the jobs and meeting stay. A period already fetched shows at once from the phone. `useCachedQuery` now keeps its state per key, so the previous period's numbers are never shown for the new one, and a late answer for an old key is ignored. It also returns `loading`.
- **No page loader** (D-201): the read cache makes most screens instant, a full-page spinner would hide saved data during a slow refresh, and pull to refresh already has the system spinner.
- **`@spine/ui-native` Skeleton:** holds still with Reduce Motion on, and is hidden from VoiceOver and TalkBack. Each loading region is announced once instead ("Loading jobs", busy). Updated a11y test and doc page.
- **Fix:** the Jobs list showed the state as the town for addresses ending in "<state> <postcode>" ("Karnataka" instead of "Bengaluru").
- **Tests:** skeleton cases added to us-mob-03, 04, 05, 22 and 23 (100 phone tests). Checked on the iPhone simulator with requests slowed down for the check.

  - Server, email and password in `FloatingLabelField` rows. Errors sit under their field ("Can't reach that server…", "Invalid email or password.").
  - The typed address is checked with `GET /health` at `<address>/api`, then at `<address>`.

  - Story Jest tests in `apps/mobile/src/__tests__` (36).
  - API integration tests `us-mob-01`, `us-mob-02` and `us-mob-10` (real HTTP with bearer sign-in).
  - Shared tests `us-mob-02` and `us-mob-10`.
- **Run on devices:** built for the iPhone 17 simulator and the Pixel 9 emulator. `apps/mobile/e2e/us-mob-01-sign-in.yaml` passes on both: wrong password, sign in, reopen still signed in, Profile, sign out. "Couldn't load your jobs" was checked by stopping the API. Fixes found on the devices:

### 2026-10-08 — US-ONB-18 fix: loading a demo works on a real install

- **The bug:** "Load demo business" failed near the end with "You don't have permission to do that. If you need to, ask an owner.". A second try then said "Demo data is already loaded."
- **Cause:** the demo Staff and Field logins were created through public sign-up, which is closed once a business has an owner (US-AUTH-08). Tests had sign-up forced open, so they never saw it.
- **Logins:** the demo people are now written directly, with a password hashed the way sign-in checks it. Loading a demo no longer goes through sign-up.
- **Failed loads:** a load that fails part-way now removes what it had added, so it can simply be tried again.
- **Tests:** a new test loads a demo with sign-up closed and the demo people not yet created; it reproduces the 403 on the old code. Another checks that a failed load leaves nothing behind.

### 2026-10-08 — `pnpm db:reset:dev` clears every table (dev tooling)

- **What changed:** the reset now truncates every table in the `public` schema, read from the database each time it runs, instead of a hand-kept list.
- **Why:** the list had fallen 22 tables behind. Those tables were still emptied through their foreign keys, but a future table without one would have survived a reset.
- **What stays:** Drizzle's migration log (in its own `drizzle` schema), so no migrations replay.

### 2026-10-08 — US-ONB-18, US-ONB-19, US-ONB-21: demo businesses by country and industry (Phase 9)

- **Choose your demo:** "Just show me around" on the welcome screen, and "Load demo data" in Settings › Data, open "Explore a demo business":
  - Seven countries: United States, India, United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, UAE and Saudi Arabia.
  - Five industries: Construction, Interior design & fit-out, Trades, IT services & agency and Professional services.
  - The country is guessed from the browser's time zone.
- **Realistic history:** each demo has about six months ending today — paid, part-paid, overdue, voided and draft invoices; quotes; jobs with milestones (and retention, variation orders); bills; expenses; a credit note; leads and meetings. Numbers follow dates.
- **Settings:**
  - On a business with no records of its own, loading also sets the country, currency, tax, financial year and template.
  - Once it has records, the country is fixed and nothing of yours changes.
  - Settings › Data names the loaded demo; a second demo can't be loaded on top.
- **India (US-ONB-19):** a Bengaluru business with a GSTIN, HSN/SAC codes, CGST + SGST, IGST, SEZ supplies, B2C large and small sales, exports under LUT, a credit note, and input GST from registered vendors. Its GSTR-1 for this month and last has every table, no problems, and totals equal to the Tax Summary.
- **UK, Australia, New Zealand, UAE and Saudi Arabia (US-ONB-21):** local contacts and prices, each country's VAT or GST, untaxed export lines, and VAT on expenses. UK invoices are titled "VAT invoice". UK new-build works are zero-rated, and mobility aids are at 5%.
- **Unchanged default:** `POST /demo-data/seed` with no body still loads Riverstone Builders, exactly as before.

### 2026-10-08 — US-ONB-20: industry templates for more kinds of business (Phase 9)

- **Four new templates:** the Template step and Settings › Industry template now list Interior design & fit-out, Trades (electrical, plumbing, HVAC), IT services & agency and Professional services, alongside Construction / Contracting, General Services and Generic. Each says what it sets up.

  - Trades adds 5700 Parts & Consumables, 5710 Tools & Equipment and 5720 Vehicle Running.
  - Professional services adds 5900 Research & Subscriptions and 6450 Professional Indemnity Insurance.

### 2026-10-08 — US-ONB-17: demo data stays out of my numbers and books (Phase 9)

- **Own number series:** demo documents are numbered `DEMO-INV-0001`, `DEMO-QUO-0001`, `DEMO-JOB-001` and so on. Your own first invoice is still `INV-0001`, with or without demo data loaded.
- **Demo spreads to new records:** anything saved for a demo contact (a quote, invoice, payment, credit note, bill, vendor payment or job), or an expense on a demo job, is demo too, and goes with the demo data.
- **"Delete all demo data" leaves no trace.** It now also removes:
  - The journal entries the demo posted, so every report, the Tax Summary, GSTR-1 and the Tally export are as if it never existed.
  - The demo number series, so loading demo data again starts at 0001.
  - Demo contacts and jobs. One that a record of your own uses (a refund or a vendor credit, say) is kept, and Settings › Data says "Kept 1 demo contact that your own records use.".
- **Ledger rules unchanged for real entries.** Only demo entries can be deleted, and only by that one action. The database refuses every other delete or change, inside that action too (D-191 amends the immutability rule for demo rows only).
- **For developers:**
  - Migration `0108`: `number_sequences.is_demo`, `journal_entries.is_demo`, the demo-inheritance triggers and the narrowed immutability triggers. It also flags the entries of demo documents already loaded.
  - `NumberingService.allocateNumber(…, { demo })`; `LedgerService.postEntry` reads the flag from the source document.
  - Demo invoices in tests now match `DEMO-INV-…`.

### 2026-10-07 — US-RPT-38: export my books for Tally (Phase 9)

- Reports › Export to Tally (Accountant group): choose From and To and press "Export". A ZIP downloads with `masters.xml`, `vouchers.xml` and `README.txt`.
- The README says how to import (Gateway of Tally › Import › Masters, then Transactions; Tally.ERP 9's menus too) and lists the accounts still on their default group.
- The page shows:
  - Ledgers, vouchers, and the number of accounts on default groups (with "review the mapping").
  - Each Spine document with its Tally voucher type and count.
- Masters: every account used in the range is a ledger under its mapped group (US-RPT-39). Customers are under Sundry Debtors and vendors under Sundry Creditors, bill-wise, with address, state, GSTIN and GST registration type.
- Vouchers come from the ledger (one per journal entry, always balanced):
  - Invoices → Sales; bills → Purchase.
  - Customer payments and money in → Receipt; vendor payments, refunds, expenses and money out → Payment.
  - Transfers → Contra.
  - Journals, opening balances and voids → Journal.
  - Credit notes → Credit Note; vendor credits → Debit Note.
- Bill-wise references name the invoice or bill (New Ref, Agst Ref, or On Account).
- Downloads are audited. `GET /exports/tally` needs "View financial statements".
- Sample files for an import check are in `docs/samples/tally/`; a test keeps them equal to what the export writes. D-186 and R-16 record the format choices.

### 2026-10-07 — US-RPT-39: map my accounts to Tally groups (Phase 9)

- Reports › Export to Tally › Account mapping lists every account with its code, its Spine type and a "Tally group" picker of Tally's predefined groups. You can filter by account type and search.
- The first time, each account is pre-mapped:
  - By money account: bank → Bank Accounts, cash → Cash-in-Hand, card → Bank OD A/c.
  - By code: 1000 → Cash-in-Hand; 1200 and 2100 → Duties & Taxes; 1500s → Fixed Assets; 2500 → Loans (Liability); 3200 → Reserves & Surplus.
  - By type: 4000–4799 → Sales Accounts; other income → Indirect Incomes; 5xxx → Direct Expenses; other expenses → Indirect Expenses; other equity → Capital Account; other assets and liabilities → Current Assets and Current Liabilities.
- An Owner changes groups and presses "Save mapping"; later exports use them. Members with "View financial statements" can read the mapping but not change it.
- `GET/PUT /exports/tally/mapping`; the saved groups are in `settings.tally_mapping`.

### 2026-10-07 — D-185: invoices post on their issue date (Phase 9)

- Issuing an invoice now dates its journal entry on the invoice's issue date (today when none was set), not on the day it's issued. A backdated invoice lands in its own month in the ledger, P&L, the Tax Summary and GSTR-1, so the GSTR-1 totals check agrees.
- An issue date inside a closed fiscal period is refused with the closed-period message.
- Voids still reverse on the day they're voided. Credit notes, which have no date of their own, post on the day they're issued.
- This closes Q-20 (D-185). The posting rules gain invariant 8.

### 2026-10-07 — US-TAX-15: print GST details on invoices and credit notes (Phase 9)

- With GST on (the document has a supply type), the invoice PDF follows the GST rules:
  - It's titled "TAX INVOICE", or "BILL OF SUPPLY" when every line is exempt or non-taxable.
  - The header shows the business's address and GSTIN.
  - "Billed to" adds the customer's address and their GSTIN when they're registered or an SEZ unit.
  - A "Place of supply" block reads, for example, "Karnataka (29) · Intra-state supply" (or Inter-state supply, or Export).
  - Each line shows its HSN/SAC, a "Taxable value", and its tax split into CGST and SGST (or UTGST, or IGST, plus any cess). Column headings carry the rate when every line has the same one, e.g. "CGST 9%".
