- Credit notes show the same GST details, plus the original invoice's number and date.
- With "Tax summary table" on (Settings › Documents), an HSN-wise summary follows the lines: taxable value, each tax and the total tax. Without GST, the summary is by rate.
- Without a GST profile nothing changes: the PDF keeps its Subtotal/Discount/Tax totals and its title.
- A line's tax is split in proportion to its rates and always adds back up to the line's tax (`splitLineTax` in `@spine/shared`).
- The PDF test helper now reads each stream by its declared length, because compressed bytes can contain "endobj". This also steadies the US-SET-10 and US-RPT-33 checks.

### 2026-10-07 — Exports under LUT, rates that carry their supply type, and recurring and variation-order lines that follow the customer's state (D-181–D-183, Phase 9)

The owner's answers to Q-18 and Q-19, plus closing the recurring and variation-order gap left by US-TAX-13.

- **Exports under LUT (D-181):** Settings › GST › "We export under LUT".
  - When it's on, an export's place-of-supply hint reads "Export under LUT, so items have no IGST.", and lines added from items have no tax and are zero-rated.
  - Changing a draft's place of supply to or from an export switches those lines.
  - When it's off, exports charge IGST as before.
- **0% rates carry their supply type (D-182):** a 0% rate now says whether its lines are zero-rated, exempt or non-taxable ("Lines with this rate are" in the rate dialog).
  - Rate rows read "0% · VAT · Exempt".
  - Picking the rate on a line gives the line that type.
  - The presets mark "Exempt" exempt and their other 0% rate zero-rated. Migration `0105` adds `tax_rates.supply_class` and backfills the preset rates.
  - The API uses the rate's class when a line doesn't name one.
- **Recurring schedules and variation orders (D-183):** their line editors work out intra- or inter-state from the contact's addresses, pick each item's matching tax, and switch lines when the contact changes, with the same banner as invoices.
  - Recurring invoices and bills also show HSN/SAC.
  - Variation orders copy the item's HSN/SAC code.
  - Each invoice a schedule creates takes the contact's place of supply at that time.
- Q-18 and Q-19 are closed.

### 2026-10-07 — US-TAX-14: add HSN or SAC codes to items and lines (Phase 9)

- In an Indian business, catalogue items have an "HSN/SAC code": 4, 6 or 8 digits, otherwise "Enter 4, 6 or 8 digits.".
- Document lines on quotes, invoices, vendor bills and vendor credits show "HSN/SAC" next to Supply type when GST is on.
  - The code is copied from the item and can be changed on the line.
  - Lines snapshot it, so issued documents keep it.
  - Recurring schedules, bundles and quote-to-invoice conversion carry it over.
- Issuing an invoice to a registered business (or SEZ unit) with item lines that have no code asks first: "<n> lines have no HSN/SAC code. GSTR-1 needs them." The choices are "Go back" or "Issue anyway".
- Catalogue import maps an "HSN/SAC" column. Spaces are dropped, and a bad code fails the row.
- Migration `0104`: `hsn_sac` on catalogue items and every line table.
- Any request body that fails its schema now answers 400 with a readable `message` (new global `ZodExceptionFilter`). Before, the 17 controllers that call `schema.parse(body)` answered 500.

### 2026-10-07 — US-TAX-13: pick intra- or inter-state GST automatically (Phase 9)

- In an Indian business with a GST state, quotes, invoices, vendor bills and vendor credits have a "Place of supply".
  - It comes from the customer's site or shipping address, else billing, else the contact's state. An overseas customer gets "Other countries (96)".
  - The hint says where it came from and which tax applies, for example "From the site address · Inter-state, so items use their IGST rate."
  - It can be changed.
  - Vendor bills and vendor credits use the vendor's state.
  - A credit note takes its invoice's.
- The supply type follows the place of supply:
  - The business's own state is intra-state.
  - Another state, or an SEZ unit, is inter-state.
  - An overseas customer is an export, which charges IGST (Q-18 still asks whether LUT exports are needed).
- Adding a catalogue item uses its intra-state tax in my state and its inter-state tax elsewhere.
- Changing the place of supply on a draft between intra- and inter-state switches every line still on its item's tax.
  - Lines changed by hand, and taxed one-off lines, keep their tax and show "Check this line's tax — the place of supply changed."
  - A banner sums up what happened: "The place of supply changed to Karnataka (29): 1 line switched to CGST + SGST; 1 line you changed by hand keeps its tax — check it."
- Catalogue items in India have "Intra-state tax" and "Inter-state tax".
  - New items start from Settings › Tax › "Default tax preference".
  - Choosing India sets that preference to GST 18% and IGST 18%.
- The place of supply and supply type are saved on every draft and frozen when the quote is sent, the invoice or credit note issued, or the bill or vendor credit recorded. Detail pages show them.
- Migration `0103`: `place_of_supply` and `supply_type` on quotes, invoices, credit notes, vendor bills and vendor credits, plus `inter_tax_rate_id` and `inter_tax_group_id` on catalogue items.
- The rules (`supplyTypeFor`, `placeOfSupplyFor`, `itemTaxFor`, `switchLineTaxes`) are in `@spine/shared` with unit tests. The API uses them through `PlaceOfSupplyService`.
- Fixed an older bug: updating a draft quote, invoice, credit note, vendor bill or vendor credit without sending its lines cleared them. A partial invoice update also reset its type to Standard, and a partial expense update reset its tax, who paid and billable. Update schemas no longer apply create-time defaults.

### 2026-10-07 — US-TAX-12: record my GSTIN and state, and each customer's (Phase 9)

- New Settings › GST pane, shown when the tax country is India. It asks for GSTIN, State, Legal name, Trade name, Registered on and Return period.
  - The GSTIN is checked for format and check character: "This GSTIN isn't valid — check the 15 characters."
  - Its first two digits must match the state: "This GSTIN belongs to <state>."
  - Typing the GSTIN fills in the state.
  - The pane notes that Spine never files returns or connects to the GST portal.
- The setup wizard opens the same form as "GST details" right after India is chosen. "Not registered yet — skip this step" moves on.
- A business in a union territory without a legislature gets its "GST n% (UT)" groups (CGST + UTGST) and their rates restored. The 12% and 28% groups stay archived.
- Contacts in an Indian business have:
  - "GST treatment": Registered business, Unregistered business, Consumer, Overseas or Special economic zone.
  - GSTIN, required for registered and SEZ contacts.
  - A State, which the GSTIN fills in when it's blank.
  - The contact page header shows the treatment, state and GSTIN.
- Each address has a State, as the place of supply comes from it.
- Contact import maps GSTIN and State columns. A GSTIN marks the contact registered. A state can be its code or name. A bad GSTIN or an unknown state flags the row.
- Migration `0102`: `contacts.gst_treatment`, `contacts.state_code` (D-146: contacts carry a state) and `addresses.state_code`. `PUT /org/tax/profile` now takes the GST fields.
- Request bodies that fail validation (`ZodValidationPipe`) now answer with the first problem as `message`, plus the full list as `issues`. Before, `message` was the issue list, which the web showed as "[object Object]".
- GSTIN and state-code helpers are in `@spine/shared` (`tax/gst.ts`).

### 2026-10-07 — US-TAX-11: mark supplies as zero-rated, exempt or outside tax (Phase 9)

- Catalogue items have a "Supply type": Taxable, Zero-rated, Exempt or "Non-taxable (outside GST/VAT)". An item with tax is always Taxable.
- Every document line carries a supply type: quotes, invoices, credit notes, vendor bills, vendor credits, recurring schedules, bundles and variation orders.
  - A line with no tax shows "Supply type". It comes from the item, else Zero-rated, and can be changed.
  - A line that gains tax becomes Taxable.
- An exempt or non-taxable line with a rate shows "An exempt line has no tax. Change the supply type to Taxable to add tax." The API refuses it with the same message.
- Lines snapshot their supply type. Issued documents keep it, and their detail pages show it after the tax (for example "· Exempt").
- Migration `0101` adds `supply_class` to `catalog_items` and every line table. Existing item lines with tax become taxable and the rest zero-rated. Heading and text lines have none.
- New `SupplyTypeField` in `apps/web/src/components`, shared by the quote, invoice, vendor bill and variation-order line editors.
- Open question Q-19: should a 0% rate such as the UK's "Exempt" imply its supply type?

### 2026-10-07 — US-TAX-09: start with my country's tax rates (Phase 9)

- The setup wizard's Tax step now asks "Where is your business registered for tax?". The choices are India (GST), United Kingdom (VAT), Australia (GST), New Zealand (GST), United Arab Emirates (VAT), Saudi Arabia (VAT) and "Another country — I'll add my own rates". The currency picked in the step before chooses the starting answer. "Another country" goes on to the single default-rate step, as before.
- India creates GST at 0, 0.25, 3, 5, 12, 18, 28 and 40% (32 rates):
  - Each slab gets CGST, SGST and UTGST halves, plus IGST at the full rate.
  - The halves are grouped as "GST 18%" and so on (intra-state). The single IGST rate is the inter-state counterpart.
  - The 12% and 28% slabs are created archived, since the 22 September 2025 rates no longer use them.
  - The UTGST rates and their "GST n% (UT)" groups are created archived. A business in a union territory restores them.
  - No cess rates are created; the Cess type is ready for when it's needed.
- The UK gets "VAT 20%", "VAT 5%", "VAT 0%" and "Exempt", and invoices are titled "VAT invoice".
- Australia (10%), New Zealand (15%), the UAE (5%) and Saudi Arabia (15%) each get their standard rate, a zero rate and "Exempt", and invoices are titled "Tax invoice".
- Settings › Tax › Country changes the country later. The new preset's rates are added and existing rates are never changed or deleted. Spine then shows "Added <n> rates. Your existing rates are unchanged — archive the ones you no longer use."
- Seeding twice adds nothing. A rate the owner already has with the same name and percentage is reused, not duplicated.
- New `GET /org/tax/profile` and `PUT /org/tax/profile { country }` → `{ profile, added }`. The presets are data in `packages/shared/src/tax/presets`. The invoice PDF prints `document_layout.invoice.title`.

### 2026-10-07 — US-TAX-10: give each rate a tax type (Phase 9)

- Each tax rate now has a tax type. For India, "Add rate" and "Edit rate" offer CGST, SGST, UTGST, IGST and Cess. Elsewhere they offer VAT, GST, Sales tax or Other. Rate rows read "9% · CGST".
- Rates from before the upgrade get the type Other and work as before (migration `0100`, `tax_rates.tax_type`).
- Tax groups gain a scope: intra-state, inter-state or either (`tax_groups.scope`).
  - For India, a group must be CGST with SGST or UTGST at the same rate, or a single IGST rate, either one with at most one cess rate. Any other mix is refused with "A GST group is CGST + SGST (or UTGST) at the same rate, optionally with cess." The mix sets the scope, and group rows read "CGST (9%) + SGST (9%) · Intra-state".
  - Outside India, a group can mix any rates, as before.
- The rate and group dialogs stay open when a save is refused, so the reason shows. Before, they closed and the error was never seen.
- `/tax-rates` and `/tax-groups` answer 400 for a body that fails validation (was 500).

### 2026-10-07 — US-RPT-40: every report laid out the same way (Phase 8)

- Every report — the statements, analysis, registers, General ledger, Day book, Job profitability, Tax Summary, Receivables and Payables — now follows one layout (D-180). The header names the range, plus any comparison or basis. Labelled filters sit on the left; Export, then any primary action, sits on the right. Then come one row of KPI cards, a chart where it helps, the table and a footnote.
- Filters apply as soon as they change; the Refresh button is gone.
- Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, Trial Balance and Cash Flow share tabs, and so do General ledger and Day book.
- New KPI cards:
  - Profit & Loss: income, expenses, net profit and net margin, plus a chart of income and expenses for each month.
  - Balance Sheet: assets, liabilities and equity.
  - Trial Balance: accounts, debits, credits and the difference.
  - General ledger and Day book: lines or entries, debits and credits.
  - Job profitability: jobs, contract value, billed to date and margin.
- Statements are one table with section headings, subtotals and a shaded total row. List reports gain a totals row.
- Receivables and Payables:
  - Four cards: Total outstanding, Current, Overdue and 90+ days.
  - A bar showing all five ages, each with its amount and share.
  - A "Show: All outstanding / Overdue only" filter in place of the overdue banner.
- Journals' "New journal" button moved next to Export.
- New `@spine/ui` components: `ReportToolbar`, `StatementTable` and `SegmentedBar`. `Table` and `DataTable` gain a `footer` totals row.
- `GET /reports/general-ledger` now returns `totals` covering every listed account.

### 2026-10-07 — Fix: labour expenses preselect Site labour on a slow connection (US-PUR-23)

- Choosing "Headcount × day rate" before the expense categories had loaded left the category empty and never showed "Preselected: posts to 5200 Direct Labour." The form now preselects it as soon as the categories arrive.

### 2026-10-07 — US-CAT-09: import catalogue items from a spreadsheet (Phase 8)

- **Catalogue › "Import"** (`ImportCatalogDialog`): choose a CSV, match its columns to Name, Description, Unit, Price, Tax, Income account and Expense account (guessed from the headings; only Name is required), then **Preview**: the first rows with "Ready", "Duplicate — skipped" or the problem — "Unknown tax <name>", "Unknown account <code>", a missing name or a price that isn't an amount ([D-161](docs/prd/12-decisions.md)).
- **Import** creates the ready rows; items whose name is already in the catalogue (or repeats in the file) are skipped and listed, never changed. The summary reads "Imported <n> items · skipped <m> duplicates · <k> rows failed", with **"Download failed rows"** (the file's own columns plus "Problem") to fix and import again.
- Tax is matched to a tax rate or group by name; accounts by code or name. Prices like "$12,500.00" are fine. "HSN/SAC" arrives with Phase 9.
- Same right as adding an item ("Create/edit own catalogue items"). API: `POST /catalog-items/import` (with `dryRun` for the preview).

### 2026-10-07 — US-PUR-31: pause, edit or stop a recurring bill (Phase 8)

- **Recurring bills › row menu**: Edit, Pause or Resume, and Delete. A paused schedule creates no bills; **Resume** sets the next date to the next future occurrence (dates passed while paused aren't created) and finishes it instead if its end has passed.
- **Edit** (or click the name) changes lines, amounts and the schedule for future bills only; bills already created are unchanged.
- **Delete** asks "Delete this schedule? Bills it already created are kept." — the schedule goes, its bills stay.
- The row menu is shared with recurring invoices (one component for both).
- API: `POST /recurring-bills/:id/pause`, `/resume`.

### 2026-10-07 — US-PUR-30: create recurring bills automatically (Phase 8)

- **The 6:00 AM run** (queue `recurring-bill-run`, every 15 minutes from 6:00 AM organisation time) creates one bill for each active schedule whose date has come: the schedule's vendor and lines, dated that day, due the set number of days later, numbered "<schedule name> · <date>" and noted "Created by Recurring bill <name>".
- **"Record the bill"** records it at once (P11). **"Save as a draft"** leaves a draft and tells Owners "Recurring bill ready to review: <name>" (in the app and by email). A bill that can't be recorded is left as a draft the same way.
- **Exactly once**: each bill carries its schedule and run date, unique together, so a repeated or racing run never makes a second bill for a date. **Missed dates** (server off) are each created once, in order, when Spine starts again ([D-159](docs/prd/12-decisions.md)).
- When the end condition is met (end date or number of bills), the schedule shows **"Finished"**.

### 2026-10-06 — US-PUR-29: set up a recurring bill (Phase 8)

- **Vendor Bills › "Recurring bills"** (`/vendor-bills/recurring`) lists each schedule's name, vendor, how it repeats, next bill date, amount, status (Active, Paused, Finished) and what a run does. "+ New recurring bill" opens `RecurringBillDialog`: Name, Vendor, lines (each with its expense account), Repeat (weekly, monthly, every 3 months, yearly) and the day, Starts on, Ends (never, on a date, after a number of bills), Due (days after the bill date), Paid from (for reference) and When it runs — "Record the bill" or "Save as a draft for me to check" ([D-159](docs/prd/12-decisions.md)).
- **"Make recurring"** on a bill opens the dialog with that bill's vendor and lines.
- New Team privilege **"Manage recurring bills"** (`vendor_bills.manage_recurring`, Manage Vendor Bills group), given to every Team that can already create bills.
- The bills themselves are created by US-PUR-30; pausing and deleting arrive with US-PUR-31.
- API: `GET/POST /recurring-bills`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /recurring-bills/:id`; tables `recurring_bills`, `recurring_bill_lines` (migration 0099).

### 2026-10-06 — US-DASH-26: switch dashboard profit between accrual and cash (Phase 8)

- **Dashboard › "Accrual | Cash"** (beside Edit layout, for members who see profit). On Cash, "Profit this month" — its figure, comparison and sparkline — is worked out on the cash basis (D-138, D-178) and says "cash basis" under the figure.
- **The money chart follows it** ([D-179](docs/prd/12-decisions.md)): Accrual shows "Income and expenses" per month from the ledger; Cash shows "Money in and out" of bank and cash accounts, as before. Accrual is the default, so the chart first reads income and expenses.
- **The choice is kept** on the member (`user.dashboard_basis`, migration 0098), so it's the same on every device.
- API: `GET /dashboard/kpis?basis=`, `GET /reports/money-in-out?basis=accrual`, `GET/PUT /users/me/dashboard-basis`.

### 2026-10-06 — US-DASH-25: see tax owed this period (Phase 8)

- **Dashboard › Tax this period** card (D-160): "Collected", "Input tax" and "Net payable" for the current month or quarter, and "<period> · paid <amount>" once a tax payment is recorded for it ("nothing paid yet" until then). The card opens the Tax Summary for that period.
- **Settings › Tax › "Return period"**: Monthly (default) or Quarterly; the card follows it.

### 2026-10-06 — US-DASH-24: see work not yet billed (Phase 8)

- **Dashboard › Ready to bill** card (D-160): "Completed milestones not invoiced <n>" with their total, and "Approved billable expenses not billed <n>" with what they'd invoice for (amount + tax). Nothing to bill: "Nothing waiting to be billed."
- The milestones line opens a list of the jobs holding them, each opening the job's Milestones tab; the expenses line opens Expenses filtered to approved billable expenses not yet on an invoice ("Show all" clears it).

- Members without "View banking" don't get the card (and the API doesn't send them balances).

- **Click an account** to open its drill-down for that period (Owners, or with "View ledger / journals").
- No expenses: "No expenses in this period." Each bar carries its name and share as its accessible name; amounts and % are written, so nothing relies on colour.
- Members without "View financial statements" don't get the card.

### 2026-10-06 — US-DASH-21: see what I owe vendors on the dashboard (Phase 8)

- **Dashboard › Payables** card (D-160): Current, Overdue and Total owed to vendors, a bar of current against overdue (with its figures as its accessible name), "Bills due in the next 7 days <n> · <amount>" and "Oldest overdue <bill> · <n> days". "Payables" opens the Payables page.
- **Overdue** opens Payables filtered to overdue bills ("Showing overdue bills only. Show all").
- Members without "View payables" don't get the card (and the API leaves the figure out). It can be moved or hidden with Edit layout like the other cards.

### 2026-10-06 — US-RPT-36: let my accountant's Team see the financial statements (Phase 8)

- **"View financial statements"** (Team › Privileges › Reports & Ledger, off by default) now opens Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, Trial Balance, Tax Summary and the revenue trend to a Team, alongside Cash Flow and the sales and purchase reports — they load and export (CSV, Excel, PDF, Print). Owners always can; Field never can, whatever their Teams ([D-136](docs/prd/12-decisions.md)).
- **Read-only**: a member with it can't post or reverse journals, edit or lock opening balances, close a period, record tax payments or change Settings. On the Tax Summary they don't see "Record tax payment" or the payments list. Account drill-downs on the statements need "View ledger / journals" as well; without it, figures aren't links.
- **Without it**, the statements show the no-access page: "You don't have access to financial statements. Ask an owner." (instead of "Owner-only report.").
- API: `GET /reports/profit-and-loss`, `/balance-sheet`, `/trial-balance`, `/revenue-trend`, `/org/tax/summary` and their exports move from `roles: owner` to `@RequireCapability("reports.view_financial_statements")`.

### 2026-10-06 — US-RPT-34: print any report (Phase 8)

- **Export › Print** opens the browser's print dialog. The printout leaves out the sidebar, breadcrumbs, filter bars, buttons, search and pagers, and fills the page with the report: its title, a line with the business name and the range or date, and the table.
- **Long tables**: printing from Print shows every row, not just the page on screen; column headings repeat on every printed page and rows aren't split. Afterwards the table is back on its page.
- Prints are black on white whatever the theme. Printing with the browser's own shortcut prints the page as it stands.
- `@spine/ui/print.css` (imported by the web app) holds the print stylesheet; `printPage()` and Table's print mode come from `@spine/ui`. Design-system pages for Table, DataTable, AppShell, Pagination and PaginationBar say how they print.

### 2026-10-06 — US-RPT-33: download any report as a PDF (Phase 8)

- **Export › PDF** on every report downloads `<report>-<from>-<to>.pdf`: the logo and business name (Settings › Business), the report name, the range or date and the currency at the top; the table with section headings and totals in bold; the basis (accrual or cash), "Prepared <date>" and "Page n of m" in the footer of every page.
- A report with more than five amount columns (Profit & Loss "Each month", Job profitability) prints landscape.
- PDFs are always light, whatever the screen's theme (D-100). Helvetica until Phase 9's fonts (D-151).
- API: `?format=pdf` on every report route, one react-pdf template for all reports.

### 2026-10-06 — US-RPT-32: export every report to CSV and Excel (Phase 8)

- **"Export"** on every report — Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, Trial Balance, Cash Flow, Tax Summary, Job profitability, Receivables, Payables, General ledger, Day book, Journals, the sales and purchase reports, and the payment and credit registers — offers **CSV** and **Excel (.xlsx)**. PDF and Print follow with US-RPT-33 and US-RPT-34.
- **Files hold what's on screen**: dates, account and source filters, Basis, "Compare with" columns, and the list's search. The general ledger exports every account the filters pick, not just the page.
- **Excel**: business name, report name, range and currency in the first rows; bold, frozen headings; amounts are real numbers with two decimals (the currency's decimals), percentages as %.
- **CSV**: plain decimal amounts with the currency in its own column, as before. Files are named `<report>-<from>-<to>` (or `-<date>`).
- The Tax Summary exports to Excel too. Receivables and Payables keep their CSV columns; their Export menu adds Excel.
- API: `?format=csv|xlsx` on every report route (`exceljs`, D-144); the `/export.csv` routes stay.

### 2026-10-06 — US-RPT-35: see profit and loss on a cash basis (Phase 8)

- **Profit & Loss › "Basis"**: Accrual (default) or Cash. On Cash the subtitle reads "<range> · Cash basis", cards show "Cash received (income)", "Cash paid (expenses)" and "Net profit (cash basis)" with the accrual figure beside it, and the table lists each account's cash-basis amount.
- **How it's counted** ([D-138](docs/prd/12-decisions.md), [D-178](docs/prd/12-decisions.md)): income is what customers paid in the range, split across each invoice's income lines in proportion; costs likewise from vendor payments on bills; expenses, journals and money in or out count as posted. A half-paid 1,000.00 services invoice is 500.00 under Sales — Services. Nothing is posted — it's a view.
- **Opening invoices**: payments on them aren't income, and the page says "Payments on invoices from before <cutover date> aren't counted — that income was in your old books." (likewise for opening bills).
- Works with "Compare with"; Export CSV carries the basis. Balance Sheet, Trial Balance and Tax Summary have no basis switch. Closes Q-04.
- API: `GET /reports/profit-and-loss?basis=cash`.

What issuing took off the credit note's own invoice counts as applied.

Newest first; search and Columns.

Read from the ledger, so vendor credits and reversals net out.

Search and Columns as on other lists.
- **Sales by item** (`/reports/sales-by-item`, the second tab): each catalogue item's quantity, sales before tax and average price, then "Items not from the catalogue" for lines typed by hand. The page says the figures read invoice lines and are before any whole-invoice discount ([D-177](docs/prd/12-decisions.md)).
- **Click a customer or item** to see its invoices; a number opens the invoice.
- **Access.** Owners, and Staff with "View financial statements".

### 2026-10-06 — US-RPT-27: compare profit and loss across periods (Phase 8)

- **Profit & Loss › "Compare with"**: "Previous period", "Same period last year" or "Each month". The first two add the other period's column plus "Change" and "Change %", with cards for Total income, Total expenses and Net profit ("▲ 11.6% vs previous period"); the subtitle reads "Jul – Sep 2026 compared with Apr – Jun 2026". "Each month" shows one column per month plus "Total" (up to 24 months).
- **Direction is never colour alone**: changes read "▲ +$6,059.53" / "▼ −$1,324.53" and "▲ +16.8%"; a change against zero shows "—".
- **Balance Sheet › "Compare with" → "Previous year end"** shows both dates side by side with the change, using Settings › Financial year.
- Whole-month ranges compare whole months (Jul–Sep with Apr–Jun; Mar with Feb); other ranges compare the same number of days.
- Report dates are now sent as the local calendar date; time zones ahead of UTC no longer shift From/To a day earlier.
- API: `GET /reports/profit-and-loss?compare=`, `GET /reports/balance-sheet?compareAsOf=`. Access is unchanged (Owner) until US-RPT-36.

### 2026-10-06 — US-RPT-26: see where cash came from and where it went (Phase 8)

- **Reports › Cash Flow** (`/reports/cash-flow`, under "Business overview"): "Cash at start", "Net change" (with ▲/▼ and words, not colour alone) and "Cash at end" cards, then "Operating activities" (net profit adjusted for receivables and retention, payables, tax, customer advances, card balances and other working capital), "Investing activities" (fixed assets, one line per account) and "Financing activities" (capital, drawings, loans, one line per account), each with its net total. This quarter to today by default.
- **Cash is the bank and cash accounts.** "Cash at end equals the total of your bank and cash accounts on <date>. Card accounts are liabilities, not cash." is checked every time; a mismatch is logged as an error and the page says so.
- **Click a line** to see the accounts behind it.
- **Access.** Owners, and Staff with "View financial statements". Field never.
- API: `GET /reports/cash-flow?from=&to=`, indirect method from `journal_lines`. Section mapping in the glossary ("Cash flow sections").

### 2026-10-06 — US-RPT-25: see the day book (Phase 8)

- **Reports › Day book** (`/reports/day-book`, under "Accountant") lists every journal entry in date order: date, source ("Invoice INV-0042", "Payment RCP-0012", "Journal JNL-0003"…), contact · narration, and each line's account, debit and credit, with totals. Today by default.

"Search entries" matches source, contact, narration and account. Entries are paged, 10 per page by default.

### 2026-10-06 — US-RPT-24: see the general ledger (Phase 8)

- **Reports › General ledger** (`/reports/general-ledger`, under "Accountant") shows each account's "Opening balance", one row per entry (date, source and number, contact · description, job, debit, credit, running balance) and "Closing balance" for a period. Balances read Dr or Cr.
- **Filters.** "From" and "To" (this quarter to today by default), "Accounts" to pick some, and "Hide accounts with no activity" (on by default). Accounts are paged ("1–10 of 14", 10 per page).

The journal then reads "Reversed", gains a "Reversal" card ("Reversed on <date> by <name>" and the reason), and "Reverse" goes.

### 2026-10-06 — US-BANK-11: review or undo a reconciliation (Phase 8)

- **"Reconciliations"** on an account's register and reconcile page opens `ReconciliationsHistory` at `/banking/<id>/reconciliations` ("Every finished reconciliation of <account>. Only the latest can be undone.").
  - Three cards show "Reconciled to" (with the closing balance), the number of reconciliations, and "Entries matched".

  - The confirmation reads "Undo this reconciliation?" and "Statement to <date> · <n> entries. Its entries go back to unreconciled; nothing is deleted."
  - Undoing takes the Reconciled tick off its entries, puts its statement lines back to unmatched, and moves "Last reconciled" back. The toast reads "Reconciliation undone".
  - It's in the audit log ("undid Reconciliation"). The account can then be reconciled to that date again.
- **API**: `GET /money-accounts/:id/reconciliations` and `POST /bank-reconciliations/:id/undo` (`banking.reconcile`). The audit log phrases "finished" and "undone" reconciliations.

### 2026-10-06 — US-BANK-10: finish a reconciliation when it balances (Phase 8)

- **"Finish reconciliation"** on the reconcile page is enabled only at a difference of $0.00. Until then the footer reads "Difference <amount> — match or create entries until it's zero."
- **Finishing** saves the reconciliation, and the page then reads "<Account> is reconciled to <date>. Its entries show the Reconciled tick in the register." The tick goes on:
  - the matched entries;
  - on an account's first reconciliation, the entries brought forward before its first statement line;
  - any entry and reversal that cancel out up to the end date (D-176).
- **Where it shows.**
  - The register's Status column now reads "Reconciled" for these.
  - Banking shows "Last reconciled <date>", and the unreconciled counts exclude reconciled entries.
  - The audit log records who finished it, the account and the closing balance.
- **Lock (invariant 10).** Voiding or deleting any document with a reconciled line (payment, vendor payment, expense, transfer, money in/out, refund, tax payment) is refused: "This entry is part of a finished reconciliation of <account> to <date>. Undo that reconciliation first." This is checked once, in `LedgerService.reverseEntry`. A document matched only in a reconciliation still in progress can still be deleted; its statement line goes back to unmatched.
- **Migration 0092**: `journal_lines.reconciliation_id`. The journal-line immutability trigger now allows a change to that column and nothing else.
- **API**: `POST /bank-reconciliations/:id/finish` (`banking.reconcile`). A later reconciliation must end after the last finished one.

### 2026-10-06 — US-BANK-09: create what's missing from a statement line (Phase 8)

- **"Create"** on an unmatched statement line opens `ReconcileCreateDrawer` ("Create from statement line"; "Saving matches the line to the new entry."). "Record it as" offers:
  - **Money in:** "Customer payment", "Transfer from another account" or "Other money in".
  - **Money out:** "Vendor payment", "Expense", "Transfer to another account", "Other money out" or "Tax payment".
- **Who sees which options.** Each option shows only with its right:
  - Customer payment: `payments.edit_own`. Vendor payment: `vendor_payments.edit_own`. Transfers and other money: `banking.record`.
  - Tax payment: Owner only.
  - Expense: Owner with expense rights. An expense posts only once approved, and Staff can't approve their own.
- **How each option records.**
  - Payments, transfers, money in/out and tax payments open their normal form, with the line's amount, date and account fixed.
  - An expense is filled in inside the drawer and approved on save.
  - When the entry posts, the line is matched to it ("Recorded and matched to <line>.").
- **Dialog changes.** `NewPaymentDialog`, `NewVendorPaymentDialog`, `TransferDialog`, `MoneyInOutDialog` and `TaxPaymentDialog` accept `prefill`. The two payment dialogs now pass the recorded payment back.
- **Fix:** the customer and vendor payment dialogs sent the picked date through UTC, which saved the previous day for anyone east of UTC (e.g. India, Australia). They now send the local date.
- No new routes: the drawer uses the normal create routes, then `PUT /bank-reconciliations/:id/matches`.

### 2026-10-06 — US-BANK-08: match statement lines to what's in Spine (Phase 8)

- **"Reconcile"** on an account's register opens `ReconcileAccount` at `/banking/<id>/reconcile`:
  - Enter "Statement end date" and "Closing balance on the statement", then "Start reconciling".
  - Three cards show "Statement closing balance", "Cleared in Spine" ("opening <x> + <n> matched") and "Difference".
  - Below them sit two lists: the statement lines up to the end date, and "Unreconciled in Spine" (entries on the account up to the end date).
- **Suggestions.** A line with exactly one Spine entry of the same amount within 3 days shows "Suggested match", with "Match" and "Not this one" (D-158).
- **Matching by hand.** Select a line, tick the entries that make it up, then "Match". Until they add up, the bar reads "Selected entries add up to <x>; the line is <y>."
- **Excluding.** "Exclude" asks for a note; the line counts as matched and shows "Excluded — <note>". "Unmatch" and "Include" undo a match or an exclusion.
- **Saving.** Everything is saved as it's made, so it's all still there after leaving the page.
- **Opening balance (D-176, new — you chose this).** An account's first reconciliation brings forward Spine's balance before the earliest statement line; later ones start from the last closing balance. An entry and its own reversal (a deleted document) both up to the end date cancel out and aren't offered.

### 2026-10-06 — Fix: Escape didn't close a drawer or dialog while a toast showed

- Radix treats an open toast as the topmost dismissable layer, so the first Escape only dismissed the toast, even with focus in a drawer or dialog. This affected every drawer and dialog that shows a toast.
- `Toast` in `@spine/ui` now passes Escape on when focus isn't on the toast. The toast closes, and once it's gone the same Escape reaches the dialog or drawer underneath, so one press closes both. With focus on the toast, Escape still closes only the toast. The design-system Toast page's keyboard table says so.
- The expense form, opened with "Edit" from a drawer's menu, used to drop focus onto the page when it closed, because the menu item that opened it was gone. Focus now returns to the drawer's "More" (or "Edit") button. `ExpenseForm` gains `returnFocusTo`.

Tests:
- `packages/ui/src/components/toast.a11y.test.tsx`: Escape with a toast and a dialog open closes both. It fails without the fix.
- `apps/e2e/tests/us-pur-10.spec.ts`: after saving an edit, focus is on "More actions", and one Escape closes the drawer while the toast still shows.

- **Privilege matrix › Banking**: "View bank balances and registers" (`banking.view`), "Record transfers and other money in or out" (`banking.record`) and "Reconcile accounts" (`banking.reconcile`), off for General Staff (migration 0077 added them to every Team, off).

### 2026-10-05 — US-OPS-26: use every new screen in dark mode (Phase 7)

- **Sweep**: every Phase 7 screen is checked in light and dark mode, with a screenshot of each attached to the test report and axe (WCAG 2.1 A/AA, contrast included) passing in both. The screens are the Owner and Field dashboards, the search palette, invoices with bulk selection, Settings › Automatic reminders and Data export, the audit log, Activity, Profile › Notifications, recurring invoices, job costing and the job profitability report.
- **What the sweep caught and fixed**:
  - Light `due-soon` and `category-amber` text (`#9A6300`) was 4.46:1 on its tint. It's now `#946000` (4.72:1).
  - Dark muted text (`#93907F`) was 4.41:1 on sunken surfaces such as table headers and the palette footer. It's now `#9A9786` (4.83:1).
  - Both values are updated in `tokens.json`, the web preset, the native tokens and the design docs.
  - The setup checklist's checkboxes and the contact filter on Invoices, Quotes, Payments, Jobs and Credit notes had no accessible name. They're labelled now.
- **Overlays and elevation as tokens**: dialogs, alert dialogs, drawers and the search palette sit on a new `scrim` token, darkened to 62% in dark mode. Menus, popovers, dialogs and toasts use new `shadow-raised`, `shadow-overlay` and `shadow-toast` tokens, which are stronger in dark mode, so surfaces stay distinct from the page. These replace the raw `bg-black/30` and `rgba(...)` shadows in 16 `@spine/ui` components.
- **Dashboard**: money-out bars use `border-strong`, as in the dark design. The sidebar shows the light wordmark in dark mode (already in place; now tested).
- **Emails and PDFs**: emails declare a light colour scheme and carry only light values (tested). PDFs have no theme.
- **E2E**: a shared axe helper (`tests/axe.ts`) injects `axe-core` (new dev dependency, already used by `@spine/ui`).

### 2026-10-05 — US-SET-16: keep data exports private (Phase 7)

- **Owner-only link**: an export's download link answers 404 to everyone but an Owner of the organisation: Staff, Field, someone signed out, or an Owner of another organisation. It's never 401 or 403, so the link reveals nothing. The ZIP is never served through `/files/:id`, even to Owners, and the response isn't cached.
- **7-day expiry**: after 7 days the link answers 404 and the file is deleted from storage. That happens when someone uses the link or opens Settings › Data export, and otherwise on an hourly sweep (`data-export-cleanup`).
- **Audit log**: preparing and downloading an export appear as "Data export" entries with the person ("Prepared", "Downloaded").
- **The ready email** links to Settings › Data export only; the file is never attached or linked.

Tests:
- `apps/api/src/modules/data-export/us-set-16.http.integration.test.ts` (6): only Owners download (everyone else 404); never via `/files/:id`; audit entries with the person; the email's link; expiry deletes the file from storage; the hourly sweep.
- `apps/e2e/tests/us-set-16.spec.ts` (1): the link for an Owner, Staff and a signed-out visitor; both actions in the audit log.

### 2026-10-05 — US-INV-21: create recurring invoices automatically (Phase 7)

- **Run.** The `recurring-invoice-run` queue fires every 15 minutes. From 6:00 AM organisation time it gives each active schedule that's due one invoice, built from its lines with that day's tax (issue date today, due after the schedule's payment terms). It goes through the same create/issue/email code as a manual invoice, so the number, ledger posting and email are identical.
- **"Issue and email"** issues and emails the invoice. **"Create a draft"** leaves a draft, and Owners get "Recurring invoice ready to review: <name>" (in-app, email, push) linking to it. If issuing fails, the invoice stays a draft for an Owner to finish.
- **Never twice.** Invoices record `recurring_invoice_id` and `recurring_run_on`, unique together (migration `0068`), so a late, repeated or racing run can't make a second invoice for the same date. A run missed while the server was off catches up once; missed dates aren't back-filled.
- **Finished.** Once the end date or number of invoices is reached, the schedule shows "Finished" and has no next date.

Tests:
- `apps/api/src/modules/invoices/us-inv-21.http.integration.test.ts` (5): issue and email (number, posting, email, next date), draft plus notification, not before 6:00 and never twice (including a race), missed-run catch-up, finished by count and by date.

### 2026-10-05 — US-INV-19: send reminders on schedule without double-sending (Phase 7)

- **Daily run.** The `invoice-reminder-run` queue fires every 15 minutes. For each organisation with automatic reminders on, once organisation time (the server's `TZ`) passes "Send at", it runs the day once: every issued invoice with a balance whose due date is a scheduled number of days away gets one reminder email ("Reminder: invoice INV-… is 7 days overdue" / "is due today" / "is due in 3 days"). If the server was off at send time, the day runs once when it comes back. Missed days aren't caught up.
- **No double-sending.** New `invoice_reminders` table, one row per invoice per day (unique `invoice_id`, `sent_on`). Manual "Send reminder" records a row too, so the run skips an invoice already reminded that day. Paid, voided and fully credited invoices are never picked.
- **Pause per customer.** "Pause automatic reminders" switch on a customer's contact page (`contacts.reminders_paused`, through `PUT /contacts/:id` with `contacts.edit_*`). Vendors don't get the switch. Members who can't edit the contact see "Automatic reminders paused" instead.
- **History.** Each automatic reminder shows "Automatic reminder sent" in the invoice history.

### 2026-10-05 — US-OPS-24: show money the same way everywhere (Phase 6)

- **One formatter.** `formatMoney(minor, currency, locale)` in `@spine/shared`, built on `Intl.NumberFormat`. It gives the currency symbol, the locale's grouping and decimal marks, the currency's own decimals and a true minus sign: "$12,024.75", "−$4,335.00", "₹1,20,247.50", "12.024,75 €". Amounts stay exact (decimal strings, never floats).
- **Web.** About 100 call sites in 55 files now use it: lists, details, builders, dashboard widgets, reports, receivables and payables, the public quote page. They used to show "12024.75 USD" or plain numbers.
  - **Locale.** Comes from Settings › Currency & locale. The server layout reads it once and `MoneyLocaleProvider` sets it before anything renders. The public quote API returns the business's `locale`.
  - **Columns.** Money columns are right-aligned, with tabular figures in the normal UI font (no more monospace), in the web app and in `@spine/ui`'s chart, donut and money input.
  - **Negatives.** Credit notes, discounts, retention, paid and credited amounts show "−$…" instead of a hand-typed "-".
- **PDFs** (quote, invoice, receipt, credit note) use the same formatter. They have an en dash for the minus, and the currency code when Helvetica has no symbol for it (D-123).
- **Emails and notifications.** Email facts, payment and expense notifications, the activity feed and the out-of-balance warning use the organisation's locale. CSV exports keep plain decimals on purpose (US-PAY-10).
- **Lint rule.** `@spine/config/eslint/money`, applied to `apps/web` and the API's PDF and email code, fails on importing `toDecimalString` and on joining an amount with a currency code (`${amount} ${currency}` or `{amount} {currency}`). It caught the catalogue price showing its currency twice.
- **Found along the way (D-124).** Rate limits counted per IP address, and the web app's server-side calls (session, membership, locale) all come from the web server's one address. So the whole team shared one bucket of 300 requests a minute, and the full E2E run tripped it ("ThrottlerException: Too Many Requests"). `SessionThrottlerGuard` now counts signed-in requests per session and public routes per IP.

Tests:
- `packages/shared/src/money/us-ops-24.test.ts` (5): the story's examples in en-US, en-IN and de-DE, the true minus, JPY decimals, exactness beyond 2^53, fallbacks.
- `us-ops-24.test.ts` (API, 3): PDF money (symbol, en dash, code fallback). `us-ops-24-lint.test.ts` (4): the lint rule fails on template strings, JSX and the import, and passes `formatMoney`.
- `session-throttler.http.integration.test.ts` (2): one user's limit doesn't throttle another on the same address; random cookies don't get around a public route's limit.
- `apps/e2e/tests/us-ops-24.spec.ts` (1): invoice amounts read "$1,234.50" with no " USD", and switch to "1.234,50 $" after changing the locale to de-DE.
- Updated for the new format: email snapshots, `us-ntf-10`, `us-rpt-12`, `quote-to-payment` and `us-ntf-10` E2E.

### 2026-10-04 — US-QUO-22: keep emailed links working until the quote is replaced (Phase 6)

- **Finding C8, explained.** The demo's fourth quote (QUO-0003) is seeded as "revised": it was sent and emailed, then revised. Revising revokes every link for the old version, and that's intended. But the revision was left as a draft, so the quote still read "sent" while its only emailed link was dead.
- **Fix.** The demo now sends the revision as well. The current version is "sent" with a working emailed link; the replaced version's link shows the branded "This quote link has expired" page (US-QUO-21).
- **Confirmed unchanged.** A link lasts 30 days. Issuing another link for the same quote never revokes the earlier ones; a queued email retry reuses its own token. Only revising a quote revokes its links. There is no separate "resend" action that could rotate tokens.

Tests:
- `us-quo-22.http.integration.test.ts` (4): every demo quote that's sent and current has an emailed link that opens; the revised demo quote's old link answers 410 "expired" while its sent revision's link opens; two links for one quote both work; a link lasts 30 days.

### 2026-10-04 — US-QUO-21: show a branded page for an expired or invalid link (Phase 6)

- **Expired or replaced.** A quote link we issued that has run out (30 days), been revoked or replaced by a revision now shows the business logo and name, "This quote link has expired" and "The link you opened is no longer active — the quote may have been updated or replaced. Contact <Business> and they'll send you the latest version.". A box follows with the business's address, email (mailto) and phone (tel), and "Sent with Spine".
- **Invalid.** A token that matches nothing (not ours, bad signature, unknown) shows a generic "This quote link isn't valid" with no business details.
- **API.** `GET /public/quotes/:token` now answers 410 `{ status: "expired", business }` or 404 `{ status: "invalid" }` instead of one generic 404. `QuotePublicTokenService.inspect()` tells the two apart: an expired token's payload is trusted only after its signature checks out and its nonce exists. The logo comes inline as a data URI, because anonymous visitors can't load `/files/:id`.
- **Business profile.** Gains "Business email" and "Business phone" (Settings › Business profile and onboarding). Saving the profile now keeps fields set elsewhere, such as payment instructions.

Tests:
- `us-quo-21.http.integration.test.ts` (5): a current link loads; a revoked link and a link past 30 days answer 410 with name, address, email and phone; tokens that match nothing, and a token signed with another key, answer 404 with no business details.

### 2026-10-04 — US-AUTH-12: keep my unsaved work when my session expires (Phase 6)

- **The dialog.** If the session has ended, a save (any create, change, delete or upload through the API client) opens "You've been signed out" with "Your session ended, so this change wasn't saved yet. Log in again to save it — the draft stays open in this tab." and "Log in again". Logging in happens inside the dialog ("Log in as <email>." and "Password"), so the page and everything typed on it stay as they were. The save isn't retried; you press it again.
- **Reading only.** If a background request gets 401 and nothing has been typed on the page, you're sent to `/login?next=<this page>`. If something has been typed, it waits for the save to show the dialog instead of losing the draft.
- **Server fix.** On capability-gated routes, a request with no session got 403 "No active organisation on session" instead of 401, because `CapabilityGuard` can run before Better Auth's guard. It now answers 401, so "signed out" and "not allowed" (US-OPS-12) can be told apart.
- **Sign-up status follow-up (US-AUTH-08).** `GET /public/signup-status` had its own limit of 60 a minute per IP. Every `/login` and `/signup` load asks it, so an office behind one address could hit the limit, and the page then wrongly said "This Spine is invite-only" on a fresh install. It now uses the global limit (300 a minute). If the check fails, the page shows the form and lets the server decide.
- **Safer `?next=`.** `/login?next=` now follows only paths on this site; `//other-host` and full URLs go to the dashboard. Visiting a protected page signed out now adds `?next=` too.

Tests:
- `us-auth-12.http.integration.test.ts` (5): no session → 401 on capability-gated and plain routes, reads and writes; an unknown session cookie → 401.
- `apps/e2e/tests/us-auth-12.spec.ts` (3): a save after the session ends opens the dialog; logging in from it keeps the page and the typed name, without repeating the save; a background 401 while reading goes to `/login?next=%2Fcontacts`; `?next=` ignores another host.

### 2026-10-04 — US-AUTH-09, US-AUTH-10: reset a forgotten password (Phase 6)

- **Ask for a link.** "Forgot password?" on `/login` opens `/forgot-password`: "Reset your password", "Enter the email you sign in with and we'll send you a link to choose a new password.", "Email", "Send reset link", "The link works once and expires in 1 hour." and "Back to log in". The same page shows whether or not email (SMTP) is set up (D-084).
- **Check your email.** `/forgot-password/sent` says "If an account exists for <email>, we've sent a link to reset its password. The link works once and expires in 1 hour." for any address. "Resend link in 0:45" counts down and stays disabled for 60 seconds. The address is kept in the tab's session storage, never in the URL.
- **Limits.** 10 requests per IP address per 15 minutes, then 429 "Too many reset requests from this network. Wait 15 minutes and try again."; at most 3 emails per address per hour (later requests get the same answer, but nothing is sent). Both are in memory, per API process (D-119).
- **The email.** "Reset your Spine password", linking to `APP_URL/reset-password?token=…`. Without SMTP nothing is sent and a warning is logged without the token. An SMTP failure is logged and the answer doesn't change. The branded layout comes with US-NTF-11.
- **Choose a new password.** `/reset-password?token=` shows "Choose a new password", "For <email>. You'll be signed out on your other devices.", "New password" ("At least 8 characters.") and "Confirm new password". Mismatched passwords show "The passwords don't match." and nothing is sent. "Save password" sets the password, ends every session for the account (web and phone), signs this browser in and opens the dashboard.
- **Used or expired links** show "This link can't be used" with "Request a new one". The token works once and expires after 1 hour.
- **Phone.** "Forgot password?" on the mobile login opens `/public/forgot-password` on the API in the phone's browser, which redirects to the web page (D-052); the app only knows the API's address.
- **API.** Better Auth `sendResetPassword`, `resetPasswordTokenExpiresIn: 3600`, `revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset: true` and a `hooks.before` IP limit. New `GET /public/password-reset/:token` → `{ email }` (404 when unknown, used or expired; doesn't consume the token) and `GET /public/forgot-password` (302 to the web page).

### 2026-10-04 — US-PAY-13: allocate a deposit payment to its advance invoice (Phase 6)

- **Paying a deposit request.** `POST /payments` now accepts allocations to advance (deposit) invoices, which it used to refuse. The advance invoice then shows "Paid", or "Partially paid" with its balance.
- **Posting (P5a, D-075).** Bank is debited; everything not allocated to an ordinary invoice, including the deposit, is credited to 2200 Customer Advances. The advance invoice never posted to AR, so there's no AR line. The money stays available as the customer's credit and is applied to the final invoice as before (P6: 2200 Dr, AR Cr).
- **Credit stays available.** Migration `0057` changes the allocation trigger: `payments.allocated_amount` (so `unallocatedAmount`, the customer's credit) counts only allocations to ordinary invoices. Allocations to advance invoices are capped separately by the payment amount and by the invoice total.
- **Deposits carry no tax.** Advance invoices are computed without tax, including when an invoice is turned into one; the final invoice's lines carry the full tax.
- **Suggestions and deletes.** The oldest-first suggestion includes open advance invoices. A payment with any allocation, advance ones included, can't be deleted. The payment confirmation email counts a deposit as credit held.
- **Paid badges.** Invoices now return a derived `paymentStatus` (`unpaid`/`partially_paid`/`paid`). The invoices list and detail show "Paid" or "Partially paid" next to the status, and "Record payment" offers advance invoices.
- **Accountant review.** The P5a posting variant is flagged for it in Q-02.

### 2026-10-04 — US-TAX-07: store rates, quantities and percentages exactly (Phase 6)

- **Exact storage.** Migration `0056` turns the 14 floating-point (`real`) columns into `numeric(18,4)`: tax rates; quantity, discount % and tax % on every document line; the catalogue default tax %; job retention %; and milestone amounts. The cast keeps each value's decimal form (8.875, 7.3, 33.3333), and issued totals (bigint) are untouched. Drizzle reads the columns as numbers, so API and web types are unchanged.
- **Exact maths.** New in `@spine/shared` (`money/decimal.ts`): exact fractions read from the decimal string, `multiplyMinor`, `percentOfMinor`, and `roundFraction`, which rounds half-up once. `computeLineTax` now works in exact fractions and takes rates as percentages (`TaxRate.percent`, formerly `rate`). That ends the float division by 100: `1.1 / 100` was `0.011000000000000001`. New `computeDocumentLine` does quantity × price, discount and tax, each rounded once.
- **One place for line maths.** Quotes, invoices, credit notes and vendor bills used to repeat the line maths in floating point; now they all call `computeDocumentLine`. So do the four web line editors, which had used `Math.round` and could show a different cent from what the server stored. Milestone resolution and retention use `percentOfMinor`.
- **Milestone percentages.** They must now total exactly 100%. Three thirds entered as 33.333 (99.999) used to pass by rounding; enter 33.3333, 33.3333 and 33.3334 instead. Recorded as D-118.

- `us-tax-07.integration.test.ts` (2): 8.875% through `POST /tax-rates` reads back as 8.875 and is stored as `8.8750`; converting real values to `numeric(18,4)` keeps them.

### 2026-10-04 — Team grants never cross organisations (security fix)

Found while testing US-OPS-12. A Staff member's capabilities were the union of every Team their membership row belonged to, without checking that those Teams belonged to the member's own organisation.
- **How it leaked.** The demo seed moves its demo users' membership rows between organisations, and their old Team memberships moved with them. The demo Staff user had collected 12 "General Staff" Teams from 12 organisations, so turning a grant off in one organisation had no effect.
- **The fix.** `hasCapability`, `getEffectiveCapabilities` and `CapabilityGuard` now count only Teams in the member's organisation, and the guard now calls `hasCapability` instead of keeping its own copy of the query. The demo seed also clears a moved member's old Team memberships.
- **Test.** A case in `us-ops-20.http.integration.test.ts` puts a Staff member into another organisation's Team that grants receivables and checks they're still refused. It fails without the fix.

### 2026-10-04 — US-INV-17: keep the exact PDF that was issued (Phase 6)

A sent quote, or an issued invoice, credit note or payment receipt, now keeps the PDF rendered the moment it was issued. Every later download or email serves those exact bytes, even after the customer's address, the logo, branding or the templates change. Drafts still render live and store nothing.
- **Storage column.** New column `issued_pdf_file_id` on `quotes`, `invoices`, `credit_notes` and `payments`. Migration `0053` adds it and copies the old `quotes`/`invoices.pdf_file_id` values across, then `0054` drops `pdf_file_id`.
- **Storing at issue.** `IssuedPdfService` (`apps/api/src/modules/pdf`) does the work.
  - After their transaction commits, `QuotesService.send`, `InvoicesService.issue`/`releaseRetention`, `CreditNotesService.issue` and `PaymentsService.create` queue `store-issued-pdf`.
  - The job renders once and stores the file through `FilesService`, so it's checksummed and write-once. It retries with backoff for about a day while storage is down; issuing never waits for it or fails because of it.
  - A document issued before this change, or whose job hasn't run yet, is stored on its first download.
  - Two first downloads at once still leave a single file.
- **PDF routes.** `GET /quotes|invoices|payments/:id/pdf` serve the stored file once the document is issued.
- **Emails.** The quote and invoice email jobs and the receipt email attach the stored file instead of rendering again; invoice reminders previously re-rendered and overwrote it. If storage is down when an email goes, the email still carries a fresh render and the store job is queued.
- **Credit-note PDF (new, D-116).** A credit note had no PDF before. It now has one in the invoice PDF's layout: "CREDIT NOTE", its number, credited to, against invoice, reason, lines and total credited. There's a new route, `GET /credit-notes/:id/pdf`, and a "Download PDF" (or "Preview PDF" for a draft) button in the credit note drawer.
- **Test and queue fixes.** The integration-test SWC config now uses the automatic JSX runtime, as the Nest build does; it was the first test to render a PDF. `QueueService.send` accepts per-queue retry options.

Tests: `us-inv-17.http.integration.test.ts` (7), against a demo-seeded org through the real routes:

- An issued invoice serves identical bytes after the business profile and contact change.
- A document issued earlier is stored on its first download.
- A sent quote, an issued credit note and a receipt are each stored and served unchanged.
- The credit-note PDF's file name is its number.
- Racing first downloads store one file.
- Storage down: issuing still succeeds, the job's work fails so it's retried, and the email still gets a PDF.

A new `.dockerignore` keeps all of these out; only `.env.example` is kept. ### 2026-10-04 — US-OPS-30: move existing files off MinIO (Phase 6)

New command `pnpm --filter @spine/api files:migrate --from s3 --to local`, which works in either direction and takes `--org <id>` to limit it to one organisation.
- **What it does.** Every file recorded on the source driver is copied to the target. Each copy is checked against the file's checksum, and only then is the record switched to the target's driver with a new id-only key. Old S3 keys contained the uploaded file name.
- **Summary.** It prints copied, skipped and failed counts. On any failure it lists the files and exits 1.
- **Safe to re-run.** The source bucket is never changed or deleted. Files already moved are skipped, and a copy left by an interrupted run is reused when its checksum matches.
- **Refuses bad files.** A file missing from the bucket, damaged (its checksum doesn't match), or blocked by a different file at the target is left on its old record.
- **Upgrade notes** are in the README ("Upgrading an install that used MinIO"): migrate, or keep MinIO with `STORAGE_DRIVER=s3`.

Logic in `apps/api/src/modules/files/migrate-files.ts`; CLI in `src/scripts/files-migrate.ts`. Tests: `us-ops-30.integration.test.ts` (6). They cover an in-memory stand-in for an old bucket with legacy name-based keys: copy and verify, attachments open afterwards with the local driver, re-run skips, an interrupted run is reused, and failures are listed while the rest still move. A real S3 run is included when `S3_ENDPOINT` is set, as in CI; it passed locally against S3Mock.

### 2026-10-04 — US-OPS-29: accept only safe uploads (Phase 6)

- **Type from the bytes.** `POST /files` reads a file's type from its first bytes, ignoring its name and the browser's claim. Anything other than JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC or PDF is refused with 415 "This file type isn't supported. Upload a photo or a PDF.", including SVG, HTML, GIF and AVIF. The stored `mime_type` is the detected type.
- **Location removed from photos.** GPS EXIF data is stripped from photos before they're stored. The GPS directory is emptied in place, so the photo isn't re-encoded and its Orientation tag is kept. This works for JPEG, PNG (the chunk CRC is recomputed), WebP and HEIC (D-115). The checksum covers the stripped bytes.
- **Safe serving.** Every file response carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and the stored `Content-Type`. Allowed photos and PDFs are served `inline`; anything else, which can only be a file stored before this change such as an old SVG logo, is served as `attachment`. The file name appears only in the `Content-Disposition` label, sanitised. Presigned S3 links set the same type and disposition.
- **File names.** Names stay labels only and storage paths come from ids. The multipart parser already reduces a name like `../../etc/passwd.pdf` to `passwd.pdf`.
- **Web.** File pickers offer only the accepted types (`PHOTO_ACCEPT`, `PHOTO_OR_PDF_ACCEPT` in `apps/web/src/lib/upload-types.ts`) instead of `image/*`, and the 415 message shows in each uploader's existing error line.

Tests: `us-ops-29.test.ts` (23: type detection, GPS stripping per format with orientation kept, PNG CRCs, Content-Disposition) and `us-ops-29.http.integration.test.ts` (8, through the real routes). The test photos are hand-built with real EXIF blocks (`test-photos.ts`) because adding `sharp`/`exifr` as dev dependencies re-resolved the mobile app's peer versions. The earlier storage tests now upload real PDF bytes. Integration 27 files pass; E2E 30/30.

### 2026-10-04 — US-OPS-28: prove stored files are intact (Phase 6)

Each stored file now has a SHA-256 checksum, so Spine can tell when a file is damaged or missing.
- **Checksum on upload.** New column `files.checksum_sha256`. Migration `0052` also adds `integrity_problem` (`damaged`/`missing`) and `integrity_checked_at`.
- **Checked on read.** `GET /files/:id` (local driver) and the PDF logo reader compare the bytes with the checksum first. A damaged or missing file returns 409 with "This file is damaged. Restore it from your latest backup.", is logged and is flagged on its row. S3 files aren't downloaded on every read; the weekly check verifies them, and one already flagged is refused the same way.
- **Weekly check.** The `file-integrity-check` job (pg-boss, Sundays 03:00) reads every file and records the outcome, and files that are intact again are cleared. Files stored before checksums existed get one from their current bytes; the job is queued once at start-up while any file still lacks one, which is the one-off backfill. A storage outage isn't counted as damage.
- **Owner warning.** When the check finds problems, each affected organisation's Owners get an in-app notification (`files_damaged`) naming the records, such as "PDF of invoice <number>" or "Receipt for expense <number>: <description>". The dashboard shows "<n> stored files are damaged or missing — restore from your latest backup." until the files are fixed. For a single file the wording is "1 stored file is damaged or missing — …". The list comes from new Owner-only route `GET /files/integrity`.
- **Write-once files.** A driver refuses to save to a key that already holds a file. The local driver hard-links the temp file into place instead of renaming it, which fails when the key already exists. So an issued document's bytes can't be replaced.
- **E2E ports.** The suite moved to ports 3110/4110 because the design-system docs app in `pnpm dev` uses 3100, which made the suite fail whenever `pnpm dev` was running.

Tests: `us-ops-28.test.ts` (write-once, checksum, wording), `us-ops-28.http.integration.test.ts` (8: checksum stored, 409 when damaged or missing, Owner-only summary, the weekly run's notification and clearing, backfill, nothing shown when intact) and `apps/e2e/tests/us-ops-28.spec.ts` (the dashboard warning). Integration suite 26 files pass (the s3 suite skips without `S3_ENDPOINT`); E2E 30/30.

### 2026-10-04 — US-OPS-27: files on local disk by default (Phase 6)

Fresh installs no longer need MinIO, whose free images were withdrawn. Files now go through a `StorageDriver` (`apps/api/src/modules/files/storage/`) with two drivers: `local` (the default) and `s3` (`STORAGE_DRIVER=s3` plus `S3_*`, for AWS S3, R2, B2 or RustFS). The `local` driver writes to `FILES_DIR`: `/data/files` in production, which is the new `spine_files` volume on the API container, and `apps/api/.data/files` in development.
- **Crash-safe writes.** A save writes a temp file, fsyncs it and renames it into place, so a crash or a failed upload never leaves a partial file that can be served. Temp files left by a crash are removed on the next start.
- **Paths from ids only.** Files are stored at `<org-id>/<2-char prefix>/<file-id>`; the uploaded name is never used in a path.
- **Driver recorded per file.** New column `files.storage_driver`. Migration `0051` backfills existing rows to `s3`, so files stored before a switch stay readable while their driver's settings remain.
- **Serving.** With `local`, `GET /files/:id` streams the file with `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, an `ETag` (304 on match) and single-range support (206/416). With `s3`, it redirects to a 5-minute presigned URL. A request with no session is allowed only with an API-signed link (`?exp=&sig=`, HMAC with `AUTH_SECRET`, at most 5 minutes; otherwise 403). No screen creates such links yet.
- **PDF logos.** Quote, invoice and receipt PDFs read the logo through `FilesService.readBytes` instead of three copies of S3 code.
- **Docker.** `docker-compose.yml` and `docker-compose.dev.yml` no longer reference `minio/minio`. The `rustfs` profile runs `rustfs/rustfs:1.0.1` with a 1 GB memory limit. The API image runs as the non-root `node` user, which owns `/data/files`.
- **Env.** `.env.example`, `.env.development.example` and `.env.e2e` gain `STORAGE_DRIVER=local`, and `S3_*` are now commented out.
- **CI.** The E2E job drops its S3 service. The unit/integration job gains S3Mock so the same storage scenarios run against both drivers.
- **Docker images.** `Dockerfile.api` and `Dockerfile.web` now copy `patches/`. Without it, `pnpm install` stopped on the missing Expo patch, so neither production image had built since that patch was added. Both images also skip building `canvas`, a test-only `packages/ui` dependency that peer dependencies pull into the install and that can't compile on Alpine. The skip applies inside the images only (`neverBuiltDependencies`); dev machines still build it. Both images now build. A smoke test of the API image with no storage settings and a `spine_files` volume passed: it runs as `node`, uploads land at `/data/files/<org>/<prefix>/<id>`, `GET /files/:id` returns 200 with type, length and ETag and identical bytes, and the file is still served after the container restarts.
- **Tests.** API integration test files now run one at a time (`fileParallelism: false`). They share one database and `ledger-integrity` truncates organisations, which made the suite fail intermittently on `main` too (deadlocks, FK violations, "too many clients").

Tests: `us-ops-27.test.ts` (34: local driver scenarios, failed and interrupted uploads, unsafe keys, driver selection, signed links, range parsing), `us-ops-27.s3.integration.test.ts` (the same 6 scenarios on S3; checked against MinIO and S3Mock) and `us-ops-27.http.integration.test.ts` (10, through the real routes). Full integration suite 26/26 files and E2E 29/29 on the local driver.

### 2026-09-14 — Extracted Home's `GaugeIndicator`/`KpiCard`/`ActionTile` to `packages/ui-native` — the same reusable-components pass, applied to the dashboard

- **Context**: a follow-up to the same-day Job Edit extraction pass, applied to the Home screen — asked what else on that screen was genuinely reusable.
- **`GaugeIndicator` (new component)**: the animated semi-circular progress gauge, ported verbatim with its full doc-comment history (the arc-path math, the spring-overshoot "comet head" animation, the tick marks) — `progress`/`trackColor`/`fillGradient`/`textColorClass` is the whole API, with zero dashboard-specific logic in the original to begin with.
- **`KpiCard` (new component)**: the gradient-filled stat card, ported the same way. `tone` (the original's implicit gradient-id/dashboard-tone concept) is now a plain, caller-supplied `gradientId` string — the component itself has no concept of KPI "tones."
- **`ActionTile` (new component)**: the Quick Actions icon+label tile. **A real, previously-unnoticed gap found and fixed during extraction**: the original tile was a plain `View` with no `onPress`/`accessibilityRole` at all — visually a tappable-looking tinted box that did nothing when pressed, despite "quick actions" implying the tiles are actionable. The new component takes a required `onPress` and real `accessibilityRole="button"`/`accessibilityState`, so a future consumer gets a genuinely tappable tile by construction. Home's own 4 tiles now show an honest "no real flow for this action yet" alert on press (this showcase app has no real quote/expense/photo/job creation flow to route to) — matching the same "display-only, no fake backing behavior" pattern already used for the period `SegmentedControl`. Uses local `useState` for pressed-state opacity, not `Pressable`'s own `style={({ pressed }) => ({...})}` callback — see `full-width-button.tsx`'s own doc comment for the confirmed, real bug in this exact app that callback form causes.
- **`apps/showcase-native`'s Home screen** now imports all three instead of defining them locally — `WelcomeCard`, the KPI carousel wrapper, the Quick Actions grid wrapper/section caption, and all mock data (`KPIS`/`RECENT_JOBS`/`QUICK_ACTIONS`/`KPI_GRADIENTS`) stay screen-local, since those are genuinely dashboard-specific.
