### 2026-09-14 — `BottomSheet`: fixed content not filling a fixed-height (`snapPoints`) sheet's real width, root-caused to `matchContents` needing to be conditional; plus `SelectListField`'s Job Edit demo grown to 120 real options

- **User report**: `SelectListField`'s bottom sheet (search box + list) wasn't full-width — narrower than the sheet itself — and asked to test with a longer (100+ item) list.
- **Root cause, confirmed by reading `@expo/ui`'s own native source (`RNHostView.swift`)**: `BottomSheet`'s `children` were wrapped in `RNHostView matchContents` UNCONDITIONALLY. `matchContents` sizes the hosted SwiftUI wrapper to the RN child's own Yoga-measured INTRINSIC size, not the sheet's actual presented width — correct for a sheet with no `snapPoints` (genuine "size to content"), but wrong for a sheet like `SelectListField`'s with real, explicit `snapPoints` (a fixed-height sheet): there's no available width for the content's `100%`/`flex: 1` to resolve against at that boundary, so it collapsed to its narrowest intrinsic content instead of stretching.
- **Fix**: `matchContents` is now conditional — `true` only when `snapPoints` is NOT set (the genuine dynamic-sizing case, e.g. `BottomSheetDemo`'s plain `<BottomSheet>`), `false` whenever `snapPoints` IS set, which lets the content fill the sheet via `RNHostView`'s own non-`matchContents` fill branch instead. This exactly matches the rule `@expo/ui`'s OWN community bottom-sheet implementation already uses for this same fork (`fitToContents = enableDynamicSizing && (!snapPointsProp || snapPointsProp.length === 0)`) — not a guessed value.
- **`SelectListField`'s Job Edit demo (`CLIENT_OPTIONS`) grown from 10 hand-written entries to 120 generated ones** (20 name prefixes × 12 suffixes, truncated to 120), per explicit request to stress-test the search + `FlatList` at a realistic "org with a real contacts list" scale — real company-name-shaped strings (not "Client 1"..."Client 120") so the search filter is meaningfully exercisable. `ClientId` widened from a literal union to plain `string` since the list is now generated, not `as const`; `loadJob()`'s demo value updated to `"client-0-0"` ("Acme Contracting Ltd.," the first generated entry) to match.
- **New test coverage**: 2 new tests in `bottom-sheet.a11y.test.tsx` asserting `matchContents` is `true`/`false` for the no-`snapPoints`/with-`snapPoints` cases respectively.
- **Two follow-up bugs, found immediately while the user tested the 120-option list above, fixed in the same entry**: (1) each option row's height visibly shrank/felt cramped once the sheet's content correctly filled its real fixed height (rows were previously laid out against an accidentally-oversized intrinsic container, before the `matchContents` fix above) — fixed with a real fixed `OPTION_ROW_HEIGHT` (52px) `height` (not `minHeight` — see the next bug) on each row, replacing the previous `py-3`-only sizing, plus `numberOfLines={1}` on the label so a long name truncates instead of wrapping and growing past that fixed height. (2) reopening the sheet after picking a far-down option (e.g. the 50th of 120) always showed the list scrolled back to the TOP — fixed via `FlatList`'s `initialScrollIndex`, computed from the selected value's index in the (unfiltered) options list at the moment the sheet opens, plus `getItemLayout` (required for `initialScrollIndex` to work without first measuring every row) and an `onScrollToIndexFailed` fallback per RN's own documented guidance; `FlatList` is keyed on a bumped-per-open `openSessionId` since `BottomSheet` keeps its content mounted across `isPresented` toggles and `initialScrollIndex` only applies at mount.
- **A THIRD, more serious bug shipped in the same round and was caught by the user immediately after: the list stopped scrolling entirely.** First diagnosis (wrong, corrected before it stuck): `getItemLayout`'s fixed-length promise disagreeing with a `minHeight`-only row that could grow — real, and fixed (see bug (1)'s `height`/`numberOfLines` fix above), but NOT the actual cause of "not scrolling." **Second attempt — giving the `FlatList` `style={{ flex: 1 }}` — also did NOT fix it**, confirmed live. **Real root cause**: `BottomSheet`'s content sits inside `RNHostView`'s non-`matchContents` SwiftUI fill branch (`.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)`), and the actual RN-side height for that subtree arrives via a size report-back through `ReportSizeToYogaNodeModifier`, not a normal Yoga layout pass a plain `flex: 1` child can reliably resolve against — the same "no resolvable dimension for a relative size" class of issue already documented at length in `full-width-button.tsx`'s history. **Fix**: the `FlatList` now gets a real, pre-computed PIXEL height (`useWindowDimensions().height * SHEET_HEIGHT_FRACTION - SHEET_CHROME_HEIGHT`, floored at 3 rows tall) instead of any flex/percentage sizing — `SHEET_HEIGHT_FRACTION` (0.75) is a single named constant shared with `BottomSheet`'s own `snapPoints` prop so the two can't drift apart. This sidesteps the native-bridge height-resolution question entirely rather than trying to make `flex`/`%` work through it.
- **Updated test coverage**: 2 new tests in `select-list-field.a11y.test.tsx` asserting `initialScrollIndex` is set to the selected option's real index (and `undefined` when nothing is selected). 124/124 `packages/ui-native` tests pass, 23/23 a11y coverage. Typecheck clean on both packages. NOTE: the scrolling fix itself (computed pixel height) was not yet confirmed on a real device at the time of this entry — the user's on-device testing loop for this fix is still in progress; re-verify against the live QA script section before considering this fully closed.

### 2026-09-14 — Job Edit (iOS): fixed the back-button discard-confirmation showing AFTER the screen closed, plus a follow-up double-alert bug found while fixing it

- **User report**: tapping the header back chevron with unsaved changes showed the discard-confirmation alert only AFTER the screen had already visibly closed, not before.
- **Root cause**: native-stack's default back button is a genuine `UIKit` control that starts its pop animation optimistically, before JS's `beforeRemove` listener gets a chance to call `event.preventDefault()`. The listener still correctly blocked the actual navigation-state change (the screen then slides back once the alert resolves), but that whole slide-away-then-back motion is exactly what was reported.
- **Fix**: the back chevron is now a custom `headerLeft` (a `Pressable` + `ChevronLeftIcon`, styled to match the native chevron via the render prop's own `tintColor`) that runs the SAME discard-check (`handleCancel`) synchronously, BEFORE any navigation starts — there's no native pop animation left to race against.
- **A second real bug surfaced immediately while testing the fix**: confirming "Discard" showed the SAME alert a second time right after. Cause: `handleCancel`'s `router.back()` call still triggers the still-armed `beforeRemove` listener, which re-checks `isDirty.current` — never cleared before the first `router.back()` call — and re-prompts for the exact same discard. Fixed by setting `isDirty.current = false` inside the discard callback, before calling `router.back()`, so the listener sees a clean form and lets the navigation through.
- Typecheck clean. Verified interactively by the user on a real iOS simulator (both the single-alert-before-close fix and the no-longer-doubled alert).

### 2026-09-13 — `FullWidthButton` moved off `@expo/ui`'s `Host`/`swift-ui Button` on iOS entirely: a real "no top spacing until first tap" bug, root-caused and fixed at the source, not worked around

- **User report**: on iOS, the Save button had no visible top spacing on first render — it sat flush against the card above it — but the correct gap appeared the instant the button was tapped, a visible "jump down."
- **Root-caused by reading `@expo/ui`'s own native source (`RNHostView.swift`)**: `Host`'s `matchContents` reports the true SwiftUI content size back to the RN shadow tree ASYNCHRONOUSLY, via `ReportSizeToYogaNodeModifier`'s `.onGeometryChange`/`.onChange(of: geometry.size)`, which only fires AFTER the first native layout pass. On mount, Yoga briefly lays out the `Host` (and its RN siblings, including the gap above it) using a stale/undersized height, which only visibly corrects once something forces an RN-side re-layout — exactly what a tap's state update does. A `setTimeout`-driven forced re-render shortly after mount was tried as a workaround first and did NOT reliably fix it (the native geometry callback's actual arrival time isn't bounded by a fixed JS timer) — abandoned in favor of removing the root cause instead.
- **A wrong intermediate diagnosis, corrected by the user before it shipped**: `job-edit-form.tsx`'s `ScrollView` `contentContainerClassName="gap-6 ..."` (a NativeWind flex `gap`) was suspected as the real cause and a `SECTION_GAP`/`marginTop` replacement was drafted — the user asked to revert this and pursue a custom-button fix in `FullWidthButton` instead, which is what shipped. That draft was fully reverted (`job-edit-form.tsx` has zero net changes in this entry).
- **The fix, iOS only**: `FullWidthButton` no longer uses `@expo/ui`'s `Host`/`swift-ui Button` on iOS at all — it's now a plain RN `Pressable` (`IOSFullWidthButton`) styled to visually approximate SwiftUI's `.borderedProminent`/`.bordered` look (solid/outlined pill, dimmed opacity while pressed, `controlSize` as a plain padding/font-size scale, `shape` as a real `borderRadius`). This eliminates the native-geometry round-trip the bug depends on entirely, rather than timing around it. Android is UNCHANGED — still the real `@expo/ui/jetpack-compose` `Button`/`OutlinedButton` with `fillMaxWidth()`, which was never affected (Android's `Host` box hugs its visible content tightly with no equivalent async gap).
- **A second real bug found while building the replacement**: `Pressable`'s own function-style `style={({ pressed }) => ({...})}` prop — standard, documented RN usage — rendered with NO styling applied at all on a real device (no background, no padding, no alignment, just bare unstyled text), confirmed via an on-device screenshot. Not fully root-caused, but the leading suspect is this app's `babel.config.js` routing every JSX element, including a bare `Pressable` with no `className`, through NativeWind's `nativewind/babel` interop wrapper — the first plain-RN-primitive `style` callback added to this package's `@expo/ui`-backed component set. Fixed by tracking pressed state with local `useState` and computing a plain (non-function) style object instead — confirmed working on a real device.
- **Tests**: `full-width-button.a11y.test.tsx` rewritten — iOS assertions now use real RNTL queries (`getByRole`, `getByText`) against actual RN primitives; Android tests (native-bridge-mock prop inspection) are unchanged. 120/120 `packages/ui-native` tests pass, 23/23 a11y coverage. Typecheck clean on both packages. Verified working on a real iOS simulator.

### 2026-09-13 — `DateTimePicker`: real `date`/`time`/`datetime` support on BOTH platforms (SIXTH design), plus a genuine `mode="datetime"` example field on Job Edit

- **Context**: the user made their own edits to `date-time-picker.tsx` (switching iOS from the community `ExpoDateTimePicker` wrapper to `@expo/ui/swift-ui`'s `DatePicker` + `Host` directly) and asked for a review before landing. Two real issues were found and are addressed here: `mode="datetime"` silently dropped the time component on iOS (a two-branch `? :` had no `"datetime"` case), and Android's community `DateTimePicker` has a documented, real limitation — no native combined date+time dialog at all — which this wrapper had never handled (it forwarded `mode` straight through, so `datetime` on Android silently fell back to date-only there too).
- **iOS**: `displayedComponentsForMode()` now has all three real branches — `"date"` → `["date"]`, `"time"` → `["hourAndMinute"]`, `"datetime"` → `["date", "hourAndMinute"]` (a real, valid combined array per `DatePickerComponent[]`'s own type, confirmed rendering as two side-by-side compact SwiftUI pills in the same control). A real, confirmed-on-device layout bug was found and fixed along the way: the two-pill `datetime` layout overflowed/clipped past the card's right edge at the existing `minWidth: 140` (sized for one date-only pill) — fixed with `minWidth: 240` specifically for `datetime` mode.
- **Android**: `AndroidDateTimePickerField` now implements a real two-step flow for `datetime` mode — tapping the trigger opens the DATE dialog first; confirming it opens the TIME dialog next (carrying the just-picked date forward, not the original value); confirming that merges the picked date's y/m/d with the picked time's h/m into one `Date` and calls `onChange` exactly once. Cancelling either step cancels the whole flow with no `onChange` call, matching the existing single-dialog behavior for `date`/`time` mode. This is the standard Android pattern for datetime entry (the same shape the Android Calendar app itself uses) — there is no native combined widget to reach for instead.
- **Confirmed, via `@expo/ui`'s own native Kotlin source (`DatePickerView.kt`), that Android's `onValueChange` genuinely only fires from inside the dialog's confirm-button `onClick`** — never on an intermediate value change — so closing the dialog in response to it (a change already present before this session's review) is correct behavior, not a premature-close bug as initially suspected before checking the source.
- **`Host.seedColor` (the new iOS mechanism for the picker's tint color) was checked against `@expo/ui`'s own `HostView.swift`** and confirmed to apply a real `.tint()` to the whole SwiftUI subtree via `SeedColorModifier` — a genuine, working equivalent to the old per-component `tint` modifier the community wrapper produced, not a lost feature.
- **New `packages/ui-native` test coverage**: 11 new/rewritten tests in `date-time-picker.a11y.test.tsx` — `date`/`time`/`datetime` `displayedComponents` on iOS, the `Host.seedColor` theming mechanism, and Android's full two-step `datetime` flow (opens date-then-time, merges correctly into one `Date`, `onChange` called exactly once, cancelling either step aborts the whole flow with no `onChange` call). 118/118 `packages/ui-native` tests pass.
- **`apps/showcase-native`'s Job Edit template gains a real `mode="datetime"` example**: a new "Site visit" field in the Schedule section (`siteVisitAt` on `JobFormValues`) — a genuinely realistic case for needing both a date and a time, unlike Start/Due date which are deliberately date-only. Verified visually on both a real iOS simulator (two side-by-side pills, no clipping after the width fix) and a real Android emulator (a single trigger pill showing the combined date+time via `toLocaleString()`, already supported by `formatValue`'s existing `datetime` branch).
- Typecheck clean on both packages.

### 2026-09-13 — Investigated the iOS-vs-Android `FullWidthButton` spacing complaint down to its real root cause; the compensating fix itself was tried, confirmed broken on-device, and reverted

- **User pushback, correctly redirecting two earlier wrong diagnoses in a row**: round 1 claimed the iOS-vs-Android gap difference was "resolved as a side effect" of switching to `shape="rounded"` — wrong, the user re-reported the same issue with fresh screenshots. Round 2 (pixel-measuring the raw gap value, which came out equal on both platforms) suggested button HEIGHT was the real issue — also wrong, per explicit correction: "the problem is not the spacing between buttons, but the View in which the buttons are there and the Notes FormSection."
- **Root cause, correctly found this time** by wrapping a real on-device `Host` in a debug-colored `View` on both platforms: Android's `Host` box hugs its visible pill tightly on every edge (zero slack). iOS's `Host` box extends real, invisible space PAST the visible pill's bottom edge — SwiftUI reserving layout space to satisfy Apple's 44pt minimum tap-target height for `.borderedProminent` buttons, which `Host`'s `matchContents` correctly measures as part of the component's true layout box even though the pill itself paints shorter. `controlSize`/`buttonBorderShape` were both ruled out as levers (neither changed the slack) before concluding this was a fixed platform behavior, not a tunable modifier value.
- **The attempted fix (a hardcoded `marginBottom: -13` on the iOS `Host` wrapper) was ITSELF wrong, and is the actual subject of this entry** — not the diagnosis above, which held up. The `-13` value came from measuring a single vertical pixel column in one screenshot; real on-device testing (a fresh user screenshot, full-width scrolled view) showed this overshot badly enough to make Save and Cancel visibly OVERLAP — their rounded corners clipping into each other, worse than the original complaint. Root cause of the mismeasurement: a single sample column can miss real overlap entirely, since two rounded-rectangle shapes overlap far more visibly near their curved corners than at dead-center — exactly where the one column happened to land.
- **Final state: the margin compensation is fully reverted.** `FullWidthButton` now applies zero compensation around its `Host` on either platform — the raw, correct `Host` box (including iOS's invisible tap-target slack) is what callers space against, matching each platform's own accessibility-mandated control sizing rather than fighting it with a guessed constant. If this is revisited, any future compensation must be measured across the FULL button width in a real, complete (not cropped) on-device screenshot, with explicit before/after checks at both rounded corners specifically — not a single center column.
- 109/109 `packages/ui-native` tests pass (the regression test now asserts NO negative margin exists, replacing the one that asserted the broken fix's presence), 23/23 a11y coverage. Typecheck clean.
- **Process note**: three consecutive attempts at this one spacing complaint each corrected the previous mistake but introduced a new one, and the only reason the second mistake (the overlap) was caught was that the user kept testing the actual running app and reporting back with real screenshots rather than accepting a "fixed" claim backed only by narrow, self-reported pixel sampling. The standing lesson from this whole thread: a fix for a purely visual discrepancy is not verified until confirmed against a full, real on-device rendering — a single-column pixel sample or a cropped screenshot is not sufficient evidence, especially for anything involving curved/rounded shapes.

### 2026-09-13 — `Button`/`FullWidthButton` gain real `controlSize` and `shape` props; a genuine `@expo/ui` API-usage bug found and fixed along the way

- **User follow-up, two parts**: (1) the `gap-3` spacing between the in-content Save/Cancel buttons looked visually different on iOS vs. Android; (2) add `controlSize` (SwiftUI's real native control-size modifier) as a `Button`/`FullWidthButton` property, plus a `shape` prop (rounded/sharp/pill) for both.
- **`controlSize`**: added as a real prop on both `Button` and `FullWidthButton`, forwarding directly to SwiftUI's own `controlSize` modifier (`mini`/`small`/`regular`/`large`/`extraLarge`) on iOS. A genuine no-op on Android — Jetpack Compose's `@expo/ui` Button has no equivalent named-size concept (only a raw `contentPadding` prop taking exact dp values, a different API shape entirely) — same "real prop, iOS-only effect" pattern already established elsewhere in this package.
- **`shape` ("pill" | "rounded" | "sharp")**: this time actually works on both platforms, using a DIFFERENT, correct mechanism from the `clipShape` approach tried and abandoned earlier this session — SwiftUI's `buttonBorderShape` modifier genuinely changes what `.buttonStyle` PAINTS (unlike `clipShape`, which only crops after the fact). `Button` gets `shape` as iOS-only (its Android path has no `shape` prop reachable through the universal `@expo/ui` wrapper it uses); `FullWidthButton` gets it working on BOTH platforms, since it already uses `@expo/ui/jetpack-compose`'s direct `Button`/`OutlinedButton`, which has a real `shape` prop.
- **A genuine `@expo/ui` API-usage bug was found and fixed while wiring Android's `shape`**: passing `Shape.RoundedCorner(...)`/`Shape.Rectangle(...)`/even a bare `Shape.Pill` as JSX (`<Shape.RoundedCorner ... />`) silently broke the ENTIRE button — it stopped rendering completely, with no crash log and no JS error anywhere, reproduced consistently across a cold Metro restart and multiple relaunches. Root-caused by fetching Expo's own docs (`docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/ui/jetpack-compose/button`), which show `shape` constructed by CALLING the function directly (`shape={Shape.RoundedCorner({cornerRadii: {...}})}`), never as JSX. Fixed by calling `Shape.RoundedCorner({...})`/`Shape.Rectangle({...})` as plain functions instead of rendering them as elements — confirmed fixed on a real Android emulator, with a real visible rounded corner on both the filled Save and outlined Cancel buttons.
- **The iOS-vs-Android spacing complaint was very likely a symptom of the shape mismatch, not the `gap-3` value itself**: a full-pill button's visible edge sits further inward from its own layout bounds than a rounded-rectangle's edge does, so the same numeric gap can look uneven purely because of shape, not spacing. Job Edit's Save/Cancel now both use `shape="rounded"`, which resolves this as a side effect.
- 108/108 `packages/ui-native` tests pass (9 new tests covering `controlSize`/`shape` on both components — the Android `Shape`-as-JSX regression is now covered by asserting the resulting modifier's exact shape, not just that SOME modifier exists), 23/23 a11y coverage. Typecheck clean on both packages. Verified on real iOS simulator AND a real Android emulator — both platforms show a genuine, visible rounded corner (previously only confirmed on iOS, since Android's bug meant the button didn't render at all until the JSX-vs-function-call fix).

### 2026-09-13 — New `FullWidthButton`: a real, confirmed `@expo/ui` limitation meant `Button`'s own `fullWidth` prop had to be reverted

- **User follow-up on the in-content Save/Cancel buttons**: make them full-width (not content-sized/pill-centered), and use a less-rounded corner. Also flagged the Notes-to-Save spacing as looking off.
- **The rounded-corner request is a real, confirmed upstream `@expo/ui` limitation, not fixable from this codebase**: on iOS, `Button` renders via SwiftUI's native `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)`, which bakes the pill/capsule shape into how the FILLED background itself is painted — a `clipShape`/`frame` modifier (the only styling hooks `Button` exposes) only crops transparent corners around what's already drawn, it cannot change the already-painted pill shape underneath. Confirmed by actually trying it (a `shape="rounded"` prop translating to a `clipShape` modifier) and observing zero visible change on a real iOS simulator. Dropped per explicit direction — no corner-radius option exists on any button component in this codebase today.
- **The full-width request took FOUR investigation rounds to actually solve, and ultimately could not be done as a prop on `Button` at all — full trail kept in `full-width-button.tsx`'s own doc comment so it isn't repeated:**
  1. `style={{ width: "100%" }}` — does nothing. Both `transformStyle.ios.ts`/`.android.ts` (the universal `style`→modifier translators `Button` uses) force-cast `style.width as number` with zero runtime validation, straight into a native `CGFloat?`/`Dp` field — there is no percentage-width concept anywhere in that layer.
  2. A flexible `frame({ maxWidth: Infinity })` via the `modifiers` escape hatch — `Infinity` does not survive the bridge (confirmed via a debug render showing it arrive natively as `maxWidth: null`; something in the prop-serialization path round-trips through `JSON.stringify`, which turns `Infinity` into `null`).
  3. `frame({ maxWidth: Number.MAX_VALUE })` (a real finite stand-in) — survives the bridge this time, but STILL doesn't visually stretch the button. Isolated by testing a small FIXED `frame({ width: 60, height: 60 })` on the same button, which DID visibly clamp/truncate it ("Sa…") — proving `modifiers`/`frame` genuinely reaches native code; the issue is specific to `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)` sizing its own pill background to the LABEL's content, independent of an outer `.frame` on the `Button` view.
  4. Even a real MEASURED fixed pixel width (via `onLayout` on a `width:"100%"` wrapping `View`, ruling out any unit/serialization issue entirely) — still no visible stretch, on a real device. Confirms this is `.buttonStyle`'s own background-sizing behavior, not a units problem.
  - **The actual fix, which required a NEW component, not a `Button` prop**: apply the frame/fill modifier to the button's LABEL CONTENT instead of the `Button` view from the outside. New `packages/ui-native` component `FullWidthButton` uses `@expo/ui/swift-ui`'s `Button` directly (bypassing the universal cross-platform wrapper `Button` uses) with a `swift-ui/Text` as `children`, carrying its own `frame({ maxWidth: Number.MAX_VALUE, alignment: "center" })` — SwiftUI's `.buttonStyle` sizes its background to fit whatever content it's given, so a full-width LABEL naturally produces a full-width pill. On Android, Jetpack Compose's `Button` has no equivalent content-vs-background split — `fillMaxWidth()` applied directly to the Button itself already stretches it correctly, no workaround needed there.
  - **`Button` itself is fully reverted to its pre-existing state** (`fullWidth` prop removed entirely, including its test coverage) per explicit direction — it was never shipped in a broken state; every attempt was caught before landing.
- Job Edit's in-content Save/Cancel now use `FullWidthButton` instead of `Button`. Verified full-width AND functionally working (header Save producing the "Job updated" toast, Cancel's discard-guard) on a real iOS simulator; verified visually full-width on a real Android emulator, though interactive tap verification on Android could not be completed in this session — the emulator stopped responding to ANY touch input partway through testing (confirmed non-specific to this change: the pre-existing, untouched Retention-held Switch and the Home tab bar item also stopped responding to `adb input tap` at the same time, while `adb`-level key events like HOME continued working normally) — a tooling/environment issue, not a code regression, disclosed here rather than glossed over.
- The Notes-to-Save spacing complaint was a side effect of the old undersized, off-center pill button making the surrounding whitespace look uneven — resolved as a side effect of the width fix; the gap now reads as the same consistent `gap-6` rhythm used between every other section on the screen.
- 100/100 `packages/ui-native` tests pass, 23/23 components have a11y coverage (the new `FullWidthButton` included). Typecheck clean on both packages.

### 2026-09-13 — Job Edit: Android header actions to match iOS (Save + More→Delete), in-content Save/Cancel below Notes on both platforms

- **User request**: bring Android's Job Edit header to parity with iOS's (a Save action plus a "More" menu containing "Delete job"), remove Android's sticky bottom Cancel/Save footer and its standalone "Delete job" button now that Delete lives in the header menu, and add a NEW always-visible Save/Cancel button pair inside the scrollable form itself, directly below Notes, on BOTH platforms.
- **Android's header needed a different API than iOS's, not just the same code duplicated**: `expo-router`'s `unstable_headerRightItems` (what iOS's Save checkmark + "•••" menu use) is explicitly `@platform ios`-only per its own type declarations — its `icon` prop only accepts an SF Symbol or static image, with no Android concept at all. Android's header actions are built instead from the older, genuinely cross-platform `headerRight` render-function API: a plain check-icon `Pressable` for Save, and `packages/ui-native`'s existing `ContextMenu` (`@expo/ui/community/menu`, a real Jetpack Compose `DropdownMenu`) wrapping an "⋮" icon for the overflow, containing "Delete job" as a destructive action — matching `profile-header-items.tsx`'s own established Android-`headerRight` icon-button styling (plain Lucide icon, `colors.onSurface`, 22px, 16px gap, 8px hitSlop) rather than inventing a new pattern.
- **Real bug found and fixed on-device, not just in code review**: the "⋮" trigger initially did nothing when tapped, reproduced consistently across several `adb input tap` attempts precisely on the icon. Root cause: `MenuView` (`@expo/ui/community/menu`'s Android implementation) already wraps its own `children` in an internal `Pressable` whose `onPress` is what opens the menu when `shouldOpenOnLongPress={false}`; wrapping the icon in a SECOND, handler-less `Pressable` as `ContextMenu`'s child made that inner `Pressable` swallow the touch as its own gesture responder before it ever reached the outer one. Fixed by passing a plain `View` (not a `Pressable`) as `ContextMenu`'s child, matching the working `ContextMenuDemo`'s own pattern (a plain `Text` element, not a `Pressable`) — confirmed fixed on a real Android emulator via `adb input tap`, both opening and dismissing the native dropdown correctly, and the header Save icon triggering `handleSave` (verified via the "Job updated" toast appearing).
- **Android's sticky bottom Cancel/Save footer and its standalone "Delete job" button are both removed entirely** — replaced by a new `View` rendered inside the `ScrollView`, directly after the Notes `FormSection`, on BOTH platforms: a full-width `Button` "Save" followed by a `variant="secondary"` "Cancel" below it. Both call the SAME `handleSave`/`handleCancel` already used by the header actions and (on iOS) the old header-only flow — this is a second, always-visible affordance for the same actions, not a new code path (`handleCancel` already ran the unsaved-changes discard guard before navigating back; that behavior is unchanged, just relocated). The `Toast`'s bottom offset (`message` confirmation banner) is simplified from a platform-conditional `bottom-24`/`bottom-8` to a flat `bottom-8` on both platforms, since there's no longer a platform-specific sticky footer to clear.
- Verified end-to-end on both a real iOS simulator and a real Android emulator: header actions present and working on both platforms, no sticky footer or standalone Delete button on Android, in-content Save/Cancel visible below Notes on both. 95/95 `packages/ui-native` tests pass (no component in that package changed); typecheck clean on `apps/showcase-native`.

### 2026-09-13 — Job Edit header: real iOS transparent-header-over-blurred-content look, matching Components/Home, with the actual (non-obvious) mechanism that makes it work

- **User request, evolving over three rounds of real feedback**: make the Job Edit header look like `(tabs)/components/[slug]`'s detail header — no large title (already correct), AND (per explicit follow-up, with real screenshots) the same transparent-header-blurring-scrolled-content look Home/Components get, with no bottom border, on iOS.
- **Round 1 (title-size investigation) produced one keeper and one red herring.** Keeper: `app/_layout.tsx`'s `job-edit/[jobId]` route now explicitly sets `headerLargeTitleEnabled: false`, matching `components/_layout.tsx`'s own explicit pattern (harmless, just parity). Red herring: dropping `job-edit-form.tsx`'s `headerStyle.backgroundColor` on iOS outright, on the assumption that omitting a background color is what makes Home/Components' headers translucent — reverted once round 2 showed it broke dark mode outright (a solid WHITE header regardless of theme, confirmed across multiple job IDs via real screenshots).
- **The actual, confirmed mechanism (found by reading `expo-router`'s own `useHeaderConfigProps.js`, not by guessing further): omitting `headerStyle.backgroundColor` does nothing for translucency by itself.** Its `translucent` value is only ever true when `headerBackground` is set, `headerTransparent` is explicitly `true`, or `(hasHeaderSearchBar || headerLargeTitleEnabled)` — Home/Components' headers only look translucent+blurred because THEY set `headerLargeTitleEnabled: true`, which is what actually flips translucency on; `scrollEdgeEffects` (`"automatic"` by default) is the separate option that then paints the real blur once the header is translucent. Job Edit has no large title by design, so it needs `headerTransparent: true` set explicitly to get the same translucency for free — this is the real fix, applied in `job-edit-form.tsx`'s own `Stack.Screen options` (iOS only; Android keeps its explicit `colors.surface` background, since it has no equivalent automatic blur to fall back on). Also gave the `ScrollView` itself an explicit `pageBackground` `style` (previously only set on its `KeyboardAvoidingView` parent) so the blur, once genuinely active, samples the correct themed color rather than a transparent layer.
- **A real structural risk was investigated and ruled out before this fix, not assumed away**: `(home)/index.tsx`'s own doc comment warns that `react-native-screens`' scroll-edge tracking needs the screen's `ScrollView` to be its own direct root, "not wrapped in an outer View" — Job Edit's `ScrollView` IS wrapped, in a `KeyboardAvoidingView`. Read `RNSScrollViewFinder.mm` (the actual native lookup) directly rather than assuming this was the blocker: it walks down through each view's FIRST subview looking for a `UIScrollView`, so a single-child wrapper like `KeyboardAvoidingView` (confirmed by reading RN's own source: it renders one plain `<View>{children}</View>` for `behavior="padding"`) does not break the lookup. This ruled out a much riskier rework (restructuring the keyboard-avoidance logic to make `ScrollView` a literal screen root) that would have reopened a previously-fixed, carefully-verified bug (Notes hidden behind the keyboard) for no reason — the real fix needed no changes to keyboard handling at all.
- Verified on a real iOS simulator, dark mode, across multiple job IDs: header now blends seamlessly into the body with no visible seam or border, matching Components' own header exactly. Typecheck clean on `apps/showcase-native`; `packages/ui-native`'s 95/95 tests and 22/22 a11y coverage unaffected (no component in that package changed).

### 2026-09-13 — Form redesign: borderless row fields + `Divider`, plus a searchable `SelectListField` for long option lists (user-requested, showcased in `apps/showcase-native`)

- **New `packages/ui-native` component: `Divider`** (`src/components/divider.tsx`) — a plain 1px full-bleed row separator for use INSIDE a form card between fields, distinct from web `packages/ui`'s `Separator` (a standalone section separator). Marked `accessibilityElementsHidden`/`importantForAccessibility="no"` as purely decorative.
- **New `packages/ui-native` component: `SelectListField`** (`src/components/select-list-field.tsx`) — the "long list" counterpart to the existing `SelectField` (a native `MenuView`, right for short fixed enums like Job Status). For a select whose options don't fit a dropdown (e.g. Client, picked from an org's contacts), this renders the same borderless row trigger and opens a `BottomSheet` with a search box pinned above a filterable, scrollable option list, checkmarking the current selection. Selection-only by design — no inline "create new" affordance; that's a separate, explicitly out-of-scope addition if a future screen needs it.
- **`TextField`/`NativeTextField` gained an additive `variant="row" | "bordered"` prop** (default `"bordered"`, unchanged for every existing consumer — login screen, search, design-system-native docs). `variant="row"` drops the field's own border/background/radius entirely, for use inside a shared-surface form card whose boundary now comes from the card + `Divider` rows between fields, not each field's own bordered box. Error state in row mode tints the field's text instead of a border (there's no border left to recolor).
- **`apps/showcase-native`'s `job-edit-form.tsx` template redesigned end-to-end** as the pilot consumer: each `FormSection` now renders an uppercase caption above ONE borderless card, with fields laid out as `FormRow`s (label left, control right) separated by full-bleed `Divider`s instead of each field being its own bordered box. Client — previously a free-text `TextField` — is now a `SelectListField` over a 10-contact demo list with search, matching the design reference the user supplied (a native-app "grouped card + row dividers" form pattern, e.g. 1Password's Add Login screen) and its explicit recommendation to use a searchable popup rather than a dropdown for long lists. Title/Job value/Notes use `variant="row"`; Status uses `SelectField variant="row"` (native menu, short enum); DateTimePicker/Switch rows are unchanged per explicit instruction (no redesign asked for those two controls) and simply drop into the new row layout, which they already matched shape-wise (label left, control right).
- **A real device-screenshot review caught a gap the first pass of this redesign missed**: `SelectField` never got the same `variant` prop `TextField`/`NativeTextField` did, so Status kept rendering its old bordered pill (visible border, its own `bg-surface`/`rounded-lg`) while every other field in the same "Details" card had already gone borderless — the exact kind of inconsistent-looking card this redesign was meant to eliminate, confirmed on a real device rather than caught by tests or typecheck (neither exercises visual appearance). Fixed: `SelectField` gained the identical additive `variant="row" | "bordered"` prop (default `"bordered"`, unchanged for every other consumer), and `job-edit-form.tsx`'s Status field now passes `variant="row"`.
- **A real environment gap found and worked around while testing `SelectListField`**: content rendered inside `BottomSheet`'s `RNHostView` bridge doesn't receive RNTL's synthetic touch-responder dispatch under `jest-expo`'s mock (confirmed by reproducing the same failure with a bare `FlatList`/`Pressable` inside a `BottomSheet`, no `SelectListField` involved) — consistent with this codebase's documented pattern for `@expo/ui`-backed components (assert against props passed into the native-bridge subtree, not a full simulated interaction through it). `select-list-field.a11y.test.tsx`'s selection test reads the row's `onPress` prop directly off the composite `Pressable` node and invokes it, rather than `fireEvent.press`.
- All 82 `packages/ui-native` tests pass, 23/23 components (including the two new ones) have a11y coverage per the existing `check-a11y-coverage.mjs` enforcement. `pnpm typecheck` is clean across `packages/ui-native` and `apps/showcase-native`. Verified via the test suite, typecheck, and a real-device screenshot review (which is what caught the `SelectField` gap above) — the rest of the layout (card/divider grouping, borderless Title/Client/Job value rows, the Client search sheet) matched the intended design in that same review.
- **Follow-up (same day): Material-style FLOATING labels, per explicit follow-up design request.** New `packages/ui-native` component `FloatingLabelField` (wraps `TextField`/`NativeTextField`): when empty and unfocused, the label sits centered in the row as the placeholder itself; on focus or once a value exists, it animates up to a small caption above the value. `SelectField`/`SelectListField` gained the equivalent static (non-animated — no real focus state) two-state `floatingLabel`/`required` props. `NativeTextField` gained a genuinely new capability to make this possible: it previously exposed no focus/blur callback at all, fixed by wiring `@expo/ui`'s real `onFocusChange` through new `onFocus`/`onBlur` props. `job-edit-form.tsx`'s Title/Client/Status/Job value/Notes all switched to this treatment; Start date/Due date/Retention held stayed on the plain-label `FormRow` shape, unchanged per instruction. A real bug was found and fixed during live verification: putting a NativeWind `className` on the animated `Text` produced a live `Cannot update a component (CssInterop.Text) while rendering a different component (CssInterop.Text)` React error — fixed by moving that one element's styling to plain inline `style`, confirmed resolved via a fresh device screenshot with no error banner. 94/94 tests pass, 22/22 a11y coverage.
- **Follow-up (same day): four visual-polish fixes from user feedback on a live device screenshot, each pixel-measured before and after, not just eyeballed.** (1) **Row height consistency** — every row in a `FormSection` card (text field, select, date picker, switch alike) now shares one fixed `ROW_HEIGHT` (56px) via `FormRow`, replacing a mix of `min-h-11` and each control's own intrinsic height, which had produced a visibly uneven row-height rhythm (divider-to-divider measurement confirmed uniform 171px rows after the fix). (2) **Value font-size mismatch** — `NativeTextField` had NO `font` modifier at all, rendering SwiftUI's system-default size (~17pt) next to `SelectField`'s explicit 14px, a real visible mismatch; fixed with `font({ size: 14 })`, now matching `SelectField` exactly everywhere `NativeTextField` renders, not only inside `FloatingLabelField`. (3) **Label-to-value spacing** — `NativeTextField` gained a new `floatingAbove` prop applying asymmetric top/bottom padding (26/6, vs. the plain symmetric row padding) specifically for a `FloatingLabelField` consumer, since the previous uniform padding left no clearance for the label floating above it; `FloatingLabelField`'s own label resting/floating vertical offsets were also loosened (14→18 / 2→6). (4) **`DateTimePicker`'s right-alignment vs. `Switch`** — SwiftUI's `.compact` style bakes its own internal trailing padding into the native pill's bounds (confirmed by comparing it to `Switch`'s tight-hugging `Host matchContents` pill), so at its existing, deliberately-unchanged `width: 140/90` (shrinking it would reintroduce a previously-fixed overflow-clipping regression) the pill's visible content sat short of the row's true right edge; fixed with a `marginRight: -16` on an outer wrapper `View` (not on the picker's own `style`, which the native pill measures against) — pixel-measured on a real screenshot at ~26px/9pt short before the fix, ~2px after. All four fixes verified via direct pixel measurement on real device screenshots (edge positions and divider-to-divider distances), not just visual impression. 94/94 tests still pass, typecheck clean.
- **Second follow-up (same day): fix (3) above was itself still measurably wrong, caught by the user on a live screenshot.** The `floatingAbove` padding chosen by eye (`top: 26`, then a first correction to `top: 21`) still left `NativeTextField` rows (Title/Job value) with a 41-42px label-to-value gap against `SelectField`/`SelectListField`'s 32-33px in the same card — visibly different spacing, not the match the previous entry claimed. Root-caused by actually pixel-scanning the label/value text-row boundaries on a real screenshot (brightness-thresholded bands along a fixed x-range) for both field types and computing the gap directly, rather than eyeballing it — the pixel-to-`padding`-point relationship isn't a clean 3x ratio (SwiftUI's system-font line-height adds its own space beyond the raw padding value), which is why the first linear correction undershot. Final value, `top: 14`, found by iterating from the observed ratio between the two prior measurements and re-verifying: now 30-31px vs. Select's 32-33px, a ≤3px residual difference that reads as matching. `native-text-field.tsx`'s own doc comment now spells out the full three-iteration history and the exact re-verification method, specifically so this number isn't "fixed" a fourth time by eye. 94/94 tests still pass, typecheck clean.
- **Android verification pass (same day, user-requested): a real Android emulator surfaced two genuine bugs iOS testing never would have caught, plus a third light-mode-only bug found independently in the same pass.** (1) **Single-line `TextField` value text rendered beside its floated label instead of below it, Android only** — RN's `TextInput` on Android defaults an unset `textAlignVertical` to `"center"`, vertically centering the value within the field's full row height regardless of any `pt-*` padding; `FloatingLabelField` only set `textAlignVertical="top"` for the `multiline` case, leaving single-line Title/Job value at Android's default. iOS's `NativeTextField` has no equivalent default-centering behavior, so this never showed up there. Fixed by setting `textAlignVertical="top"` unconditionally. (2) **A real, separate root cause once (1) was fixed: `TextField`'s `variant="row"` height/padding overrides had no effect on Android at all**, confirmed by testing values from `pt-6` up through an intentionally extreme `paddingTop: 100` (which only ever produced identical text position or outright clipping, never a proportional shift) — traced to `TextField`'s className merging being a plain array `.join(" ")` with no `cn`/twMerge dedup, unlike every other field component in this package. A caller-supplied override className (`FloatingLabelField`'s `"h-14 pt-7 pb-1"`) landed in the final string ALONGSIDE `TextField`'s own base `"h-11 px-0"` rather than replacing it, and NativeWind resolved the resulting `h-11`-vs-`h-14` conflict by its own internal rule-generation order — which happened to always keep `h-11`, so no override from any caller could ever take effect. Fixed by routing `TextField`'s className through `cn`, matching `SelectField`/`SelectListField`/`Button`'s existing pattern; re-verified with a full row-height/label-gap pixel measurement showing Title and Job value now within 1-2px of Status/Client's own label-to-value gap (33-35px across all four Details rows) — a real fix, not just a plausible theory, confirmed via before/after screenshots on a real Android emulator. (3) **Light mode showed NO visible card/group boundaries at all, on both iOS and Android** — this screen's page background and card background were BOTH `#FFFFFF` in light mode (`colors.background` and `colors.surface` are identical in `tokens/colors.ts`'s light palette; only dark mode's `background`/`surface` already differed, which is why this went unnoticed through the whole feature's dark-mode-only development). First fix attempt swapped the CARD to `surface-sunken`, which restored contrast but read backwards (a slightly-gray card floating on a white page) versus the standard iOS/Material convention; per an explicit follow-up request, the final fix instead makes the PAGE background use `surfaceSunken` while cards stay on the normal `surface` token — gray page, white cards, matching dark mode's own already-correct direction. Verified on both a real iOS simulator and a real Android emulator in light mode. All three fixes: 94/94 tests pass, typecheck clean on both `packages/ui-native` and `apps/showcase-native`.
- **Two more real, reported follow-up bugs (same day): the Notes field was completely untappable, and even after that fix its spacing/sizing didn't read as a textarea.** (1) **Notes (the form's one `multiline` field) accepted no taps at all** — `FloatingLabelField`'s outer wrapper used `className="h-full ..."` unconditionally; `h-full` resolves against the immediate parent's own height, which is correct for every single-line field (whose parent is `FormRow`'s fixed-height slot) but Notes' actual parent (`job-edit-form.tsx`'s own wrapping `View`) has no explicit height at all, so `h-full` collapsed to a near-zero real hit-test area even though the underlying `TextField`'s own explicit `h-24` still drew a normal-looking box — confirmed live (tapping produced no focus ring, no keyboard, nothing) and root-caused precisely (not just plausibly): a new regression test asserts the wrapper's className never contains `h-full` when `multiline`, verified to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the fix. Fixed by sizing the wrapper to content for `multiline` instead of `h-full`. (2) **Once (1) was fixed, Notes' spacing was still wrong — reused the single-line field's tuning wholesale instead of having its own, and had no real minimum height**, so an empty/short value collapsed to roughly one line tall rather than reading as a proper multi-line textarea. Fixed with a dedicated `MULTILINE_FLOATING_TOP` (vs. the single-line `FLOATING_TOP`) for the label's floated position, a multiline-specific `floatingAbove` padding on the iOS `NativeTextField` branch (SwiftUI's `frame({ minHeight: 96, alignment: "top" })`, matching Android's existing `h-24`), and a top-anchored (not vertically-centered) wrapper layout for `multiline`. Verified live on a real iOS simulator: the Notes card now shows a real multi-line-sized box with its placeholder anchored top-left, matching the height of a genuine textarea rather than a single input row. 95/95 tests pass (new regression test included), typecheck clean.

### 2026-09-04 — `packages/ui-native` reworked onto `@expo/ui` (real SwiftUI/Jetpack Compose), plus a new native-only `apps/showcase-native` on expo-router (user-requested rework)

- **Full-replace, per component, onto `@expo/ui`**: every `packages/ui-native` control with a genuine native-backed equivalent — Button, Switch (new), Select (was `@react-native-picker/picker`), Slider (new), ContextMenu (new), DateTimePicker (new), BottomSheet (new) — is now backed by `@expo/ui`'s real SwiftUI (iOS) / Jetpack Compose (Android) components via a `Host` bridge, not NativeWind/`cva`-styled RN primitives. `@expo/ui@57.0.16` + `react-native-worklets@0.10.1` are now **hard dependencies** of `packages/ui-native` (accepted tradeoff: `apps/mobile` gains these native modules even though it doesn't use any `@expo/ui`-backed component yet — confirmed not to break its install/build). The 9 components with no native equivalent (Card, Badge, Avatar, EmptyState, Skeleton, Spinner, StatusChip, TextField, Toast) got a Phase 4 visual-consistency pass only — unchanged API/behavior, still NativeWind-styled.
- **New theming bridge**: `useNativeColors()`/`useNativeHostTheme(seedColor?)` (`src/theme/use-native-colors.ts`) resolve design-system color tokens into either a raw hex value or a `<Host colorScheme seedColor>` prop pair — `@expo/ui`'s own theming mechanism, since most native-bridge components take no direct color prop at all.
- **New `apps/showcase-native`** — a native-only (no web/Expo Go fallback) showcase app on `expo-router` (the first app in this monorepo to use it), specifically to use `unstable-native-tabs` (`NativeTabs`) as real routed native tab-bar chrome plus a genuine collapsing large-title header. Deliberately does NOT replace `apps/design-system-native` (still the doc app for the OLD NativeWind-primitive/React-Navigation approach, including its own still-current `@expo/ui` iOS-only pilot pages) or touch `apps/mobile` — both remain on React Navigation + `FloatingTabBar` unchanged. Ships 4 tabs (Home, Components — 16 demo screens, Templates — List+Detail and Settings, Profile) built out across Phases 3–5.
- **Real bugs found and fixed along the way** (all now documented in CLAUDE.md's new dedicated bullets, so future work doesn't re-discover them): a Swift 6/Xcode 26.x crash in `expo-modules-jsi` (fixed via a `pnpm patch`); `pnpm.overrides` silently not applying to an unmet peer dependency (reanimated needed to become a direct dependency instead); a real on-device crash passing a bare string as `@expo/ui` Button's `children` (fixed by routing through `label`); `NativeTabs.Trigger` silently dropping a route-group tab when named `"index"` instead of the group's own registered name (`"(home)"`); a `headerBlurEffect`/`scrollEdgeEffects` conflict (removed the former, since the latter already gives free real blur on iOS 26+); `headerLargeTitleEnabled` rendering its title over screen content without `contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior="automatic"` on every ScrollView underneath it; and — the highest-value bug, caught only via real on-device tap testing (`adb shell input tap`), not by typechecking — `<Link asChild><View>` rendering tappable-looking rows that never navigate, since `asChild` clones `onPress` onto its child but `View` has no press semantics; fixed by using `Pressable` in three list screens.
- **a11y testing adapted, not replaced**: `@expo/ui`-backed components render as opaque native-bridge mocks under jest-expo with no queryable accessibility tree, so their `.a11y.test.tsx` files assert against the props passed into the bridge component (e.g. `modifiers`) instead of RNTL's role/state queries — still a real, meaningful regression net, just one level shallower; true native a11y semantics are verified manually on a real device. All 60 `packages/ui-native` tests pass, 17/17 components have a11y coverage (enforced by the existing `check-a11y-coverage.mjs` script).
- Verified end-to-end on both a real iOS simulator and a real Android emulator throughout — Phase 3's native chrome (tab bar, large-title header, scroll-edge blur/fade), Phase 4's mixed native+restyled screens, and Phase 5's full component/template navigation walk (including tapping into a dynamic `[jobId]`/`[slug]` route) were all confirmed live via screenshots, not just by reading the code. `pnpm typecheck` is clean across `packages/ui-native`, `apps/showcase-native`, `apps/design-system-native`, and `apps/mobile`. See CLAUDE.md's new `packages/ui-native`/`apps/showcase-native` bullets for the full architectural detail this summary doesn't repeat.

### 2026-08-30 — `FloatingTabBar`: fixed a real, distinct tab-label misalignment bug on iOS simulator (user report), and the verification gap that let it through

- **User report, on a real iOS simulator**: "Messages" sat visibly lower than the other 4 tabs — reported right after the icon-alignment fix (entry below) shipped, which made it initially look like a regression of that same bug. It wasn't: this was a genuinely different bug the icon-library migration never touched.
- **Root cause**: the label `<Text>` in `floating-tab-bar.tsx` had no `numberOfLines` set. "Messages" (tied with "Expenses" for the longest label) could wrap to two lines on a real, narrow ~390pt-wide iPhone screen — each of 5 tabs shares one `max-w-md` pill, so per-tab horizontal space is genuinely tight — while shorter labels ("Home", "Jobs") stayed on one line. Since each tab's `Pressable` centers its icon+label as one vertical block, a two-line label shifts that whole block relative to its single-line neighbors.
- **The real lesson**: the previous fix's own verification (a headless-browser check confirming identical icon positions) used a ~900px-wide desktop browser window — far wider than any real phone, so it could not have caught a width-constrained text-wrapping bug. This time, re-verified at a genuinely realistic narrow viewport (390×844, an iPhone 14-class size) instead of an arbitrary desktop window.
- **Fix**: added `numberOfLines={1}` (forbids wrapping) plus `adjustsFontSizeToFit`/`minimumFontScale={0.8}` (shrinks a genuinely-too-long label slightly rather than clipping it, matching iOS's own `UITabBarItem` behavior for long labels) to the label `Text`.
- **Verified at the correct viewport this time**: a headless-browser check at 390×844 showed identical icon `top`/`height` and label `top` values across all 5 tabs after the fix, with "Expenses"/"Messages" correctly truncating ("Expens…"/"Messa…") instead of wrapping — confirmed both via measured coordinates and a screenshot.
- Verified beyond that: full workspace `typecheck`/`lint`/`test` clean (12/12/11/11/10/10, 18 `ui-native` tests); a real `expo export --platform ios` for `apps/mobile` bundles successfully.
- **CLAUDE.md updated** with both the fix and the explicit lesson: verify mobile components at a realistic narrow viewport (not just "some browser window"), especially anything with per-item flex-divided horizontal space and text content.
- Stories: `packages/ui-native` component fix — no PRD story of its own.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (`packages/ui-native` foundational stage).

### 2026-08-30 — Migrated `packages/ui-native`'s icons from `@expo/vector-icons` to `lucide-react-native`, fixing a real icon-alignment bug (user request)

- **User report + request**: tab bar icons/labels weren't level with each other (a screenshot showed Home sitting visibly lower than the other four tabs), plus a request to switch to Lucide icons — the same set web's `packages/ui` already uses via `lucide-react` — for cross-platform consistency, with 24×24pt icon sizing.
- **Root-caused before touching code**: the misalignment traced to `@expo/vector-icons`' Feather icon FONT having inconsistent internal glyph vertical-centering per icon — a well-known icon-font characteristic, not a layout bug in `FloatingTabBar`/`TabBarIcon` themselves. Confirmed the fix would land as a side effect of the requested Lucide migration (SVG icons render a uniform, predictable bounding box) before committing to the full migration, rather than patching Feather directly.
- **Full migration across every icon usage in the repo**: `TabBarIcon` now takes an icon COMPONENT reference (`icon={Home}`) instead of a string name — more type-safe (a typo is a build error, not a silently-blank icon) and removes the need for a separate icon-name union type. Migrated `apps/design-system-native`'s theme toggle (`Sun`/`Moon`/`Monitor`), search buttons (`Search`), and both tab-bar doc screens' demos, plus `apps/mobile`'s real tab bar (`House`/`Briefcase`/`DollarSign`/`User`). `@expo/vector-icons` removed entirely from all three `package.json`s (confirmed via a repo-wide grep before considering it done); `lucide-react-native` + its `react-native-svg` peer added as direct dependencies wherever an icon is actually rendered.
- **A real, meaningful bundle-size regression found and fixed before landing**: the natural barrel import (`import { Home } from "lucide-react-native"`) pulls in the ENTIRE 1892-icon set regardless of which few are used — confirmed directly in a compiled bundle (1892 `"Lucide*"` name references present) and its real cost (`apps/design-system-native`'s web bundle went 1.4MB → 2.9MB). Switched every import to Lucide's per-icon subpath form (`import House from "lucide-react-native/icons/house"`), which tree-shakes correctly — confirmed the same bundle dropped to ~1MB afterward (below the pre-migration Feather baseline) with only the actually-used icon names present.
- **A separate, unrelated Jest infrastructure bug found and fixed while running tests post-migration**: `packages/ui-native`'s test suite couldn't `require()` `lucide-react-native` at all (`SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'`) — `@react-native/jest-preset`'s `customExportConditions = ['require', 'react-native']` matched Lucide's `"react-native"` export condition (an ESM-only build) before its `"require"` condition (CJS), and Jest's CJS runtime can't load ESM. Fixed by overriding `testEnvironmentOptions.customExportConditions: ["require"]` in `packages/ui-native/jest.config.js` — scoped to Jest's own resolution only; confirmed Metro (the real bundler) is unaffected and still correctly resolves the `"react-native"` condition for actual builds.
- **Verified the alignment fix with a real measurement, not just a screenshot**: a headless-browser `getBoundingClientRect()` check on all 5 tabs' icons showed identical `top` (529px) and `height` (24px) values after the migration.
- Verified beyond that: full workspace `typecheck`/`lint`/`test` clean (12/12/11/11/10/10, 18 `ui-native` tests); real `expo export` bundles for both `apps/mobile` (iOS) and `apps/design-system-native` (web) succeed and are smaller than their pre-migration baselines.
- **CLAUDE.md updated** with the full icon-library rule (per-icon subpath imports required, canonical vs. alias icon names, the bundle-size trap, the Jest config fix) so this doesn't get silently reverted to a barrel import or re-broken by a future icon-library swap.
- Stories: `packages/ui-native` component fix/migration — no PRD story of its own.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (`packages/ui-native` foundational stage).

### 2026-08-30 — `FloatingTabBar` now matches iOS's real `UITabBar` spec and animates a sliding selection highlight (user request)

- **User request, a fourth round following the entry below**: match iOS's actual tab bar spec (height, icon size, label font size) rather than the earlier arbitrary sizing, and make the active-tab highlight slide between tabs on selection instead of instantly swapping, "like iOS".
- **Sizing researched, not guessed**: confirmed iOS's stock `UITabBar`/`UITabBarItem` defaults (49pt content height — excludes the home-indicator safe-area inset, still added separately via `insets.bottom`; 25×25pt icons; 10pt labels) via web search cross-checked against known values, since this is a long-stable, well-documented spec. Replaced the earlier 22px icon/11px label guesses with named constants (`TAB_BAR_HEIGHT`, `TAB_ICON_SIZE`, `TAB_LABEL_FONT_SIZE`); `FLOATING_TAB_BAR_RESERVED_HEIGHT` is now derived from `TAB_BAR_HEIGHT` instead of a separate hardcoded number.
- **Sliding highlight, replacing each tab's own instant background toggle**: a single `Animated.View` capsule positioned via `Animated.Value`s for `x`/`width`, measured per-tab through `onLayout` (stored in a `useRef` map, since layout callbacks are async and can resolve in any order) and animated with `Animated.spring` whenever `state.index` changes. The very first measurement (initial mount) is special-cased to `setValue` directly rather than animating, since animating from an `Animated.Value`'s unset default of 0 would otherwise visibly slide the highlight in from the top-left corner on first paint. Uses `useNativeDriver: false` since `left`/`width` aren't in the native-driver's supported style-property allowlist (only transforms/opacity are) — an accepted tradeoff for a single infrequent transition, not a high-frequency animation.
- **Verified the animation is real, not just present in code**: a headless-browser screenshot captured ~80ms into a Home→Messages tap (a non-adjacent tab, to make any snap-vs-slide difference obvious) shows the highlight genuinely mid-flight over an intermediate tab while the destination tab's color/content had already updated — confirmed against before/mid-animation/settled screenshots, not just a single before/after pair that could hide an instant-snap bug.
- Verified beyond that: full workspace `typecheck`/`lint`/`test` clean (12/12/11/11/10/10, 18 `ui-native` tests — the color-resolution test was rewritten to check the color passed into each tab's `tabBarIcon` rather than a `Pressable`'s own background style, since the highlight is no longer part of any individual tab's style and `onLayout` doesn't fire under `react-test-renderer`'s fake layout engine); real `expo export --platform ios` for `apps/mobile` bundles successfully.
- **CLAUDE.md updated** with the exact iOS spec numbers/sources and the sliding-highlight implementation notes (why `useNativeDriver: false`, why the first-measurement special case exists).
- Stories: `packages/ui-native` component refinement — no PRD story of its own.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (`packages/ui-native` foundational stage).

### 2026-08-30 — `FloatingTabBar`: a fully custom, from-scratch bottom tab bar in `packages/ui-native`, refined through three rounds of screenshot-driven feedback (user request)

- **User request, following the themed-tab-bar entry below**: a screenshot of GitHub's iOS app — a floating, rounded, inset pill tab bar (not full-width/flush with the screen edge), asking for the same look, explicitly to be kept as part of `@spine/ui-native`. Confirmed scope first: this needed React Navigation's `tabBar` prop (a full replacement of the default tab bar), not just theming it — a materially bigger component than `spineTabBarScreenOptions`, since it takes over everything the native tab bar normally provides for free (safe-area insets, active-state detection, press handling, accessibility roles).
- **New `packages/ui-native/src/navigation/floating-tab-bar.tsx`**: `FloatingTabBar` (a floating rounded-pill container, active tab shown in a soft highlight capsule) and `FLOATING_TAB_BAR_RESERVED_HEIGHT` (since the bar is `position: absolute` and floats over content, every screen needs matching bottom padding or its last row hides behind the bar). `apps/mobile`'s `Tab.Navigator` wired to it via the `tabBar` prop, with `useSafeAreaInsets()` feeding `sceneStyle`'s padding. Shipped with a "Floating Tab Bar" doc screen (a live embedded demo, reusing the `NavigationIndependentTree` pattern from the entry below) and a regression test (`floating-tab-bar.test.tsx`: focused-tab selection state, tap-to-navigate, light/dark color resolution).
- **Round 1 — layout correction from an explicit screenshot re-check**: the first version showed the label only on the active tab in a horizontal icon-then-label row; the reference screenshot showed icon stacked above label on EVERY tab. Fixed, and `FLOATING_TAB_BAR_RESERVED_HEIGHT` bumped 64→76 to fit the taller stacked layout.
- **Round 2 — two more user-reported visual bugs from a second screenshot**: (1) the pill used `rounded-3xl` (a large but fixed radius), which reads as a rounded rectangle, not a true pill — fixed to `rounded-full`. (2) A visible white area appeared behind the floating bar specifically in the doc-screen demos — root-caused to the demo's own preview box having no background color (its rounded corners revealed the page's white background underneath) AND the demo's `NavigationContainer` never receiving a `theme` prop (the same class of bug as the original nav-header fix, recurring because each live-demo doc screen owns a separate `NavigationContainer` from `RootNavigator`'s) — fixed in both `tab-bar.tsx` and `floating-tab-bar.tsx`'s demos. Also added `pointerEvents="box-none"` to the tab bar's outer wrapper, found while re-reviewing the component for the pill fix (the transparent padding around the pill was capturing touches meant for content behind it) — not separately reported, but a real correctness bug worth fixing in the same pass.
- **Round 3 — a third screenshot showed the active-tab highlight capsule wasn't a true pill either**: `rounded-2xl` (a small fixed 16px radius) on an item roughly 65px tall reads as a rounded rectangle, most visible on the rightmost tab where its corner meets the outer pill's own curve. Fixed to `rounded-full`, matching the outer container. Also expanded both live demos from 3 to 5 tabs (Home/Jobs/Expenses/Messages/Profile) per explicit request, to exercise the layout with a more realistic tab count.
- **Every round verified visually, not just by reading the diff**: live headless-browser (Playwright) checks after each fix, including an actual screenshot comparison against the reference for rounds 2 and 3, confirming the pill shape, capsule shape, background, and 5-tab layout all render correctly in both light and dark mode before considering each round done.
- Verified beyond that: full workspace `typecheck`/`lint`/`test` clean (12/12/11/11/10/10, 18 `ui-native` tests) after every round; a real `expo export --platform ios` for `apps/mobile` and `--platform web` for `apps/design-system-native` both bundle successfully with the final version.
- **CLAUDE.md updated** with the final component shape and all three correction rounds, so a future contributor touching this component understands why `rounded-full` (not a fixed-radius class) is required on both the outer pill and the inner highlight, and why the doc-demo `NavigationContainer`/preview-box pattern must always include a theme + background.
- Stories: `packages/ui-native` component addition — no PRD story of its own.

- **User request**: "I want to have a customised bottom nav bar... Fixed with `NavigationIndependentTree` (React Navigation's own supported mechanism for a self-contained nested tree, re-exported from `@react-navigation/native`) wrapping the demo's own `NavigationContainer` — confirmed working on both layouts afterward, including actually clicking between the demo's tabs, not just that it renders.

### 2026-08-30 — `navigation-theme.ts` moved into `packages/ui-native`; `apps/mobile`'s bottom-tab bar gets the same dark-mode fix proactively (user-prompted audit)

- **User question, not a bug report this time**: "what about components like top bar, bottom navbar etc?" — prompted an audit of what `apps/mobile` actually uses from `@spine/ui-native` vs. hand-rolled navigation chrome. Answer: React Navigation's own bottom-tab bar and (potential future) headers are NOT `@spine/ui-native` components and were never meant to be — they're native chrome rendered by React Navigation itself, themed via its own `theme` prop mechanism, the same category as the nav-header bug fixed for `apps/design-system-native` two entries below.
- **Found the identical gap already present in `apps/mobile`, just latent**: its `NavigationContainer` (wrapping the bottom-tab bar) never passed a `theme` prop either — no visible bug yet only because `apps/mobile` has no dark-mode toggle UI shipped, but the exact same "tab bar stays light in dark mode" bug was waiting to happen the moment one did.
- **Fix, done proactively rather than waiting for it to ship as a bug report**: moved `spineLightNavigationTheme`/`spineDarkNavigationTheme` out of `apps/design-system-native` (where they were app-local) into `packages/ui-native/src/navigation/navigation-theme.ts` — since they're a pure function of the shared `lightColors`/`darkColors` tokens with zero app-specific logic, there was no reason for `apps/mobile` to duplicate them. Exported via a new `@spine/ui-native/navigation` subpath (matching the existing `./tokens` pattern), with `@react-navigation/native` added as an **optional peer dependency** of `packages/ui-native` (not a hard dependency, so apps that don't use React Navigation aren't forced to install it). Both `apps/design-system-native/src/navigation/root-navigator.tsx` and `apps/mobile/src/navigation/root-navigator.tsx` now import from the shared location and pass `theme={resolvedMode === "dark" ? spineDarkNavigationTheme : spineLightNavigationTheme}` to their respective `NavigationContainer`s.
- Verified beyond typecheck/lint/test (all clean, 12/12/11/11/10/10): a real `expo export --platform web` for `apps/design-system-native` and a real `expo export --platform ios` for `apps/mobile` (1498 modules) both bundle successfully with the new shared subpath import.
- **CLAUDE.md updated** to describe the shared location and the optional-peer-dependency choice, and to note this was fixed proactively in `apps/mobile` before it had a visible toggle to expose the bug.
- Stories: infrastructure/refactor — no PRD story of its own; prevents a bug from shipping twice in the same codebase.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (tooling, alongside the `packages/ui-native` foundational stage).

### 2026-08-30 — Two more real theming bugs found via live headless-browser testing: nav header stayed light in dark mode, and "system" never tracked the real OS/browser preference (user-reported)

- **User reports, two items with a screenshot**: (1) on mobile, the top nav header bar stayed light while the rest of the screen was correctly dark; (2) in the web browser, switching to "system" didn't pick up the real OS/browser dark preference.
- **Bug 1 — nav header ignores the app's theme entirely**: React Navigation's native-stack header isn't a NativeWind-styled component at all — it's rendered by React Navigation itself, outside the className-based component tree, and only reacts to `NavigationContainer`'s `theme` prop, which `RootNavigator` never passed (so it silently used React Navigation's own generic light `DefaultTheme`, unrelated to this app's tokens, regardless of the app's actual dark/light state). Fixed with new `src/navigation/navigation-theme.ts` (`spineLightNavigationTheme`/`spineDarkNavigationTheme`, built from `lightColors`/`darkColors`), selected in `RootNavigator` via `useTheme().resolvedMode`.
- **Bug 2 — a genuine upstream bug in the installed `react-native-css-interop@0.2.6`, root-caused by reading its actual source**: on web, `colorScheme.set("system")` never checks `prefers-color-scheme` at all — its only special case is `value === "dark"`; every other value (including `"system"`) falls into an unconditional `classList.remove(...)`, i.e. "system" always resolves to light on web regardless of the real preference. Reproduced live (not just read in source) with a headless-browser test forcing `prefers-color-scheme: dark`: the app stayed in light mode. Fixed with a web-only workaround in `packages/ui-native/src/theme/theme-provider.tsx`: an `applyPreference` helper that, for `"system"` on `Platform.OS === "web"`, resolves `window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)")` directly and calls `.set("dark" | "light")` — never `.set("system")` on web — with a live `matchMedia` `change` listener (ref-tracked, cleaned up on every preference change to avoid a listener leak from repeated toggling) so an OS-level switch while parked on "system" is still picked up live. Native keeps calling `.set("system")` directly (unaffected by this specific bug).
- **A second, subtler part of bug 2 found only by testing the fresh-boot case separately from the explicit-toggle case**: the original code only ever called `nativeWindColorScheme.set(...)` when `storage.getPreference()` resolved a STORED value — a brand-new session (no stored preference, the common case) fell back to NativeWind's own default resolution for "system", which hits the exact same bug. Fixed by applying the effective preference (`stored ?? "system"`) unconditionally at boot, not only when a stored value exists.
- **Verified with real headless-browser (Playwright) tests, not just re-reading the fix**, covering every combination: fresh page load with the browser set to dark (previously stuck light, now correctly dark); explicit cycle back to "system" with the browser set to light (correctly light); the same cycle with the browser set to dark (correctly dark); and a live OS-preference-change simulation while parked on "system" (correctly re-applies without a reload). Full workspace `typecheck`/`lint`/`test` (12/12, 11/11, 10/10) all pass.
- **CLAUDE.md updated** with both root causes and fixes as standing rules — the React Navigation header point applies to any future screen/navigator this app or `apps/mobile` adds, and the `colorScheme.set("system")` bug is a trap for any future direct use of `nativewind`'s `colorScheme` API on web.
- Stories: bug fixes in `packages/ui-native`/`apps/design-system-native` theming — no PRD story of their own.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (tooling, alongside the `packages/ui-native` foundational stage).

- **User report, following up on the entry immediately below**: after the dark-mode CSS fix landed, the toggle still looked broken — pressing it to what the user expected to be dark mode didn't visibly do anything. Investigated live (not just re-reading the fix) with a real headless-browser (Playwright) run against a freshly started dev server: clicking through the toggle DID correctly flip every color to the right dark values (`.dark` class toggled on `<html>`, `bg-background` genuinely resolved to the dark token's `rgb(18, 17, 16)`) — the CSS/runtime fix from the entry below is confirmed genuinely working, not still broken.

A user pressing the toggle and reasoning about state from the icon shown would end up on the wrong actual preference relative to what they intended, making a correctly-working toggle look broken.
- **Fix**: corrected the map to `light: "sun"`, `dark: "moon"`, `system: "monitor"` — icon now reflects the CURRENT preference (not the state you'd switch to), matching normal theme-toggle icon conventions.
