### 2026-08-30 — Fixed a third, deeper shipped bug: the light/dark/system theme toggle never actually changed anything (user-reported)

- **User report**: "the dark/light/system toggle does not work" — a third bug found in the same theming investigation chain as the two entries immediately below, and the deepest one: this wasn't a single-component fix, it was a repo-wide latent bug.
- **Root cause, chased to the actual compiler behavior, not assumed**: every `packages/ui-native` themed color (`bg-surface`, `text-on-surface`, etc.) was registered in both `apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js` and `apps/design-system-native/tailwind.config.js` via a `{ DEFAULT: light, dark: darkValue }` color-object shape. This is NOT a real Tailwind convention — `DEFAULT`/`50`/`100`/.../`900` are the only color-object shapes Tailwind's flattening recognizes, so the `dark` sub-key was silently ignored and every color compiled to one fixed light-mode value. Confirmed directly (not inferred): a real `expo export --platform web` bundle's compiled CSS had ZERO `.dark` selectors anywhere. The runtime toggle mechanism itself (`nativewind`'s `colorScheme.set(...)`, `theme-provider.tsx`) was correctly flipping the `dark` class on `document.documentElement` the whole time — there was just no dark-mode CSS for that class to switch anything to. This bug predates all of today's work and affects `apps/mobile` too, just never noticed there since that app has no theme-toggle UI wired to any screen yet.
- **Fix, verified working before rolling out broadly**: rewrote both `tailwind.config.js` files with `flatColors`/`flatDarkColors` helpers that register every color TWICE — once under its plain name (light value), once under `<name>-dark` (dark value) — then paired every themed utility class across every touched file with an explicit `dark:<name>-dark` variant of the same base name (`bg-surface dark:bg-surface-dark`, including on `active:`-prefixed classes: `active:bg-surface-sunken active:dark:bg-surface-sunken-dark`, confirmed this exact stacking order compiles correctly). Verified the mechanism in isolation first (one class, one component, one real bundle export showing a genuine `.dark\:bg-background-dark:is(.dark *){...}` rule with the correct color) before committing to the full rollout.
- **Full rollout across the whole `packages/ui-native` surface plus every consumer**, executed as one large, systematic pass: `packages/ui-native/src/components/{button,text-field,card,badge}.tsx` (all themed classes in `cva` variants and plain classNames); every file authored for `apps/design-system-native`'s desktop shell/search palette/doc-page primitives (`desktop-shell.tsx`, `desktop-sidebar.tsx`, `desktop-top-bar.tsx`, `doc-page.tsx`, `component-preview.tsx`, `search-palette.tsx`, `doc-section.tsx`, `home.tsx`, `root-navigator.tsx`'s `SearchButton`, plus two inline classes found on `app/components/card.tsx`'s raw example `<Text>`); and every existing themed class in `apps/mobile/src/features/auth/login-screen.tsx`, `apps/mobile/src/features/home/home-screen.tsx`, and `apps/mobile/src/navigation/root-navigator.tsx`'s loading state. Deliberately left untouched: `code-block.tsx` (permanently-dark code-block chrome, same "always dark" pattern as web's Toast/Tooltip — intentionally theme-invariant) and `theme-toggle.tsx`'s icon color (already correctly resolved via `useColorScheme()` in JS, since `Feather`'s `color` prop takes a raw value, not a className — a different, already-correct pattern from the `dark:` className one).
- **A known residual gap, documented rather than silently left**: `TextField`'s `placeholderTextColor="#726C5A"` is a native RN prop, not a NativeWind className — this pattern doesn't cover it, so placeholder text stays light-mode-colored in dark mode too. Same class of gap as the loading-spinner bug in the entry below (a raw color prop that needs its own `useColorScheme()`-driven resolution), not yet fixed — noted in CLAUDE.md as a known follow-up.
- Verified beyond a component-level check: full workspace `typecheck`/`lint`/`test` (12/12, 11/11, 10/10) all pass; re-confirmed independently (not just trusting the rollout's own report) by re-inspecting a fresh `expo export --platform web` bundle myself — real `.dark`-scoped rules exist for every token (`bg-surface-dark`, `bg-background-dark`, `text-on-surface-muted-dark`, `border-border-strong-dark`, `active:dark:bg-primary-hover-dark`, etc.), each with the correct dark color value; also re-verified `tailwind-merge`'s dedupe (the fix from the disabled-text bug two entries below) still works correctly now that `dark:` pairs exist — `dark:` and plain classes are tracked as separate conflict groups, so pairing didn't reintroduce that earlier bug.
- **CLAUDE.md updated** with a full standing rule (the exact broken shape to never use again, the exact correct pattern including the `active:dark:` stacking detail, and an explicit callout that there is no automated check for a missing `dark:` pair — unlike the a11y-coverage script, this is a discipline rule that must be applied by hand on every new themed class).
- Stories: bug fix in `packages/ui-native` foundational work — no PRD story of its own.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (`packages/ui-native` foundational stage).

### 2026-08-30 — Fixed a second, related shipped bug: Button's loading spinner was invisible too (user-reported)

- **User report**: "The loading is not visible properly in the button" — a direct follow-on to the disabled-text fix immediately below. `<Button loading>` (default `primary`/`danger` variant) rendered a white `ActivityIndicator` against the button's own now-transparent disabled-look background, invisible in light mode.
- **Same root cause as the disabled-text bug, missed the first time**: `loading` sets `isDisabled` internally, which correctly makes `buttonVariants` apply the disabled look (`bg-transparent`) regardless of variant — but the `ActivityIndicator`'s `color` prop was still hardcoded to `#FFFFFF` for `primary`/`danger`, a leftover from before that background became transparent. The earlier fix addressed the reported disabled-TEXT symptom but didn't re-derive the spinner's color, which depends on the exact same `isDisabled`-driven background change.
- **Fix**: spinner color now resolves from `nativewind`'s `useColorScheme()` against `lightColors.onSurfaceMuted`/`darkColors.onSurfaceMuted` (`packages/ui-native/src/tokens`) — the same color the disabled label text uses — instead of a variant-conditioned hardcoded hex, for every variant.
- **Regression test added and verified to actually catch the bug**, same discipline as the disabled-text fix: `button.a11y.test.tsx` gained a test asserting the rendered `ActivityIndicator`'s `color` prop is `lightColors.onSurfaceMuted` and never `#FFFFFF`, confirmed to fail (reproducing the exact reported symptom) when the color-resolution change is reverted, before shipping.
- **CLAUDE.md updated** with the general lesson: when a prop changes visual state via a shared flag like `isDisabled`, audit every other prop/element whose value was computed assuming the OLD state, not just the one originally reported — a partial fix can leave a sibling bug from the same root cause.
- Verified beyond the new test: full workspace `typecheck`/`lint`/`test` (12/12, 11/11, 10/10) all pass; a real `expo export --platform web` bundle still builds successfully.
- Stories: bug fix in `packages/ui-native` foundational work — no PRD story of its own.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (`packages/ui-native` foundational stage).

### 2026-08-30 — Fixed a real, shipped bug: Button's disabled label text was invisible on web (user-reported)

- **User report**: "The disabled button text is not visible" — reproduced on `apps/design-system-native`'s Button doc screen, `<Button disabled>` (default `primary` variant) rendered white text (`text-white`, from the variant) on its disabled transparent background instead of the intended `text-on-surface-muted`.
- **Root cause, chased past an initial wrong fix**: `packages/ui-native/src/components/button.tsx` modeled `disabled` as an independent `cva` boolean variant (`buttonVariants`/`textVariants` each concatenating a variant class like `text-white` and a disabled-override class like `text-on-surface-muted` for the SAME CSS property). `packages/ui`'s own Button avoids this exact conflict on web via Tailwind's `disabled:` pseudo-class — real elevated selector specificity that wins regardless of source order — but NativeWind has no `:disabled` pseudo-class equivalent for `Pressable`, so both classes here were plain same-specificity utilities. Confirmed (not assumed) that cva's own class-string order does NOT decide the winner: an initial fix attempt using `compoundVariants` still produces the same string-order shape and was rejected once traced through `cva`'s actual source (`cx(base, variantClasses, compoundVariantClasses, ...)`) — the real decider is Tailwind's CSS-discovery order at build time, which is why the same source code could look fine in one build and break in another.
- **Real fix**: added `tailwind-merge`/`clsx` as dependencies (mirroring `packages/ui`'s own `cn` helper, which `packages/ui-native` didn't have until now) and a matching `src/lib/cn.ts`. Both `buttonVariants(...)` and `textVariants(...)` calls in `button.tsx` are now wrapped in `cn(...)`, which deterministically dedupes conflicting same-property classes by keeping the later one — verified directly against the installed `tailwind-merge` (`bg-primary ... bg-transparent` → keeps `bg-transparent`; `text-white text-on-surface-muted` → keeps `text-on-surface-muted`), not just inferred from documentation.
- **Regression test added and verified to actually catch the bug**: `button.a11y.test.tsx` gained a test asserting every variant's disabled label className contains `text-on-surface-muted` and never matches `text-white` — confirmed it fails (reproducing the exact reported symptom) when the `cn(...)` wrapping is reverted, and passes with the fix restored, before shipping either the test or the fix alone.
- **CLAUDE.md updated** with a standing rule: any `packages/ui-native` component composing two independently-conditioned class sets touching the same CSS property (a variant axis + a disabled/error/etc. axis) must route the final className through `cn`, never `cva`'s raw output or manual string/array concatenation — audited `text-field.tsx`/`card.tsx`/`badge.tsx` for the same pattern and confirmed none of them have it (`TextField`'s `error` ternary only ever includes one of its two border classes, never both).
- Verified beyond the new test: full workspace `typecheck`/`lint`/`test` (12/12, 11/11, 10/10 including all 29 `apps/e2e` tests) all pass; a real `expo export --platform web` bundle confirms the compiled output carries `text-on-surface-muted` on the disabled label.
- Stories: bug fix in `packages/ui-native` foundational work — no PRD story of its own.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (`packages/ui-native` foundational stage).

### 2026-08-30 — `apps/design-system-native` gains a search palette and an icon-based theme toggle; fixed a NativeWind sidebar-width bug (user feedback)

- **User feedback, two items**: (1) the desktop sidebar rendered full-width instead of the intended 224px; (2) the app was missing `apps/design-system`'s search (⌘K palette) and Sun/Moon icon theme toggle.
- **Sidebar width bug, root-caused not just patched**: inspected a real `expo export --platform web` bundle's compiled CSS and confirmed `w-56`/`shrink-0` never appeared in the output at all — NativeWind was silently dropping those width/flex classNames on `ScrollView` specifically for web. Fixed with an explicit inline `style={{ width: 224, flexGrow: 0, flexShrink: 0 }}` on `desktop-sidebar.tsx`'s `ScrollView`, with a comment warning not to revert it to a className.
- **`@expo/vector-icons` added** (bundled with Expo SDKs, but needed as an explicit direct dependency for pnpm to link it) — the icon library for both the theme toggle and the new search button, since no icon library existed anywhere in the repo yet.

- **Search palette** (`src/components/search-palette.tsx`): re-implements `apps/design-system`'s `SearchPalette` UX — type-to-filter over the same `component-registry.ts` list, select to jump — using RN's `Modal`/`TextInput`/`FlatList`, since `cmdk` (what web uses) is DOM-only. Wired into both shells: `desktop-top-bar.tsx` gained a Search button (with a `⌘K` hint shown only on `Platform.OS === "web"`) that `desktop-shell.tsx` opens and resolves against its own selection state; `root-navigator.tsx` gained a matching `SearchButton` in the stack's `headerRight` for the mobile shell, navigating via `navigation.navigate("Component", { slug })` on select. Cmd/Ctrl+K global capture is wired via a web-only `document.addEventListener` inside `SearchPalette` itself — native has no equivalent hardware-keyboard convention, so native users open it via the button only.
- Verified beyond typecheck/lint (both clean across the whole workspace, 12/12 and 11/11): a real `expo export --platform web` bundle succeeds (647 modules, 1.3MB — up from 553/838KB, the increase being `@expo/vector-icons`' bundled icon-font assets), and the sidebar's fixed inline width is present in the compiled bundle.

### 2026-08-30 — Phase 5 (Mobile) Stage 4: Auth (S-11.1) — and a real design correction to the mobile auth mechanism

- **Login, session persistence, and sign-out are wired end-to-end**: `apps/mobile/src/lib/auth/auth-client.ts` (Better Auth's `expoClient` from `@better-auth/expo`, pinned to `1.6.26` to exactly match `apps/api`'s resolved `better-auth` version — the two packages' versions track 1:1, confirmed against npm before picking one), a new `LoginScreen` (`src/features/auth/login-screen.tsx`, built from `@spine/ui-native`'s `TextField`/`Button`), and `RootNavigator` now branches on `useSession()` — no session renders `LoginScreen`, a session renders the existing tab shell, `isPending` (the brief window while `expoClient` restores a persisted session from `expo-secure-store` on cold start) shows a spinner so a returning user never flashes the login screen. `ProfileScreen` gained a real sign-out.
- **A real architecture gap found and corrected, not a peripheral bug**: the Phase 5 plan (and the PRD's own §5 "JWT for mobile" phrasing) assumed minting a `jwt()`-plugin JWT and sending it as `Authorization: Bearer` would authenticate API requests. It doesn't — `@thallesp/nestjs-better-auth`'s `AuthGuard` forwards request headers into `auth.api.getSession(...)`, which only ever resolves a session via a cookie or (with Better Auth's separate `bearer()` plugin) a session token sent as a Bearer header; it never verifies a `jwt()`-minted JWT at all. Discovered via a live 401 against a real protected endpoint (`GET /org/members/me/capabilities`), not a typecheck — confirmed by reading `@thallesp/nestjs-better-auth`'s actual guard source before concluding this wasn't a config mistake on this repo's side.
  - **Fix**: added Better Auth's `bearer()` plugin to `apps/api/src/auth/auth.ts` — the standard "send the session over a header instead of a cookie" mechanism, exactly RN's situation (no cookie jar). Mobile's `@spine/sdk`-backed `api-client.ts` now sends the session token directly as Bearer (`src/lib/auth/token.ts`'s `getSessionToken()`) instead of a separate minted-JWT round trip; `jwt()`/`jwtClient()` stay configured/available for a possible future third-party/external JWKS-verification need, but are no longer part of mobile's own request-authentication path. `token.ts`'s old JWT-caching/refresh logic is gone entirely — the session token needs no separate expiry tracking (the session itself is the 30-day/7-day-refresh lifetime from Stage 1's session-config entry), so there's no minting round trip left to cache.
  - **The extraction detail was verified empirically, not assumed**: `expoClient` only exposes the session via `getCookie()` (a `name=value; ...` cookie-string reconstruction, meant for a `Cookie:` header), not a bare-token accessor — `getSessionToken()` regex-extracts the `session_token` cookie's value from it. Two non-obvious facts about that value were confirmed against a real running instance before shipping: (1) it's Better Auth's SIGNED cookie form (`<token>.<hmac-signature>`), captured directly from a live sign-up's actual `Set-Cookie` header rather than assumed, and confirmed the `bearer()` plugin's own signature-verification branch accepts that signed form directly; (2) `@better-auth/expo`'s cookie parsing already URL-decodes the value before storing it, confirmed by loading its real `parseSetCookieHeader` function against that captured header in a throwaway Node script — so no extra decoding step was needed in `getSessionToken()`. A curl round trip (sign up → capture the raw cookie → send that exact value as Bearer → 200 with real capability data) is the actual proof this works, run against `apps/api`'s live instance, not inferred from documentation.
- **A pnpm-monorepo TS friction, isolated and documented, not worked around silently**: `@better-auth/expo` and `apps/mobile`'s own `better-auth` resolve to the exact same version (1.6.26, confirmed) but as two structurally-distinct pnpm-isolated package instances, which breaks TypeScript's generic inference across the Better Auth plugin array (`Cannot find name` / generic-unification errors that don't reflect any real behavioral mismatch — both instances resolve identical `@better-fetch/fetch@1.3.1` too, checked before reaching for a cast). Fixed with a narrow, explicitly-commented `as BetterAuthClientPlugin` widening cast at the one point it's needed (`expoClient(...)` in the plugins array), plus one downstream `useSession()` consumer typing the specific fields it reads by hand, rather than chasing pnpm's resolution graph further or fighting the type system with broader casts.
- Verified beyond typecheck: real Metro bundle exports for both platforms succeeded post-auth-integration (1492 modules, 4MB Hermes bytecode — up from 1213/2.9MB pre-auth); the corrected Bearer-auth mechanism proven end-to-end against `apps/api`'s live instance (sign-up → session token → authenticated request → 200 with real data; an unauthenticated request to the same endpoint still correctly 401s); full `apps/api` integration suite re-run twice post-`bearer()` to confirm the new plugin introduces no regressions (failures present both times are the same already-documented pre-existing parallel-run flakiness — a different random subset of unrelated files each run, not `bearer()`/auth-clustered).
- Stories: S-11.1 ("log in once, stay logged in").
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (Auth stage).

### 2026-08-30 — Phase 5 (Mobile) Stage 3: `packages/ui-native` foundational components, NativeWind theming

- **`packages/ui-native`** — the native component library, mirroring `@spine/ui`'s discipline (per-component `.a11y.test.tsx`, an enforced coverage-check script) with RN-appropriate substitutions rather than a literal port. Four foundational components shipped: `Button`, `TextField`, `Card` (+`CardHeader`/`CardTitle`/`CardDescription`/`CardContent`/`CardFooter`), `Badge` — all styled via NativeWind `className`, not `StyleSheet`, and built on RN primitives (`Pressable`/`TextInput`/`View`/`Text`) rather than trying to reuse `@spine/ui`'s Radix-based components, which are DOM-only.
- **Tokens ported from `docs/DESIGN.md`/`packages/config/tailwind-preset.css`** into `src/tokens/{colors,spacing,typography}.ts` — plain TS objects (light/dark color palettes, radius, spacing, a type scale), not CSS custom properties, since React Native has no CSS custom-property support at all; kept in sync by hand with the web tokens, documented explicitly as such in the token files' own comments.
- **Light/dark/system theming — the Phase 5 plan's own required (not optional) piece**: `src/theme/theme-provider.tsx` wraps NativeWind v4's native `colorScheme.set("light" | "dark" | "system")` API, which already implements the exact three-state precedence web's `next-themes` uses (explicit choice wins, else OS preference) — no custom precedence logic needed, just a thin persistence layer. Storage-agnostic via an injected `ThemeStorage` interface; `apps/mobile/src/lib/theme-storage.ts` supplies the real `expo-secure-store`-backed implementation (reusing the same storage mechanism the auth flow will use, rather than adding AsyncStorage as a second dependency for one small value).
- **Accessibility testing without axe-core**: React Native has no DOM, so `packages/ui`'s axe-core-based `expectNoA11yViolations` can't be ported literally. `src/test/a11y.ts`'s `expectAccessibleRole`/`expectAccessibilityState` assert against RN's own `accessibilityRole`/`accessibilityLabel`/`accessibilityState` props instead — the two failure modes an actual screen reader user would hit that a plain render-and-snapshot test wouldn't catch. `scripts/check-a11y-coverage.mjs` ports `packages/ui`'s same enforced-coverage script (fails if any `src/components/*.tsx` lacks a matching `*.a11y.test.tsx`), wired into `packages/ui-native`'s own `test` script.
- **A real, reproduced bug caught and fixed while building the a11y test helper itself**: `expectAccessibleRole`'s first version imported `Text` from `"react-native"` and compared `node.type === Text` to find a button's nested label — this silently failed in one specific test (but not others, and not in a standalone debug script) because Jest's module registry resolved `Text` to a different module instance in `src/test/a11y.ts` than in `src/components/button.tsx`, despite both importing from the same package. Root-caused by dumping `findAll()` output during debugging (confirmed the actual `Text` node with the right content was present in the tree — the identity comparison was the bug, not the render). Fixed by matching on the component's `displayName`/`name` string instead of a reference comparison, which has no such module-identity dependency.
- **NativeWind wired into `apps/mobile`**: `babel.config.js` (`babel-preset-expo` + `nativewind/babel`, `jsxImportSource: "nativewind"`), `metro.config.js` (`withNativeWind`, plus monorepo `watchFolders`/`nodeModulesPaths` wiring so Metro picks up changes in workspace packages), `tailwind.config.js` (imports `@spine/ui-native/tokens` directly rather than duplicating the palette a second time, `darkMode: "class"` — NativeWind's own dark-mode toggle mechanism, matching how `colorScheme.set(...)` flips it), `global.css`, and a `nativewind-env.d.ts` type-augmentation file (needed separately in the consuming app, not just the library — TypeScript project references don't propagate a dependency's own ambient `.d.ts` triple-slash references automatically).
- **Two real Metro/tooling gaps found and fixed while wiring this up, not just typechecked**: (1) an initial `metro.config.js` set `resolver.disableHierarchicalLookup: true` to scope monorepo module resolution — this broke resolving `react-native-css-interop` (NativeWind's own transitive dependency, present in pnpm's store but not hoisted to a flat `node_modules` entry), fixed by removing that setting and, since `apps/mobile` doesn't otherwise declare it, adding `react-native-css-interop` as an explicit direct dependency so Metro's normal resolution reaches it. (2) `packages/config/eslint.expo.config.js`'s first version (`[...expoConfig, ...tseslint-based-base]`) threw "Cannot redefine plugin '@typescript-eslint'" — `eslint-config-expo` already registers that plugin itself; fixed by composing via `eslint/config`'s `defineConfig` helper (matching how `eslint-config-expo`'s own config is built) and layering only this repo's one custom rule override on top, explicitly scoped to `files: ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx"]` so it never applies to plain `.js`/`.mjs` config files where the plugin isn't registered — a second real failure, caught by testing `eslint .` against `packages/ui-native`'s root config files directly, not just its `.tsx` source.
- `apps/mobile`'s Home screen now renders real `@spine/ui-native` components (`Card`/`Button`/`Badge`) against real tokens — a genuine integration proof, not just a component existing in isolation; S-11.2's actual data-backed home screen is still a later stage.
- **Verified beyond typecheck/lint**: real Metro bundle exports for both `--platform ios` and `--platform android` succeeded post-NativeWind-integration (1213 modules, 2.9MB Hermes bytecode each — up from 838 modules/1.9MB pre-NativeWind, confirming the whole token/theme/component chain is actually included and compiling, not just present in source). Full workspace `build`/`lint`/`typecheck`/`test` — including all 29 `apps/e2e` tests — passes clean.
- Stories: infrastructure underpinning all of S-11.1 → S-11.8; no PRD story of its own.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (`packages/ui-native` foundational stage).

### 2026-08-30 — Phase 5 (Mobile) Stage 2: `apps/mobile` scaffold, `packages/sdk`, and `packages/config`'s Expo preset

- **`apps/mobile`** — a real Expo (managed workflow, SDK 57) app, TypeScript, React 19/RN 0.86, matching the workspace's existing React version. Scaffolded via `create-expo-app`'s `blank-typescript` template then stripped of template-only files (`AGENTS.md`, its own `CLAUDE.md`, `LICENSE`, a `.claude/settings.json` enabling an unrelated plugin) that would otherwise conflict with or shadow this repo's own. Renamed to `@spine/mobile`, wired to `@spine/config`'s new presets (below) and `@spine/sdk` (workspace dependency).
- Bottom-tab navigation shell (`src/navigation/root-navigator.tsx`, React Navigation — native tabs + native stack, not a custom router) with four placeholder screens (Home / Jobs / Expenses / Profile, no Timesheet — matching the Phase 5 plan's own scoping against Jobber's tab set). `src/features/{home,jobs,expenses,profile}/` holds one screen file per tab; `src/lib/{auth,db,sync}/` created empty, ready for the next stages (auth, SQLite cache, outbox).
- Renamed the navigation directory from the template's default `src/app/` to `src/navigation/` — Expo Router auto-detects any `app/` directory by convention and was probing it as a router root (a harmless but confusing log line, "Using src/app as the root directory for Expo Router," since this app deliberately uses React Navigation, not Expo Router) — the rename removes the ambiguity rather than leaving a footgun for later.
- `app.json`: real branding (`Spine`, `com.spine.app` bundle id/package), `userInterfaceStyle: "automatic"` (respects OS light/dark on first launch, per the dark/light/system requirement design decision), `expo-secure-store` plugin pre-registered for the next stage's session-token storage.
- **`packages/config`** gained the two presets the Phase 5 plan called for: `tsconfig/expo` (Expo's own `tsconfig.base` compiler options inlined rather than `extends`-referenced — a cross-package `extends` pointing at a dependency `packages/config` itself doesn't have installed silently failed to resolve, breaking JSX/module settings for every consumer in a confusing way; inlining avoids that resolution hazard entirely) and `eslint/expo` (composes `eslint-config-expo`'s React/React Native/Hooks rules with this repo's existing shared base, rather than hand-rolling RN lint rules from scratch).
- **`packages/sdk`** — the typed client Stage 1's OpenAPI/Swagger work exists to feed. `pnpm generate` runs `openapi-typescript` against the live API's `/api/docs-json`, committing the generated `src/generated/openapi.d.ts` (172KB, regenerable, not hand-maintained) rather than gitignoring it, so the types are available without requiring a live API instance first. `src/client.ts` is a small hand-written fetch layer (not a generated request client — orval/openapi-fetch's heavier client wrappers were deliberately skipped, per the Stage 1 plan's own reasoning) mirroring `apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts`'s shape, with two changes for the mobile offline-outbox use case: `Authorization: Bearer` instead of a cookie, and a CALLER-SUPPLIED `Idempotency-Key` (the outbox generates one UUID at queue-time and reuses it across every replay, matching `idempotency.interceptor.ts`'s exact same-key-same-endpoint-replays contract) rather than one generated fresh per call.
- **Verified beyond typecheck/lint**: real Metro bundle exports for both `--platform ios` and `--platform android` succeeded (838 modules, 1.9MB Hermes bytecode each) — the strongest available proof the app actually boots in this sandboxed environment, since no iOS Simulator/Android emulator GUI was available to launch directly (simulator runtime profiles reported unavailable; no `emulator` binary present). Confirmed the `src/app` → `src/navigation` rename removed the Expo Router auto-detection log line on re-export. Also ran the FULL workspace `build`/`lint`/`typecheck`/`test` (including the `apps/e2e` Playwright suite, 29/29 passing) to confirm nothing else in the monorepo regressed — an initial run showed 29 e2e failures, traced to an unrelated `turbo run dev` process (from a separate terminal session, not started by this work) occupying the same ports e2e's own `webServer` tried to bind; re-ran clean once that process was stopped.
- A known, accepted peer-dependency warning: `apps/mobile`'s Expo-pinned `react@19.2.3` (an exact pin from the scaffold) vs. `react-dom@19.2.8`'s peer requirement (hoisted from web/design-system, which use a loose `^19.0.0` range) — cosmetic, since `apps/mobile` never touches `react-dom` at all (RN has no DOM), not worth forcing a version override that could fight Expo's own tightly-coupled React/RN compatibility contract.
- Next Phase 5 stage: `packages/ui-native` (foundational components — Button/TextField/Card/Badge — with NativeWind theming ported from `docs/DESIGN.md`, including the light/dark/system token resolution and the a11y-test + gallery-entry discipline, per the Phase 5 plan).
- Stories: infrastructure underpinning all of S-11.1 → S-11.8; no PRD story of its own.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (scaffold stage — `apps/mobile` now exists).

### 2026-08-30 — Phase 5 (Mobile) API prerequisite, part 3: OpenAPI/Swagger setup, and pinning the Better Auth session lifetime

- Added `@nestjs/swagger` (pinned to the `^11.x` line matching this repo's Nest v11 — the latest `12.x` release requires Nest v12 as a peer and produced real peer-dependency warnings on install; confirmed a compatible `11.4.7` exists before installing it instead). `apps/api/src/main.ts` now calls `SwaggerModule.createDocument`/`.setup("api/docs", ...)`, exposing both a browsable UI and a JSON doc at `/api/docs-json` — the input `packages/sdk` (a later Phase 5 stage) will generate typed clients from via `openapi-typescript`.
- **Deliberately not a retroactive documentation pass over the whole API** — per §5's own "two known clients, not a public API" REST rationale, DTOs are decorated incrementally, scoped to only the routes Phase 5's mobile app actually calls: `POST /jobs/:id/assignees`, `POST /jobs/:id/milestones/:milestoneId/complete`, `POST /jobs/:id/photos`, `POST /jobs/:id/notes`, `POST /quotes/:id/accept-in-person`, `POST /expenses`, `POST /files` (multipart, `@ApiConsumes`/`@ApiBody` with a binary-format schema). New `*.dto.ts` files per module (`jobs.dto.ts`, `quotes.dto.ts`, `expenses.dto.ts`) — plain classes with `@ApiProperty`/`@ApiPropertyOptional`, hand-kept in sync with their corresponding `packages/shared` zod schema field-for-field; every route's own zod-based runtime validation is completely unchanged, these classes exist purely for doc/codegen accuracy. Explicit `type: "string"` on every nullable-string field, since `@ApiPropertyOptional({ nullable: true })` alone doesn't reliably infer the type from a `string | null` TS annotation without the swagger CLI plugin enabled (a real gap caught by inspecting the generated JSON doc directly — an undecorated field silently rendered as `type: "object"`, not a compile error).
- Verified end-to-end against a live boot, not just typecheck: `/api/docs-json` returns all 168 mapped routes; the five decorated routes' request bodies resolve to correctly-shaped, fully-typed schemas (spot-checked their raw JSON, not just presence of a `requestBody` key).
- **Explicit Better Auth session lifetime** (`apps/api/src/auth/auth.ts`): a top-level `session: { expiresIn, updateAge }` block — 30 days / 7-day rolling refresh — replacing Better Auth's previously-undocumented defaults (7-day expiresIn / 1-day updateAge). This is a different config key from the pre-existing `databaseHooks.session.create` hook (org-activation logic, untouched) — confirmed the distinction directly against `@better-auth/core`'s `init-options.d.mts` before writing it, since the two share the name `session` but live at different nesting levels. No per-client-type session config exists in Better Auth, so web and the Expo app share this one value; "any session used at least once a week never actually expires" covers a field crew's realistic usage pattern without an unboundedly long session on a lost/reassigned device. Mobile itself never touches this session directly — see the prior on-site-acceptance entry's auth-flow note; it re-mints a 15-minute JWT from the underlying session via `/api/auth/token` on every foreground, only falling back to a real login if the session itself is actually expired/revoked. Verified against a live boot: a real sign-up/sign-in round trip produces a session expiring exactly 30 days out, `activeOrganizationId` is still set correctly by the pre-existing hook, and `/api/auth/token` still mints a working JWT from it.
- This closes out Phase 5's API-prerequisite stage (job crew assignment, on-site quote acceptance, this entry) — the next Phase 5 stage is scaffolding `apps/mobile` itself, per the Phase 5 implementation plan.
- Stories: infrastructure supporting S-11.1 and the mobile outbox generally; no PRD story of its own.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (API prerequisite stage — now complete).

### 2026-08-30 — Phase 5 (Mobile) API prerequisite, part 2: on-site quote acceptance

- New authenticated endpoint `POST /quotes/:id/accept-in-person` (S-11.7 — a field/staff/owner user presents a quote on their own device and captures the customer's on-site signature/acceptance). Deliberately a SEPARATE code path from the existing public accept-link flow (`PublicQuotesService.respond`, `@Public()`, no session) rather than bolting an authenticated actor onto a service built to have none — the public path's schema has no concept of an accepting user and its audit semantics (token-only, IP+user-agent provenance) shouldn't change. `QuotesService.acceptInPerson` shares the same row-locked concurrency discipline (`send`/`revise`'s established pattern) and fires the same "quote accepted" owner notification + variation-order nudge as the public path, just via its own transaction rather than a shared helper — see the method's own doc comment for the reasoning.
- New columns on `quotes`: `acceptanceMethod` (`"public_link" | "in_person"`, new `quote_acceptance_method` enum) and `acceptedByUserId` — both null unless/until a quote is accepted via this new path specifically, never touched by the public accept flow. Migration `0049_narrow_tyger_tiger` (drizzle-kit generated).
- New dedicated workflow-action capability `quotes.accept_in_person` (not own/others — "who can accept in person" isn't an ownership question, same shape as `quotes.send`/`quotes.revise`). Field always passes it unconditionally regardless of Team grants (added to `FIELD_ALWAYS_CAPABILITIES` in `capability.util.ts`, alongside milestone completion) — this is the entire point of S-11.7. Backfilled onto every Team with `quotes.send` already granted (migration `0050_add_quotes_accept_in_person_capability`, hand-authored, `WHERE NOT EXISTS`-guarded).
- The request body takes `{ signatureFileId, comment? }` — the signature image is uploaded first via the existing `POST /files` (Field can already call this), then referenced by id, same two-step pattern every other file-attaching endpoint in this codebase already uses.
- **`QuotesController` is class-decorated `@OrgRoles(["owner", "staff"])`, which would have silently blocked Field from this route entirely** — caught before it became a client-only bug: the new route carries its own `@OrgRoles(["owner", "staff", "field"])` override (NestJS's `getAllAndOverride` resolves method-level metadata before class-level, same override mechanism `approveDiscount` already uses in the narrowing direction).
- **A real bug shipped and was caught by this change's own tests**: the first version of `acceptInPerson` called `hasCapability(...)` without its `fieldAlwaysPasses: true` argument, so Field silently 403'd despite being listed in `FIELD_ALWAYS_CAPABILITIES` — the set alone doesn't do anything; every call site has to actually pass the flag. Exactly the class of mistake CLAUDE.md's permission-model section already warns about for this file. Fixed and covered by a dedicated "Field always passes... with zero Team grants" test so it can't silently regress.
- 6 new integration tests in `quotes-ownership.integration.test.ts` (new "Accept in person" describe block, plus a `fieldUserId` fixture added to the file): capability gate, Field unconditional pass, `acceptedByUserId`/`acceptanceMethod` recorded correctly, a second accept attempt on an already-accepted quote is rejected (not silently re-applied), an out-of-org `signatureFileId` is rejected, Owner bypass. All pass.
- Fixed five other integration test files that hand-construct `QuotesService` directly (`catalog-quotes-history`, `variation-order-tax`, `public-quotes-respond-notifications`, `public-quotes-view-notification-throttle`, `quotes-ownership`) to pass the service's new `NotificationsService` constructor dependency.
- **Discovered and fixed a real migration-tracking gap while verifying this**: `drizzle-kit migrate` had recorded migration `0049` as applied against both the dev and test databases without its SQL ever actually running (`quotes.acceptance_method`/`accepted_by_user_id` were absent from both despite a clean "migrations applied successfully" report) — applied the pending SQL directly and confirmed against `information_schema.columns` on both databases before re-running tests. Root cause not fully isolated (worth revisiting if it recurs), but not a Phase-5-specific issue — flagging here since it could silently affect any future schema migration in this repo if the same drizzle-kit/journal state recurs.
- Confirmed, again, that this repo's existing `test:integration` full-suite run has pre-existing cross-test flakiness under parallel execution (a different unrelated file fails on each run — `teams.service`, `members.service`, `notifications`, `meetings` all independently observed) — every quotes/jobs test touched by this change was consistently green across multiple full-suite runs; the flakiness is orthogonal to this change, not introduced by it.
- No mobile UI consumes this endpoint yet (`apps/mobile` doesn't exist) — deferred to whenever the mobile Quotes screen itself is built, per the plan's staged build order.
- Stories: unblocks S-11.7, S-03.12 (mobile finishing half).
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (API prerequisite stage).

### 2026-08-30 — Phase 5 (Mobile) API prerequisite, part 1: job crew assignment

- Blocking discovery from Phase 5 scoping: `jobs` had no assignee column at all, so S-11.2's "today's assigned jobs" mobile home-screen query had nothing to filter on. Added a `job_assignments` join table (`apps/api/src/db/schema/jobs.ts`, migration `0047_fearless_romulus`) rather than a single `assignedToUserId` column — a field-service job commonly has a crew, not one owner, unlike `contacts.assignedToUserId`'s single-pipeline-rep shape. Unique on `(jobId, userId)` so re-assigning an already-assigned user is a safe no-op, not a constraint violation — this matters once the mobile outbox (later Phase 5 work) can retry an assign call after a flaky connection.
- New dedicated workflow-action capability `jobs.assign` (`packages/shared/src/schemas/permissions.ts`) — assigning/unassigning crew is a different question from "can I edit this job's own fields," so it's gated separately from `jobs.edit_own`/`edit_others`, matching `jobs.release_retention`'s existing single-grant shape. Backfilled onto every Team that already has `jobs.edit_own` granted (migration `0048_add_jobs_assign_capability`, hand-authored, guarded by `WHERE NOT EXISTS`) so existing orgs don't lose office access to a feature that didn't exist before.
- `JobsService`: `assign`/`unassign`/`listAssignees`, plus `list()` gained an `assignedToUserId` filter mirroring `ExpensesService.list`'s `mine` query-param precedent exactly. New routes on `JobsController`: `GET/POST /jobs/:id/assignees`, `DELETE /jobs/:id/assignees/:userId`, and `GET /jobs?assignedToMe=true`. Read (`listAssignees`) is unconditional like every other GET on this controller; assign/unassign check `jobs.assign` directly (not `@RequireCapability` at the route, since this isn't own/others-shaped — no per-record ownership to defer to the service for).
- **Web UI wired in the same change**, per CLAUDE.md's own rule that a capability split isn't complete until the UI reflects it: a new "Crew" tab on the job detail page (`apps/web/src/app/(app)/jobs/[id]/crew-section.tsx`) — lists assignees, and (capability-gated via `useCapability("jobs.assign")`) a member picker sourced from the existing `GET /org/members` endpoint (same source `expenses-explorer.tsx`/`team-detail-view.tsx` already use) to assign/unassign.
- 5 new integration tests in `jobs-ownership.integration.test.ts`'s existing "Jobs & Milestones ownership split" suite (new "Crew assignment" describe block): capability gate, assign/unassign round-trip, idempotent re-assign, Owner bypass, and the `assignedToUserId` list filter. All pass; confirmed the codebase's existing `ledger-integrity.integration.test.ts` deadlock-under-parallel-run flakiness pre-dates this change (reproduced identically against unmodified `main`) rather than being a regression.
- This is API/web-only — `apps/mobile` doesn't exist yet. It's the first of several Phase 5 API-side prerequisites (see the Phase 5 implementation plan) that need to land before mobile's own screens are buildable; on-site quote acceptance (`quotes.accept_in_person`) is next.
- Stories: unblocks S-11.2 (mobile home screen); no PRD story of its own for the web-side crew UI, built to the bar the mobile home screen needs.
- Phase: Phase 5 · Mobile Field Companion (API prerequisite stage).

### 2026-08-29 — Automated accessibility regression testing for `@spine/ui` (axe-core + vitest), closing the recommended follow-up from the WCAG 2.1 AA audit

- Closes the "Automated accessibility-testing tooling (axe-core/jest-axe or similar)" line from "Next up" (removed below), recommended as a follow-up by that day's earlier formal WCAG 2.1 AA `@spine/ui` audit-and-fix pass — every one of the library's 78 components now has a real, enforced automated a11y regression test instead of relying on a fresh manual audit each time.
- **Infra** (`packages/ui`): `vitest.config.ts` (jsdom environment, setup file), `src/test/setup.ts` (`@testing-library/react`'s `cleanup` after each test, plus `matchMedia`/`IntersectionObserver`/`ResizeObserver` jsdom polyfills needed by Carousel/embla and other components that don't otherwise mount in jsdom), `src/test/a11y.ts` (`expectNoA11yViolations(container)` — runs axe-core scoped to `wcag2a`/`wcag2aa`/`wcag21a`/`wcag21aa` rule tags, matching the audit's own stated bar, and throws a formatted violation list on failure). Deliberately does **not** use `vitest-axe`'s matcher entrypoint (`vitest-axe/extend-expect`) — that package's 0.1.0 build ships an empty `extend-expect.js`, discovered while wiring this up — so `expectNoA11yViolations` calls `axe-core` directly instead, simpler and fully typed with no dependency on a broken third-party build.
- **Enforcement, not just convention**: `packages/ui/scripts/check-a11y-coverage.mjs` fails if any `src/components/*.tsx` file lacks a matching `*.a11y.test.tsx`, wired into `packages/ui`'s own `test` script (`vitest run && node scripts/check-a11y-coverage.mjs`) — picked up automatically by the existing root `pnpm test` → `turbo run test` → CI's "Unit tests" step, no CI file changes needed. CLAUDE.md's `@spine/ui` rules section gained a matching "every component ships with an a11y test in the same change" rule, mirroring the existing design-system-doc-page rule, so future components (new or changed) don't silently drift out of coverage.
- **Rollout**: one `.a11y.test.tsx` per component (78 total, 177 tests), each rendering a representative default/open state — Radix overlays (Dialog, AlertDialog, Popover, Select, HoverCard, Toast, Tooltip) opened via their controlled `open`/`defaultOpen` prop and asserted against `document.body` since Radix portals content there; components with no controlled-open prop (ContextMenu, DropdownMenu, Combobox, DatePicker) opened via real `@testing-library/user-event` interaction instead; multi-state components (Alert's 4 variants, Checkbox's checked/indeterminate/disabled, Table's grouped-row mode, etc.) covered with 2-4 cases each, matching the depth of the original manual audit rather than one generic render per component.
- **Five genuine, previously-unfound accessibility bugs caught and fixed** by the very first real run of this net — exactly the class of regression this tooling exists to catch:
  - `calendar-mini.tsx`: `role="grid"` rendered weekday-header and day cells as direct children with no `role="row"` wrapper (invalid ARIA structure, `aria-required-children`/`aria-required-parent`) — fixed by grouping cells into per-week `role="row"` containers (padded to a full 7 columns so the grid stays rectangular). A second, independent issue in the same component: the weekday-header cells had `role="columnheader" aria-hidden="true"` together, which hides otherwise-meaningful header text from the accessibility tree entirely — the stray `aria-hidden` was removed.
  - `calendar.tsx`: month view's day grid had the same missing grid/row-structure gap as `calendar-mini.tsx` above — fixed the same way (`role="grid"` + `aria-label` on the outer container, `role="row"` on the weekday-header row and each week row).
  - `multi-select.tsx`: the trigger `<button role="combobox">` had no way to receive an accessible name at all — no `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` prop existed on `MultiSelectProps`, and visible inner text (placeholder/selected chips) doesn't satisfy a `role="combobox"` element's WAI-ARIA naming requirement, so axe's `button-name` rule flagged every real call site as a critical violation. Fixed by adding `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` to `MultiSelectProps`, forwarded onto the trigger. **Follow-through beyond the library itself**: grepped `apps/web` for every real `<MultiSelect>` call site (11 across 10 files — Invoices/Quotes/Expenses/Contacts ×2/Leads/Catalog ×2/Jobs/Vendor Bills/Credit Notes explorers, plus Settings → Tax's rate-group picker) and added a matching `aria-label` to each, since the new prop being optional meant the actual shipped app screens were still failing the same rule until wired up — a library-level fix alone would have left the real bug live in production.
  - `slider.tsx`: `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` passed to `<Slider>` landed on Radix's `SliderPrimitive.Root`, but Radix puts `role="slider"` on the `Thumb` — so a label never reached the actual interactive element (`aria-input-field-name`). Also, only one hardcoded `Thumb` was rendered regardless of how many values were passed, so a multi-thumb range slider (e.g. a min/max discount range) would silently render with a missing second thumb. Fixed by rendering one labeled `Thumb` per `value`/`defaultValue` entry. The one real `apps/web` call site (`logo-crop-dialog.tsx`'s zoom slider, which had a visible "Zoom" text label with nothing connecting it programmatically) gained a matching `aria-label="Zoom"`.
  - `rich-text-editor.tsx`: the Bold/Italic/Bulleted-list/Numbered-list/Link toolbar buttons were icon-only with no accessible name (`button-name`) — fixed with a matching `aria-label` on each (Link's toggles between "Add link"/"Remove link" based on active state).
- **Verified, not just claimed**: full `pnpm vitest run` inside `packages/ui` — 79 test files (78 component + 1 pre-existing), 177 tests, all green; `node scripts/check-a11y-coverage.mjs` reports 78/78; `pnpm --filter @spine/ui typecheck lint`, `pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck lint`, `pnpm --filter @spine/design-system typecheck lint build` (all 83 routes still prerender statically) all clean; whole-workspace `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` (matching CI's own steps) both clean, only pre-existing unrelated lint warnings in `apps/api`.
- Design-system doc page: `apps/design-system/src/app/components/multi-select/page.tsx` updated with the two new `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` props in its API Reference table and its live example, per CLAUDE.md's "component API change ships with its doc page in the same change" rule. No other component's public API changed (the `calendar`/`calendar-mini`/`slider`/`rich-text-editor` fixes were internal accessibility corrections with no new/changed props visible to a consumer, aside from `Slider` already accepting `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` as standard HTML attributes before this change — only where they landed changed).
- Not built, deliberately out of scope for this pass: visual regression screenshot testing, a real screen-reader-driven test (axe-core checks static ARIA/DOM structure, not actual assistive-tech behavior), and touch-target-size assertions (still out of scope per the original audit's own stated 2.1 AA boundary).

### 2026-08-29 — E2E coverage for Dashboard v2, Reports, and the public quote page (closes the "never visually verified in a browser" gap for all 3)

- **4 new spec files** (`apps/e2e/tests/`): `dashboard.spec.ts`, `reports.spec.ts`, `public-quote-page.spec.ts`, `route-smoke.spec.ts` — 28 new tests on top of the existing `quote-to-payment.spec.ts` smoke test (29 total). Structural assertions only (real content renders, correct data, correct interactive behavior) — deliberately no pixel-diffing/screenshot snapshots, since font/OS rendering differences make those brittle across local-macOS vs CI-Linux, and what was actually missing before was "does this even render," not "is it pixel-perfect."
- **`fixtures.ts`** — a new `seededOrg` fixture (`test.extend`) that signs up a fresh org and calls the real `POST /demo-data/seed` once, giving Dashboard/Reports/route-smoke tests non-empty charts/reports/lists without hand-driving UI creation flows for every test (the create/send/accept/convert/issue/pay flow already has dedicated coverage in `quote-to-payment.spec.ts`). **Worker-scoped, not per-test** — this was a real bug caught live: a per-test-scoped version meant 25+ tests each independently seeding, and each seed sends ~7 quotes through the real `quote-send-email` pg-boss queue (PDF render + SMTP send per email); the resulting 100+ job backlog starved OTHER tests' own email-dependent assertions (`quote-to-payment.spec.ts`, `public-quote-page.spec.ts`) well past a 45-second wait, intermittently failing tests that had nothing to do with the seeded orgs at all. Scoping the fixture to `{ scope: "worker" }` (one seed per spec file, since `workers: 1`) fixed the root cause and cut full-suite runtime from ~3.5 minutes with flakes to a stable ~55 seconds.
- **`global-setup.ts`** — clears MailDev's inbox once before the whole suite runs, since a local MailDev instance persists across separate test invocations and would otherwise accumulate cruft from prior runs indefinitely.
- **Dashboard v2** (`dashboard.spec.ts`): every widget in `WIDGET_LABELS` renders with real seeded content; the pinned KPI summary row; Field role's shorter, non-financial widget composition (via a genuinely separate browser context/login, not just a different session token, since `/login` redirects an already-authenticated session straight back into the app); "Edit layout" hide/show toggle, including that the layout persists across a reload. **Drag-reordering is deliberately NOT covered** — `ReorderableItem` uses native HTML5 drag-and-drop, and neither Playwright's `dragTo()`, manually dispatched `DragEvent`s (several variants tried, including awaiting between dispatch calls for React state to flush), nor raw `mouse.down/move/up` reliably trigger a real browser drag session for it; every attempt left `dragover`'s `defaultPrevented` false, meaning the component's own `ctx.draggedId` guard never saw a live drag and silently no-opped. This was flagged as the likely outcome before starting this work and confirmed live — see the test file's own top comment for the full investigation trail and what would need to change to revisit it (a Playwright-native HTML5-DnD solution, or migrating the component to a pointer-events library).
- **Reports** (`reports.spec.ts`): all 3 tabs (P&L, Balance Sheet, Job Profitability) render real seeded lines; clicking an account line opens the drill-down dialog with real transaction rows; CSV export links exist with correct hrefs for both P&L and Balance Sheet.
- **Public quote page** (`public-quote-page.spec.ts`): renders a sent quote and lets the customer decline it (extends `quote-to-payment.spec.ts`'s own accept-only coverage); an already-resolved quote shows its resolution (not the decision buttons) on a **fresh** page load, not just immediately after the in-page response; an invalid/nonexistent token shows a clear error instead of a blank page. New `sendQuoteAndGetPublicLink` helper in `helpers.ts` (contact + quote + send + read the real link back from MailDev) factors out the pattern this file needed 3 times.
- **Route smoke pass** (`route-smoke.spec.ts`): every remaining route section not already covered by a dedicated file (Contacts, Leads, Catalogue, Jobs, Meetings, Invoices, Credit Notes, Payments, Receivables, Vendor Bills, Expenses, Vendor Payments, Payables, Team/Users, Team/Teams, Profile) loads with no console errors and shows its own heading; a separate check confirms Contacts/Invoices/Jobs show real seeded rows, not just an empty state. Vendor Bills/Expenses/Vendor Payments/Payables all render real seeded data too — `demo-data.service.ts`'s `seedPurchases` covers them, correcting an earlier assumption in this same session that they weren't seeded.
- **Verified live, repeatedly**: full 29-test suite passed 3 consecutive clean runs after the worker-scoping fix (previously 3/29 tests failed intermittently on every run). `pnpm typecheck`/`pnpm lint`/`pnpm build` clean across the whole monorepo; the pre-existing `apps/api` integration suite (170 tests) re-confirmed unaffected.

### 2026-08-29 — Browser automation (Playwright) + a real E2E smoke test (closes the CLAUDE.md testing-expectations gap: "E2E smoke test covering quote → invoice → payment")

- **New `apps/e2e` workspace app** — Playwright driving real `apps/api`+`apps/web` instances (built + started via `playwright.config.ts`'s `webServer` array, not mocked), against a dedicated scratch database (`spine_e2e`, same "own DB because tests TRUNCATE real tables" reasoning as `.env.test` — see `.env.e2e`'s own comment) on ports offset from local dev (3100/4100) so the suite can run alongside a normal `pnpm dev` session.

### 2026-08-29 — History for Jobs and Purchases (closes the last remaining "no history view" gap — every module now has one)

- **Gap**: Jobs (Jobs, Milestones, Job Photos, Job Notes) and Purchases (Expenses, Expense Categories, Vendor Bills, Vendor Payments) already wrote real `audit_log` rows via `AuditLogService.record()` on every mutation (CHANGELOG's own prior claim that these were "empty `@Module({})` stubs" was stale — confirmed false by grep before starting), but had no `GET /:id/history` endpoint or web History button, the same gap Invoices/Payments/Credit Notes and Catalogue/Quotes each closed earlier this session. This closes it for the remaining modules — every document/record type in the app now has a working History view.
- **Purchases (4 resources)** — mechanically identical to the Invoices/Catalogue/Quotes precedent: `getHistory(orgId, id)` on each service (confirms the record exists via the existing `getOne`, then `auditLog.listForEntity`), `GET /:id/history` on each controller, no `@RequireCapability`. `expenses.controller.ts`'s route carries `@OrgRoles(["owner", "staff", "field"])` explicitly (matching every other GET on that Field-reachable controller, which has no class-level default). Web: `HistorySection` button added to `expense-detail-drawer.tsx`'s footer, per-row in `purchases-pane.tsx`'s Expense Categories list (no dedicated detail page exists for categories), `vendor-bill-detail.tsx`'s action-button row, and `vendor-payment-detail-drawer.tsx`'s footer.
- **Jobs (3 resources with existing writes)** — `JobsService.getHistory` (`entityType: "job"`) and `MilestonesService.getHistory(orgId, jobId, milestoneId)` (`entityType: "milestone"`), routed at `GET /jobs/:id/history` and `GET /jobs/:id/milestones/:milestoneId/history` (nested under the job, matching the existing `GET /jobs/:id/milestones` list route's URL shape). **Strictly scoped per entity type, no cross-resource aggregation** — a job's own history never includes its milestones' rows and vice versa (verified by a dedicated test assertion), the same "no merging" precedent `QuotesService.getHistory` set for `quote_events`. Web: `HistorySection` on `job-detail.tsx`'s action row, and a per-row button on each milestone in `milestones-section.tsx`.
- **Job Notes and Job Photos (2 resources, needed NEW audit writes)** — these had zero `audit_log` writes of their own before this change (only a job-level `photo_added`/`note_added` row existed). `AuditEntityType` gained `"job_photo"`/`"job_note"`. `JobsService.addPhoto`/`addNote` were not previously transactional; both are now wrapped in `db.transaction(...)` so the insert and its audit write(s) are atomic — each writes the pre-existing job-level row (kept, still feeds the job's own history) plus a new dedicated row scoped to just that photo/note's own id, read via new `getPhotoHistory`/`getNoteHistory` methods and `GET /jobs/:id/photos/:photoId/history`/`GET /jobs/:id/notes/:noteId/history` routes. Both are create-only resources (no update/delete routes exist for either), so their history is typically a single "created" row — built anyway for UI consistency with every other resource. Web: a small `HistorySection` button per photo card in `photos-section.tsx` (required restructuring the card from one big `<a>` wrapper into an image-only `<a>` plus a separate metadata row, since an interactive button can't nest inside an anchor) and per note row in `notes-section.tsx`.
- **Variation Orders — deliberately excluded, not a gap.** `variation-orders.service.ts` writes every audit entry (both `create` and `apply`) with `entityType: "job", entityId: <jobId>` — variation-order creation/acceptance is logged as a job-level event, with no variation-order-specific `entityId` ever recorded. There is no variation-order-scoped history buildable without inventing a new entityType and a backfill migration, which was out of scope for this pass. Documented inline in `jobs-history.integration.test.ts` rather than silently worked around.
- **Tests**: `purchases-history.integration.test.ts` (7 cases) and `jobs-history.integration.test.ts` (8 cases) — both follow `catalog-quotes-history.integration.test.ts`'s structure (services constructed by hand, sibling-record isolation assertions, 404 checks). The Jobs suite specifically asserts the no-cross-aggregation rule: a job's history excludes its own milestone's/photo's/note's dedicated rows, and a milestone's history excludes the job-level `milestones_set` row. Full integration suite (170 tests across 23 files) passes cleanly, including the previously-known-flaky `ledger-integrity.integration.test.ts` (no flake this run). Typecheck, lint, and build all clean for both `@spine/api` and `@spine/web`.

### 2026-08-29 — Quote rejections now trigger an owner notification (closes a long-standing "Next up" item)

- **Gap**: `PublicQuotesService.respond()` only fired `NotificationsService.notify()` when `outcome === "accepted"` — a customer rejecting a quote on the public page produced no email/in-app notification at all, matching S-03.7's literal "viewed or accepted" wording but leaving owners with no proactive heads-up on a rejection (they'd only see it by later opening the quote itself). Pre-documented as an explicit, considered gap in CHANGELOG's "Next up" list ("worth reconsidering if real usage shows owners want to know about rejections just as promptly").
- **Fix**: `respond()`'s notification branch is now unconditional across both outcomes rather than gated on `accepted` — a shared block derives the verb ("accepted"/"rejected") and in-app `type` (`quote_accepted`/`quote_rejected`) from `outcome`, reusing the exact same subject/text/`recipientRoles`/`link` shape either way. No new schema or migration needed — `notifications.type` is a free-form string column (`notifications.ts`'s own doc comment: "not currently used for anything beyond display/future filtering"), and the web notification drawer/bell already render generically off `message`/`link` with no per-type branching, so `quote_rejected` needed zero frontend changes.
- **Tests**: `public-quotes-respond-notifications.integration.test.ts` (2 cases) — rejecting a quote sends exactly one `quote_rejected` notification and zero `quote_accepted`; accepting still sends exactly one `quote_accepted` and zero `quote_rejected` (a regression guard against the two outcomes cross-contaminating). Full integration suite (151 tests across 20 files, including the new file) passes cleanly — no flake this run, including the previously-known-flaky `ledger-integrity.integration.test.ts`. Typecheck, lint, and build all clean for `@spine/api`.

### 2026-08-29 — Repeat public-quote-view notifications are now throttled (closes a long-standing, pre-documented "Next up" item)

- **Gap**: every successful public view of a quote's share link fired an owner-notification email/in-app row unconditionally, with no de-duplication — a customer opening the link 5 times generated 5 "viewed" emails. Confirmed pre-approved scope: CHANGELOG's own "Next up" section had carried this exact fix ("throttling to 'at most one viewed notification per hour per quote' or similar") as a suggested follow-up since the feature first shipped, deliberately deferred at the time as "inventing scope" beyond S-03.7's literal wording.
- **`PublicQuotesService.view()`**: before inserting the new `quote_events` row, now checks whether a `viewed`-type event for this quote already exists within the last hour (`VIEW_NOTIFICATION_THROTTLE_MS`); if so, the `NotificationsService.notify()` call is skipped for this view. The `quote_events` audit-trail insert itself is completely unaffected — every view still gets its own row, per that table's own existing "a customer can legitimately view multiple times, each view is a real event worth its own row" design; only the notification is throttled, not the log. `accept()`/`reject()` (a structurally separate code path via `respond()`) are untouched — acceptance is already inherently one-shot (a `GoneException` blocks any second response), so there was never a repeat-notification problem to solve there.
- **Deliberately a simple read-then-write, not a stricter locking scheme** — two near-simultaneous views of the same link could theoretically both read "no recent view" before either's notify call fires, causing a rare duplicate email under that narrow race. Accepted as a reasonable tradeoff for a best-effort noise-reduction heuristic on a non-critical notification, documented inline rather than hidden.
- **Tests**: `public-quotes-view-notification-throttle.integration.test.ts` (3 cases) — a burst of views within the window produces one notification but N `quote_events` rows; backdating the prior view past the window allows a fresh notification; two different quotes throttle independently of each other. Full integration suite (149 tests across 19 files) passes; the 3 failures seen mid-run are the same pre-existing cross-file parallel-run flake confirmed unrelated across every prior phase — the new test file itself passed 3/3 in isolation and in the full run.
- `quotes.ts`'s `quoteEvents` schema doc comment (which previously asserted "no PRD language calling for de-duplicating repeat-view notifications... reasonable follow-up if it proves noisy") updated to describe the now-real throttle instead.

### 2026-08-29 — Contact persons/addresses gain their own capabilities; per-contact Leads list gets the same UI gating Activities got earlier today (user-reported)

- **Two new independent, non-ownership capabilities**: `contacts.manage_persons` and `contacts.manage_addresses`. Contact persons and addresses have no `createdByUserId` of their own — both are pure sub-fields of the contact record, whole-array-replaced inside `PUT /contacts/:id` (see `contacts.ts`'s own schema comment), never independently created/updated/deleted entities — so a true own/others split doesn't apply. Each is instead a single Team-configurable grant, checked in `ContactsService.update` in ADDITION to (not instead of) the existing `contacts.edit_own`/`edit_others` ownership check on the parent contact, only when the request payload actually includes `contactPersons`/`addresses` respectively. Confirmed with the user before implementing (the alternative — full own/others via a schema migration adding `createdByUserId` to both tables — was explicitly declined as unnecessary complexity for fields always edited as part of the parent contact).
- **Gap**: the web UI for both sections (`contact-persons-section.tsx`, `addresses-section.tsx`) showed New/Edit/Remove unconditionally to every viewer; the API was already correctly blocking non-owners via the single shared `contacts.edit_own`/`edit_others` check it used before this change, so a Staff user without contact-edit rights would see the buttons, click them, and 403 on save.
- **`apps/web/src/app/(app)/contacts/leads-section.tsx`** (the per-contact flat list, a separate component from the org-wide `/leads` kanban board) had zero client-side capability gating despite `LeadsService` correctly enforcing `leads.edit_own`/`leads.edit_others` all along — same class of bug as `activities-section.tsx`, fixed earlier the same day, and found by the user asking about it directly rather than by another audit pass. Fixed identically: extracted each row into its own `LeadRow` component (so `useCanEditOwnership` can be called normally, not once per item inside the parent's `.map()` — Rules of Hooks), gated the Edit pencil per-row and "Add lead" on `leads.edit_own`.
- **Migration** (`0046_add_contacts_manage_persons_addresses.sql`): backfills both new capabilities onto every existing Team that already has `contacts.edit_own` granted, preserving today's behavior (any Team that could edit a contact could implicitly touch its persons/addresses) until an Owner narrows it. Applied to dev and integration-test databases.
- **Tests**: 4 new cases in `contacts-catalog-ownership.integration.test.ts` covering `manage_persons` required in addition to `edit_own`, `manage_addresses` independent of `manage_persons`, the base ownership check still applying (a `manage_persons` grant with no contact-edit access is still rejected), and Owner bypass. Full integration suite (141 tests across 17 files) passes; the 3 intermittent failures seen mid-session are the same pre-existing cross-file parallel-run flake confirmed unrelated in every prior phase — the new tests themselves passed 4/4 in isolation and in the full run.
- PRD §2.1 (2 new rows) and a new story S-01.18 with acceptance highlights; CLAUDE.md documents this as a third variant of the capability-splitting pattern (own/others, plain workflow capability, and now "one grant per sub-resource with no creator of its own"), and records the Leads-in-contact-detail gap as a reminder that server-correctness doesn't imply UI-correctness per component.

### 2026-08-29 — Activities' Edit/done-toggle web UI was never wired to `activities.edit_own`/`edit_others` (found during a full privilege-system audit)

- **Gap**: prompted by "is everything related to privileges complete?", a full audit cross-checked every own/others resource's server-side ownership enforcement against its web UI. Every other resource (Contacts, Catalogue, Leads, Quotes, Meetings, Purchases, Jobs, Invoices, Payments) was correctly gated — only **Activities** slipped through. `apps/web/src/app/(app)/contacts/activities-section.tsx` rendered its Edit pencil icon unconditionally on every logged activity, and the done/undone Checkbox was always enabled — a Staff user granted only `activities.edit_own` (not `edit_others`) could click Edit or toggle done/undone on a colleague's activity and get a 403 from `ActivitiesService.update`/`markDone`/`markUndone`'s existing `requireOwnershipCapability` check, instead of the affordance simply not being there.
- **Fix**: extracted each row into its own `ActivityRow` component so `useCanEditOwnership` could be called normally (calling it once per item inside the parent's `.map()` would violate the Rules of Hooks the moment the activity count changes between renders — same constraint documented for `meetings-calendar.tsx`/`milestones-section.tsx` elsewhere in this codebase, but here the fix is the simpler "extract a real component" route since there was no render-prop constraint forcing a manual re-derivation). The Edit button is now hidden (not just disabled) without `edit_own`/`edit_others`; the Checkbox is disabled under the same condition (kept visible, since the completion state itself is still useful information). **Log activity** is now gated on `activities.edit_own` too — previously shown unconditionally.
- **Not a bug, left as-is**: `activities.delete_own`/`delete_others` have zero UI consumer — there is no delete action for activities anywhere in the web app today (a pre-existing feature gap, not a privilege-gating bug, since there's no button to hide). Similarly, `credit_notes.edit_own`/`edit_others`/`delete_own`/`delete_others` are fully enforced server-side but have no UI at all (only `credit_notes.issue`, via the create-and-immediately-issue dialog, is wired) — no false affordance exists since neither feature is built. Both are pre-existing scope gaps, not part of this fix.
- Full typecheck/lint/build clean for `@spine/web`. `docs/qa-script.md` §13.2 gained a regression step for the Edit-icon/checkbox/Log-activity gating.

- **Second layer, matching the "hide entry point + defense-in-depth" pattern already used for Team/Users pages**: `SettingsDialog` itself now takes an `isOwner` prop and refuses to render any pane content (`if (!isOwner) return null`) — in case a future second entry point is added without remembering this gate. Both layers are UI convenience only; the API independently re-checks every request regardless.
- Confirmed with the user: Expense Categories (inside the Purchases pane, the one section that uses the normal Team-configurable `expense_categories.edit_own`/`edit_others` capability rather than Owner-only) is intentionally hidden along with everything else when Settings itself is hidden — a Staff user with that capability grant would need a different surface to manage it, out of scope for this fix.
- Full typecheck/lint/build clean for `@spine/web`. `docs/qa-script.md` §1 gained a regression step confirming the Settings menu item is absent for Staff/Field.

### 2026-08-29 — Meetings calendar now enforces capability gating on the calendar surface itself, not just the popover (user-reported)

- **Gap**: `meetings.edit_own`/`meetings.edit_others` were already correctly enforced server-side and in the quick-view popover's Edit/Delete buttons, but three other paths bypassed all of it: (1) clicking/dragging empty calendar space always opened the "New meeting" dialog regardless of capability, and clicking Save threw a raw API 403 instead of the dialog never appearing; (2) double-clicking a meeting the viewer couldn't edit jumped straight to the full edit dialog, skipping the (correctly-gated) popover entirely; (3) a meeting the viewer couldn't edit was still draggable and resizable on the calendar grid.

Its `onEventDoubleClick` handler now short-circuits to a no-op for a non-editable meeting instead of opening the full edit dialog — by design (confirmed with the user) there's no separate "read-only edit dialog" to open instead; the quick-view popover already IS the read-only view, reachable via ordinary single-click.
- **`meeting-quick-view-popover.tsx`**: when `canEdit` is `false`, the Pencil "Edit" button is replaced by an inert Eye icon labelled "View only" (title/aria-label), rather than simply disappearing as it did before — a visible signal that this is a read-only view, not just an absent action. Clicking it does nothing (confirmed with the user) — there's no separate content to show beyond what the popover already displays.
- **`apps/design-system`**'s Calendar doc page gained rows for both new props.
- Full typecheck/lint/build clean for `@spine/ui`/`@spine/web`/`@spine/design-system`. `docs/qa-script.md` §6.3 gained regression steps covering create-gating, per-meeting edit-gating (drag/resize/double-click/popover icon), and Owner bypass.

### 2026-08-29 — Own/others privilege split, Phase 4 (final phase): Invoices, Payments, Credit Notes

- **This closes out the entire own/others privilege-split rollout (PRD §9)** — every module in the app now uses this pattern. The single undifferentiated `invoices.manage` capability (which had covered invoice creation, issuing, voiding, emailing, reminders, payment recording/deletion, and credit notes all at once since Phase 2) is replaced by 19 new capabilities across three independent own/others groups.

- **No schema migration needed** — `invoices`, `payments`, and `credit_notes` all already had `createdByUserId` since their own original migrations (from before this rollout began). - **Ownership-vs-status ordering fixed in the same change it was introduced** — none of `InvoicesService`, `PaymentsService`, `CreditNotesService` had any ownership check before this phase, so CLAUDE.md's "ownership check must run BEFORE the draft-only status check" warning had nothing to violate yet; `requireOwnershipCapability` calls were added immediately after each service's existing `NotFoundException` lookup and before the existing status/allocation check, exactly mirroring `VendorBillsService`'s already-shipped ordering — verified with a dedicated test asserting a non-owner gets 403 (missing capability), not 400 (only a draft can be edited), on a non-draft invoice.
- **`GET /reports/invoices-due-this-week`** (the dashboard "invoices due" widget) lost its `invoices.manage` gate entirely — it's a read across every invoice, same unconditional-GET convention as every other list/report route in this codebase; `DASHBOARD_WIDGETS`' `invoices-due` entry updated to `capability: null` to match.

Caught and fixed a pre-existing UI bug while wiring this up: `invoice-detail.tsx`'s "Delete draft" button was gated on `canEdit` instead of a real delete check — now correctly split into `canEdit`/`canDelete`.
- **Tests**: `invoices-payments-credit-notes-ownership.integration.test.ts` (9 cases) covering all three resources' own/others behavior, the ownership-before-status-check ordering, a legacy-unowned-payment case, and Owner bypass. Full integration suite (137 tests across 17 files) passes; typecheck, lint, and production build clean for `@spine/shared`/`@spine/api`/`@spine/web`. The intermittent failures seen mid-session (different files each run — `members.service.integration.test.ts`, `meetings.service.integration.test.ts`, `teams.service.integration.test.ts`) are the same pre-existing cross-file parallel-run flake confirmed unrelated across every prior phase, not a regression; the new test file itself passed 9/9 in every run, including in isolation.

### 2026-08-29 — Own/others privilege split, Phase 3: Jobs & Milestones

- **Capabilities**: `jobs.update_milestones` replaced by `jobs.edit_own`/`jobs.edit_others` (job update), `jobs.release_retention`, `milestones.edit_own`/`edit_others` (define/edit the milestone set AND mark a milestone complete — see below), `milestones.invoice`, `job_notes.edit_own`/`edit_others`, `job_photos.edit_own`/`edit_others`, `variation_orders.edit_own`/`edit_others`, `variation_orders.apply`. Per the user's own explicit choice, delete capabilities were skipped entirely for Jobs/Milestones/Photos/Notes/VariationOrders since no delete route exists anywhere on these resources — only Owner-only via `@OrgRoles` for anything destructive-adjacent. `job_notes.edit_others`/`job_photos.edit_others`/`variation_orders.edit_others` are reserved (no update route exists for these — create-only today), kept for shape consistency with every other own/others pair in this codebase.
- **Milestone ownership is unusual**: a milestone's "own" is whoever last replaced the WHOLE set via `PUT /:id/milestones` (`MilestonesService.setAll` now writes `createdByUserId: actorUserId` onto every row it writes), not who completes it — per the user's own explicit choice. A job with zero milestones has no owner, so only `milestones.edit_others` can define the very first set.

New `FIELD_ALWAYS_CAPABILITIES` in `capability.util.ts` (a second single-source-of-truth set alongside the existing `FIELD_OWN_CAPABILITIES`) and a 3-way `fieldAccess: "none" | "own" | "always"` param on `requireOwnershipCapability` (replacing the old boolean `fieldAlwaysPassesOwn`) express this. **Bug caught and fixed in the same change**: `getEffectiveCapabilities`'s Field branch only ever consulted `FIELD_OWN_CAPABILITIES`, so the web UI would have shown Field's "mark complete" button as hidden even though the service layer would have let the click through — fixed to fold in `FIELD_ALWAYS_CAPABILITIES` too, with a new assertion added to the existing `get-effective-capabilities.integration.test.ts`.
