- **Schema**: new `created_by_user_id` on `milestones` and `job_photos` (migration `0043`) — `job_photos.createdByUserId` duplicates the existing `uploadedByUserId` under the standard column name every other own/others module uses, backfilled from it for existing rows; `milestones.createdByUserId` is left `NULL` for pre-migration rows (no prior "who defined this set" data exists to backfill from — correctly unowned until the next `PUT /:id/milestones`).
- **Migration** (`0043_lowly_the_renegades.sql`): schema change plus a hand-appended data migration backfilling `jobs.update_milestones`'s existing Team grants onto all 13 new Phase 3 capabilities, and backfilling `job_photos.created_by_user_id` from `uploaded_by_user_id`. Applied to both the dev and integration-test databases.
- **`GET /jobs/milestones/due`** (the dashboard "milestones due" widget, S-09.12) lost its capability gate entirely — it was previously piggybacked on `jobs.update_milestones` even though it's a read across every job, same as every other unconditional `GET` route in this controller; `DASHBOARD_WIDGETS`' `milestones-due` entry updated to `capability: null` to match.
- **Web UI wired in the same phase** (per the established "future phases include their own UI" rule): `job-detail.tsx` and all five tab sections (`MilestonesSection`, `VariationOrdersSection`, `PhotosSection`, `NotesSection`) now derive their own `useCapability`/`useCanEditOwnership` checks instead of the old coarse `role === "owner" || "staff"` approximation that predated `capabilities-context.tsx`. Milestones' per-row "mark complete" button needed the same `meetings-calendar.tsx` workaround (`useCanEditOwnership` can't run inside a `.map()` callback whose iteration count isn't fixed across renders — Rules of Hooks) — resolved by reading the raw `capabilities` map via `useCapabilities()` once and re-deriving the own/others branch manually per row. Quote detail's pre-existing "Convert to job" button gained a `jobs.edit_own` check it never had (a gap from before this pattern existed, closed while touching the adjacent code).

Full integration suite (128 tests across 16 files) passes; typecheck and production build clean for `@spine/shared`/`@spine/api`/`@spine/web`. The one failure seen mid-session (`ledger-integrity.integration.test.ts`'s `TRUNCATE ... organization CASCADE` deadlock) is the same pre-existing cross-file parallel-run flake confirmed unrelated in earlier phases, not a regression.

### 2026-08-29 — Own/others privilege split: web UI now hides/disables actions the current user's Team grants don't allow

- **Gap closed**: every own/others phase so far (Contacts/Catalogue/Leads/Activities, Quotes/Meetings, Purchases) was API-only — the server correctly 403'd an unauthorized action, but the web app still showed the button regardless, so a Staff user without a grant would click Edit/Delete/Approve/etc. and get a raw error toast instead of the button simply not being there. Flagged directly by the user; fixed before starting Phase 3 (Jobs) rather than letting the gap compound further, and future phases will wire their own UI as part of the same phase's work going forward instead of a separate catch-up pass.
- **New API endpoint**: `GET /org/members/me/capabilities` (`members.controller.ts`), backed by a new `getEffectiveCapabilities` in `capability.util.ts` — one query returning the caller's full effective capability set (every `CAPABILITIES` entry mapped to `true`/`false`), reusing the same Owner/Field/Staff-Team-union resolution `hasCapability` already used, but computed once instead of once per capability. Also introduces `FIELD_OWN_CAPABILITIES`, a single source of truth for which `_own` capabilities Field always passes (previously only implicit at the two Expenses call sites), so the endpoint and the service-layer checks can never drift apart on what Field can do.
- **New web plumbing**: `capabilities-context.tsx` — a `CapabilitiesProvider` (mounted once in `AppLayout`, fetches the new endpoint once per session) plus two hooks: `useCapability(cap)` for a plain capability check, and `useCanEditOwnership(recordCreatedByUserId, {own, others})` for the own/others pattern, mirroring `requireOwnershipCapability`'s exact "own" definition (creator match, `null`/unset counts as unowned) so the UI's notion of "own" can never drift from the server's. This is UI convenience only — hiding an action the user can't use — never a security boundary; every mutating endpoint still independently re-checks server-side regardless of what the UI shows.
- **Frontend types caught up to the schema**: `Contact`, `CatalogItem`, `Lead`, and `ExpenseCategory` (both the shared `expenses/types.ts` shape and a separate local copy in `settings/panes/purchases-pane.tsx`) were all missing `createdByUserId` in their hand-written TypeScript interfaces even though the API had carried the column for multiple phases — added across all four.
- **Wired into every resource covered by Contacts/Catalogue/Leads/Quotes/Meetings/Purchases so far**: row-action menus, detail pages/drawers, and "+ New X" create buttons (including empty-state actions) across Contacts, Catalogue, Leads, Quotes, Meetings, Expenses, Expense Categories, Vendor Bills, and Vendor Payments. Several places that previously did their own coarse role-based gating (`ExpensesExplorer`'s Approve/Reject, `MeetingsCalendar`'s Edit/Delete) were replaced with the real capability checks instead of just adding a redundant second layer. Quotes' detail page also had its own "own" bug fixed while wiring this up — Send/Delete previously reused the same `canEdit` local as the Edit button even though Send and Delete are separate dedicated capabilities from Edit.
- One structural constraint documented in code: `meetings-calendar.tsx`'s per-meeting own/others check can't use the `useCanEditOwnership` hook directly, since it runs inside a `renderEventPopover` callback (invoked per-meeting during render, not a component) — calling a hook there would violate the Rules of Hooks the moment a different meeting renders. Resolved by reading the raw `capabilities` map via `useCapabilities()` once at the top of the real component and re-deriving the same own/others branch manually inside the callback.
- Verified: typecheck and a full production build (`next build`) both clean for `@spine/web`; full API integration suite (121 tests across 15 files) unaffected — `capability.util.ts`'s new export is additive, no existing call site's behavior changed.

### 2026-08-29 — Own/others privilege split, Phase 2: Purchases — Expenses, Expense Categories, Vendor Bills, Vendor Payments (S-07.9)

- **New wrinkle this phase**: Expenses is the first resource in this pattern where **Field** has real write access to their own records today (submit/edit/delete their own expense, per §2.1's existing "Submit expense: Field ✅"). The ownership-check helper (`hasCapability`/`requireOwnershipCapability` in `capability.util.ts`) previously failed closed for Field unconditionally, since no earlier resource in this pattern (Contacts/Catalogue/Leads/Activities/Quotes/Meetings) ever granted Field write access — moving the check into the service would have silently taken away Field's existing access. Fixed by adding an opt-in `fieldAlwaysPasses`/`fieldAlwaysPassesOwn` parameter (default `false`) that makes Field always pass the `_own` half only, never `_others` — Field stays fixed/non-configurable (never touches the Team privilege matrix) while keeping its pre-existing behavior. Confirmed with the user before implementing rather than assuming.
- **Also confirmed with the user**: Expense Categories has no creator field at all (org-level config, typically set up once during onboarding) — added `createdByUserId` anyway for consistency with every other resource in this pattern, even though "own" is expected to rarely matter in practice for this one.
- **Capabilities**: `expenses.submit`/`purchases.manage` replaced by **four independent own/others capability groups** — `expenses.*`, `expense_categories.*`, `vendor_bills.*`, `vendor_payments.*` (the last only gates create/delete — no update route exists for vendor payments). `expenses.approve` is unchanged (still a single capability — an approver reviewing someone else's submission was never an ownership question). - **Schema**: new `created_by_user_id` on `expense_categories` (migration `0041`). `expenses.submittedByUserId`, `vendor_bills.createdByUserId`, `vendor_payments.createdByUserId` already existed.
- **Migration** (`0042_split_purchases_expenses_manage_capability.sql`): backfills existing Team grants — `expenses.submit` → the four new `expenses.*` own/others capabilities; `expenses.approve` → `expenses.reject`/`mark_billed`/`bill_to_customer` (their actual prior gate, documented in the migration's own comment for why that's the correct source rather than `expenses.submit`); `purchases.manage` → all of `expense_categories.*`/`vendor_bills.*`/`vendor_payments.*`. Verified against the real dev DB.
- **Tests**: `purchases-ownership.integration.test.ts` (10 cases) covering all four resources' own/others behavior, legacy-unowned records, Owner bypass, and — the case unique to this phase — Field always passing `edit_own`/`delete_own` on their own expense while still being correctly blocked from a colleague's. Full integration suite (117 tests across 14 files) passes; typecheck and production build clean for `@spine/shared`/`@spine/api`/`@spine/web`.
- PRD §2.1 (21 new/changed Purchases rows), new story S-07.9 with acceptance highlights, CLAUDE.md's reusable checklist gained an explicit "Field-reachable resource" sub-section documenting the new flag, and `docs/qa-script.md` gained §13.5 covering all four resources plus the Field-specific own-vs-others distinction.

### 2026-08-29 — Own/others privilege split, Phase 1: Quotes and Meetings (S-03.13/S-01.17)

- **Scoping decision**: a much larger follow-up request ("do the same for other modules") covering Quotes, Jobs & Milestones, Purchases, Meetings, Invoices, Payments, and Credit Notes was surveyed first (research pass over every module's current capability, ownership fields, and delete semantics before any design), then explicitly phased per user direction rather than delivered as one large batch — Meetings and Quotes first (cleanest fits: real ownership signal, no workflow-action ambiguity), Purchases/Jobs/financial-documents as later phases.
- **Design decisions confirmed with the user before implementation**: workflow actions that aren't edits (send/revise a quote, and — for later phases — approve/void/issue) get their OWN dedicated Team-configurable capability rather than folding into `edit_own`/`edit_others`, since "can I edit my own draft" and "can I send/approve/void" are different questions. Financial-document modules (Invoices/Payments/Credit Notes, later phases) will get independent capability families rather than continuing to piggyback on `invoices.manage`.
- **Quotes**: `quotes.manage` replaced by `quotes.edit_own`/`edit_others`/`delete_own`/`delete_others` (gating create/update/delete, all already draft-only at the service level) plus two new dedicated capabilities, `quotes.send` and `quotes.revise`, for the one-way status-transition routes. `quotes.approve_discount` unaffected. Ownership check runs in `QuotesService` BEFORE the existing draft-only status check, so a non-owner gets a 403 (missing capability) rather than a 400 (wrong status) on a non-draft quote — verified with a dedicated test. `jobs.controller.ts`'s variation-order-create route (previously `quotes.manage`) now uses `quotes.edit_own` as the closest equivalent until Jobs gets its own capability family in a later phase.
- **Meetings**: `meetings.manage` replaced by `meetings.edit_own`/`edit_others`/`delete_own`/`delete_others`, keyed on `organizerUserId` (meetings have no separate `createdByUserId` — the organizer set at create time is the ownership signal, same "assigned person" pattern as leads' `ownerUserId`). This is layered on top of, and completely independent from, the pre-existing read-visibility system (private/org + invite list) — verified explicitly that the ownership split never widens who can SEE a meeting.
- **No schema migration needed** — both `quotes.createdByUserId` and `meetings.organizerUserId` already existed. Only a data migration (`0040_split_quotes_meetings_manage_capability.sql`, same hand-authored pattern as `0036`/`0037`/`0039`) was needed, expanding every existing Team's `quotes.manage`/`meetings.manage` grants into the new capabilities. Verified against the real dev DB.
- **Existing test fixed, not just new tests added**: `meetings.service.integration.test.ts` predates capabilities entirely and called `update()`/`delete()` directly with an organizer user that had zero Team grants — now correctly rejected by the new in-service ownership check. Fixed by giving that test's organizer a real `meetings.edit_own`/`delete_own` grant via a Team, matching how a real Staff user would be set up, rather than weakening the new check.
- **Tests**: `quotes-ownership.integration.test.ts` (6 cases) and `meetings-ownership.integration.test.ts` (5 cases), both following the established pattern (own/others independence, legacy-unowned records, Owner bypass). Full integration suite (107 tests across 13 files) passes; typecheck and production build clean for `@spine/shared`/`@spine/api`/`@spine/web`.
- PRD §2.1 (six new Quotes rows, four new Meetings rows, replacing the old single rows), new stories S-03.13/S-01.17 with acceptance highlights, CLAUDE.md's permission-model bullet generalized into a reusable "how to extend this pattern to a new module" checklist (ownership column → capabilities → service check → backfill migration → docs → tests) rather than re-describing each module separately, and `docs/qa-script.md` gained §13.3 (Quotes) and §13.4 (Meetings) walkthroughs — §6.3's older meetings-capability check updated to point at §13.4 instead of describing the now-removed `meetings.manage`.

### 2026-08-28 — Leads & Activities: same "own vs others" edit/delete privilege split as Contacts/Catalogue (S-01.16)

- **Follow-up request**: extend the Contacts/Catalogue own-vs-others split (below) to Leads and Activities, which still shared one `leads.manage` capability covering both.
- **Ownership model decisions**: `leads` gained a new `createdByUserId` column (it already had `ownerUserId`, the assigned pipeline rep — a reassignable field deliberately NOT used for the ownership check, since a permission boundary must stay stable even after a lead changes hands); `activities` already had `createdByUserId` from its original schema (distinct from `assignedToUserId`, the delegated-to user). Both resources use creator, not assignee, as "own" — consistent with Contacts/Catalogue.
- **Capabilities**: `leads.manage` replaced by two more independent four-capability groups — `leads.edit_own`/`leads.edit_others`/`leads.delete_own`/`leads.delete_others` and `activities.edit_own`/`activities.edit_others`/`activities.delete_own`/`activities.delete_others` (8 total, following the same pattern as `contacts.*`/`catalog.*`). Activities' `markDone`/`markUndone` are gated as edits (`edit_own`/`edit_others`), not a separate action. `GET /leads/summary-by-stage` (the pipeline dashboard widget) dropped its capability gate entirely, becoming unconditional like every other read in this feature — it was the one remaining read-gated route.
- **Migration**: `0038_panoramic_sage.sql` (schema, `leads.created_by_user_id`) and `0039_split_leads_manage_capability.sql` (hand-authored data migration, same pattern as `0036`/`0037`) — expands every existing Team's `leads.manage` grant into all 8 new capabilities, preserving full pre-split access. Verified against the real dev DB (3 teams migrated correctly).
- **Tests**: new `leads-activities-ownership.integration.test.ts` (12 cases) — own/others edit and delete, legacy unowned records, Owner bypass, cross-resource independence (Leads grants don't imply Activities grants), and two cases specific to this resource pair: reassigning a lead's `ownerUserId` or an activity's `assignedToUserId` to a user with no grants does NOT let that user edit the record — only the actual creator (or someone with `_others`) can. Full integration suite (96 tests across 11 files) passes cleanly when run without cross-file interference; confirmed the one flaky failure mode seen mid-session (`ledger-integrity.integration.test.ts`'s `TRUNCATE ... organization CASCADE` colliding with other files' in-flight orgs when many integration files run concurrently) is pre-existing test-isolation debt in that file, unrelated to this change — reproduced it disappearing when that file is excluded or run alone.
- Privilege-matrix UI required no new code — the existing generic `group`-driven rendering (built for Contacts/Catalogue) picked up "Manage Leads" and "Manage Activities" as two more collapsible groups automatically from the updated `CAPABILITY_LABELS`.
- PRD §2.1 (new table rows, S-01.16 story + acceptance highlight) and CLAUDE.md's permission-model bullet rewritten to cover all four resources generically; `docs/qa-script.md` gained a new §13.2 walkthrough covering the Leads/Activities-specific reassignment-vs-ownership distinction.

### 2026-08-28 — Contacts & Catalogue: "own vs others" edit/delete privilege split, independent per resource (S-01.15/S-02.5)

- **Feature request**: an Owner wanted every Staff user to always see every contact/catalogue item regardless of creator (already true — read was never gated), but wanted finer control over *editing/deleting*: some Teams should only touch records they created, others should be able to touch anyone's, independently for edit vs. delete, and — per explicit follow-up UI direction — independently for Contacts vs. Catalogue too, not one shared grant covering both.
- **PRD/CLAUDE.md updated first, then revised again mid-implementation**: `docs/archive/spine-prd.md` §2.1's permission table and FEAT-01/FEAT-02 (new stories S-01.15, S-02.5), plus a CLAUDE.md permission-model bullet. The first pass shared one capability family across both resources; a follow-up UI mockup made clear Contacts and Catalogue needed fully independent grants and a grouped matrix UI, so the capability list, migration, service wiring, and both docs were revised a second time before this shipped.
- **Capabilities**: the single `contacts.manage` capability is replaced by **two independent four-capability groups** — `contacts.edit_own`/`contacts.edit_others`/`contacts.delete_own`/`contacts.delete_others` for Contacts, and `catalog.edit_own`/`catalog.edit_others`/`catalog.delete_own`/`catalog.delete_others` for Catalogue (8 total, not shared). A ninth capability, `leads.manage`, was split out for Leads/Activities (explicitly out of scope for the ownership split) since they were also piggybacking on `contacts.manage`.
- **Schema**: new nullable `created_by_user_id` column on `contacts` and `catalog_items` (migration `0035_real_molten_man.sql`), set once at creation, never reassigned. A `null` creator (legacy pre-migration rows) is treated as unowned — only the `_others` capability can touch it, never `_own`.
- **Enforcement moved from route guard to service layer** for update/archive/restore/delete: `@RequireCapability` can't express "own vs others" at the route level since ownership depends on the record, which isn't loaded until the service runs. New `apps/api/src/auth/capability.util.ts` (`hasCapability`, `requireOwnershipCapability`) is called from `ContactsService`/`CatalogService` right after their existing read-before-write lookup, each against its own resource's capability family. `create` uses a simple `@RequireCapability("contacts.edit_own")`/`@RequireCapability("catalog.edit_own")` at the controller, since a brand-new record is always "own" the instant it's created.
- **Upgrade migrations** (hand-authored, same pattern as the earlier `0033_backfill_meetings_manage_capability.sql`): `0036_split_contacts_manage_capability.sql` expands every existing Team's `contacts.manage` grant into `contacts.*`/`catalog.*`/`leads.manage` (all sharing the same value initially, since they were one capability); `0037_split_catalog_from_contacts_capability.sql` then copies each `contacts.edit_own`/etc. grant into the matching `catalog.*` capability, since that's the only value that preserves a team's actual pre-split Catalogue access (it was the same check as Contacts until this point). Both verified against the real dev DB (3 teams migrated correctly at each step) and safe to re-run (`WHERE NOT EXISTS` guarded).
- **Privilege-matrix UI** (`team-detail-view.tsx`): capabilities sharing a new optional `group` field on `CAPABILITY_LABELS` now render nested under one header row that's actually collapsible — a chevron + label acts as the expand/collapse toggle (local `collapsedGroups` state, defaults expanded), separate from the header's own "grant all in this group" switch, so clicking one never fires the other. "Manage Contacts" and "Manage Catalogue" are the first two groups, each listing its four own/others rows underneath when expanded. Toggling a group switch sends all four grants in one `PUT .../privileges` call; toggling an individual row still works as before. The grouping is generic (driven by the `group` field, not hardcoded to these two resources), so a future capability group can opt in the same way.
- **Tests**: `contacts-catalog-ownership.integration.test.ts` (9 cases) covering own-record edit/delete succeeding with only the `_own` grant, others'-record edit/delete requiring the `_others` grant, the two grants being independent of each other, legacy unowned records requiring `_others`, Owner bypassing the check entirely, and — the case added for the independent-groups revision — a Team with only `contacts.edit_own` granted being correctly blocked from editing a Catalogue item. Full integration suite (84 tests) passes; typecheck clean across `@spine/shared`/`@spine/api`/`@spine/web`.
- `docs/qa-script.md`'s §13.1 walkthrough rewritten for the grouped/independent UI — two Staff accounts in different Teams, explicitly verifying Contacts and Catalogue grants don't leak into each other.

### 2026-08-28 — Fix: invited Staff users got a phantom solo org, which could silently scope their session to it instead of the real org (user-reported)

- **Bug**: a Staff user invited by email, who signed up and accepted the invitation, would see zero contacts/catalogue items after signing out and back in — the API returned real empty arrays (`GET /contacts`, `GET /catalog-items`), not a 403 or client-side rendering issue.
- **Root cause**: `databaseHooks.user.create.after` in `apps/api/src/auth/auth.ts` unconditionally created a brand-new solo organisation for **every** signup, including a user signing up purely to accept a pending invitation (the `/signup?inviteId=` flow). That user ends up with two memberships — the throwaway solo org plus the real invited org after accepting. `databaseHooks.session.create.after` re-runs on every login (not just first signup) and backfills `activeOrganizationId` from `member` whenever unset; its original unordered `.limit(1)` query could non-deterministically pick either membership, sometimes silently re-scoping a re-logged-in Staff user back onto their empty solo org with no error at all.
- **Fix**: `user.create.after` now checks server-side for a pending, unexpired `invitation` row matching the signing-up user's email and skips org creation entirely when one exists — an invited user gets **zero** memberships at signup and exactly **one** (the real org) once they accept, never a phantom solo org in the first place. `session.create.after`'s fallback query also now orders by `member.createdAt` DESC (most-recently-joined org wins) as defense-in-depth for any legitimate multi-org case, rather than accepting whatever unordered row Postgres returns first.
- **Verification**: live-reproduced against the real dev DB before writing the fix (owner signup → invite staff → staff signup → staff accepts → staff signs out/in again), confirming the wrong org was picked; confirmed fixed after the change. Turned into a permanent regression test, `signup.integration.test.ts`'s new `"does not create a throwaway solo org for a user signing up to accept a pending invitation"` case, asserting zero memberships pre-accept, exactly one post-accept, and the correct active org after a fresh re-login. Full `src/auth`, `src/modules/teams`, `src/modules/org` integration suites (37 tests) pass. Also manually confirmed against the real reported accounts (`hp@gmail.com` owner / `sk@gmail.com` invited staff) after cleaning up the pre-existing phantom org their earlier signup had created.
- Not a permissions/capability bug — confirmed while investigating that `GET /contacts`/`GET /catalog-items` already carry no capability or ownership-based read restriction (any authenticated org member can read); this was purely a session/org-scoping defect.

### 2026-08-28 — S-07.6 web UI: "Bill to customer" action on the expense detail drawer

- **Gap closed**: `POST /expenses/:id/mark-billed` (S-07.6's backend half) has existed since Phase 4 Stage 2, but required a caller to already have created an invoice line and pass its id — no web action ever called it, flagged as a known gap.
- **Design decision**: chose expense-first over invoice-first, and "create a brand-new invoice" over "append to an existing draft." The codebase's only precedent for converting one entity into an invoice (`MilestonesService.invoiceMilestone` / `InvoicesService.createFromMilestone`) always creates a fresh draft invoice, entity-first from the source entity's own detail view — never appends a line into an existing draft's `InvoiceLineEditor`. Appending to an existing draft would have needed new, unprecedented `InvoicesService` logic; this instead reuses the exact same shape already proven for milestones.
- **Scope**: expenses have no `contactId` of their own — only an optional `jobId` (a job's `contactId` is who gets billed). "Bill to customer" is therefore only actionable when the expense has a job attached; an expense logged without one shows an inline explanatory note instead of the button, rather than adding a new "pick an arbitrary contact" UI pattern.
- New `ExpensesService.createInvoiceFromExpense` (`apps/api/src/modules/purchases/expenses.service.ts`) composes `InvoicesService.create` (a new `type: "standard"` draft invoice, one line for the expense's gross amount — `amount + taxAmount`, untaxed, matching `markBilled`'s own "reimburses the gross amount, no re-taxing" doc comment) with `markBilled` in one server-side action, mirroring `invoiceMilestone`'s exact two-service composition (each service keeps its own transaction boundary, retry-safety via `IdempotencyInterceptor`, not a shared transaction). New `POST /expenses/:id/bill-to-customer` controller route (`owner`/`staff`, `invoices.manage`, same gate as `mark-billed`). `PurchasesModule` now imports `InvoicesModule` for `InvoicesService` (no circular dependency — confirmed `InvoicesModule`'s own import graph has no path back to `PurchasesModule`).
- Web: expense detail drawer (`apps/web/src/app/(app)/expenses/expense-detail-drawer.tsx`) gained a "Bill to customer" footer button (visible once approved + billable + has a job + not already billed), a confirm dialog, and a redirect to the new invoice on success — mirrors `jobs/[id]/milestones-section.tsx`'s "Raise invoice" → `window.location.href` pattern exactly, same as `invoiceMilestone`'s own web counterpart. An expense that's billable but has no job shows an inline info alert explaining why the button isn't there instead of silently omitting it. The "Billable" field now reads "Yes — billed" once `billedOnInvoiceLineId` is set.
- Verified end-to-end against the real running dev API via curl (fresh throwaway org, not the shared seeded one): created a job/contact/expense, approved it, called `bill-to-customer` — got back a real draft invoice with the correct `contactId` (matching the job's contact) and a line totaling `amount + taxAmount`; confirmed a second call correctly 400s ("already been billed"); confirmed `GET /expenses/:id` reflects the new `billedOnInvoiceLineId`. Also verified via `pnpm --filter @spine/api typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @spine/api build` (catches DI wiring issues a typecheck alone wouldn't), and `pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck` — all clean.
- Not visually verified in a browser (no browser-automation tooling in this environment, same limitation noted throughout this project) — worth a manual click-through of the new button/dialog/redirect alongside any future click-through pass.

### 2026-08-12 — Fix: invite/visibility fields were missing from the actual create/edit meeting dialog (user-reported)

- **Bug**: the meeting invites feature below shipped with attendee/visibility editing reachable only via a follow-up popup after CREATING a new meeting, and a "Manage attendees" icon in a sidebar list — never inside the actual "New meeting"/"Edit meeting" dialog itself, where a user naturally looks for it. Editing an existing meeting had no attendee access from its own dialog at all.
- **Fix**: `@spine/ui`'s `Calendar` gained a new `renderExtraFields` prop — a generic escape hatch for consumer-specific fields the built-in event editor has no concept of, rendered inline in the same create/edit dialog, right where `contactOptions`' optional Contact field already renders (same "generic slot fed consumer-owned data" shape, not a meetings-specific addition to the shared component). `onEventCreate`/`onEventUpdate` both gained an additive second `extra?: Record<string, unknown>` parameter carrying whatever `renderExtraFields` last reported via its `setExtra` callback — backward compatible, every existing caller that ignores the second argument (the design-system demo page) is unaffected. New meetings-app-local `MeetingAttendeesFields` component fills this slot with the visibility toggle + attendee `MultiSelect`, replacing the old post-create-only popup — both create and edit now save visibility/attendees in the same action as the rest of the form, no separate step. The sidebar's "Manage attendees" entry point (`MeetingAttendeesPanel`) still exists separately for viewing response status and self-service accept/decline/tentative, which don't belong in the create/edit form.
- A real second bug caught while building the fix, before it shipped: naively seeding the picker's local `visibility` state to `"private"` unconditionally would have silently flipped an `org`-visibility meeting back to private the moment someone opened its edit dialog and clicked Save without touching that section — `MeetingAttendeesFields` now receives the meeting's actual current `visibility` as `initialVisibility` and re-seeds from it (not just on first mount, but on every distinct meeting the dialog is reused for, since Calendar's editor dialog is a single reused component instance, not remounted per open).
- CLAUDE.md's `@spine/ui`-component-change rule applied in the same change: `apps/design-system`'s Calendar doc page gained the new `renderExtraFields`/widened-callback-signature prop-table rows plus a live demo section (`ExtraFieldsDemo`, a minimal text-field stand-in, since a real attendee picker needs org-member data the design-system app doesn't have).
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @spine/ui`/`@spine/web`/`@spine/design-system` all typecheck clean; both apps' production builds succeed; `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` (62 tests, unaffected — this is a pure frontend fix) still passes.

### 2026-08-12 — Meeting invites, private/org visibility, and reminder notifications (S-01.10 → S-01.12, S-10.20 → S-10.22)

- **Outlook-style meeting invites, requested by the user.** Every meeting now has a `visibility` (`private`, default — only the organizer and invited attendees can see it — or `org`, visible to everyone) and an invite list (new `meeting_attendees` table: `userId` nullable with `ON DELETE SET NULL` so a departed member's historical attendance record survives their removal, `status` invited/accepted/declined/tentative, unique on `(meetingId, userId)`). This closes a real pre-existing gap: `GET /meetings`/`GET /meetings/:id`/the dashboard's "upcoming meetings" widget had **zero read-side visibility filtering** before this change — any org member could list or fetch any meeting in the org via the API regardless of who organized it. `MeetingsService.list`/`getOne`/`upcomingForDashboard` now all enforce it server-side (never a client-side filter of an already-fetched list): Owner sees everything per §2.1's blanket-access rule; Staff/Field only see `org`-visibility meetings or `private` ones they organize or are invited to; `getOne` 404s (never 403s) on an invisible private meeting so its existence can't leak via a status-code side channel.
- **New `meetings.manage` capability** (Team-configurable) replaces meetings' previous piggyback on `contacts.manage` for create/update/delete. A hand-authored backfill migration (`0033_backfill_meetings_manage_capability.sql`, following `0022`'s idempotent style) copies each existing team's `contacts.manage` grant onto `meetings.manage`, so no existing Staff member silently loses meeting-management access at deploy. Read access to a meeting is explicitly independent of this capability — see CLAUDE.md's updated permission-model section.
- **Self-service accept/decline/tentative** (`POST /meetings/:id/respond`, no capability gate, only requires an attendee row) — an attendee's first response never notifies the organizer (the invite notification already covered that moment); a later change (e.g. accepted → declined) does, via a new `meeting_response_changed` notification. The organizer gets a synthetic, pre-accepted `meeting_attendees` row at creation time so reminder/response logic never has to special-case "is this the organizer."
- **`NotificationsService.notify()` gained `recipientUserIds`** alongside its existing `recipientRoles`, for targeting specific people rather than a role — the trap guarded against (and covered by a dedicated integration test): passing only `recipientUserIds` must NOT also silently default-include every Owner via the old `roles ?? ["owner"]` fallback. Three new event types: `meeting_invited`, `meeting_removed`/`meeting_cancelled`, `meeting_response_changed` — all delivered through the existing three channels (in-app, email, push) with no UI change needed, since the notification panel already renders any `{type, message, link}` generically.
- **`meeting_starting_soon` reminder — the first genuinely time-triggered (not action-triggered) job in this codebase.** `QueueService` gained a `schedule(queueName, cron, data?)` wrapper (pg-boss v12.27 supports `boss.schedule()`, but had zero callers before this). A new `MeetingReminderWorker` polls every 5 minutes (`*/5 * * * *`) rather than scheduling a one-shot job per meeting at creation — a one-shot approach would need rescheduling/cancelling on every edit, attendee change, or delete, which a poll sidesteps entirely. Only accepted/tentative attendees are reminded, never declined ones. Recurring meetings (rule-based, not stored as individual occurrences) are reminded before **every** occurrence, not just the first ever — a new `remindedForOccurrenceStart` column tracks which specific occurrence an attendee was last reminded for, compared against a minimal self-contained "next occurrence on/after now" stepper (no date-fns dependency added to `apps/api`; mirrors `@spine/ui`'s `calendar-utils.ts` semantics without duplicating its full range-expansion machinery, since the worker only ever needs the single next occurrence). Lead time resolves per-user override → org default (`settings` key `meeting_reminder_lead_minutes`) → hardcoded 15-minute fallback; both the org default (new Settings pane) and the per-user override (new Profile & Preferences control, `PUT /users/me/meeting-reminder-lead-minutes`) are editable in the web UI.
- **Frontend**: the attendee picker and visibility toggle live entirely in `apps/web/src/app/(app)/meetings/` (new `MeetingAttendeesPanel`), deliberately NOT added to `@spine/ui`'s generic `Calendar`/`CalendarEventEditor` — those have no attendee/visibility concept and CLAUDE.md requires an `apps/design-system` doc-page update for any `@spine/ui` API change, real process cost for a feature only this one page needs (matching existing precedent: `meetings-calendar.tsx` already owns its own delete-confirmation flow around the generic `Calendar` for the same reason). Since `Calendar`'s `onEventUpdate` fires identically for a drag-move and a full dialog save with no way to distinguish the source, attendee/visibility editing happens via a follow-up dialog right after creating a new meeting, plus a "Manage attendees" entry point in a new sidebar "Upcoming" list — drag/resize updates always preserve a meeting's existing visibility/attendees untouched. Notification deep links (`/meetings?id=...`) fetch that specific meeting and open its attendees panel.
- **Tests**: `meetings.service.integration.test.ts` (11 tests — full visibility matrix across Owner/organizer/invited/outsider, `getOne` throws `NotFoundException` not `ForbiddenException`, the organizer's synthetic attendee row, `respond()`'s first-response-is-silent/redundant-is-noop behavior), `notifications.service.recipient-targeting.integration.test.ts` (4 tests — the `recipientUserIds`-must-not-leak-to-Owners trap, roles-only/userIds-only/neither/both all asserted against real persisted `notifications` rows), `meeting-reminder.worker.integration.test.ts` (7 tests — exactly-once delivery via an injectable `now`, idempotency against a second tick, declined-never-reminded, all three lead-time resolution tiers), plus 2 new cases in `capability.guard.integration.test.ts` for `meetings.manage`. All 62 integration tests pass (9 files), including the pre-existing `ledger-integrity` suite (unaffected — this feature touches no money/posting code). `pnpm --filter @spine/api build`/`pnpm --filter @spine/web build` both succeed.
- Stories: S-01.10, S-01.11, S-01.12, S-10.20, S-10.21, S-10.22 (all new — added to `docs/archive/spine-prd.md` in the same session, per the user's own explicit requirements review before implementation began).

### 2026-08-12 — Fix `ReorderableList`'s drag-and-drop for grid layouts (user-reported)

- **Bug**: dragging a widget diagonally (top-right → bottom-left, bottom-left → top-right) or between two cards on the same row didn't work. Root cause: `ReorderableItem`'s drop-position check compared pointer Y against the target card's own vertical midpoint — correct for a single-column list (where every item shares one X position, so Y alone always determines before/after), but wrong the moment the dashboard's redesign (same day, previous entry) put this component inside a 2-column CSS grid. In a grid, array order and 2D visual position diverge: two cards in the same row share a Y range, so a Y-only check can't distinguish "drop to my left" from "drop to my right," and it has no way to reason about a diagonal drag at all.
- **Fix**: `ReorderableItem` now detects, once per drag, whether its container actually lays out in more than one column (`hasMultipleColumns` — checks whether any two of the container's direct children share a top offset) and switches the decision axis accordingly: a single-column list still uses the Y-midpoint check exactly as before (unchanged behavior, zero regression risk for any future row-list consumer), a multi-column grid uses the X-midpoint of whichever card is currently being hovered instead — since a grid's true array neighbors are its left/right siblings, not the card above/below. This resolves same-row moves (X now unambiguous) and diagonal moves (whichever card you drop on is the target; X-half of that card decides before/after, with no dependency on where the drag started).
- No new dependency, no change to `ReorderableList`'s own `moveItem` splice logic (already correct — it was only ever fed a wrong `dropBefore` value for the 2D case) or to any consuming code (`DashboardShell`, the design-system demo page) — the fix is entirely inside `ReorderableItem`'s own `onDragOver` handler.
- Verified: typecheck clean across `@spine/ui`/`@spine/web`/`@spine/design-system`; both apps' production builds succeed; `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` (38 tests, unaffected — this is a pure frontend component fix) passes; live server-rendered HTML confirmed no runtime error. **Same caveat as every dashboard v2 stage**: the actual drag behavior (same-row swap, diagonal move) was reasoned through and fixed at the algorithm level, not visually confirmed in a browser — no browser-automation tooling exists in this environment.

### 2026-08-12 — Dashboard v2 Stage 5 follow-up: drag the real widget cards, not a separate text list (user-reported)

- **User-reported UX problem, same day as Stage 5 landing**: the original "Customize dashboard" flow swapped the entire widget grid for a plain vertical text list (label + drag handle + eye icon, no live preview) while editing, only showing the real result after clicking "Done" — the user was rearranging blind. Presented three alternatives (drag the real cards in place, a no-drag checkbox+arrows panel, or dropping customization entirely); user picked dragging the real cards.
- **`packages/ui/src/components/reorderable-list.tsx` generalized** — `ReorderableItem` no longer imposes a fixed row-flex visual (grip icon + label + eye icon inline); it's now a bare drag/drop wrapper with no opinion on its children's layout, so it can wrap an entire widget `Card` instead of only a text row. `ReorderableList`'s own container `className` is likewise fully caller-controlled (a grid, in the dashboard's case, not just a flex column). Two new small shared primitives — `DragHandle` (the grip icon) and `HideToggle` (the eye/eye-off button) — extracted so both the dashboard's card-overlay UI and any future row-list UI can reuse the same controls without duplicating them. A new `useReorderableItemDragState(id)` hook exposes one item's own `isDragging`/`isOver` so a wrapping component can render its own drag feedback (the dashboard uses this for a focus ring around the drop target) instead of `ReorderableItem` imposing one fixed look.
- **`DashboardShell` rewritten again**: "Edit layout" no longer swaps to a separate list — it overlays a small drag-handle + hide-toggle control (with the widget's label) onto each card's own top-right corner, in the actual grid, using the exact same `WIDGET_COMPONENTS` render path as the normal view. Hidden widgets stay visible-but-dimmed while editing (so they can be found and re-shown) and disappear entirely once editing ends. Dropping onto a target card now shows a visible ring around it as drag feedback.
- **Same-row widgets given equal height** (separately reported): the grid now sets `items-stretch` (CSS grid's own default, made explicit) and every layer between the grid cell and each widget's own `Card` root — the plain view's wrapper, `ReorderableItem`'s wrapper, and the edit-mode overlay's wrapper — propagates `flex flex-1` down to it, so two widgets sharing a row (e.g. a tall chart next to a short list) now match height instead of the shorter one sizing to its own content.
- **`apps/design-system`**'s `/components/reorderable-list` doc page rewritten to demonstrate the new layout-agnostic shape — a card-grid example (mirroring the dashboard's actual usage) as the primary demo, plus a plain row-list example showing the old shape is still achievable, just no longer the component's own opinion.
- Verified: typecheck clean across `@spine/api`/`@spine/ui`/`@spine/web`/`@spine/design-system`; `pnpm --filter @spine/web build` and `pnpm --filter @spine/design-system build` both succeed (caught and fixed one real lint failure in the new design-system demo page — a ternary used as a statement); `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` (38 tests, unaffected) passes; live server-rendered HTML confirmed the new "Edit layout" button label and no runtime errors. **Caveat, same as every other dashboard v2 stage**: the actual drag interaction, overlay positioning, and equal-height row rendering were not visually verified in a browser — no browser-automation tooling exists in this environment.

### 2026-08-12 — Dashboard v2 Stage 5 (final): per-user widget customization (S-09.13) — dashboard v2 complete

- **Fifth and final staged commit.** Real, persisted per-user drag-to-reorder and hide/show of dashboard widgets — the first per-user dashboard-LAYOUT preference in the app (distinct from the existing `user.themePreference`, a single flat value, not a list). This closes out dashboard v2 (S-09.11 → S-09.14, S-10.19) in full.
- **New `user.dashboardLayout` jsonb column** (migration `0031_skinny_angel.sql`, applied to both the dev and `spine_test` databases), nullable — absent means "registry default order, nothing hidden." A single JSON column rather than a dedicated table, per the plan's own justification: the whole layout is always read/written as one atomic unit, never queried per-widget, the same flexible-shape role `settings.value` already plays for org-level preferences one table over.
- **`packages/shared/src/schemas/dashboard-widgets.ts`** gained `dashboardLayoutSchema` (`widgetKey` deliberately `z.string()`, not `z.enum(...)` against the registry — a stale/removed key must stay storable, only skipped at merge time, so a user is never blocked from saving a layout change just because a widget was removed since they last saved) and `mergeDashboardLayout` — a pure function (no React, no fetch) computing the actual render order from a saved layout + the viewer's currently-visible widget set, **unit-tested** (6 new tests: default order with no saved layout, position-based ordering, preserved hidden flags, dropping a stale/no-longer-visible key, appending a newly-visible widget at the end, and a fully-stale saved layout never crashing).
- **`PUT`/`GET /users/me/dashboard-layout`** — added to the existing self-service `UsersController` (S-10.17's Profile & Preferences), same "no `@OrgRoles`, any authenticated user edits their own row" reasoning as `themePreference`'s own route.
- **`ReorderableList`/`ReorderableItem`** — new `@spine/ui` components, native HTML5 drag-and-drop (no new dependency) matching `KanbanBoard`/`KanbanCard`'s existing idiom exactly (`draggable` + `onDragStart`/`onDragOver`/`onDrop`, drag state in a small context) — a single-list reorder only needs "compare pointer Y against the target row's own midpoint to decide before/after," which is strictly simpler than Kanban's own multi-column drop-target case that this codebase already solves in-house. Documented in `apps/design-system` (`/components/reorderable-list`, registered in `lib/nav.ts`) per this repo's own rule that every `@spine/ui` change ships its doc page in the same change.
- **`DashboardShell` rewritten** from a fixed hand-curated JSX composition into a keyed render driven by a new `widget-registry.tsx` (`WIDGET_COMPONENTS`/`WIDGET_LABELS` maps, `DashboardWidgetKey → component`). **User-confirmed design decision before building**: reordering means widgets can no longer sit in hand-paired 2-column groups (e.g. Revenue trend next to AR aging) — the layout is now one flat auto-flowing responsive grid (2 columns desktop, 1 mobile) in whichever order the merged layout produces, not fixed row groupings, since arbitrary per-user reordering can't preserve a fixed pairing. A "Customize dashboard" toggle swaps the grid for the `ReorderableList` edit view; toggling hide/show or completing a drag both persist immediately via `PUT`. The default (no-saved-layout) grid renders immediately from the registry's own order rather than blocking on the layout fetch — only the customize-mode edit list waits for the real saved state, avoiding a blank-page flash for first-time viewers.
- Verified end-to-end: typecheck clean across `@spine/api`/`@spine/web`/`@spine/ui`/`@spine/design-system`; `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` (38 tests) and the new `packages/shared` unit tests (28 tests total, 6 new) both pass; `pnpm --filter @spine/web build` succeeds. Live-verified the full persistence contract via curl against the seeded dev org: `GET` returns `null` with nothing saved, a `PUT` with a genuinely stale/removed widget key succeeds (200, stored as-is — confirming the write-time schema never rejects it), and running that exact saved payload through the real `mergeDashboardLayout` function reproduced the expected reordered/hidden output precisely. **Caveat**: the actual drag interaction and on-screen reflow were not visually verified in a browser — no browser-automation tooling exists in this environment (same limitation noted throughout this session); verification here is the data/logic layer (API round-trip + the exact merge function the UI calls), not a pixel-level check.
- `docs/qa-script.md` §15 gained the full customize-mode flow (drag reorder, hide/show, persistence across reload and re-login, restore-position-on-unhide, per-user independence) — steps renumbered accordingly.

### 2026-08-12 — Dashboard v2 Stage 4: org-wide activity feed + 3 new notification event types (S-09.14)

- **Fourth of 5 staged commits.** A "what just happened" feed across the org, distinct from the existing per-recipient notification bell (S-10.11) — and 3 new event types that ALSO feed that same bell, since they go through the identical `.notify()` trigger point every other event type already uses.
- **Architecture decision, made deliberately before writing code**: the feed reads each event's own source-of-truth table directly (5 small typed queries — `quote_events`, `payments`, `expenses`, `jobs`, `milestones`), merged/sorted/limited in application code, rather than either (a) a hand-written cross-table SQL `UNION` or (b) sourcing from `notifications` itself. `notifications` is structurally per-recipient and fan-out-on-write (rows only exist for users who were org members *at notify time*), which would make retroactive visibility impossible — a new Staff member should see last week's job-completed event, which a `notifications`-sourced feed could never show them. The 5-small-queries approach keeps each source's message text as readable TypeScript, not embedded SQL string concatenation, and avoids a type-unsafe cross-table UNION.
- **New `apps/api/src/modules/dashboard/activity-feed.service.ts`/`.controller.ts`** — `GET /dashboard/activity-feed`, session-gated only (every role reaches it; the service does its own role-based filtering — `role === "field"` skips the `payments`/`expenses` queries entirely, never fetched, not post-filtered, matching the PRD's "financial-events-excluded activity feed" requirement for Field). **Discovered and fixed a near-miss**: a `DashboardModule` already existed (S-12.9's setup checklist, `DashboardController`/`DashboardService`) — the first draft of this stage's new module would have silently overwritten it wholesale. Caught before committing by diffing against `git show HEAD:...` on the file path; the real fix folds both controllers into the same `DashboardModule` on distinct sub-paths (`/dashboard/checklist`, `/dashboard/activity-feed`), no route collision, checklist untouched.
- **3 new `.notify()` call sites**, following the exact existing pattern (`payments.service.ts`, `public-quotes.service.ts`): `ExpensesService.approve()` → `expense_approved`; `JobsService.update()` → `job_completed`, fired only on a genuine `pending/active/on_hold → completed` transition (guarded against re-firing on an unrelated update to an already-completed job — verified live); `MilestonesService.completeMilestone()` → `milestone_completed`. Each required adding `NotificationsService` to that service's constructor and `NotificationsModule` to its owning module's imports (`PurchasesModule`, `JobsModule` — no circular-import risk, confirmed against `QuotesModule`'s existing identical dependency).
- **User-confirmed product decision**: these 3 new call sites send a real email to Owner/Staff on every occurrence, same as every other `.notify()` site — there is no email-free variant of `notify()`, and the alternative (adding one) would have diverged from this codebase's established single-trigger-point pattern for no clear benefit.
- **`ActivityFeed` web widget** — full-width card, last 6 entries, relative timestamps ("2h ago", "3d ago"), each linking to its source document. Added to both the Owner/Staff and Field `DashboardShell` branches (unlike every other financial widget, Field DOES see this one — just with financial event types excluded server-side).
- Verified end-to-end against the live seeded org: typecheck and `pnpm --filter @spine/web build` both clean, `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` (38 tests, unaffected). Live-triggered a real milestone completion and job completion via curl, confirmed both appeared at the top of `GET /dashboard/activity-feed` within the same request cycle with correct messages/links; confirmed a same-status job update does NOT re-fire `job_completed` (no duplicate entry); created a real Field-role member and confirmed their feed contains zero `payment_received`/`expense_approved` entries while still showing `milestone_completed`; confirmed the dashboard page renders "Recent activity" for both Owner and Field. Test data reverted to its original state after verification (job/milestone status rolled back, throwaway Field account deleted).
- `docs/qa-script.md` §15 gained the activity-feed steps (including a MailDev email check) and a dedicated Field-feed-exclusion check; §12 (Notifications) gained a step confirming the 3 new event types also reach the existing bell/drawer with no separate wiring.

Every individual widget still independently self-gates on its own data endpoint's 403/error regardless of this role branch; the shell's role check is a layout/UX decision about which widgets to even attempt, not the security boundary.

- `docs/qa-script.md` §15 extended with the 4 new widget steps, the meeting-scope Settings toggle check, and a dedicated Field-layout check (steps renumbered accordingly).

### 2026-08-11 — Dashboard v2 Stage 1: backend data layer (S-09.11, S-09.12 partial)

- **First of 5 staged commits building out S-09.11 → S-09.14/S-10.19 (dashboard v2)**, per the requirements review and staged plan documented in this session — API-only groundwork, no web UI yet. - **`MilestonesService.dueAcrossJobs(orgId, {withinDays})`** — new. The first cross-job milestone query in the app; `MilestonesService.list` stays job-scoped (used by the job detail page), this is the all-jobs "what's due" view S-09.12's dashboard widget needs. Only `pending` milestones count as due; overdue and due-within-window are both included in one query, sorted soonest/most-overdue first. `GET /jobs/milestones/due` (`jobs.update_milestones`, reachable by Field too since Field holds this capability by default) — declared before `@Get(":id")` in `JobsController` since Nest matches routes in declaration order.

Distinct from the existing `/leads` kanban board, which groups its own full-row `list(orgId)` client-side (that board needs every lead in memory for drag-and-drop; the dashboard widget only needs totals). `GET /leads/summary-by-stage` (`contacts.manage`), declared before `@Get(":id")` for the same route-ordering reason as above.

Generalizes `dashboardSummary`'s existing "this month's income-account journal credits" computation to a selectable trailing window, one query grouped by calendar month in application code rather than N separate date-range queries. `GET /reports/revenue-trend?months=` — Owner-only, no capability bypass, same gate as P&L/Balance Sheet since it's derived from the same income-account history.
- **`ReportsService.invoicesDueThisWeek(orgId)`** — new. A thin filter over `receivables()`'s already-computed invoice list (`dueDate` within the next 7 days) — no new balance computation, matching every other report's "one source of truth" rule. `GET /reports/invoices-due-this-week` (`invoices.manage`).
- **`MeetingsService.list`** gained an optional `organizerUserId` filter (the underlying `meetings.organizer_user_id` column already existed — no migration needed) — the method itself has no opinion about when to apply it; Stage 3 owns the actual scope decision (org setting + Field's hard own-only rule).
- AR aging donut and job-profitability ranked-list widgets (both slated for Stage 2) need **no new backend at all** — pure client-side transforms of the already-existing `GET /reports/receivables` and `GET /reports/job-profitability` payloads.

An earlier planning draft had incorrectly marked AR aging and job profitability as Owner-only.

Idempotent: re-running seed reuses an existing `user` row by email instead of erroring, and a real ordering bug was found and fixed where the throwaway auto-org Better Auth's signup hook creates was being deleted *before* the new membership row was re-pointed at the real org — since `member.organizationId` cascades on `organization.id`, this silently deleted the membership the very next statement was trying to update. Fixed by re-pointing the membership first, then deleting the now-safely-orphaned auto-org only if it differs from the target org.
- **`DemoDataService.deleteAll`** extended to remove every new entity type in FK-safe order (credit notes before invoices, since `credit_notes.invoiceId` is `onDelete: restrict`; meetings and demo members last), with real per-type counts returned alongside the existing ones.
- **`apps/api/src/db/reset.ts`**: its hardcoded `TABLES` truncation list had drifted since before Jobs/Tax/Purchases/Credit Notes/Meetings/Teams existed — missing ~19 tables, meaning `pnpm db:reset` was silently leaving stale rows behind in every table added since. Fixed and verified exhaustively (every `pgTable(...)` name across `apps/api/src/db/schema/*.ts` cross-checked against the array, zero missing/extra). **Deliberately does not seed demo data itself** — user explicitly wants `pnpm db:reset` to stay a bare wipe, with demo data only ever loaded through the existing onboarding "Load demo data" UI flow, matching real first-run behaviour.
- New migration `0030_purple_doctor_octopus.sql` (`member.is_demo`, `meetings.is_demo` + its `(org_id, is_demo)` index) — applied to both the dev DB and the separate `spine_test` integration-test database (`.env.test`'s own `DATABASE_URL`, which needed the same migration run against it manually since it isn't auto-migrated).
- Verified end-to-end against a live local instance: full seed → inspect every new entity type via curl/psql → `deleteAll` → re-seed cleanly a second time (confirming idempotency, including for Sarah/Marcus's reused accounts). `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` (38 tests) and both apps' typecheck pass.
- `docs/qa-script.md`'s §1 (Setup, Signup/onboarding) gained coverage for every new seeded entity plus a `pnpm db:reset` note in Setup.

### 2026-08-10 — `DemoDataService.deleteAll` count accuracy across all five entity types

- **All five counts (`contactsDeleted`/`catalogItemsDeleted`/`quotesDeleted`/`invoicesDeleted`/`paymentsDeleted`) now report the real number of rows actually removed inside the transaction, not `demoX.length`** — the same fix Phase 3 already applied to `jobsDeleted` after live testing caught the discrepancy there. ### 2026-08-10 — S-05.4: advance/deposit invoices — the last open story in Phase 2 · Money In

- **Design decision made with the user before building**: an `advance`-type invoice posts NOTHING to the ledger on issue — no debit AR, since nothing is actually owed for goods/services yet (an advance is a deposit *request*, not a claim on work already done). `InvoicesService.issue()` now branches on `existing.type === "advance"`: it still allocates a real gapless number and flips to `issued`, but skips the whole AR/revenue/tax posting block entirely (`journalEntryId` stays `null`). §7.2's own "Advance received" row (debit Bank/Cash, credit Customer Advances) is a *payment*-received posting, not an invoice-issued one, and it already existed — `PaymentsService.create` fires it the moment a deposit is actually recorded as an unallocated payment (S-06.4). "Advance applied to invoice" (debit Customer Advances, credit AR) also already existed (`PaymentsService.applyCredit`, S-05.5). So S-05.4 turned out to be almost entirely about *not* posting on issue and getting the surrounding guards right, not a new posting rule.
- **Real correctness bugs found and fixed while adding the advance-invoice guards**: `PaymentsService.create`'s and `applyCredit`'s own balance checks, and `suggestAllocation`'s own balance computation, were all still computing `totalAmount - amountPaid` — missing the `creditedAmount` subtraction added when credit notes (S-05.6) landed earlier this session. All three now correctly compute `totalAmount - amountPaid - creditedAmount`, so a payment/credit application against a partially-credited invoice no longer over-estimates its remaining balance.
- New guards across every place an invoice's "balance" is read for allocation purposes: `PaymentsService.create`/`applyCredit`/`suggestAllocation` and `CreditNotesService.create` all now reject an `advance`-type invoice with a clear, actionable error (it never posted to AR, so there's nothing to allocate a payment or credit note against) — both server-side (the actual enforcement) and client-side (`record-payment-dialog.tsx`/`apply-credit-dialog.tsx` now filter advance invoices out of their own "pick an invoice" lists, so the dead-end option isn't even offered).
- Web: the invoice builder's existing type selector (Standard/Advance/Progress — it turned out to already exist) is now backed by real behavior; the invoice PDF shows "DEPOSIT INVOICE" instead of "INVOICE" for this type; a "Deposit" badge appears next to the status badge on both the invoices list and detail page; "Record payment"/"Issue credit note" buttons are hidden on an advance invoice's own detail page (same reasoning as the server-side guards).
- Verified live end-to-end: created and issued a $500.00 advance invoice, confirmed via direct SQL that zero journal entries were posted for it, confirmed its PDF renders with the "DEPOSIT INVOICE" title, confirmed attempting to record a payment allocated to it is rejected with a clear error, then recorded that same $500.00 as an unallocated payment instead and confirmed the real "Advance received" posting fired correctly (debit Bank $500.00 / credit Customer Advances $500.00, balanced) — the actual intended lifecycle works end-to-end, not just the issue-time behavior in isolation. `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` (38 tests) and both apps' `typecheck` still pass unchanged.
- **This closes out Phase 2 · Money In** — every story in FEAT-05/FEAT-06/FEAT-09's Phase 2 scope is now built. Phase 3 · Jobs & Construction Billing is next per the PRD's own phase order.

### 2026-08-10 — S-02.3: revenue posting split by each line's own catalog-item income account

- **Closes a long-flagged Stage 1 simplification.** `InvoicesService.issue()` previously posted an invoice's entire net subtotal to one blended revenue account (the seeded 4100 "Sales — Services" default, or a caller override) — flagged in that method's own doc comment and CHANGELOG's Next-up since Invoicing Stage 1 first landed. Now posts one credit line PER distinct income account: each `item`-type line's `lineSubtotalAmount` (post-discount, pre-tax net) is grouped by its own catalog item's `incomeAccountId` (`catalog_items.incomeAccountId`, an existing S-02.3 field that was populated in the schema but never actually read at posting time until now) via a new `InvoicesService.resolveRevenuePostingLines` helper.
- A line falls back to the same default/override account as before when it has no `catalogItemId` (a free-form line never added from the catalogue) or its catalog item has no `incomeAccountId` set (S-02.3 is a PRD "SHOULD," not "MUST" — an org that never bothered configuring per-item income accounts gets exactly the old single-blended-line behavior, reached via the fallback path rather than a separate code path, so nothing changes for orgs not using the feature). Discount/tax handling is unchanged — still net-of-discount per line, tax still posts as its own single line to Output Tax Payable.
- Verified live end-to-end: created a catalog item ("Widget") with its `incomeAccountId` explicitly set to a second seeded revenue account (code 4000, "Sales — Goods," distinct from the seeded default 4100 "Sales — Services"), built and issued a two-line invoice mixing that item with a plain free-form line, and confirmed via direct SQL that the posted journal entry split correctly: $50.00 credited to Sales — Goods (4000), $100.00 credited to Sales — Services (4100, the free-form line's fallback), $150.00 debited to Accounts Receivable — balanced, and each line landed on the account it should have. `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` (38 tests, including `ledger-integrity.integration.test.ts`) and `typecheck` still pass unchanged.

Reuses the exact same `INVOICE_SEND_EMAIL_QUEUE`/`InvoiceEmailWorker` as `sendEmail` (S-05.7) rather than a parallel mechanism — a reminder IS an invoice email, just reminder-flavored copy — via a new `isReminder?: boolean` job-data flag. ### 2026-08-10 — S-05.6: credit notes against an issued invoice

- **First new document type since Quotes/Invoices**: `credit_notes`/`credit_note_lines` (`apps/api/src/db/schema/credit-notes.ts`, migration `0024_fancy_makkari.sql`). Structurally the simplest of the three — `draft -> issued` only, no void (there's no PRD story asking to undo a credit note; a mistaken one is left as a small permanent correction, matching CLAUDE.md's "nothing financial is ever deleted" literally rather than inventing a reversal-of-a-reversal nobody asked for). Always tied to one specific `invoiceId`, which must be `issued` (a credit note against a draft/void invoice makes no sense — nothing's posted to AR yet, or the posting was already reversed).
- New `invoices.creditedAmount` column (denormalized running total, same "fast single-row check" reasoning as `amountPaid`) — kept as its own field rather than folded into `amountPaid`, since a credit note reduces what's owed without any cash changing hands, a meaningfully different fact for future reporting even though both currently feed `balanceDue = totalAmount - amountPaid - creditedAmount`. Every existing `balanceDue`/`isOverdue` computation updated to account for it: `InvoicesService.list/getOne`, `isOverdue()`, `InvoicePdfDocument` (which also gained a "Credited" line item), `InvoiceEmailWorker`'s balance-due email copy, and `ReportsService.receivables` (S-06.7) — nothing double-counts or drifts.
- `CreditNotesService.issue` posts §7.2's "Credit note issued" row — **debit Revenue + Tax Payable, credit Accounts Receivable** (the mirror image of "Invoice issued") — and is blocked if the credit note's total would push the invoice's effective remaining balance below zero (a credit note corrects what's owed, it can't manufacture a negative-balance/refund-owed state). `revenueAccountId` is optional on `issue()`, same default-to-account-4100 fallback as `InvoicesService.issue`'s own.
- Web: `CreateCreditNoteDialog` on the invoice detail page — deliberately a single free-form line (description + one total amount), not a multi-line builder like invoices/quotes, since a credit note is a small one-off correction and no PRD wording asks for more. Create-then-issue happens as one atomic action (closer to how a payment is recorded in one step than how an invoice is built as a draft first). The amount is submitted as the line's tax-inclusive total with `taxRatePercentage: 0` rather than exposing a separate tax-rate field — the server's line-tax computation treats its `unitPriceAmount` as pre-tax and adds tax on top, which would have silently inflated a credit beyond what the user typed had this dialog tried to back-calculate a pre-tax amount from a tax-inclusive total. `CreditNotesSection` shows issued credit notes read-only, same pattern as `PaymentsSection`.
- Verified live end-to-end against seeded demo data: created and issued a $500.00 credit note against a $3,950.00-balance invoice, confirmed the invoice's `balanceDue` dropped to $3,450.00 and `creditedAmount` to $500.00, confirmed the posted journal entry directly in Postgres (debit Sales — Services $500.00 / credit Accounts Receivable $500.00, balanced), confirmed a second over-credit attempt (a credit note total exceeding the invoice's now-reduced remaining balance) correctly 400s, and confirmed the receivables/AR-aging report (S-06.7, built earlier this session) correctly reflects the reduced balance with no double-counting. `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` (38 tests, run against the newly-migrated schema) and both apps' `typecheck` still pass unchanged.
- Not built (explicitly out of scope for this pass, flagged in Next-up): demo-data seeding doesn't yet include a sample credit note (PRD §11.3's seed-data spec doesn't call for one specifically, unlike its "3 jobs"/"retention"/"expenses" callouts); no standalone `/credit-notes` list page (reachable only from the invoice it corrects, same "invoice-triggered, not yet a standalone page" scope Payments started with before S-06.4 gave it a `/payments` page of its own).
