### 2026-08-10 — S-06.6 receipt PDF, and a real cross-cutting bug fix: `CapabilityGuard` was silently no-op'ing "no active org" 403s on every `@RequireCapability` route over real HTTP

- **S-06.6 — receipt PDF**, exact structural mirror of `InvoicePdfService`/`InvoicePdfDocument` (`apps/api/src/modules/pdf/payment-pdf.service.ts` + `payment-pdf.template.tsx`): renders a payment's own stored `payments`/`payment_allocations` rows (never re-reads invoices for current data, matching CLAUDE.md's "documents snapshot their data" spirit extended to a receipt) into a branded PDF — business logo/name/address, received-from/date/method/reference, an "Applied to" table when allocated to one or more invoices, amount received, and a "held as credit" line when partially/fully unallocated (S-06.4). `GET /payments/:id/pdf` (live-rendered, same convention as `InvoicesController.getPdf`) and `POST /payments/:id/send-receipt` (synchronous — not queued via pg-boss like `InvoiceEmailWorker`, since a receipt resend is a low-volume, user-initiated single action, not something issued in bulk; see `PaymentsService.sendReceiptEmail`'s own doc comment) are both new. `payment-detail-drawer.tsx` gained "Download PDF" and "Email receipt" buttons in its footer, same pattern as `invoice-detail.tsx`'s own PDF/email buttons. The payment-creation confirmation email (`sendConfirmation`, unchanged) deliberately still doesn't attach the PDF — it fires synchronously inside `create()`'s post-commit path, and a slow PDF render has no business blocking or risking that confirmation; the PDF is opt-in via the new render-on-demand actions instead.
- **A real, previously-undetected bug found and fixed while verifying the above against a real running server**: every `@RequireCapability`-gated POST endpoint (invoices `issue`/`void`/`send-email`, payments `create`/`delete`, quotes, catalog, etc. — anything layered with `CapabilityGuard` on top of `@OrgRoles`) was unconditionally 403'ing with "No active organisation on session" over real HTTP, despite a valid session with `activeOrganizationId` set and an `owner` membership row confirmed directly in Postgres. `CapabilityGuard`'s own doc comment claimed Nest would run `@thallesp/nestjs-better-auth`'s internal `AuthGuard` first (since `AuthModule.forRoot(...)` is imported before `CapabilityGuard` is registered in `app.module.ts`'s `providers` array) and populate `request.session` before `CapabilityGuard.canActivate` read it. That assumption was wrong: confirmed live with a temporary debug log that `request.session` is `undefined` inside `CapabilityGuard` even on routes where `@OrgRoles`' own check on the *same request* already passed — Nest does not order cross-module global `APP_GUARD`s by import position, only by each module's own discovery order in the DI graph, and that order put `CapabilityGuard` first. This had been invisible until now because `capability.guard.integration.test.ts` (the guard's only existing test coverage) hand-builds a fake `ExecutionContext` with `request.session` pre-set directly — it exercises the guard's authorization *logic* correctly but never exercises real guard-ordering over real HTTP, so the ordering bug had zero test coverage. **Fix**: `CapabilityGuard` now resolves the session itself via `auth.api.getSession()` (the exact same primitive `AuthGuard` uses internally, via `fromNodeHeaders`), falling back to `request.session` first in case it's already set — no longer trusts guard ordering in either direction. Verified live end-to-end post-fix: a fresh signup's session immediately passed a capability-gated `POST /payments` (previously 403'd instantly), `POST /invoices/:id/issue` likewise, and the new `POST /payments/:id/send-receipt` succeeded and actually delivered a PDF-attached email through a real local SMTP server (MailDev). Full `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` (38 tests, including `capability.guard.integration.test.ts` itself) still passes unchanged.
- This is a correctness bug against CLAUDE.md's own "server-side authorization on every endpoint" rule in the sense that the *previous* behavior was fail-closed (over-rejecting, not under-authorizing) — no security hole, every affected route simply refused every caller including legitimate owners/staff — but it meant a meaningful slice of the app's actual mutating surface (issuing/voiding invoices, recording/deleting payments, anything capability-gated) may never have actually been reachable over real HTTP outside of hand-built unit-style guard tests. Worth a project-wide sanity pass (smoke-testing a few more capability-gated POST/PUT/DELETE routes for real, not just via `capability.guard.integration.test.ts`'s synthetic context) next time any of them are touched, in case there's a second, unrelated reason any specific route still fails post-fix.

### 2026-08-10 — Close known gaps from the permissions work: HTTP-level tests, invite-as-owner removal, expired-invite UX, docs

- **First real HTTP-level test harness in this codebase.** Every prior "integration" test called services/guards directly against real Postgres, never through NestJS's own routing — so `@OrgRoles`/`CapabilityGuard` were never actually exercised as a real request hits them. New `apps/api/src/test-utils/test-app.ts` boots the real `AppModule` via `@nestjs/testing` and issues real `fetch` requests with real session cookies against an ephemeral port; `members.http.integration.test.ts` uses it to cover deactivate/reactivate/promote/demote through the real controller+guard chain, including the one thing service-layer tests structurally couldn't prove — a Staff session gets a genuine 403 from an owner-only route, and an unauthenticated request gets a genuine 401. Needed `unplugin-swc` in `vitest.integration.config.ts`: Vitest's default esbuild transform doesn't emit `emitDecoratorMetadata` output, which Nest's DI relies on for parameterless-typed constructor injection (e.g. `Reflector` with no explicit `@Inject`) — without it, `Test.createTestingModule` fails to resolve dependencies that boot fine under `nest build`'s real `tsc` compilation. Full 38-test integration suite passes.
- **Owner can no longer be granted at invite time.** Now that promote-to-Owner exists (below), inviting someone directly as `"owner"` was a redundant, inconsistent second path. `POST /org/invitations` now rejects `role: "owner"` server-side (Better Auth's own `createInvitation` would otherwise allow it — its own check only blocks a caller from inviting the `creatorRole` if *they* aren't already that role, which an Owner always is); the shared invite-role dropdown (onboarding + Users page) drops "Owner" from its options. Verified live: inviting as owner 400s with a clear message, inviting as staff still works.
- **Expired invites now read as expired, not just "pending but a bit late."** The Users page's pending-invites list gives an expired row the same `bg-overdue-bg text-overdue` badge styling already used for overdue invoices, inline copy explaining the link no longer works, and switches its Resend button from ghost to secondary variant so it reads as the obvious next action.
- **CLAUDE.md's permission-model section corrected** — it previously said invitation-acceptance didn't exist at all; that's been true since 2026-08-09 (below). Updated to describe the real flow (`sendInvitationEmail` → `/accept-invite/[id]` → Better Auth's `getInvitation`/`acceptInvitation`, both requiring a session matching the invited email) and to note Owner is only ever granted via promote, never invite.
- Stories: none new (hardening/gap-closing on S-10.2/S-10.13-16's existing scope), but the HTTP test harness is genuinely reusable infrastructure — the next module wiring `@OrgRoles`/`@RequireCapability` for the first time (see the Next-up item above) should write its guard-chain tests the same way, not fall back to service-layer-only coverage.

### 2026-08-09 — Fix invite emails never sending, add pending-invite listing, Teams detail UX fixes (user feedback on the permissions work)

- **Invite emails were silently never sent.** Better Auth's `organization` plugin only emails an invitee if a `sendInvitationEmail` callback is configured — ours had none, so `POST /org/invitations` created a real `invitation` row with zero user-visible effect, no error, no log. Wired `sendInvitationEmail` in `auth.ts` (reusing the existing `EmailService`/Nodemailer-SMTP wrapper, graceful no-op if SMTP isn't configured per CLAUDE.md's degradation rule) to send a real email linking to a new accept-invitation page.
- **Built the full accept-invitation flow this unlocked** — it didn't exist anywhere before. New `apps/web/src/app/accept-invite/[id]`: Better Auth's `getInvitation`/`acceptInvitation`/`rejectInvitation` both require an authenticated session matching the invited email (they never create an account inline), so the page branches on session state — no session → prompts sign up (a new `?inviteId=&email=` query-param variant of the existing signup form, landing back on the accept screen instead of onboarding) or log in (`?next=` redirect support added to `/login`); session with the wrong email → explains and offers sign-out; matching session → shows org/role and Accept/Decline. Since `getInvitation` itself can't reveal the invited email pre-auth, added a small unauthenticated `GET /public/invitations/:id` (same trust model as the existing public quote-acceptance link — reachable by anyone with the id, throttled, exposes only email/role/org name for a still-pending invitation) so the signup link can pre-fill and lock the email field instead of leaving it blank.
- **`GET/DELETE/:id/resend` added to `/org/invitations`** — feedback item "list all users including who's been sent an invite." Lists pending invitations (Better Auth's `listInvitations` returns every status; filtered to pending here), cancels one, or resends via `createInvitation`'s own built-in `resend: true` flag (refreshes expiry, re-sends the email, keeps the same invitation id — no manual cancel-then-recreate needed). Users page now shows a separate "Pending invites" section below the members table.
- **Team detail page**: Members and Privileges are now `Tabs` instead of two stacked sections, and gained an explicit "Back to teams" button matching the existing `contacts/[id]` back-button convention (a breadcrumb's clickable middle segment alone doesn't read as a strong back affordance one level deep).
- Verified end-to-end against real Maildev (not just asserted): an invite email arrives with a working link, accepting it joins the *invited* org (confirmed via the invitee's `role`/`isPrimaryOwner` after accept, not their own auto-created org from signup), the invitation drops out of the pending list once accepted, and resend/cancel both work — including a resent email actually landing in Maildev a second time.
- Stories: S-10.2 (invite flow, now actually functional end-to-end), the pending-invites half of S-10.13/S-10.18.

### 2026-08-09 — New permission model: multiple Owners, Teams with a privilege matrix, capability-gated API, Users/Teams web area, Profile & Preferences

- **This is the PRD/CLAUDE.md permission-model rewrite** (multi-Owner with one protected Primary Owner, Teams subdividing the Staff tier with a configurable privilege matrix, Owner and Field staying fixed/non-configurable) turned into working code across four phases, plus a fifth Profile & Preferences slice. Docs were updated first in an earlier session (`docs/archive/spine-prd.md` §2.1/§4.2/§7/§9/§12, `CLAUDE.md`'s new "Permission model" section) — this entry is the implementation.
- **Phase A — schema**: `teams`/`team_memberships`/`team_privileges` tables, `member.is_primary_owner` with a partial unique index enforcing at most one Primary Owner per org at the DB level (not just application logic), a hand-authored backfill migration seeding a Primary Owner + default "General Staff" team for every pre-existing org, and Primary-Owner/default-team seeding wired into the real signup hook (not just the standalone seed script).
- **Phase B — API**: a new `CapabilityGuard`/`@RequireCapability` decorator layered *on top of* the existing `@OrgRoles` (never replacing it) — Owner always bypasses, Field always rejects, Staff passes iff the union of their Teams' grants includes the capability. Full `TeamsModule` (CRUD, privilege-matrix upsert, member assignment with org/role validation, default/last-team deletion guards). `MembersService` gained `promote`/`demote`/`transferPrimaryOwner`, each protecting the Primary Owner invariant the same way the pre-existing sole-owner deactivation guard already did. `@RequireCapability` wired additively onto every existing mutating endpoint (contacts/leads/activities/meetings/catalog/quotes/invoices/payments) — Jobs/Ledger/Expenses/Reports left alone since they don't exist yet (see Next-up).
- **Phase C — web**: a new top-level, Owner-only "Team" sidebar section with real routes (`/team/users`, `/team/teams`, `/team/teams/[id]`) replacing the old Settings-dialog `TeamPane` — gated both by hiding the nav link for non-Owners and by each page independently re-checking Owner status server-side via a new `GET /org/members/me`, since a hidden link was never meant to be the actual access control. The privilege-matrix UI renders straight from `@spine/shared`'s `CAPABILITIES`/`CAPABILITY_LABELS` — the same list `CapabilityGuard` enforces — so the UI can't offer a capability the server doesn't also check.
- **Phase D — Profile & Preferences**: a new self-service page (name/email/password/avatar/theme) reachable by every role including Field, via Better Auth's own `updateUser`/`changeEmail`/`changePassword` APIs rather than raw writes. Needed loosening `POST /files` from owner+staff to owner+staff+field (a Field user's own avatar upload was otherwise 403'd) and a new `themePreference` column on `user` so the theme setting persists server-side instead of only in `localStorage`. This app has no email-verification flow configured, so an email change here applies immediately, not with re-verification — documented as a known gap, not silently assumed away.
- Verified at every phase against real Postgres/a real boot, not just typechecked: 34 integration tests passing by the end of Phase D, a real `nest start` confirming every new route registers and DI resolves, and curl-driven end-to-end walkthroughs (signup → Primary Owner, team CRUD, capability enforcement, cross-role rejection, profile updates) against live dev servers.
- Stories: S-10.13 → S-10.18, S-10.17 (Profile & Preferences), the permission-model half of §2.1's rewrite.

### 2026-08-09 — Fix the ACTUAL root cause of the recurring org-membership loss: integration tests were wiping the dev DB

- The prior entry's fix (org-creation failure handling in the signup hook) was real and correct, but did NOT explain why the user's account kept losing its organisation/membership repeatedly, even after being manually repaired, with no code changes in between and no DB/Docker resets on their part (confirmed directly with the user: they only restart the Node process via `nest start --watch`).
- **Found the actual cause**: `apps/api/src/db/ledger-integrity.integration.test.ts`'s own cleanup runs `TRUNCATE journal_lines, journal_entries, accounts, organization RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE`. There was only ONE `DATABASE_URL` in `.env`, shared between the real local dev server and `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration`. `TRUNCATE organization ... CASCADE` deletes every row that references `organization.id` — every `member` row in the whole database, cascading further to `session`/etc. — regardless of which org they belong to. Every time that test suite ran against the shared dev DB (including by this session itself, run repeatedly as part of verifying earlier fixes — directly causing the exact symptom being investigated, on the user's own real account, live, mid-session), it silently wiped every real org/membership in the database as a side effect of test cleanup, with zero relationship to demo data, restarts, or the signup hook.
- **Fixed with proper test-DB isolation**, per the user's own choice over a narrower "don't TRUNCATE so broadly" patch: new `.env.test` (repo root, checked into git — no secrets, just a DB name) overrides `DATABASE_URL` to a separate `spine_test` database on the same local Postgres server. `apps/api/package.json`'s `test:integration` script now loads `.env.test` before `.env` (dotenv-cli is first-file-wins per key, not last — got this backwards on the first attempt, caught immediately by re-running and confirming the dev DB's org count still dropped, then fixed the `-e` flag order and reverified). CI is unaffected — it already spins up its own single-use, ephemeral Postgres container per run (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), so this override is a no-op there regardless.
- **README updated** with the one-time `spine_test` database creation + migration steps, and a note on why `test:integration` must never share a `DATABASE_URL` with local dev again.
- Also removed the temporary diagnostic logging (`requireOrgId`'s own logging, `session.create.after`'s logging, and a global `AuthErrorLoggingFilter`) added earlier in this same investigation to help catch a live occurrence — no longer needed now that the real cause is confirmed and fixed; reverted those three spots back to their exact pre-diagnostic form.
- **Re-repaired the user's account** (org + owner membership + chart of accounts) one final time now that it's actually safe from being wiped again — their session row itself didn't survive the last TRUNCATE either, so this required a fresh login rather than being invisible, which is expected and harmless.
- Verified conclusively, not just asserted: recorded the dev DB's exact `organization`/`user` row counts, ran `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` (all 6 tests passing) TWICE in a row, and confirmed the counts were bit-for-bit identical before and after both runs — proof of isolation, not just "it seems fine." Also reconfirmed `hp@gmail.com`'s membership survived both runs.
- Stories: none (dev-infra bug fix, no new scope) — but this was actively corrupting local dev state throughout this entire debugging session and probably others before it.

### 2026-08-09 — Fix: a signup whose org-creation step failed left a permanently broken, unrecoverable account

- User reported "insufficient permission" on every page after restarting the dev server, with `Organization plugin error: You are not a member of this organization` in the API logs, and suspected it was related to demo data. Investigated live against the real dev DB rather than guessing: ruled out demo-data code (grepped `demo-data.service.ts` — it never touches `member`/`organization`), ruled out a plain process restart (reproduced sign up → seed demo data → kill and restart the API process → same session cookie still worked correctly), ruled out DB/Docker resets (user confirmed they only restart the Node process, never Postgres), and ruled out Better Auth's session-refresh mechanism (read its own source: a refresh only `UPDATE`s `expiresAt` on the existing session row, never touches `activeOrganizationId` or creates a new row). Found the actual cause by querying the dev DB directly: the user's real account (`hp@gmail.com`) had a `user` row and a valid `session`, but the session's `activeOrganizationId` pointed at an organisation id that didn't exist anywhere in the `organization` table, and the account had zero rows in `member` at all — the org-creation step of signup (`apps/api/src/auth/auth.ts`'s `user.create.after` hook, which calls `auth.api.createOrganization` then `seedChartOfAccounts`) had failed for that one signup at some point, silently, while the user row itself was already committed and the login flow reported success.
- **Immediate fix**: recreated a real organisation + owner membership + chart of accounts for the affected account via a one-off script that called the exact same `auth.api.createOrganization`/`seedChartOfAccounts` calls a real signup uses, then pointed their existing session at it — confirmed live via SQL that the session now resolves to a real org with a real owner membership. No re-login needed. Script was deleted after running; it was a one-off recovery tool, not general-purpose.
- **Root-cause fix**: `databaseHooks.user.create.after` in `auth.ts` now wraps `createOrganization`/`seedChartOfAccounts` in a try/catch. On failure, it deletes the organisation (if one got created before the failure — it has no FK back to the user/member that created it, so it would otherwise leak as a permanent, empty, unowned org) and the just-created user row (its `member`/`session`/`account` rows cascade automatically via existing `onDelete: "cascade"` FKs), then re-throws — so a signup whose org setup fails now fails LOUDLY and completely, leaving no trace, rather than silently succeeding into a permanently broken, unrecoverable account. The user is free to retry signup with the same email afterward.
- **New regression test** (`apps/api/src/auth/signup.integration.test.ts`) — force-fails `seedChartOfAccounts` via `vi.spyOn` inside a real `auth.api.signUpEmail` call and asserts both the user row and the org row are gone afterward, reproducing the exact failure mode found live rather than only testing the happy path the existing test already covered.
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @spine/api` `typecheck`/`lint`/`build` all clean; `test:integration` passes (3 tests now, was 2 — the new failure-path test plus the two pre-existing signup assertions). Live: confirmed the happy-path signup flow is completely unaffected (fresh signup → session correctly gets a real `activeOrganizationId` → a guarded endpoint returns 200), and confirmed the originally-reported account (`hp@gmail.com`) now resolves correctly end-to-end.
- Stories: none (bug fix, no new scope) — though this directly protects PRD §6.8's implicit guarantee that a completed signup produces a working account.

### 2026-08-09 — Fix: clicking a later occurrence of a recurring meeting silently moved the whole series' start date

- User reported that on `/meetings`, clicking a repeating event's second-to-last occurrence moved the whole series' start day to the clicked occurrence. Real bug in `@spine/ui`'s `Calendar` component (`packages/ui/src/components/calendar.tsx`), not `/meetings`-specific — every consumer of `Calendar` with recurring events was affected.
- **Root cause**: the event editor dialog (`CalendarEventEditor`) pre-fills its `start`/`end` form state from `state.instance.occurrenceStart`/`occurrenceEnd` — the CLICKED occurrence's own computed date — rather than from the series' own `event.start`/`event.end`. Editing a recurring event always rewrites the WHOLE series (per the dialog's own "Editing a recurring event updates the entire series" copy, and `handleSave`, which has no per-occurrence branch — it calls `onEventUpdate` with the same event `id` regardless of which occurrence was clicked). So opening the editor on any occurrence past the first and clicking Save — even with zero changes — silently wrote that occurrence's date back as the new series start, since the form's `start` value was never the series' real anchor to begin with. `event.start === occurrenceStart` only for the FIRST occurrence (and always true for a non-recurring event), which is exactly why this only surfaced on later occurrences, matching the user's own report.
- **Fixed**: `CalendarEventEditor`'s edit-mode effect now seeds `start`/`end` from `event.start`/`event.end` (the series' own anchor), never from the clicked instance's occurrence dates. No behavior change for non-recurring events (`occurrenceStart`/`occurrenceEnd` always equal `event.start`/`event.end` for those, per `CalendarEventInstance`'s own doc comment) — this only changes what happens when a recurring event's 2nd+ occurrence is clicked.
- **Design-system docs updated** (`apps/design-system/src/app/components/calendar/page.tsx`'s Recurrence section) to explain this explicitly — a non-obvious "any occurrence edits the whole series, keyed off the series' own start" rule worth documenting so it isn't reintroduced by a future change to the editor.
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @spine/ui`/`@spine/web`/`@spine/design-system` `typecheck`/`lint`/`build` all clean; `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` passes (unaffected — pure UI-layer fix). Traced the actual data path end-to-end to confirm the fix reaches `/meetings` specifically: `meetings-calendar.tsx`'s `handleUpdate` sends whatever `event.start` the editor returns straight through as `PUT /meetings/:id`'s `startAt` — before the fix this was the clicked occurrence's date on a 2nd+ occurrence edit; after, it's always the series' own original start, matching the intended "editing updates the whole series, without moving it" behavior. No browser-automation tooling available in this environment to click through the actual UI, so this was verified by tracing the full pre-fill → submit → API-payload path rather than a live click-through.
- Stories: none (component bug fix, no new scope).

### 2026-08-09 — "Load demo data" now seeds business profile, industry template, and currency

- User asked whether onboarding's demo data included settings like business profile — it didn't. `POST /demo-data/seed` (the only caller is the onboarding welcome step's "Use demo data" button, which skips every other wizard step) previously left `business_profile`/`industry_template`/`currency` completely unset, so a demo org's quote/invoice PDFs rendered with a blank header and Settings' Business/Template panes showed nothing, despite the rest of the org looking fully populated.
- **New `DEMO_BUSINESS_PROFILE`/`DEMO_INDUSTRY_TEMPLATE`/`DEMO_CURRENCY` constants** (`apps/api/src/modules/demo-data/demo-data.service.ts`) — a fictional "Riverstone Builders" general contractor (name/address/industry text, no logo — seeding a fake one would need a real S3/MinIO upload through `FilesService` from inside a seed script, out of scope; the PDF header degrades to text-only exactly as it already does for any real org with no logo uploaded, so this is cosmetic, not a functional gap). Industry template is `"construction"` and currency is explicit `USD`, chosen to match `DEMO_CONTACTS`/`DEMO_CATALOG_ITEMS`, which are already construction-themed — a demo org whose data looked construction-flavored but was tagged "generic" in Settings would be a confusing mismatch for anyone evaluating the industry-template feature.
- **New `DemoDataService.seedSettingIfUnset()`** — writes a setting only if the org doesn't already have one at that key, via the newly-injected `SettingsService` (`DemoDataModule` now imports `OrgModule`). Confirmed with the user's own "is this safe to call twice" bar this codebase applies everywhere: seeding twice leaves the first seed's values in place, and — more importantly — seeding after a REAL business profile was already set (a realistic path if this were ever called from somewhere other than the pre-wizard welcome step) doesn't clobber it. In practice `seed()`'s only caller runs before any settings step could have set these, so the guard is currently a formality, but it's an explicit one rather than a silently relied-on assumption.
- **`deleteAll()` deliberately does NOT remove these settings** — same reasoning already applied to a demo contact with posted ledger history (see the earlier "Demo data now covers Invoices + Payments" entry): a `settings` row is a singleton per org+key, not a taggable/deletable "demo" row, and removing it would leave the org with literally no business profile rather than restoring some prior state (there is no prior state to restore to — the guard above already means these are only ever set once, at seed time). Leaving them in place after "delete all demo data" matches how a real org's own settings are never touched by that action either way.
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @spine/api` `typecheck`/`lint`/`build` all clean; `test:integration` passes. Live end-to-end against a real local dev Postgres: seeded a fresh org and confirmed `business_profile`/`industry_template`/`currency` all populated correctly via `GET /org/settings/:key`; re-ran seed on the same org and confirmed the values were unchanged (not re-randomized or duplicated); on a separate fresh org, set a real business profile FIRST (`PUT /org/settings/business_profile`, "Real Company Inc"), then seeded, and confirmed the real profile survived untouched — the guard works as designed, not just in the happy path.
- Stories: S-12.8/F12 (demo data), extending its existing partial coverage — no new story number.

### 2026-08-09 — Dialog follow-up #2: fix Calendar's event editor losing its height cap entirely (scrollbar gone, footer pushed off-screen)

- The previous same-day fix (migrating Calendar's event editor to `DialogBody`) introduced a worse regression, caught by the user from a screenshot: the dialog lost its height cap entirely — no scrollbar, and the Cancel/Create event buttons rendered below the dialog's own rounded border, cut off by the viewport.
- **Root cause**: Calendar's event editor is the only `DialogContent` usage in the whole codebase (checked every other call site to confirm) where `DialogHeader`/`DialogBody`/`DialogFooter` are wrapped in an extra element — a `<form onSubmit={...}>`, needed to make the Enter key and the submit button actually save the event. A plain `<form>` is not a flex container by default, so even though `DialogContent` is `flex flex-col` with a `max-h-[85vh]` cap, `DialogBody`'s `flex-1 overflow-y-auto` had nothing to flex against — the `<form>` itself just grew to fit all its content, unbounded, pushing `DialogContent` (and the footer inside it) taller than the cap could actually constrain, since `DialogContent`'s `max-h` was fighting a child that refused to shrink.
- **Fixed**: the `<form>` itself is now `className="flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col"` — `flex-1` lets it claim `DialogContent`'s bounded height, `min-h-0` overrides the flex-item default (`min-height: auto`, which lets a flex child grow past its container to fit its own content) so it actually respects that height, and `flex-col` makes it a proper flex parent for `DialogHeader`/`DialogBody`/`DialogFooter` to lay out inside. This is the same "flex child needs `min-h-0` to make `overflow-y-auto` on ITS OWN child actually engage" issue as the `settings-dialog.tsx` fix earlier the same day — same root cause, different location.
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @spine/ui` `typecheck`/`lint` clean; `pnpm --filter @spine/web` `typecheck`/`build` clean. Live: confirmed no other `DialogContent` usage anywhere in the app wraps its header/body/footer in an intermediate non-flex element the same way (grepped every call site) — this was a one-off, not a pattern needing a wider fix. `/meetings` briefly 500'd on the first request after the change (same transient Fast-Refresh recompile pattern noted in both earlier Dialog entries today), settled to consistent 200s with real page content on follow-up requests.
- Stories: none (component fix, no new scope).

### 2026-08-09 — `@spine/ui` Dialog: pinned header/footer, scrollable body (new `DialogBody`), rolled out everywhere

### 2026-08-09 — Invoice detail page now shows every payment allocated against it

- User asked to see all payments related to an invoice on the invoice detail page — nothing surfaced this before; the earlier "Web UI for Invoices and Payments Stage 1" session explicitly scoped that out.

Each row carries `allocatedToThisInvoice` — that payment's specific allocation against THIS invoice, distinct from its own `amount` — since a single payment can legitimately span several invoices (S-06.2) and the page needs "how much of this payment applies here," not just "this payment touched this invoice somewhere."

- **New `apps/web/src/app/(app)/invoices/payments-section.tsx`** — a read-only "Payments" card on the invoice detail page (each row: payment number linking to `/payments`, date, method, reference, and the amount allocated specifically to this invoice), rendered between the Lines and Totals cards. ### 2026-08-09 — Payments Stage 1 (API only) — record + multi-invoice allocation, oldest-first suggestion, unallocated credit, DB-enforced allocation limits

- Second stage of Phase 2 · Money In, continuing straight on from Invoicing Stage 1 per the user's own sequencing choice. Scoped to the ledger-correctness core (S-06.1, S-06.2, S-06.3, S-06.4, S-06.5) — receipt PDF (S-06.6) and the receivables/AR-aging view (S-06.7) are their own follow-up stage, same split pattern Invoices used for its own PDF-vs-email staging.
- **New `payments`/`payment_allocations` tables** (`apps/api/src/db/schema/payments.ts`, migration `0019_outstanding_nocturne.sql`, applied to the dev DB). A payment is recorded against a *contact*, not directly against an invoice, per §7's own data model — required for S-06.4 (a payment with no invoice yet, held entirely as unallocated customer credit). `payments.allocatedAmount` is a denormalized running total; `unallocatedAmount` (`amount - allocatedAmount`) is what a partial or fully-unapplied payment's remaining credit is. A payment has no draft state, unlike quotes/invoices — S-06.1's own wording ("record a payment") is a single atomic action.
- **New DB-level allocation-limit trigger** (`apps/api/drizzle/0020_payment_allocation_limits.sql`, hand-authored in the same style as the pre-existing `0001_ledger_integrity_triggers.sql`, registered in `drizzle/meta/_journal.json`/`0020_snapshot.json` the same way `0001` was) — directly implements §6's own F6 acceptance highlight: *"allocations can never exceed either the payment amount or the invoice balance — enforced at the database level, not just the UI."* A per-row CHECK can't express this (it's a cross-row sum), so — exactly like `journal_lines`' own balance check — it's a `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` constraint trigger that re-sums on every insert/update/delete and also keeps `payments.allocated_amount` in sync as a side effect, so the invariant holds even if a future caller ever writes `payment_allocations` directly rather than through `PaymentsService`.
- **New `PaymentsService`/`PaymentsController`** (`apps/api/src/modules/payments/`): `create()` validates each allocation against its invoice's live remaining balance and the payment's own total before writing (app-level check ahead of the DB trigger, for a clearer error message), writes the allocation rows, bumps each allocated invoice's `amountPaid`, and posts ONE balanced journal entry per payment covering both applicable §7.2 rules at once — "Payment received" (debit Bank/Cash, credit AR) for the allocated portion, "Advance received" (debit Bank/Cash, credit Customer Advances) for any unallocated remainder — reasoning that the cash received is one real-world event, not two. `suggestAllocation()` (S-06.3) is a pure read: sorts a contact's outstanding issued invoices oldest-`dueDate`-first (nulls last) and greedily fills each until the payment amount runs out, returned as a starting point for the caller to edit before actually submitting `create()`. `delete()` only allows removing a payment with zero allocations (posts a reversing entry via the existing `LedgerService.reverseEntry`); an allocated payment is permanent, matching CLAUDE.md's posture on posted financial events. `bankAccountId` is an optional per-request override (mirrors `InvoicesService.issue`'s own `revenueAccountId` pattern), defaulting to the seeded "Bank Account" (code 1010).
- `AuditEntityType` gained `"payment"`.
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @spine/shared build`, `typecheck`+`lint`+`build` all clean across `@spine/api`; `pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck` unaffected (no web changes this stage either). `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` passes, including the ledger-integrity test's `TRUNCATE ... CASCADE`, which reaches the new tables transitively via `organization`'s own cascade. Recorded a separate pure-unallocated $50 advance (S-06.4), confirmed it deletes cleanly with a correctly-linked reversing journal entry, and confirmed attempting to delete the earlier *allocated* `RCP-0001` correctly 400s.

### 2026-08-09 — Phase 2 kickoff: Invoicing Stage 1 (API only) — draft CRUD, issue with real ledger posting, void with reversal, PDF

- First work on Phase 2 · Money In (`docs/archive/spine-prd.md` §12: S-05.1's scratch path, S-05.2, S-05.3, S-05.8). Scoped, with the user's agreement, to "Invoices core first" — data model, draft/issue/void, numbering, PDF, and journal postings — before Payments, advances, credit notes, or a web UI, mirroring how Quotes Stage 1 also shipped API-only before its web builder followed.
- **New `invoices`/`invoice_lines` tables** (`apps/api/src/db/schema/invoices.ts`, migration `0018_mature_phil_sheldon.sql`, applied to the dev DB) — structurally a close mirror of `quotes`/`quote_lines` (same snapshot-on-write convention, same cascade-delete + full-replace lines, same draft-is-mutable/issued-is-immutable shape) with invoice-specific additions: `status` includes a terminal `void` (not just draft/issued), `type` (`standard`/`advance`/`progress`) and `sourceQuoteId`/`jobId`/`milestoneId` are present now as nullable scaffolding for S-03.10/S-05.4-5/Phase 3 even though nothing sets them yet, `retentionAmount` and `amountPaid` are present for the same forward-compatibility reason, and `journalEntryId`/`voidJournalEntryId` point at the two `journal_entries` rows an invoice's lifecycle can produce.
- **New `LedgerService`** (`apps/api/src/modules/ledger/ledger.service.ts`) — the first domain-facing journal-posting code in the app; previously `journal_entries`/`journal_lines` existed only as schema plus a DB-trigger integrity test with hand-inserted rows. `resolveSystemAccount(s)` looks up an org's seeded system accounts (AR, Retention Receivable, Input/Output Tax, AP, Customer Advances) by their well-known chart-of-accounts codes; `postEntry` writes a balanced entry (with its own app-level balance check ahead of the DB's deferred constraint trigger, for a clearer error message) inside the caller's own transaction, never its own; `reverseEntry` posts a debit/credit-swapped mirror of an existing entry and links it via `reversedById`, implementing CLAUDE.md's "corrections are reversing entries, never edits" for the first time in this codebase. Every future domain module (Payments, Purchases, Expenses) is meant to post through this same service, per CLAUDE.md's "posting rules live in one module."
- **New `InvoicesService`/`InvoicesController`** (`apps/api/src/modules/invoices/`) — CRUD on drafts (full-replace lines, same server-computed-totals-only convention as `QuotesService`, duplicated rather than shared per each module's own doc comment on why), `POST /invoices/:id/issue` (allocates the gapless number via the existing `NumberingService`, flips draft→issued, and posts the §7.2 "Invoice issued" entry — debit AR, credit Revenue + Output Tax Payable — inside the same transaction as the status flip, so a posting failure rolls back the whole issue), and `POST /invoices/:id/void` (S-05.8: requires a `reason`, blocked if `amountPaid > 0` since Stage 1 has no payment-unwind flow yet, posts a reversing entry via `LedgerService.reverseEntry`). Revenue posts to a single blended account per invoice (defaults to seeded code 4100 "Sales — Services", overridable via an optional `revenueAccountId` in the issue request body) rather than splitting by each line's own catalog-item income account — a documented Stage 1 simplification, see "Next up".
- **New `InvoicePdfService`/`InvoicePdfDocument`** (`apps/api/src/modules/pdf/invoice-pdf.template.tsx`) — same `@react-pdf/renderer` approach and logo-as-data-URI fetch (with graceful degradation) as `QuotePdfService`, adapted for invoice fields (due date instead of "valid until", a highlighted balance-due row when `amountPaid < totalAmount`).
- `AuditEntityType` gained `"invoice"`/`"invoice_line"` (API-side only so far — the web copy in `contacts/types.ts` has no invoice history view to wire up yet, since there's no invoice web UI in this stage).
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @spine/shared build`, `typecheck`+`lint`+`build` all clean across `@spine/api`; `pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck` unaffected (no web changes this stage). `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` passes, including the pre-existing ledger-integrity test, whose `TRUNCATE ... CASCADE` now also covers the new tables cleanly. Live end-to-end against a real local dev Postgres (isolated throwaway org/contact, cleaned up after except the org/contact/journal rows themselves, which `journal_lines.contact_id`'s `onDelete: restrict` correctly refused to let be deleted — left in place, harmless, in a never-reused org, matching this project's own established practice for this exact situation): created a draft invoice (10 × $100.00 @ 8% tax → $1,000.00 subtotal / $80.00 tax / $1,080.00 total), issued it (number `INV-0001`, journal entry posted and confirmed balanced via direct SQL: debit AR $1,080.00 = credit Sales $1,000.00 + Output Tax $80.00), confirmed editing an issued invoice and voiding an already-void invoice both correctly return 400, then voided it with a reason (reversing entry posted, linked via `reversedById`, confirmed the AR account's net balance across both entries is exactly $0.00), and confirmed the PDF endpoint returns a valid single-page PDF.

### 2026-08-09 — Fix long-flagged issues: `isCompany` partial-update bug; confirmed Catalogue delete is correct as-is

- Worked through the two outstanding items flagged in "Next up" from prior sessions.
- **Fixed**: `updateContactSchema` was `createContactSchema.partial()`, so `isCompany`'s `.default(false)` still fired on parse even when the field was entirely absent from a `PUT /contacts/:id` body — silently resetting a company contact back to "individual" on any partial update that didn't happen to include `isCompany` (e.g. a logo-only or notes-only save). `contacts.service.ts`'s own `input.isCompany !== undefined` gate was already correct; the schema defeated it upstream by never letting `isCompany` actually be `undefined`. Fixed by giving `updateContactSchema` (`packages/shared/src/schemas/contacts.ts`) its own explicit shape — every field `.optional()`, none `.default()`d — instead of deriving it from the create schema. `createContactSchema` itself is untouched, so create-time defaulting still works.
- **Reviewed, not a bug**: Catalogue's unguarded hard-delete was flagged speculatively before Quotes existed. Quotes now exists, and `quote_lines.catalogItemId` is a real FK — but `onDelete: set null` was the deliberate original design (provenance-only; every line snapshots its own name/price/tax and never re-reads the catalog item). Confirmed live that deleting a referenced catalog item correctly leaves quote lines intact with `catalogItemId` nulled, matching the intended behavior; no guard needed or added.
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @spine/shared build`/`typecheck`/`lint`, `@spine/api typecheck` all clean. Live end-to-end against a real local dev Postgres using isolated throwaway test orgs (cleaned up after, except one leftover unarchived contact in a never-reused throwaway org — harmless, doesn't touch real dev data): reproduced the exact pre-fix bug first (`PUT /contacts/:id` with only `notes` set would have flipped `isCompany` to `false`), confirmed the fix holds (`isCompany: true` survives the same partial update), and confirmed create-time defaulting is unaffected (`POST /contacts` with no `isCompany` still yields `false`). Separately verified the catalog-item delete-while-referenced scenario end-to-end via curl.
- Stories: none (bug fix / verification, no new scope).

### 2026-08-09 — S-01.9 follow-up: Odoo-style multi-calendar sidebar, activity overlay, collapsible rail

- User asked for a right-side sidebar closer to Odoo's calendar: multiple toggleable "calendars," a checkbox to overlay activities, and a collapsible panel. This app has no external calendar sync, so "multiple calendars" was grounded in real data rather than fabricated: each org member becomes a toggleable calendar (real `GET /org/members` + each meeting's existing `organizerUserId`), not a placeholder concept.
- **`Calendar` (`@spine/ui`) gained `readOnlyEventIds`/`onReadOnlyEventClick`** — events whose id is in the set skip drag/resize entirely and route clicks to the caller's own handler instead of the built-in editor dialog. Required real internal-architecture changes, not just a page-level wrapper: `handleEventClick` now checks the set before opening the editor; `TimeGridEvent` (the Day/Week draggable block) takes a new `isReadOnly` flag that swaps its move/resize pointer handlers for a `stopPropagation`-only handler (so a click doesn't fall through and start a slot-create drag underneath) and hides the resize handles; `onEventUpdate` is also guarded centrally as defense in depth. Month/Agenda views needed no changes — they have no drag, only the already-centralized click path. `CalendarEventInstance` is now exported from `@spine/ui` (previously internal-only) since callers need its type for `onReadOnlyEventClick`. Design-system docs updated: API tables, a feature bullet, and a new live "Read-only overlay" example — per CLAUDE.md's docs-drift rule.
- **`/meetings` sidebar rewrite** (`meetings-calendar.tsx`): a `Calendars` `Collapsible` section lists every org member with an avatar + checkbox (real names/ids from `GET /org/members`, matched against each meeting's `organizerUserId` — unchecking one filters it out of `events` client-side); a top-level checkbox toggles all members at once. A `My Activities` checkbox fetches `GET /activities` and overlays every activity with a `dueAt` as a 30-minute placeholder block in a neutral `slate` color (activities have no real end time, so this is a deliberately short, visually distinct marker, not a fabricated duration) using the new `readOnlyEventIds` mechanism — clicking one opens a small read-only `Dialog` (type, notes, due time) instead of the meeting editor, and it can't be dragged. All three toggle states (sidebar collapsed, hidden organizers, activities visible) persist to `localStorage`, matching the sidebar-collapse pattern already used by `app-layout.tsx`. The whole right rail collapses via a `PanelRightClose`/`PanelRightOpen` button (same icon pair the main app sidebar already uses for its own collapse, for visual consistency), independent of the `Calendars` sub-section's own collapse.
- **Fixed a pre-existing hydration bug surfaced while testing this**: `useState(new Date())` seeded the calendar's `date` at module-init time, which could render server-side with a `new Date()` several days stale relative to the client's real clock in a long-running dev session (confirmed via the HTTP `Date` response header being correct while the rendered week label wasn't — a Next.js dev-mode staleness issue, not app logic, since `toolbarLabel`'s week-range math is a pure function of `date`). Fixed structurally regardless of root cause: the page now renders a neutral loading placeholder until a `hydrated` mount effect re-seeds `date` with a client-computed `new Date()`, so SSR never emits date-derived text that could mismatch the client. Also replaced the activity-detail popup's hand-rolled backdrop `<div>` (found not to close on Escape, blocking further interaction) with the real `Dialog` component, inheriting Radix's focus trap and Escape-to-close for free.
- Verified: `pnpm --filter @spine/ui typecheck`/`lint`, `@spine/web typecheck`/`lint`/`build`, `@spine/design-system typecheck`/`lint`/`build` all clean. Live against a fresh isolated test org (a contact, a meeting, and an activity with a `dueAt`, cleaned up after): confirmed via Playwright the toolbar's week label now matches the mini-calendar's highlighted day (no hydration mismatch), the Calendars section lists the test org's member with a working per-member checkbox, toggling "My Activities" shows/hides the activity marker in a visually distinct style from the real meeting, clicking the activity marker opens the read-only Dialog (title/due time) and Escape closes it, and the whole sidebar (plus the Calendars sub-section independently) collapses/expands correctly.
- Stories: S-01.9 (follow-up polish, no new story).

### 2026-08-08 — S-01.9: meeting scheduling — new `/meetings` calendar page + contact linkage

- Not in the original PRD — user asked for a dedicated meeting-scheduling page similar to a reference Outlook/Google-Calendar-style screenshot, with contacts linkable to meetings and those meetings surfacing on the contact's own Timeline tab. Confirmed nothing like this existed in `docs/archive/spine-prd.md` (only `activities`' own flat `meeting` type — a to-do-style log entry with a single `dueAt`, not a scheduled time range), so this was added as **S-01.9** to FEAT-01 · Contacts & CRM (full acceptance-highlights text in the PRD) before being built, per this repo's established practice for new scope (same as S-10.12's addition earlier in the project). - **New `meetings` table** (`apps/api/src/db/schema/meetings.ts`, migration `0017_cultured_jackal.sql`, applied to the dev DB): `id, orgId, contactId (nullable, onDelete: set null), title, startAt, endAt, allDay, color, description, location, recurrence (jsonb), organizerUserId, createdAt, updatedAt`. Deliberately a separate table from `activities`, not folded in — a real calendar event needs a time range and optional recurrence that `activities`' flat `dueAt` was never designed to hold; `activities`' own "meeting" type is untouched. `contactId` uses `set null` (not `activities`' `cascade`) since a meeting has its own independent existence — deleting the contact shouldn't destroy the meeting record, unlike an activity whose whole purpose is being about that contact.

New `packages/shared/src/schemas/meetings.ts` (`createMeetingSchema`/`updateMeetingSchema`, `endAt >= startAt` refined) — required a `pnpm --filter @spine/shared build` since it's a built package, not source-consumed like `@spine/ui`.

Fully backward compatible — omit `contactOptions` and the field simply doesn't render, so every other hypothetical `Calendar` caller is unaffected. Design-system docs updated in the same change (`apps/design-system/src/app/components/calendar/page.tsx`): API tables, a feature-list bullet, and a new live "Linked to a contact" example — per CLAUDE.md's docs-drift rule.
- **New `/meetings` page** (`apps/web/src/app/(app)/meetings/`): composes `Calendar` (now with `contactOptions` wired from the org's contact list) with a persistent right-side rail — `MiniCalendar` (already existed, previously only used inside `Calendar`'s own toolbar popover) plus a "Meetings by contact" summary list — matching the reference screenshot's always-visible mini-calendar rather than Calendar's own click-to-open popover version. Full width, same `FULL_WIDTH_ROUTES` opt-in mechanism the Pipeline board uses (`app-layout.tsx`), since a scheduling calendar is wide-by-nature content. Meetings are fetched for a rolling ±2-month window around the visible date (re-fetched only when the date navigates outside that window) rather than computing each view's exact visible range, which would have meant duplicating logic private to `calendar.tsx`.

Migration applied to the real local dev Postgres. ### 2026-08-08 — S-01.3: per-contact Timeline tab (quotes + activities merged)

Documented at `apps/design-system/src/app/components/timeline/page.tsx` (added to `nav.ts` under Data display) with a live demo, feature list, anatomy, API reference, and a real-usage code example, per CLAUDE.md's docs-drift rule.

Wired into `contact-detail.tsx` as a new "Timeline" tab, made the default (first) tab ahead of "Contact persons", since PRD's own framing ("so I know where we stand before a call") makes it the primary view now that there's real data to show.

### 2026-08-08 — Fix: Lost column was pushed off-screen; Pipeline page now full width

- User reported the Lost column wasn't visible on the pipeline board. Root cause: `KanbanColumn` (from the redesign below) always used a fixed 272px width, and 5 columns × 272px + gaps reliably exceeded the ~1136px of content width `AppShellContent`'s 1200px reading-width cap left after the sidebar and page padding — Lost was rendering, just scrolled off the right edge of `KanbanBoard`'s `overflow-x-auto` row with only a thin native scrollbar as the (easy to miss) hint that more columns existed.
- **`KanbanColumn` (`@spine/ui`)** now defaults to flexible width (`flex: 1 1 0%`, floored at a new `minWidth` prop, default 200px) instead of a fixed 272px — columns spread out to fill whatever width the board is given. `width` is kept as an explicit opt-out for callers who want a fixed, non-flexing column width instead. Design-system docs (`apps/design-system/src/app/components/kanban/page.tsx`) updated: feature list, API table, and a new "Sizing" paragraph covering the width side of the existing height-sizing guidance, plus the live demo no longer passes a fixed `width` so it matches the new default.
- **`AppShellContent` (`@spine/ui`)** gains a `fullWidth?: boolean` prop (default `false`, preserving every existing page's behavior) that swaps its wrapper's `max-w-[1200px]` for `max-w-none` — for pages whose content is wide by nature (a multi-column board) rather than form/prose, where the cap just wastes space. Documented in `apps/design-system/src/app/components/app-shell/page.tsx`'s feature list and API table per CLAUDE.md's docs-drift rule.
- **`apps/web/src/components/app-layout.tsx`** (the one place across the whole app that renders `AppShellContent`, wrapping every authenticated page) now computes `fullWidth` from a small `FULL_WIDTH_ROUTES` pathname allowlist (currently just `/leads`) using the same `usePathname()` + prefix-match already used for sidebar nav active-state — an explicit per-route opt-in, not a global change, so every other page (Contacts, Settings, Quotes, etc.) keeps its existing 1200px cap unchanged. The page header (`AppShellHeader`) benefits automatically since it renders inside the same now-uncapped wrapper as the board — no separate change needed for "the title should be full width too."

### 2026-08-08 — S-01.8: import contacts from CSV

- Last remaining Phase 1 story per the PRD's own list (`S-01.1 → S-01.8`) — a 3-step wizard (upload → map columns → preview & confirm), not a fixed-header-template approach, since real CSV exports from other CRMs/spreadsheets rarely share one header convention. Column mapping is auto-guessed by loose header-name matching (case/punctuation-insensitive aliases) but always shown and overridable before any row is touched.
- **API**: `POST /contacts/import` (`ContactsController`) accepts an array of already-validated `CreateContactInput` rows (capped at 500 — see below) and `ContactsService.importMany()` loops them through the existing single-contact `create()` path sequentially, one per row — same duplicate-detection (matching phone/email, PRD §9's "warns but does not block"), same audit-log write, same transaction shape as a manual create, with no parallel bulk-insert logic to keep in sync. One row's failure doesn't abort the batch; each is reported independently.
- **Web**: `apps/web/src/app/contacts/import/` — `build-rows.ts` (pure CSV-row → validated-row transform, kept outside React for testability), `import-contacts-dialog.tsx` (the 3-step wizard, `papaparse` for parsing), wired into `contacts-explorer.tsx` via a new "Import CSV" button.
- **A code-review pass before shipping caught six real issues**, all fixed:
  1. **Duplicate detection missed archived contacts.** The dialog was reusing the page's own filtered `contacts` state (default excludes archived) for client-side duplicate matching — an archived contact with a matching email would never be flagged, silently re-creating it as a new active contact. Fixed by fetching a dedicated `?includeArchived=true` list specifically when the import dialog opens, not reusing the page's filtered view.
  2. **Server-side duplicate warnings were discarded.** `create()` already returns `duplicateWarning` (used by the single-contact create drawer), but the import wizard's results screen never read it from the per-row response — a duplicate the client-side check missed (e.g. against a contact created by an earlier row in the same batch) would be silently created with no indication anywhere. Fixed: the results screen now shows a "created, but possible duplicates" section per row.
  3. **A failed import request had no safe retry path.** `apiClient` mints a fresh idempotency key per call, and `importMany` doesn't roll back on a later row's failure — a network drop or timeout after the server had already committed some rows gave the user no way to know what succeeded before clicking "Import" again, risking duplicate creation. Fixed: the error path now re-fetches contacts and recomputes duplicate flags before returning to the preview screen, so anything that already landed shows up flagged rather than silently re-created.
  4. **No client-side email format validation.** A malformed email (e.g. "not-an-email") passed the preview screen as "Ready," then failed the server's `z.string().email()` for the *entire batch* at once (the whole `rows` array is validated atomically before any row runs) — one bad email blocked every other valid row with a generic error. Fixed by validating email format client-side in `build-rows.ts`, so it's caught and flagged per-row before submit.
  5. **Auto-mapping collision: a column named "Company" silently mapped to the `isCompany` boolean instead of the contact's name.** The alias list had a bare `"company"` string matching both intents; a CSV using "Company" to mean the company's name would have that text silently discarded (parsed as `false` for a boolean field it was never meant for). Fixed by moving "Company"/"company" to the `name` field's aliases and requiring the fuller `"iscompany"` for the boolean.
  6. **Sequential per-row processing risked a slow/timed-out request on a large import.** Measured locally at ~3ms/row; lowered `MAX_IMPORT_ROWS` from 1000 to 500 to keep worst-case request time comfortably bounded rather than parallelizing (which would let two rows in the same batch race each other's duplicate-detection query — a correctness regression not worth the throughput gain at this scale).
- **Verified live**: created and archived a contact, confirmed the default `GET /contacts` excludes it but `?includeArchived=true` includes it (reproducing the bug before the fix), then confirmed a re-import of a matching email against the archived contact correctly surfaces `duplicateWarning` end-to-end through to the API response. Tested a >500-row payload rejected by the cap, a missing-required-field row rejected by zod, and a 200-row real import completing in ~0.6s. `pnpm typecheck`/`lint`/`build` all pass clean across `@spine/api`/`@spine/web`.
- **User-reported UI bug, fixed same session**: the dialog's close (X) button sat visibly misaligned from the title, and the panel had a large empty area below short steps (e.g. the initial upload dropzone). Root cause: the dialog used `@spine/ui`'s `DialogContent size="lg"`, which is documented and correctly used elsewhere (Settings) for tall, multi-pane, self-padding layouts — it deliberately ships zero default padding and a fixed `h-[min(720px,85vh)]`. This wizard is a single-pane, variable-height flow that never added its own matching padding, so the title sat flush in the corner against the close button's fixed `top-4 right-4` inset, and the fixed height stretched short steps to fill 720px regardless of content. Fixed by switching to `size="md"` (which already has the correct, proven `p-5` spacing this button design assumes) with only its width overridden, restoring natural content-driven height, and aligning header/body/footer to a consistent `p-5`.

### 2026-08-08 — S-12.9: wire the dashboard setup checklist to real completion state

- User asked "what's next" after the production Docker fix; picked S-12.9 (the dashboard's "first customer / first item / first quote" checklist, previously a static always-unchecked placeholder from before Contacts/Catalogue/Quotes existed) as the last small gap in Phase 1's own story list.
- New `DashboardModule`/`DashboardService`/`DashboardController` (`apps/api/src/modules/dashboard/`) — `GET /dashboard/checklist` returns `{hasCustomer, hasItem, hasSentQuote, dismissed}` in one call: three parallel existence checks (`isDemo: false` + not-archived/not-draft, so demo-seeded data and unsent draft quotes don't count) plus the persisted dismissed flag, all from the `settings` table's `dashboard_checklist_dismissed` key.
- **Review pass caught a real authz bug before this shipped**: the original version wrote dismissal through the existing `PUT /org/settings/:key`, which is `@OrgRoles(["owner"])`-only by design (real org config shouldn't be staff-writable) — but the checklist itself is shown to and dismissible by every org member, so any staff/field user hit a silent 403 on dismiss (and on the new auto-dismiss-when-complete behavior), making the checklist reappear on every visit forever for anyone but the owner. Fixed with a dedicated `POST /dashboard/checklist/dismiss` (no `@OrgRoles` restriction, matching the read side) that writes straight to the same `settings` row rather than loosening the owner-only gate for every other setting.
- Review also caught a stuck-spinner regression in the first draft: the fetch-error `.catch` set a "not dismissed" flag but never populated `status`, so a failed `/dashboard/checklist` call left the card permanently showing its loading spinner instead of degrading. Fixed by collapsing to one endpoint/one error state — a failed fetch now hides the card entirely rather than getting stuck.
- Six parallel review passes (different angles: line-by-line diff, cross-file authz tracing, reuse/duplication, simplification/efficiency, altitude/conventions, removed-behavior) were run against this change; the authz bug and stuck-spinner bug were independently rediscovered by multiple passes, which is what confirmed they were real rather than false positives. Also fixed on the review's recommendation: the auto-dismiss-on-completion write is now guarded by a ref so a component remount doesn't refire it while a prior write is in flight, and its failure is logged instead of silently swallowed.
- Two findings were deliberately left as-is: (1) auto-dismiss is a one-way ratchet — if an org later archives its only contact, the checklist won't reappear even though `hasCustomer` would now report `false`, since dismissal isn't re-evaluated once persisted; this matches the manual Dismiss button's own semantics (a user's "stop showing me this" is durable, not re-triggered by later data changes) and wasn't flagged as wrong by any reviewer, just noted. (2) The three checklist items are hand-enumerated in both `DashboardService` and `setup-checklist.tsx` with no shared contract between them — fine at three items, would be worth a shared `packages/shared` list if a fourth item (e.g. "first invoice," once Invoices exists) gets added later.
- **Verified live**: signed up a fresh user/org, confirmed `GET /dashboard/checklist` starts all-false; created a real contact, catalog item, and quote (draft) and confirmed the flags flip on individually and only once the quote is actually sent (not while still a draft); confirmed `POST /dashboard/checklist/dismiss` persists and `GET` reflects it afterward. `pnpm typecheck`/`lint`/`build` all pass clean across `@spine/api`/`@spine/web`. Confirmed via the controller's decorators (no `@OrgRoles` on either dashboard route, unlike `SettingsController`'s explicit `@OrgRoles(["owner"])`) that the authz fix is structurally correct, matching this codebase's established "guard behavior is purely decorator-driven" pattern verified in every prior session.

### 2026-08-08 — Fix the production Docker stack (never actually worked end-to-end until now)

- User asked to review the README's dev setup instructions for completeness; that led to finding two real, pre-existing production-blocking bugs while manually running `docker compose --profile minimal up` for the first time in this project's history (`docker-compose.yml`'s production path had never been exercised end-to-end before). Neither is related to today's push-notification work — both are older bugs in already-shipped code, just never caught because nobody had booted the prod compose stack until this session.
- **Bug 1 — the image build itself failed.** `better-auth`/`drizzle-orm` declare `better-sqlite3` as a peer dependency (one of several drivers Drizzle supports, even though this app only ever uses the Postgres driver) — `pnpm install` inside bare `node:20-alpine` tries to compile its native addon and fails with no Python/C toolchain present. Fixed by adding `RUN apk add --no-cache python3 make g++` to both `docker/Dockerfile.api` and `docker/Dockerfile.web`'s base stage.
- **Bug 2 — the API container crash-looped on every boot**, even after the image built: `apps/api/dist/main.js` (compiled by `nest build`, run via plain `node` in production — no ts-node/tsx) imports `@spine/shared`, but `packages/shared/package.json`'s `main`/`exports` pointed straight at its `.ts` source with no compiled `dist/` at all. This only ever worked in dev because `nest start --watch`/Next.js both transpile `.ts` on the fly — the packaged, `node`-only runtime can't. (A comment already in `packages/shared/tsconfig.json`, written when this first bit `apps/api`'s dev runtime, documents half of this same root cause but the production/compiled-runtime half was never actually fixed.) Fixed by giving `@spine/shared` a real build step: `tsconfig.build.json` (emits to `dist/`, `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` so the `.ts`-suffixed internal imports resolve as `.js` in the compiled output), a `build` script, `package.json`'s `main`/`types`/`exports` repointed at `dist/`, `turbo.json`'s `dev` task given `dependsOn: ["^build"]` so a fresh `pnpm install && pnpm dev` builds `@spine/shared` automatically instead of breaking immediately, and `docker/Dockerfile.api` now runs `pnpm --filter @spine/shared build` explicitly before `pnpm --filter @spine/api build` (the api's own `nest build` script has no notion of building its workspace dependencies). `@spine/ui` didn't need the same treatment — `apps/web`'s Next.js build already bundles it from source via `transpilePackages`, and web has no compiled-`node`-only runtime step the way the API does.
- **Verified for real**, not just by inspection: built both production images from a clean Docker build cache, booted the full `minimal` profile (db + api + web + Caddy) against a throwaway `.env`, confirmed `GET /api/health` returns `200` through Caddy's reverse proxy, ran `db:migrate` inside the running `api` container against the real containerized Postgres (all 29 tables created, including today's `push_subscriptions`/`notifications`), and completed a real `POST /api/api/auth/sign-up/email` signup through the full stack. Confirmed `pnpm build`/`pnpm typecheck`/`pnpm lint`/`pnpm --filter @spine/shared test` all still pass at the repo root with the new build step wired in. Torn down and cleaned up afterward (containers, images, volumes); the local dev `.env` was untouched (backed up before the test, restored after).
- README updated: production section now includes the migrate step, and notes that `scripts/install.sh`/`backup.sh`/`restore.sh` (S-10.7/S-10.8/S-10.9) don't exist yet — deliberately not built this session despite the temptation, since the PRD explicitly schedules them for Phase 6 (after Jobs/Invoices/Payments/Mobile exist) and building them now would mean building ahead of the PRD's own sequencing, then reworking them as later phases add services. `.env.development.example` also gained the `VAPID_*` block it was missing (present in `.env`/`.env.example` but silently absent from the dev template a contributor is told to copy).

### 2026-08-08 — S-10.12: browser/OS push notifications (bell/panel's third delivery channel)

- User asked whether browser notifications fire when a new in-app notification arrives (S-10.11's bell/panel) — they don't; that channel only updates a badge while a Spine tab is open. Per the user's request, added S-10.12 to the PRD first (browser/OS push via the Web Push API + a service worker, distinct from a foreground-only `Notification()` popup because it must fire even with the tab backgrounded or the browser itself not focused), got approval, then implemented it.
- **Data model**: new `push_subscriptions` table (`apps/api/src/db/schema/push-subscriptions.ts`) — one row per (user, device), holding the Web Push `endpoint` + `p256dh`/`auth` keys, unique on `endpoint` (upserted on re-subscribe). Added to `db/reset.ts`'s `TABLES` list.
- **API**: new `PushService` (`apps/api/src/modules/notifications/push.service.ts`), deliberately mirroring `EmailService`'s `isConfigured()` gate — with no `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`/`VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` set, the whole channel silently no-ops rather than erroring, per §6.8's "boots with only 3 required env vars" rule. `NotificationsService.notify()` now sends push (in addition to its existing email + in-app-row channels) to every device of each `inApp` recipient. A 404/410 from the push service (expired/revoked subscription) auto-deletes that row so it isn't retried forever; any other failure is logged and swallowed — a push failure must never block the business event that triggered it. New `NotificationsController` routes: `GET /notifications/push/public-key`, `GET/POST/DELETE /notifications/push/subscribe(s)`.
- **Web**: `public/sw.js` (new service worker — `push` + `notificationclick` handlers, focuses/opens the relevant page on click), `use-push-subscription.ts` hook (registers the worker, drives `Notification.requestPermission()` + `PushManager.subscribe`, only ever triggered by an explicit user action per the acceptance highlight — never on page load), and a new "Browser notifications" Settings pane (`push-pane.tsx`) with a per-device on/off toggle reflecting `unsupported`/`not-configured`/`denied`/`unsubscribed`/`subscribed` state.
- `apps/web/eslint.config.js` now ignores `public/**` — `sw.js` runs in the ServiceWorker global scope (`self`, no DOM), which isn't a target this repo's shared eslint config's globals cover; it's a static asset served as-is, not app source, matching how build output is already excluded.
- `.env.example` documents the optional `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`/`VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY`/`VAPID_SUBJECT` trio and points to `npx web-push generate-vapid-keys`; no separate `NEXT_PUBLIC_` copy needed since the browser fetches the public key from `GET /notifications/push/public-key` at runtime.
- **Verified live** end-to-end against the real dev Postgres + a real VAPID keypair: signed up a user, subscribed a real EC-keypair-backed fake endpoint via the actual `POST /notifications/push/subscribe` route, then called the real `NotificationsService.notify()` (not a mock) with `inApp` set — confirmed it wrote the in-app row, called `PushService.sendToUser()`, made a genuine authenticated POST to Google's FCM endpoint via `web-push` (got a real `410 Gone` back since the endpoint path was fake but well-formed), and correctly auto-deleted the now-stale subscription row (2 subs → 0). Confirmed `GET /notifications/unread-count` reflected the new row and `GET /notifications/push/subscriptions` reflected the cleanup. Ran a full `db:reset` afterward and confirmed `push_subscriptions` is included (29 tables truncated, up from 28). `pnpm typecheck`/`lint`/`build` all pass clean across `@spine/shared`, `@spine/api`, `@spine/web`.
- **Not verified initially**: the actual browser-side permission prompt, service worker registration, and on-screen toggle UI — no browser-automation tooling exists in this environment. This gap was closed by the user directly: they enabled the Settings toggle, granted the Chrome permission, and confirmed a real `push_subscriptions` row was created with a genuine FCM endpoint. A manual server-side test send (`web-push.sendNotification` against that live subscription) returned FCM's real `201 Accepted`, confirming the whole server pipeline. The user then reported not seeing a notification pop up in one instance — traced (via `chrome://serviceworker-internals` and DevTools' manual "Push" test button) to two separate, non-bug explanations rather than any code defect: (1) DevTools' bare "Push" test button sends no payload, and `sw.js`'s handler correctly no-ops on `!event.data`; (2) opening the quote link fresh **did** trigger a visible native notification, confirming push → service worker → `showNotification()` all work end-to-end — the one earlier miss is consistent with Chrome/macOS's known behavior of suppressing a notification when its triggering tab is already focused. No code change was needed. ### 2026-08-08 — Fix a React key warning in Table's grouped-row mode (user-reported)

- User reported a browser console error: `Each child in a list should have a unique "key" prop` on `quotes-table.tsx`'s use of the new `Table`/`DataTable` `groupBy` mode (added for item 4's version-grouping, user feedback session). Root cause: `packages/ui/src/components/table.tsx`'s grouped-row branch returned a bare `<>...</>` shorthand fragment from inside `pageGroups.map((group) => ...)` with no key on it (the key had been mistakenly placed on the `<tr>` nested one level inside instead) — a shorthand fragment can't carry a `key` prop at all, so React had nothing to identify each group by.
- Fixed by switching to the explicit `<Fragment key={group.key}>` form (imported from `react`) and removing the now-redundant `key` from the inner `<tr>` (it isn't itself part of an array being mapped, so it never needed one).
- **Verified**: `pnpm --filter @spine/ui typecheck`/`lint` and `pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck`/`build` all pass clean. **Not verified**: the browser console itself wasn't re-checked for the warning's absence (no browser automation tooling in this environment) — the fix is a direct, mechanical correction of a well-understood React requirement (a fragment returned from `.map()` needs the same explicit-key treatment as any other list-returned element), not something ambiguous enough to need runtime confirmation beyond the type/build checks already run.
