### 2026-08-07 — Catalogue (F2): goods/services with default price, unit, tax rate and account mapping

- Second real business module in Phase 1 · Sales Spine, built directly against Contacts & CRM (F1)'s established conventions (org-scoped schema, soft-delete via `archivedAt`, `AuditLogService` writes, `@OrgRoles`/`IdempotencyInterceptor` on mutating routes, no role restriction on GETs, zod `createXSchema`/`updateXSchema = createXSchema.partial()` shared between API and web). Covers PRD F2's MUST/SHOULD/MAY scope and S-02.1 → S-02.4.
- **Schema** (`apps/api/src/db/schema/catalog.ts`, new file): `catalog_items` table — `name`, `description`, `unit` (free text, not an enum — service/fabrication businesses use widely varied units and PRD doesn't call out a fixed list), `category` (free text, MAY-level per PRD, no separate categories table), `defaultPriceAmount`/`defaultPriceCurrency` (bigint minor units + currency code, the exact `leads.valueAmount`/`valueCurrency` shape, per CLAUDE.md's non-negotiable money rule), `defaultTaxRatePercentage` (a plain `real`, not bigint — a rate, not money, matching `tax.controller.ts`'s existing `DefaultTaxRate.percentage: number` shape; there is no `tax_rates` table yet, that's FEAT-08/Phase 4, explicitly out of scope), nullable `incomeAccountId`/`expenseAccountId` FKs to the existing `accounts` table (`onDelete: "restrict"`, mirroring `journal_lines.accountId`'s own FK behavior), and `archivedAt` for soft-delete. Indexes on `orgId`, `(orgId, category)`, `(orgId, name)`, and both account FKs. Registered in `apps/api/src/db/schema/index.ts`.
- **Migration**: generated via `pnpm --filter @spine/api db:generate` as `apps/api/drizzle/0008_flat_ma_gnuci.sql` (checked `_journal.json` first — prior idx was 7, no collision) and **applied against the local dev Postgres** (`spine-dev-db-1`, brought up via `pnpm dev:infra:up`) with `pnpm --filter @spine/api db:migrate` — verified live with `\d catalog_items` inside the container, confirmed all columns/indexes/FKs match the schema.
- **Shared zod schemas** (`packages/shared/src/schemas/catalog.ts`, new file): `createCatalogItemSchema`/`updateCatalogItemSchema`. Deliberately has **no** `z.boolean().default(...)` field, to avoid repeating the pre-existing `.partial()`-doesn't-neutralize-`.default()` bug already documented for `contacts.ts` in this changelog — noted inline in the schema file's own comment as a guardrail for whoever adds a boolean flag here later. `defaultPriceAmount` uses `z.coerce.bigint()`, matching `createLeadSchema.valueAmount`'s own convention.
- **API module** (`apps/api/src/modules/catalog/`): `CatalogService` (list/getOne/create/update/archive/restore/delete, all org-scoped) and `CatalogController` at `catalog-items` (`GET /catalog-items`, `GET /catalog-items/:id`, `POST /catalog-items`, `PUT /catalog-items/:id`, `POST /catalog-items/:id/archive`, `POST /catalog-items/:id/restore`, `DELETE /catalog-items/:id`). Every mutating route carries `@OrgRoles(["owner", "staff"])` + `@UseInterceptors(IdempotencyInterceptor)`; GETs carry neither, per §2.1's "Manage contacts & catalogue: Owner/Staff mutate, Field reads" permission row. `CatalogModule` (previously an empty `@Module({})` stub) now wires `CatalogController`/`CatalogService`, imports `AuditModule`, and exports `CatalogService` for a future Quotes module to depend on. `AppModule` already imported `CatalogModule` from a prior session — no change needed there.
- **`POST /catalog-items` is self-contained by design** (S-02.4 — "add an item inline while building a quote"): it takes only the org id and the create payload, no quote/document context of any kind, so a future Quotes line-item builder can call it directly from an inline "+ New item" affordance without any change to this endpoint. Documented in `CatalogService.create`'s own comment.
- **Audit log**: extended `AuditEntityType` (`apps/api/src/modules/audit/audit-log.service.ts`) with `"catalog_item"`. Every create/update/archive/restore/delete writes an `audit_log` row with `contactId: null` (catalog items have no owning contact — the column exists specifically for the five Contacts entity types, per `audit.ts`'s schema comment, now updated to explain the non-Contacts case). There is no `GET /catalog-items/:id/history` endpoint or web history view — out of this task's scope, matching how Contacts' own audit rollout started with writes-only-plus-one-endpoint rather than a system-wide view; see "Next up" for the still-open system-wide rollout.
- **`DELETE /catalog-items/:id` is intentionally unguarded** right now — unlike `ContactsService.delete()` (which blocks on `journal_lines` references before allowing a hard delete), nothing FKs to `catalog_items` yet since Quotes/Invoices (the future line-item holders) don't exist. This is flagged both in `CatalogService.delete()`'s own comment and in "Next up" below for whoever builds Quotes/Invoices next.
- **Web** (`apps/web/src/app/catalog/`, new directory): `page.tsx` (route, `?new=1` auto-opens the create Drawer, matching `contacts/page.tsx`), `catalog-explorer.tsx` (client state: status filter, load/refresh, toasts), `catalog-table.tsx` (the only list view — no card/list-view switcher like Contacts, since F2's scope is a flat CRUD list, kept proportionate per the task brief), `catalog-item-drawer.tsx` (one Drawer handling both create and edit — pass `item` to edit, omit to create; unlike Contacts there's no separate full detail page, Edit opens the same Drawer in place), `catalog-form.tsx` (name/description/unit/category/price/currency/tax-rate/income-account/expense-account; pre-fills currency from `GET /org/settings/currency` and tax rate from `GET /org/tax/default-rate` **only for a brand-new item** — an existing item's stored values always win; account pickers call the pre-existing `GET /org/accounts` endpoint, grouped by type, filtered to `income`/`expense`), `catalog-row-actions.tsx` (Edit/Archive-Restore/Delete dropdown + delete confirmation, mirroring `contact-row-actions.tsx`), `catalog-skeleton.tsx`, `entity-toast.tsx` (duplicated from Contacts' own small hook rather than extracted — no cross-module coupling reason to share a ~20-line hook yet), `types.ts` (hand-written `CatalogItem`/`Account`/`AccountsByType` types mirroring the API's JSON shape, same convention as `contacts/types.ts` since `packages/sdk` is still empty).
- Reused `@spine/ui`'s existing `MoneyInput` component (already built, previously only used in `apps/design-system`'s docs and nowhere in a real feature) for the default-price field — right-aligned, currency/minor-unit-aware, rejects keystrokes producing more fractional digits than the currency supports.
- Added a `/catalog` entry to `apps/web/src/lib/nav-sections.tsx`'s "Sales" section, alongside Contacts, with a `Package` icon (lucide-react).
- **Verified**: `pnpm --filter @spine/shared typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @spine/api typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @spine/api lint`, `pnpm --filter @spine/api build`, `pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @spine/web lint`, and `pnpm --filter @spine/web build` all pass (the web build confirms `/catalog` is a registered route in the production build output). Also started the built API (`pnpm start`) against the local dev Postgres and confirmed `GET /catalog-items` returns `401` (auth-gated, as expected without a session cookie) rather than a 404 or a startup crash — positive confirmation the module is wired into the running app, not just type-clean. **Not verified**: no browser-interactive testing was performed (no browser automation tooling exists in this environment) — the create/edit Drawer, account-picker population, and MoneyInput behavior have not been exercised through an actual UI session, only confirmed to compile, lint, and build cleanly against the real schema/API shape.
- **Not built** (explicitly out of scope per the task brief): Quotes (F3) itself, a `tax_rates` table / multi-rate tax-group CRUD (FEAT-08), a `GET /catalog-items/:id/history` endpoint or web history view, and any delete-guard on `catalog_items` (nothing references it yet to guard against). Line-level price override (S-02.2) needed no work here — the model already keeps `defaultPriceAmount` uncoupled from any document; a future quote/invoice line simply stores and can override its own price at add-time, which nothing in this schema prevents or entangles.

### 2026-08-06 — Formal WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility audit-and-fix pass across `@spine/ui`

- The audit-and-fix pass from "Next up" above (`A formal accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) pass per component`), now resolved and removed from that list. Scope: all 69 components in `packages/ui/src/components/`, plus the design-token layer they draw from (`packages/config/tailwind-preset.css`) and `docs/DESIGN.md`'s spec. `apps/api` was not touched (out of scope per the task brief); `apps/design-system` doc pages were updated only where a component's API/behavior genuinely changed.
- **Contrast, token-level (the highest-leverage fixes — one CSS value change cascades to every consumer)**: computed real WCAG contrast ratios (relative-luminance formula, not eyeballed) for every text/background token pair declared in `packages/config/tailwind-preset.css`, in both light and dark mode. Six light-mode pairs failed the 4.5:1 body-text minimum and are now fixed at the token level (dark mode was already compliant everywhere checked):
  - `--color-neutral-500` (backs `--color-on-surface-muted`, used across 43 component files, and `--color-draft`): `#8a8578` → `#726c5a`. Was 3.68:1 on `--color-surface` and 3.26:1 on `--color-draft-bg` — both real, live failures on every muted/secondary text label and every "Draft" status chip in the app. Now 5.24:1 / 4.64:1 (worst case).
  - `--color-paid`: `#1a7f4b` → `#177044` (was 4.44:1 on `--color-paid-bg`, now 5.40:1) — StatusChip's "Paid" chip renders at 12px, so the 4.5:1 threshold applies in full (no large-text exception).
  - `--color-category-teal`: `#0f7c7c` → `#0d6e6e` (was 4.41:1 on its `-bg`, now 5.33:1) — `calendar.tsx` renders event-title text in this color.
  - `--color-category-pink`: `#c4408a` → `#a63571` (was 3.93:1, now 5.19:1) — same calendar usage.
  - `docs/DESIGN.md`'s own color spec table updated to match every changed hex, with an inline comment recording the before/after ratio, so the doc and the shipped CSS custom properties stay in sync (they'd drifted apart before: the doc asserted "financial-status colors are independently verified per mode for 4.5:1" while `draft`/`paid`/`category-teal`/`category-pink` in light mode did not actually clear it).
- **A real, live dark-mode bug in Toast/Tooltip — not a contrast tweak, a broken pairing**: `toast.tsx` and `tooltip.tsx` both used `bg-neutral-900` + hardcoded `text-white`/`text-neutral-300`/`text-neutral-400`, intending permanently-dark chrome regardless of the app's theme (matching `docs/DESIGN.md`'s own toast/tooltip spec: `backgroundColor: neutral-900, textColor: #FFFFFF`). But `--color-neutral-900` is theme-*reactive* — it's also `--color-on-surface`, so in dark mode it resolves to `#f3f2ee` (near-white). White text on that background computed to **1.12:1** — every toast and every tooltip in the entire app was effectively unreadable in dark mode. Fixed by introducing three new theme-*invariant* tokens (`--color-inverse-surface: #211f1a`, `--color-inverse-on-surface: #ffffff`, `--color-inverse-on-surface-muted: #d3d0c9`, declared once in `:root` with no dark-mode override, so they hold the same value in both themes) and repointing both components at them instead of the reactive `neutral-900`/hardcoded whites. Also added a missing focus-visible ring to `ToastClose` while in that file (it had none).
- **Other real per-component fixes** (grouped by category; each verified against Radix's own source/types first, per the task's "don't add ARIA that duplicates what Radix already provides" instruction, so these are gaps Radix genuinely leaves to the wrapper):
  - *Forms*: `FormField`'s render-prop previously dropped `required` entirely — a screen reader user had no way to know a field was required beyond a purely visual asterisk. Now passes `aria-required`/`required`/`aria-invalid` through to the control, and the visual asterisk is `aria-hidden` (decorative only, not the sole carrier of the information). `HelperText` now sets `role="alert"` when rendering an error, so validation messages are announced when they appear. `Input`/`Textarea`/`MoneyInput` now self-set `aria-invalid` from their existing `error` prop when the caller doesn't pass `aria-invalid` explicitly (previously `error` only changed the border color).
  - *Custom listbox-style pickers with no Radix Combobox primitive underneath* (`Combobox`, `MultiSelect` — composed from Popover + cmdk/a hand-rolled listbox, not Radix's own Combobox, which doesn't exist) and `DatePicker`: trigger buttons were missing `aria-expanded`/`aria-haspopup`, so assistive tech had no way to know these were disclosure triggers or whether they were open. Fixed on all three.
  - *`calendar-mini.tsx` (hand-rolled, no Radix primitive)*: day-grid cells and the prev/next-month buttons had zero focus-visible treatment at all; no `aria-current="date"` for today; no `aria-selected` for the selected day (color alone conveyed selection); day buttons' only accessible name was the bare day-of-month number ("14"), no month/year/weekday context. Added `role="grid"`/`role="gridcell"`, full `aria-label`s (e.g. "Tuesday, August 4, 2026"), `aria-current`/`aria-selected`, and focus-visible rings throughout.
  - *`calendar.tsx` (hand-rolled Outlook-style scheduler, no Radix primitive)*: already had solid keyboard support in most places (roving-tabindex month grid with arrow keys, `role="button"`+`onKeyDown` event blocks with full `aria-label`s, `aria-pressed` color swatches) — two real gaps found and fixed: the month-view day-number button and per-day event-chip buttons had no focus-visible ring of their own (relying on inconsistent browser defaults against tinted backgrounds).
  - *`Sidebar`'s `SidebarNavItem` and `AppShell`'s `AppShellSidebar`*: when the sidebar is collapsed to its icon-only rail, the text label was fully unmounted (`{!collapsed && <span>...}`), leaving a collapsed nav item with zero accessible name — an icon with nothing for a screen reader to announce. Fixed in both call sites by keeping the label in the DOM with `sr-only` instead of unmounting it.
  - *`Table`'s sortable column headers*: no `aria-sort` on the `<th>` (so the current sort direction wasn't exposed to assistive tech) and no focus-visible ring on the sort button. Both fixed. `Pagination`'s prev/next/page-number buttons had no focus-visible ring at all — fixed.
  - *`Breadcrumb`*: the current/last crumb had no `aria-current="page"` (only a visual font-weight difference); its links had no focus-visible ring. Both fixed.
  - *Missing focus-visible rings on several Radix-wrapped triggers that had `outline-none`/`focus:outline-none` with no replacement*: `NavigationMenuTrigger`, `MenubarTrigger` (both real gaps — Tab-focusing an unopened trigger had zero visible indicator), `AccordionTrigger`, `TabsTrigger`/`TabsContent`, `PasswordToggleFieldToggle`, `ResizableHandle` (a 1px-wide drag handle, given `focus-visible:bg-primary` rather than a ring — a ring reads oddly on something that thin; `react-resizable-panels` itself already supplies `role="separator"`/`aria-valuenow`/keyboard arrow-key resizing, confirmed by reading its source, so only the missing visual indicator needed fixing).
  - *`Spinner`*: `aria-label="Loading"` was set directly on the bare `<svg>` (via lucide's `Loader2`) — an SVG has no implicit ARIA role, so an `aria-label` there isn't reliably exposed as an accessible name by every screen reader. Now wrapped in a `role="status"` span carrying the label (default "Loading", now an overridable `label` prop), with the icon itself `aria-hidden`.
  - *`Alert`*: all four variants (info/warning/critical/success) share the exact same `text-on-surface` text color — only the background tint differs — and `icon` was optional with no default; a `grep` across `apps/web` confirmed every real call site (`team-pane`, `signup`, `contacts-explorer`, `contact-detail` ×2, `contact-form`, `login`, `business-profile-step`, `invite-team-step`) omits the icon prop, meaning every error/warning banner in the shipped app was conveying its severity by background color alone. Fixed by giving `Alert` a default icon per variant (Info/AlertTriangle/AlertCircle/CheckCircle2) that only a `null` icon prop suppresses, plus `role="alert"` for `critical` and `role="status"` for the other three so banners are actually announced.
  - *`Carousel`*: no `role="region"`/`aria-roledescription="carousel"` on the root and no `role="group"`/`aria-roledescription="slide"` on items (a screen reader user had no indication this was a carousel or which slide was showing); embla-carousel's scroll-snap animation duration didn't respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (it's a JS/physics-driven scroll, not a CSS transition, so it's invisible to Tailwind's motion tokens and needed handling via `matchMedia` + Embla's own `duration` option). Both fixed.
- **Verified — real, not claimed**: `pnpm --filter @spine/ui typecheck` (pass), `pnpm --filter @spine/ui lint` (pass), `pnpm --filter @spine/design-system typecheck` (pass), `pnpm --filter @spine/design-system build` (pass, all 83 static routes generated). Also ran `pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck` as an extra check since `apps/web` is a real `@spine/ui` consumer and `Alert`/`Spinner` both gained new (backward-compatible, additive-only) behavior — passes clean, confirming no regression. Contrast ratios were computed with a real relative-luminance/WCAG-formula script (not estimated), run against every token pair actually used as text-on-background or text-on-tinted-background in the codebase, cross-checked by grepping for which components actually consume `category-pink`/`category-teal`/etc. before deciding a fix was in scope.
- **Not verified, stated plainly, matching this repo's established honesty convention**: no browser-automation tooling exists in this environment, so nothing above was interactively exercised — no real screen reader was run against any component, no keyboard-only pass was done in an actual browser, and no visual regression screenshot comparison was taken. All findings came from reading component source directly against Radix's own primitive source/types (to avoid duplicating ARIA Radix already supplies correctly) and computing contrast mathematically from the actual hex values in `tailwind-preset.css`.
- **Design-system doc pages updated** (only where API/behavior genuinely changed, per CLAUDE.md's rule — internal-only fixes with no visible API surface change, e.g. adding a focus ring class or an `aria-invalid` default, were left undocumented since nothing about how a consumer uses the component changed): `apps/design-system/src/app/components/alert/page.tsx` (new default-icon-per-variant behavior, `role` mapping), `.../spinner/page.tsx` (new `label` prop, `role="status"` wrapper), `.../form-field/page.tsx` (render-prop now also passes `aria-invalid`/`aria-required`/`required`, `HelperText`'s new `role="alert"`). No new components were added; no new component-page nav entries were needed.
- **Deferred, stated explicitly rather than silently dropped**: (1) `Carousel`'s prev/resize drag handles inside `calendar.tsx`'s time-grid event blocks (pointer-only resize, no keyboard equivalent) — judged acceptable since the same result (changing an event's start/end time) is fully reachable via the keyboard-operable event-editor dialog, but flagged here rather than asserted as a non-issue without discussion. (2) No automated accessibility-testing tooling (axe-core/jest-axe) was installed — genuinely out of scope per the task brief ("do NOT... install unless clearly trivial and in scope"); **recommended as a follow-up** so future component changes get a regression net instead of relying on a fresh manual audit each time. (3) `calendar.tsx`'s full arrow-key grid navigation (month view) was already present from a prior session and re-verified working correctly by reading it, not changed. (4) Touch-target sizing (WCAG 2.5.5, AAA in 2.1 / 2.5.8 in 2.2) was explicitly out of scope for this 2.1 AA pass and wasn't audited — `@spine/ui` targets web only right now per CLAUDE.md (mobile is a separate not-yet-built Expo app), so this wasn't treated as a blocking gap.
- Stories: resolves the "A formal accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA) pass per component" line from "Next up" (removed below); not tied to a specific numbered PRD story (a cross-cutting design-system quality pass, not a feature).
- Phase: Phase 0 · Foundation (`@spine/ui` and `docs/DESIGN.md` are both Phase 0 deliverables; Phase 1 · Sales Spine work is unaffected).

### 2026-08-06 — CI pipeline (Postgres-backed `test:integration`) + onboarding/Settings business logo real upload (S-12.2's last remaining half)

- Two small, independent items pulled off "Next up" in the same session.
- **CI pipeline** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, new — no `.github/` directory existed before). Runs on every push to `main` and every PR: checkout → `pnpm/action-setup` → Node 20 (`actions/setup-node` with pnpm cache) → `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` → `pnpm lint` → `pnpm typecheck` → `pnpm build` → `pnpm test` (unit tests, all packages via Turborepo) → `pnpm --filter @spine/api db:migrate` → `pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration`. A `postgres:16` service container (matching the PRD's pinned Postgres version, `docker-compose.dev.yml`'s own image) provides the database, with a `pg_isready` healthcheck so the job doesn't race a not-yet-ready container. `DATABASE_URL`/`AUTH_SECRET`/`APP_URL` are set as job-level env vars (a throwaway CI-only secret string for `AUTH_SECRET`, not a real credential) — confirmed by reading both integration test files (`apps/api/src/db/ledger-integrity.integration.test.ts`, `apps/api/src/auth/signup.integration.test.ts`) first that neither needs anything beyond a reachable `DATABASE_URL` (both already fall back to a `localhost:5432` default if unset) and that `auth.ts` only reads `AUTH_SECRET` (any string works for a test run, Better Auth doesn't validate its strength). `db:migrate`/`test:integration`'s existing `dotenv -e ../../.env` prefix was checked directly (via a local `mv .env` experiment) to confirm `dotenv-cli` silently skips loading when the file is absent rather than erroring — so no `.env` file needed to be fabricated in CI; the job-level env vars flow through untouched.
- **Verified**, not just written: ran the exact CI steps locally. `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm build` (all packages, via `turbo run <task>`) each pass clean from a fresh state (`apps/web/.next`/`apps/design-system/.next` removed first). Most importantly, ran `DATABASE_URL="postgres://spine:spine@localhost:5432/spine" AUTH_SECRET="ci-test-secret-not-for-production-use-only" APP_URL="http://localhost:3000" pnpm --filter @spine/api test:integration` against the real local dev Postgres (`docker-compose.dev.yml`'s `db` service, already running, migrations already applied) — both integration test files passed (5 tests total: the 4-test ledger-integrity suite, the 1-test signup suite), confirming the exact env-var shape the new workflow provides is sufficient, not just plausible. Did not spin up an actual `postgres:16` container fresh (no Docker-in-Docker attempted here) — the local dev Postgres is also version 16 per `docker-compose.dev.yml`, so this is a close proxy for the CI service container, not a byte-identical re-run of the workflow file itself; genuine GitHub Actions execution (secrets, runner environment, Actions cache behavior) is unverified, stated plainly, since that requires actually pushing and watching a run.
- **Business logo real upload** (S-12.2's remaining half, called out in the prior session's "Next up"): `apps/web/src/app/onboarding/steps/business-profile-step.tsx`'s "Logo URL" text field (paste-a-URL, explicitly marked as an interim placeholder in that file's own doc comment) is replaced with a real upload control, `BusinessLogoUpload` (new, `apps/web/src/app/onboarding/steps/business-logo-upload.tsx`). Since `BusinessProfileStep` is shared verbatim between the onboarding wizard and `apps/web/src/app/settings/panes/business-pane.tsx` (confirmed by reading both call sites before touching anything), this one change covers both surfaces — no separate Settings-side work needed.
- **Reused the existing Contacts upload plumbing rather than rebuilding it**: `BusinessLogoUpload` follows the exact pick → crop → `POST /files` flow `ContactLogo`/`LogoCropDialog` already established for contact/contact-person photos — file picker → object URL → `LogoCropDialog` (crop step) → `cropAndResizeImage` (canvas crop+downscale) → `apiClient.upload("/files", file)` (multipart, existing endpoint, unchanged). **Two files with zero Contacts-specific logic were promoted out of `apps/web/src/app/contacts/` into `apps/web/src/lib/`** (`crop-and-resize-image.ts`, `logo-crop-dialog.tsx`) so both the Contacts and onboarding/Settings call sites import the same shared implementation instead of a duplicated copy — confirmed via `grep` first that only `contact-logo.tsx` imported either file before moving them, so `contact-logo.tsx`'s two import lines are the only fix-ups the move required. `LogoCropDialog` gained one new optional prop, `cropShape?: "round" | "rect"` (default `"round"`, preserving Contacts' existing circular-avatar behavior unchanged) — a business logo is a square mark, not a face, so it crops with `cropShape="rect"` while contacts keep the circular crop.

Grepped the compiled production bundle (`apps/web/.next/static/chunks/`) and confirmed the literal strings `"Upload business logo"` and `"Logo uploaded"` (from `BusinessLogoUpload`'s own markup) appear in the shipped chunk — direct static proof the new component is wired into the built onboarding page (and, since it's the same shared `BusinessProfileStep`, the Settings business pane too). Confirmed via `twMerge`'s conflict-resolution behavior (read `packages/ui/src/lib/cn.ts`) that the new component's `rounded-md` override on `Avatar`'s base `rounded-full` class resolves correctly rather than both classes fighting.

The genuine GitHub Actions run (pushing and watching `.github/workflows/ci.yml` execute against a real ephemeral `postgres:16` service container) is likewise unverified — only a close local proxy (existing dev Postgres, same major version) was run.

### 2026-08-06 — Edit everywhere on Contacts (persons/addresses/leads/activities) + the first real audit-log write instrumentation and a History tab

- Two pieces, requested together: (1) closing the "no way to edit an existing contact person/address/lead/activity" gap left open by every prior Contacts session — only add and delete existed on all four sub-entity sections — and (2) the codebase's first real writes to `audit_log` (previously zero writers anywhere, table schema-only, per "Next up" above), scoped to Contacts, plus a `GET /contacts/:id/history` endpoint and a web History tab reading real entries.
- **Part 1 — edit dialogs.** `contact-persons-section.tsx`, `addresses-section.tsx`, `leads-section.tsx`, `activities-section.tsx` (all `apps/web/src/app/contacts/`) each gained an edit affordance: a `Pencil` icon-button per list row, opening the **exact same Dialog** the section already used for "Add X" (per the task brief's explicit instruction not to build a second form), keyed off one new `editingId: string | null` piece of state — `null` means adding, a set id means editing that row. Dialog title and the primary button's label flip ("Add contact person" → "Edit contact person", "Add" → "Save changes") but the fields/layout are identical, confirmed by construction since it's literally the same JSX, not a parallel copy.
  - Contact persons/addresses reuse the existing whole-array-replace `PUT /contacts/:id` (unchanged endpoint) — `toInput()` now includes each row's `id` (previously omitted, since add/remove never needed it), and a new `handleSave()` either appends a new entry (add) or replaces one array element in place by id (edit) before calling the same `persist()` helper both flows already shared. `PersonInput`/`AddressInput` types were introduced with `id` as **optional** (a new row has none until the array-replace PUT assigns it), fixing a TypeScript error the naive change first produced (`Property 'id' is missing` — the add-path literal had no `id` field, the edit-path spread did).
  - Leads/activities call the pre-existing `PUT /leads/:id`/`PUT /activities/:id` endpoints directly (confirmed both already existed in `leads.controller.ts`/`activities.controller.ts` before touching anything, per the brief) — `handleSave()` branches on `editingId` to `PUT` vs the existing `POST`.
  - Idempotency: no new endpoints were added by Part 1 (edit reuses `PUT /contacts/:id`, `PUT /leads/:id`, `PUT /activities/:id`, all already wired with `@UseInterceptors(IdempotencyInterceptor)` before this session) — confirmed rather than assumed by reading each controller first, and re-confirmed live (see Verified: a replayed `Idempotency-Key` on a `PUT /contacts/:id` returned the exact stored response, not a re-applied write).
  - Select-inside-Dialog z-index (the prior session's `z-popover`/`z-modal` fix) was not touched — the edit dialogs are the same `DialogContent` JSX as the add dialogs that already exercised it (addresses' type Select, leads' stage Select, activities' type Select), so no new exercise was needed beyond what already existed; not independently re-verified interactively (no browser tooling — see Not verified below), same as every prior z-index claim in this file.
- **Part 2 — `AuditLogService`** (`apps/api/src/modules/audit/audit-log.service.ts`, new; `apps/api/src/modules/audit/audit.module.ts` now provides/exports it instead of being a literal `@Module({})` stub). `record(tx, {orgId, actorUserId, action, entityType, entityId, contactId, changes})` inserts one row into `audit_log`; `tx` is typed `Database | Transaction` (`Transaction` is a new type alias in `apps/api/src/db/client.ts`, `Parameters<Parameters<Database["transaction"]>[0]>[0]` — drizzle-orm's `tx` callback parameter is structurally a different type than `Database` itself, so a type that only accepted `Database` wouldn't type-check when called from inside a `db.transaction(async (tx) => ...)` block) so every call joins whatever transaction its caller is already inside, never a separate unguarded write. `action` is a short verb (`created`/`updated`/`archived`/`restored`/`deleted`/`removed`/`marked done`/`marked undone`); `entityType` is one of `contact`/`contact_person`/`address`/`lead`/`activity`; `changes` is a plain `{field, from, to}[]` — a shallow diff, not a full snapshot, per the task brief's own preference. A static `AuditLogService.diffFields(before, input)` helper (shared by every call site) implements exactly the brief's suggested rule: for each key present in `input` (an `undefined` field means "not touched," matching the codebase's existing partial-update convention), if it differs from `before`'s value, record one `{field, from, to}` entry — deliberately not a generic deep-diffing library.
- **Denormalized `audit_log.contact_id`** (new nullable FK, `ON DELETE CASCADE` to `contacts.id`, migration `apps/api/drizzle/0007_real_galactus.sql`, idx 7 — confirmed as the correct next index against `_journal.json`'s last entry, idx 6, before generating, per this session's explicit caution about the earlier migration-numbering collision). Chosen over joining across four different sub-entity tables to answer "which contact does this row belong to" — populated on every audit row this pass writes (equal to `entityId` for `entityType: "contact"` rows; the sub-entity's own `contactId` otherwise; `null` only for a hard-deleted contact's own final "deleted" entry, see below). Three new indexes: `audit_log_org_idx`, `audit_log_contact_idx`, `audit_log_entity_idx` (composite on `entity_type, entity_id`).
- **Contact-person/address diffing** (`contacts.service.ts`'s `update`, the whole-array-replace method): reads the existing `contactPersons`/`addresses` rows *before* the transaction (needed to diff by id — the array-replace re-insert always mints brand-new row ids even for entries the client sent an existing `id` on, so post-insert ids can't be compared against pre-update ids). A new private `recordArrayDiff()` positionally pairs each `input[i]` entry against the corresponding freshly-inserted `after[i]` row (both arrays are built from the same input array in the same order) to know the new row's real id for `entityId`, while matching against `before` by the input entry's own `id` field: a match with changed fields → `updated`; an entry with no `id` or an unrecognized `id` → `created`; a `before` row with no matching input entry → `removed`. `create`'s equivalent path (no diffing needed, everything is new) records one `created` entry per inserted person/address directly.
- **The contact's own scalar-field diff** (`contacts.service.ts`'s `update`) reads the row *before* the update (`existing`, already fetched for the 404 check) and diffs it against `input` — with `contactPersons`/`addresses` explicitly destructured out first, since they're not real columns on `contacts` and diffing them naively against `existing` (which has no such keys) produced a nonsensical `"contactPersons: null → [...]"` noise entry, caught live during verification (see Verified) and fixed before this entry was written, not left in.
- **Hard-delete's audit entry** (`contacts.service.ts`'s `delete`) records `contactId: null`, not the contact's own id — `audit_log.contact_id` has `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so a row pointing at the very contact about to be hard-deleted would cascade-delete itself in the same transaction, destroying the entry meant to record the deletion. `entityId` still captures which contact this was; it's just correctly unreachable from `GET /contacts/:id/history` afterward, since that contact no longer exists to have a history page.
- **`GET /contacts/:id/history`** (`contacts.controller.ts`, delegating to a new `ContactsService.getHistory()` → `AuditLogService.listForContact()`): confirms the contact exists (org-scoped, reuses `getOne`) then returns every `audit_log` row with `contact_id` matching, newest-first, **actor names resolved server-side** via a `LEFT JOIN` to `user` on `actorUserId` (chosen over a client-side second lookup, per the brief's stated preference — "simpler for the client, avoids a second lookup"). No `@OrgRoles` restriction, matching every other GET in this module — history is a read.
- **Every mutating method across all three services now calls into `AuditLogService`**: `contacts.service.ts` (`create`/`update`/`archive`/`restore`/`delete`), `leads.service.ts` (`create`/`update`/`delete`), `activities.service.ts` (`create`/`update`/`markDone`/`markUndone`/`delete`). `archive`/`restore`/`delete` on contacts, and `create`/`update`/`delete` on leads/activities, were previously single-statement non-transactional writes — each now wraps its write + audit insert in `this.db.transaction(...)` so the two are atomic together, per the task brief's explicit requirement. Controllers for all three now pass `session.user.id` through as `actorUserId` (previously unused for this purpose in `leads.controller.ts`/`activities.controller.ts`'s mutating routes beyond `create`, which already threaded `session.user.id` through for `createdByUserId`). Activities' `contactId` is nullable (an activity can be linked to just a `leadId`) — a new private `resolveContactId()` on `ActivitiesService` falls back to looking up the lead's own `contactId` when the activity has none directly, so an activity logged only against a lead still shows up in that lead's contact's History tab.
- **Web History tab** (`apps/web/src/app/contacts/history-section.tsx`, new; wired into `contact-detail.tsx`'s `Tabs` as a fifth tab alongside Contact persons/Addresses/Leads/Activities): reverse-chronological list, one line per entry — `"{actor} {verb} {subject}[: field a → b, ...]"`, e.g. "Audit Tester updated a contact person: name Jane Doe → Jane A. Doe" or "Audit Tester archived this contact" (state-transition actions like archive/restore/mark-done have no `changes` array and render without the suffix). Relative time via `date-fns`'s `formatDistanceToNow` (full timestamp in a `title` tooltip) — `date-fns` was already a dependency of `@spine/ui` (used by its `Calendar` component) but not of `apps/web` directly; added `"date-fns": "^4.1.0"` to `apps/web/package.json` (same range `@spine/ui` already declares, resolves to the same hoisted `4.4.0`) rather than relying on transitive hoisting, confirmed via `grep` first that nothing else in `apps/web` already imported it. `AuditEntry`/`AuditFieldChange`/`AuditEntityType` types added to `apps/web/src/app/contacts/types.ts`, mirroring `AuditLogService.listForContact`'s row shape, matching this file's existing hand-written-mirror convention (no generated SDK yet). ### 2026-08-06 — Contacts photo upload follow-up: crop-and-resize step before upload

- **Not a new PRD story** — a direct follow-up to this session's "Contacts photo-upload work" (the "Contacts & CRM redesign/expansion" entry below, which added `ContactLogo`/the Files/S3 module, and the "Contacts redesign follow-up" entry above it, which extended the same upload flow to contact-person photos). Both flows previously uploaded whatever file the native picker returned, full-size and unmodified. This adds a crop-and-resize step between file selection and upload.
- **`react-easy-crop` added to `apps/web/package.json`** (`^5.2.0`, resolved `5.5.7`) — confirmed via `grep` it wasn't already a dependency before adding. No other new dependencies.
- **`apps/web/src/app/contacts/crop-and-resize-image.ts` (new)**: a standalone `cropAndResizeImage(imageSrc, crop, options)` helper, deliberately separate from any dialog UI so it's testable/reusable independent of it. Takes `react-easy-crop`'s `onCropComplete` pixel-crop rectangle (already in source-image coordinates) and does the crop + downscale in a **single `drawImage` call**: source rectangle = the crop region, destination rectangle = the final output canvas — no intermediate full-resolution canvas pass needed. Output size is `Math.min(1, maxDimension / cropWidth, maxDimension / cropHeight)` applied to the crop's own width/height, so it **only ever downscales** — a crop selection already smaller than 256×256 (default `maxDimension`) is never enlarged, confirmed by explicit test cases (see Verified). Encodes via `canvas.toBlob()` at `image/jpeg`, quality `0.85` by default (both overridable) — checked `apps/api/src/modules/files/files.controller.ts`/`files.service.ts` first per the brief: `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (10MB) is the only server-side restriction, `mimeType` is stored as free-text metadata with no allowlist/validation, so `image/jpeg` was a free choice made for size efficiency at avatar dimensions, not a constraint the API forced.
- **`apps/web/src/app/contacts/logo-crop-dialog.tsx` (new)**: `LogoCropDialog`, a `@spine/ui` `Dialog` (`size="md"`, the existing centered-task-dialog variant — no new Dialog size needed) hosting `react-easy-crop`'s `<Cropper>` locked to `aspect={1}` and `cropShape="round"` (matching the avatar's circular display; no aspect-ratio picker since square is the only option needed) plus a `@spine/ui` `Slider` for zoom (1×–3×). Cancel discards the picked file and closes with no upload (also revokes the picked file's object URL — see below). Save runs `cropAndResizeImage` then calls the caller's `onConfirm`, showing its **own** `Spinner`-in-button loading state (`saving`) while cropping + uploading happens, disabling both Cancel and Save meanwhile — decided this was needed rather than relying solely on `ContactLogo`'s existing avatar-overlay spinner, since that overlay is on the avatar itself, behind the now-open dialog, and wouldn't be visible until the dialog closes.
- **`apps/web/src/app/contacts/contact-logo.tsx`**: `handleFileSelected` no longer uploads directly — it creates an object URL (`URL.createObjectURL`) from the picked file and opens `LogoCropDialog` with it; a `useEffect` cleanup plus an explicit revoke on cancel/confirm prevents leaking `blob:` URLs across repeated picks. The actual `apiClient.upload("/files", file)` call moved into `handleCropConfirm`, now uploading the **cropped/compressed File** `cropAndResizeImage` returns, not the original picked file — everything downstream (`onUploaded` callback, `uploading` state driving the avatar-overlay spinner) is unchanged. **No change to `ContactLogo`'s external API** (`name`/`fileId`/`size`/`editable`/`onUploaded`) — confirmed by reading its six call sites (`grep -rln "ContactLogo" apps/web/src`: `contact-detail.tsx`, `contact-form.tsx`, `contact-persons-section.tsx`, `contacts-card-view.tsx`, `contacts-list-view.tsx`, plus `contact-logo.tsx` itself) and none needed edits.
- **Landed entirely in `apps/web/src/app/contacts/`, not `packages/ui`**: `LogoCropDialog` composes an existing `@spine/ui` `Dialog`/`Slider`/`Button`/`Spinner` around one third-party crop widget for one specific use case (square avatar/logo crop) — the same call this session's "Contacts redesign follow-up" entry made for the four "Add X" section dialogs (Dialog composition stays app-level until a second real consumer needs the same shape). No `apps/design-system` doc page added or owed, per CLAUDE.md's rule, since no `@spine/ui` primitive was added or changed.
- **Verified**: dev stack already up (`docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml ps` — Postgres/MinIO healthy, 23h uptime; both `apps/api`/`apps/web` dev servers already listening on 4000/3000, no restart needed). `apps/web/.next` proactively removed before building, per this session's established `.next`-race gotcha. `pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck`, `lint`, `build` each run sequentially — all clean, `react-easy-crop`'s `Area`/`CropperProps` types resolved correctly with no `any`. Confirmed via `grep -rn "canvas" apps/web/src apps/design-system/src` before writing that there was no prior canvas precedent in the repo — this is a clean new implementation, not a match to an existing pattern. Grepped the compiled production bundle (`apps/web/.next/static/chunks/`) and confirmed `"Crop logo"` (the dialog title), `cropShape`/`reactEasyCrop` (the third-party Cropper), and `"Could not encode the cropped image."` (the helper's own error string) all appear in both `app/contacts/page-*.js` and `app/contacts/[id]/page-*.js` — direct static proof the new code shipped into both pages that render `ContactLogo`.
- **Resize math verified by isolated arithmetic, not a real canvas run**: no browser is available in this environment, and plain Node has no `<canvas>`/`Image`/`HTMLCanvasElement` — `sharp` is also not installed (checked `node_modules/.bin` and the tree for it, absent), so the actual pixel-drawing code (`ctx.drawImage`, `canvas.toBlob`) could not be executed end-to-end. Instead, the exact scale/dimension formula from `cropAndResizeImage` (`Math.min(1, maxDimension / cropWidth, maxDimension / cropHeight)` applied to compute `outputWidth`/`outputHeight`) was copied verbatim into a standalone script run via `node --experimental-strip-types` against six cases: a large square crop (2000×2000 → 256×256), a large non-square crop (3000×1500 → 256×128), a small square crop below the cap (100×100 → 100×100, confirming no upscale), an exact-256 crop (256×256 → 256×256), a just-over-256 crop (257×257 → 256×256), and a tiny crop (10×10 → 10×10, confirming no upscale). All six passed both assertions (`output ≤ 256` and `output ≤ source`). This confirms the dimension math is correct; it does **not** confirm the actual `drawImage`/`toBlob` calls execute without error in a real browser, or that `react-easy-crop`'s drag/zoom interaction and `onCropComplete` callback behave as expected — those remain unverified, stated plainly, matching this session's established honesty pattern.
- **Not verified, stated plainly**: any real browser interaction — opening the crop dialog, dragging/zooming the crop area, clicking Cancel/Save, watching the avatar-overlay spinner appear after the dialog closes, or an actual end-to-end upload of a real cropped image reaching `POST /files` and rendering back via `GET /files/:id`. No browser-automation tooling is available in this environment; everything above was code-reviewed, typechecked, and confirmed present in the compiled bundle, but not interactively exercised.
- Stories: no new PRD stories — a UX-quality follow-up to S-12.2/S-01.x's already-shipped logo/photo upload, tightening what gets uploaded rather than adding new scope.
- Phase: Phase 1 · Sales Spine (same phase as the entries it follows up on).

### 2026-08-06 — Contacts redesign follow-up: Drawer sizes + fixed header/footer, a real `@spine/ui` z-index fix, Dialog-based add-flows, and contact-person photos

- **Not a new PRD story** — a direct fix for five specific problems the user found reviewing the immediately-prior two entries ("Contacts & CRM redesign/expansion" and, transitively, the Files module it introduced). Five pieces, all in one pass: (1) a `size` prop on Drawer, (2) sticky Drawer header/footer with a scrollable body only, (3) a real `@spine/ui` z-index fix so popovers/selects/menus render above dialogs/drawers, (4) the four contact-detail "Add X" sections converted from inline-expanding forms to Dialogs, (5) contact-person photo upload.
- **`packages/ui/src/components/drawer.tsx`, Issue 1**: `DrawerContent`'s `drawerVariants` (`cva`) gains a `size` prop — `sm` (`max-w-sm`) / `md` (`max-w-md`, default) / `lg` (`max-w-2xl`) — named identically to `DialogContent`'s existing `size` prop (`md`/`lg`) for consistency, though the two don't share a value set (Dialog's `lg` is a large centered panel measured against viewport height; Drawer's `lg` is just a wider edge-anchored panel — no need for the two to be numerically identical, only for the naming convention to match). Default (`md`) is exactly the old hardcoded `max-w-md`, so no existing/uncommitted Drawer usage regresses from omitting `size`.
- **`drawer.tsx`, Issue 2**: `DrawerContent` is now a bare `flex h-full flex-col` with **no padding of its own** (previously it was `p-5` on the whole content, with `DrawerHeader`/`DrawerFooter` as plain unstructured flex divs and the footer only reaching the bottom via `mt-auto` — fine for short content, broke on tall content since header/body/footer scrolled as one block). `DrawerHeader` is now `shrink-0` with its own `border-b` + padding, pinned to the top; a new `DrawerBody` export is the **only** scrollable region (`flex-1 overflow-y-auto`, its own padding); `DrawerFooter` is `shrink-0` with its own `border-t` + padding, pinned to the bottom. Checked `DialogContent`/`AlertDialogContent` in the same file's sibling components first for a precedent header/body/footer split — neither had one (both are short, non-scrolling dialogs by design), so this is a new pattern specific to Drawer, not copied from an existing split. Every current `Drawer`/`DrawerContent`/`DrawerHeader`/`DrawerFooter` usage in the codebase was found via `grep -rln` (just `apps/web/src/app/contacts/contact-create-drawer.tsx`) and updated to wrap `ContactForm` in the new `DrawerBody`.
- **`packages/ui/src/components/select.tsx` + seven sibling popover-style components, Issue 3 — a real component-library bug, fixed at the library, not per-page**: confirmed directly by reading source that `SelectContent` used `z-[1000]` while `Drawer`/`Dialog`/`AlertDialog` used `z-[1300]` for their overlay and content — a `Select` opened from inside a `Drawer` or `Dialog` was genuinely rendering at a lower stacking layer than the drawer/dialog itself, i.e. hidden behind it. Checked every `z-[…]` value across `packages/ui/src/components/{select,combobox,multi-select,dropdown-menu,context-menu,menubar,popover,hover-card,tooltip,toast,dialog,alert-dialog,drawer}.tsx` and established one consistent scheme instead of a one-off bump: `dropdown`(1000, unused directly by any component now, kept as the floor of the scale) → `sticky-header`(1100) → `overlay`(1200, Dialog/AlertDialog's backdrop) → `modal`(1300, Dialog/AlertDialog/Drawer's panel) → **`popover`(1600, NEW — Select/Combobox/MultiSelect/DropdownMenu/ContextMenu/Menubar/Popover/HoverCard)** → `toast`(1700) → `tooltip`(1800, the ceiling). `popover` is deliberately layered *above* `modal`: any of those eight components can be triggered from inside a Dialog/Drawer and must always render on top of the modal that hosts it. Confirmed `docs/DESIGN.md`'s "Elevation & Depth" section already *documented* a z-index scale as a plain YAML-ish spec (`dropdown:1000 … tooltip:1500`), but it was never wired as real CSS and the doc's own ordering had the same bug baked in (dropdown-tier below modal-tier) — so this fix corrects both the doc and adds the missing `popover` tier, rather than just patching component code against a doc that was itself wrong. **Added real tokens**: `packages/config/tailwind-preset.css` gains `--z-dropdown` … `--z-tooltip` as CSS custom properties (both in `:root` and re-exposed via `@theme inline`, exactly matching how every other token in that file — colors, radii, durations — is already structured), which Tailwind v4 turns into real utility classes (`z-dropdown`, `z-modal`, `z-popover`, etc.). Every one of the eleven components above now uses the utility class instead of a hardcoded `z-[N]` arbitrary value — confirmed via `grep -rn "z-\[" packages/ui/src/components/` returning zero matches after the change. `docs/DESIGN.md` updated to match (its own z-index list corrected, plus a new paragraph in "Elevation & Depth" spelling out why `popover` sits above `modal`).
- **Design-system doc pages updated in the same change, per CLAUDE.md's rule**: `apps/design-system/src/app/components/drawer/page.tsx` — added `DrawerBody` to every example, documented the new `size` prop in the API table and a features-list bullet, added a live "Sizes" example showing `sm`/`lg` side by side. `apps/design-system/src/app/components/select/page.tsx` — added a features-list bullet on the new stacking guarantee and a new live "Inside a Dialog" example (a `Select` rendered inside `DialogContent`, proving the fix interactively in the docs app itself, not just asserted in prose). `apps/design-system/src/app/components/dropdown-menu/page.tsx` — same features-list bullet, since DropdownMenu is the other component this task's Issue 4 exercises inside a Dialog/Drawer live. No `apps/design-system/src/lib/nav.ts` changes needed — all three already have nav entries, only existing pages' content changed.
- **Issue 4 — `contact-persons-section.tsx`, `addresses-section.tsx`, `leads-section.tsx`, `activities-section.tsx`**: each section's `adding` boolean + inline-expanding bordered form is now a `@spine/ui` `Dialog`, controlled via local `open` state (a plain `Button` as the opener, not a `DialogTrigger` — `Dialog`'s root is just `DialogPrimitive.Root`, and controlling `open`/`onOpenChange` directly from the section's own state matches the idiom `settings-dialog.tsx`/`app-user-menu.tsx` already established for exactly this reason, keeping the dialog's open state external to anything that might unmount its trigger). Form fields moved into `DialogContent`/`DialogHeader`/`DialogTitle`/a plain flex body/`DialogFooter` with Cancel/Save actions; `onSaved`/`onCreated`/`onChanged` wiring is unchanged — the dialog closes and the parent list refreshes exactly as the inline form did before. `AddressesSection` and `LeadsSection` and `ActivitiesSection`'s dialogs each contain a `Select` (address type, lead stage, activity type) — a second, independent live exercise of the Issue 3 z-index fix beyond Drawer, confirmed the same way (compiled-bundle class-name check, see Verified).
- **Issue 5 — contact-person photos**: `apps/api/src/db/schema/contacts.ts`'s `contactPersons` table gains `logoFileId` (nullable, `references(() => files.id, { onDelete: "set null" })`) — the exact same pattern as `contacts.logoFileId` a few lines above it, mirrored deliberately rather than reinvented. Migration `0006_polite_arclight.sql` (idx 6, confirmed as the correct next index against `apps/api/drizzle/meta/_journal.json`'s last entry, idx 5, *before* generating — the prior session's migration-numbering collision was a known risk here, avoided by checking first) generated via `drizzle-kit generate` and applied via `pnpm --filter @spine/api db:migrate`, clean on the first try (no repeat of the prior session's stale-timestamp hiccup). `packages/shared/src/schemas/contacts.ts`'s `contactPersonInputSchema` gains `logoFileId: uuidSchema.optional().nullable()` — flows through `updateContactSchema`'s existing `.partial()` and the create schema's array automatically, no separate schema needed. `contacts.service.ts`'s two `contactPersons.map(...)` blocks (create's insert, update's delete-then-reinsert) each gain one line, `logoFileId: person.logoFileId ?? null`, alongside the existing `name`/`title`/`email`/`phone`/`isPrimary` fields — a straightforform additive change, no structural change to the insert/update logic itself. **Sequencing, worked through deliberately since it differs from the contact-level logo flow**: a contact already has an `id` by the time its logo is uploaded, so `contact-logo.tsx`'s flow is upload → `PUT /contacts/:id { logoFileId }` immediately. Confirmed via `git diff` that no `@OrgRoles` decorator or other role-gating code was touched anywhere in this pass (the one visible diff to `contacts.controller.ts` predates this task, from the immediately-prior session's array-type-filter change) — the field-role permission matrix this module already established was not re-exercised live this pass since nothing in the mutation/authorization path changed, only additive fields flowing through the exact same already-gated endpoints.

### 2026-08-06 — Contacts & CRM redesign/expansion: a real Files/S3 module, a stat-cards+multi-view list page, a tabbed detail page, and targeted field additions

- **Not a new PRD story** — this is a significant redesign and expansion of the Contacts module built this session, on top of the two entries immediately below ("Contacts & CRM (F1)" and "Contacts & CRM (F1) follow-up"). Four pieces: (1) a real S3/MinIO-backed Files module, replacing the literal `@Module({})` stub that existed at `apps/api/src/modules/files/files.module.ts`; (2) a Contacts list page rebuild (stat cards, Table/List/Card view switcher, multiselect filters, Drawer-based create); (3) a Contacts detail page rebuild (back button, logo upload, Tabs replacing the prior session's two-column layout); (4) two targeted new fields (`taxId`, `website`) plus a `logoFileId`, in one migration.

- **Files module** (`apps/api/src/modules/files/`, new `apps/api/src/db/schema/files.ts`): `@aws-sdk/client-s3` + `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner` added to `apps/api/package.json` (neither existed anywhere in the repo before — confirmed via `grep -r "@aws-sdk"` first, per the task brief). `s3-client.ts` reads `S3_ENDPOINT`/`S3_BUCKET`/`S3_ACCESS_KEY`/`S3_SECRET_KEY` and returns a `null` client (never throws) when `S3_ENDPOINT` is unset — confirmed directly against the real source via `S3_ENDPOINT="" npx tsx -e "..."` (see Verified) rather than assumed from reading the code. `forcePathStyle: true` is set since MinIO doesn't support virtual-hosted-style bucket addressing. Every caller (`FilesService.upload`/`getSignedUrl`) checks for `null` first and throws `ServiceUnavailableException` (503) with a clear "attachments are unavailable" message — per CLAUDE.md's graceful-degradation rule, this must degrade the file feature, never the process, and S3_* is correctly never in the 3-required-env-vars boot list.
- **`files` table** (org-scoped, same conventions as `contacts.ts`: `uuid` PK via `defaultRandom()`, `org_id` FK to Better Auth's `organization.id`, `timestamp(..., { withTimezone: true })`): `id`, `orgId`, `key`, `originalFilename`, `mimeType`, `sizeBytes`, `uploadedByUserId`, `createdAt`. **Deliberately not polymorphic** — no `attachableType`/`attachableId`. Checked this schema's own precedent for "referenced from elsewhere" first (`journal_lines.contact_id`/`job_id`, both plain nullable FKs to one specific table) and followed it: `contacts.logoFileId` is a plain nullable FK on `contacts` itself, not a field on `files`. When quotes/invoices need attachments later they get their own FK column(s), same pattern, not a speculative generic association built for hypothetical future consumers.
- **Upload/serve endpoints** (`files.controller.ts`): `POST /files` (`@OrgRoles(["owner", "staff"])`, `FileInterceptor("file")` from `@nestjs/platform-express` — already a dependency, `main.ts` already uses this platform adapter — plus `IdempotencyInterceptor`, in that decorator order so multer parses the multipart body into `request.file` before the idempotency check reads headers/session). `main.ts`'s `bodyParser: false` (needed so Better Auth can read its own raw request stream) does not interfere — multer/`FileInterceptor` attaches its own per-route middleware and never touches Nest's global body parser, confirmed by the upload endpoint working end-to-end live (see Verified), not just by reading the framework's docs. `GET /files/:id` 302-redirects to a short-lived (`300s`) signed URL rather than proxy-streaming bytes through the API process: this is a single-host, self-hosted deployment (`docker/Caddyfile` reverse-proxies `api`/`web` under one origin; MinIO is its own directly-reachable service per `docker-compose.dev.yml`/`.env.example`), so a signed URL avoids burning an API request-handling thread per download for a case with no per-download authorization logic beyond "does this file belong to my org" (already covered by the org-scoped lookup before signing). A proxy-stream approach would only earn its cost if MinIO weren't reachable from the browser directly, which isn't the case in this stack.
- **A real gap found and fixed, not just documented**: MinIO starts with zero buckets — neither `docker-compose.dev.yml` nor the prod compose file provisions the `spine` bucket, so the very first upload attempt failed live with `NoSuchBucket` during this session's own verification. Rather than requiring an undocumented manual `mc mb` step on every fresh environment, `FilesService` now self-heals: `HeadBucket` (checked, cached in-process after the first success) then `CreateBucket` only on a 404. Confirmed by deliberately removing the bucket (`mc rb --force local/spine`) and re-uploading — it recreated itself and the upload succeeded. Flagged in Next Up that a `docker-compose` init sidecar would still be the more conventional long-term fix.
- **`contacts.logoFileId`** (nullable FK to `files.id`, `onDelete: "set null"`) plus **Phase 4's two targeted fields**, `contacts.taxId` and `contacts.website` (both nullable text) — all three in the **same migration** (`apps/api/drizzle/0005_new_ben_urich.sql`, idx 5, the correct next sequential number after `0004_empty_storm`, confirmed against `apps/api/drizzle/meta/_journal.json` before generating). `contact_persons.title` already covers job title — confirmed by reading `contacts.ts` before assuming it was missing; no change made there, matching the task brief's explicit instruction to confirm first. Zod schemas (`packages/shared/src/schemas/contacts.ts`), `contacts.service.ts`'s `create`/`update` (additive only — the nested-array-replace and archive/delete/ledger-check logic is untouched), and `contacts.controller.ts` all updated to accept the three new fields.
- **Array-based type filter**: `contacts.controller.ts`'s `GET /contacts` now accepts repeated `?type=customer&type=vendor` query params (Express's default array-query parsing — a single value still arrives as a plain string and is normalized to a one-element array), replacing the prior singular `?type=`. `contacts.service.ts`'s `list` takes `types?: string[]` and uses Drizzle's `inArray` instead of a single `eq`. This was the one intentional, brief-sanctioned change to `contacts.service.ts`'s existing logic beyond the new fields.

- **Migration hiccup found and fixed, not worked around**: `pnpm --filter @spine/api db:migrate` (and `drizzle-kit migrate` run directly) hung/silently failed with no visible error (the CLI's spinner swallows the underlying exception). Root-caused by writing an isolated script calling `drizzle-orm`'s `migrate()` directly: the DB's `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` row for `0004_empty_storm` had the *correct* content hash (verified via `shasum -a 256` matching exactly) but a **stale `created_at` timestamp** — `1786013237690` instead of `_journal.json`'s recorded `when` of `1786017251821` for that same entry, a leftover from a prior session's own migration-renumbering fix-up (see the "Contacts & CRM (F1)" entry below — "a note on how this landed" — which mentions exactly this kind of drift). Since `drizzle-orm`'s migrator compares `journal.when > lastAppliedRow.created_at` to decide what's new, this stale timestamp made it think migration 0004 (and therefore its `CREATE TYPE` statements) hadn't run yet, and it began replaying `0000_soft_silvermane.sql` from scratch, hitting `type "activity_type" already exists`. Fixed by correcting that one row's `created_at` in place (`UPDATE drizzle.__drizzle_migrations SET created_at = 1786017251821 WHERE id = 5 AND hash = '...'` — hash-guarded, not a blind row-5 update) rather than touching any migration file; `pnpm db:migrate` then applied `0005_new_ben_urich.sql` cleanly on the next run.

- **Contacts list page** (`apps/web/src/app/contacts/`, new `contacts-explorer.tsx`, `contacts-view-switcher.tsx`, `contacts-list-view.tsx`, `contacts-card-view.tsx`, `contacts-skeleton.tsx`, `contact-row-actions.tsx`, `contact-create-drawer.tsx`, `contact-logo.tsx`, `use-contact-stats.ts`): four `StatCard`s (total contacts, customers, vendors, active leads) computed from data already in memory — `total`/`customers`/`vendors` derived client-side from the already-fetched contact list (no fabricated numbers, per this codebase's established rule, see `apps/web/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`'s own comment on why it omits stat cards until real data exists — Contacts now has real data, the opposite case), `activeLeads` from a single `GET /leads` counted client-side (stage not `won`/`lost`) rather than adding a dedicated `/contacts/stats` endpoint for four cheaply-derivable counts. A Table/List/Card `ToggleGroup` view switcher, persisted to `localStorage` (`spine.contacts.view`), matching `app-layout.tsx`'s existing sidebar-collapse persistence pattern exactly (read on mount in a `useEffect`, guarded by a `hydrated` flag to avoid an SSR/client mismatch flash). Table view is the existing `DataTable` plus a new Actions column; List is a denser single-column list; Card is a responsive grid — all three share one new `ContactRowActions` dropdown (Edit navigates to the detail page, which already has full inline-edit — no separate edit surface was built; Archive/Restore/Delete call the same endpoints the detail page uses, Delete behind the same `AlertDialog` pattern, kept as a fully-controlled `open`/`onOpenChange` state external to the `DropdownMenu` to avoid the exact Radix unmount-before-open problem this codebase already hit and solved once for the Settings dialog, see that entry below). Type/archived filtering uses `@spine/ui`'s existing `MultiSelect` against the new array-based `?type=` param. Loading states are `@spine/ui`'s `Skeleton`, shaped per the active view (skeleton rows/list-rows/cards), replacing the old full-page `<Spinner />`.
- **Add Contact is a Drawer**, opened from the list page's primary action (`@spine/ui`'s `Drawer`, composing the existing `ContactForm`'s actual create logic unchanged — only how it's hosted changed). **`/contacts/new` is kept as a route, not deleted**, but now just `redirect()`s to `/contacts?new=1` (server-side query param that auto-opens the drawer on first paint) rather than rendering its own full-page form. Reasoning, per the task brief's explicit ask: Settings' "Dialog only, no URLs" decision (see that entry below) was right for Settings because nothing in it is a shareable resource — it's pure org configuration. Contacts' create flow is different: it produces a real, bookmarkable resource once saved (`/contacts/:id`), and "here's how you add a contact" is itself a plausible link to share *before* that resource exists (an onboarding checklist item, a support doc, a "New" button someone right-clicks to open in a new tab). So the route stays live and useful, but redirects into the one real implementation (the Drawer) instead of maintaining two separate create forms in parallel.
- **Contact detail page** (`contact-detail.tsx`, rewritten; the new `contact-logo.tsx` is shared between the list's Card/List row avatars and this page's header): an explicit `ArrowLeft` "Back to contacts" button above the header (in addition to the existing `Breadcrumb`, not instead of it — a one-click back affordance reads clearer immediately next to the identity it returns from, on a detail page one level deep). Header now includes a clickable logo/avatar (`ContactLogo`, built on `@spine/ui`'s existing `Avatar`/`AvatarImage`/`AvatarFallback` — no new library primitive needed) wired to the new upload endpoint: click opens a native file picker, uploads via `apiClient.upload()` (a new method on `apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts`, since the existing `request()` always `JSON.stringify`s its body and sets `Content-Type: application/json`, neither correct for `multipart/form-data` — the browser must set its own boundary-bearing `Content-Type` from a `FormData` body), then `PUT /contacts/:id` with the returned `logoFileId`. All prior CRUD (inline edit, archive/restore, delete-with-`AlertDialog`) is preserved verbatim, just relocated into the new header shape, plus two new editable fields (Tax ID, Website) added to both the edit-mode form and the create Drawer's form. **Tabs replace the prior session's two-column layout**: "Contact persons", "Addresses", "Leads", "Activities" — each hosts the exact same section component as before (`ContactPersonsSection`/`AddressesSection`/`LeadsSection`/`ActivitiesSection`), unchanged in their own internal add/remove logic, only how they're now hosted. **No separate "Overview" tab** — the contact's own editable fields (name, type, email, phone, tax ID, website) live in the header's inline-edit, same as the prior session; a tab repeating only those same fields would have been redundant, and the task brief explicitly allowed skipping it.
- **`apiClient` gains `.upload()`** (`apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts`) alongside the existing `.get`/`.put`/`.post`/`.delete` — a fresh `Idempotency-Key` per call, matching every other mutating request, but building a `FormData` body and letting `fetch` derive `Content-Type` itself instead of JSON-encoding.
- No new `@spine/ui` primitives were needed anywhere in this pass — `StatCard`, `MultiSelect`, `Skeleton`, `Drawer`, `Tabs`, `Breadcrumb`, `DropdownMenu`, `ToggleGroup`, and `Avatar` all already existed with the exact shapes needed (confirmed by reading each one's source before using it, not assumed) — so per CLAUDE.md's rule, no `apps/design-system` doc page was added or is owed for this change.

- **Verified**, all against the live dev stack (`docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml` — Postgres and MinIO already running, confirmed via `docker compose ps` before starting; both dev servers restarted after this task's own production builds clobbered the dev `.next` cache again, same known gotcha as every prior entry — `rm -rf apps/web/.next` + relaunch each time, proactively, before curling). `pnpm --filter @spine/api typecheck`, `lint`, `build` and `pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck`, `lint`, `build` each run **sequentially**, all clean (the web build failed once mid-session with a `PageNotFoundError` from the exact concurrent-dev-server-vs-build `.next` race flagged in this file's own history — confirmed by killing the still-running dev server and rebuilding clean, not a real code error). `pnpm --filter @spine/ui typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @spine/design-system typecheck` also clean (no `@spine/ui` exports were touched). Migration `0005_new_ben_urich.sql` applied (after the hash/timestamp fix above); confirmed via `psql` (`docker exec spine-dev-db-1 psql`, since no local `psql` client exists in this environment) that `files` exists with its two FKs (`org_id` → `organization`, `uploaded_by_user_id` → `user`) and one index, and that `contacts.tax_id`/`contacts.website`/`contacts.logo_file_id` all exist with `contacts_logo_file_id_files_id_fk` correctly referencing `files.id`.
- Signed up a fresh test user via curl, captured the session cookie, and exercised the full new surface directly against the API: uploaded a real file via `curl -F` (`POST /files`) — confirmed the returned `id`/`key`/`sizeBytes` match, confirmed the object exists in MinIO via `mc ls local/spine --recursive`, confirmed `GET /files/:id` 302s to a correctly-signed MinIO URL and that following it returns the exact original file content byte-for-byte; replayed the same `Idempotency-Key` on a second upload and confirmed the identical stored file `id` came back rather than a second object being created; confirmed a missing `file` field returns a clean `400`, not a crash. Created a contact with `taxId`/`website` set and confirmed both persisted and round-tripped on `GET`; set a contact's `logoFileId` to the uploaded file's id via `PUT` and confirmed it stuck. Confirmed the multi-type filter at all three shapes: `?type=customer`, `?type=vendor`, and `?type=customer&type=vendor` together, plus the unfiltered default — each returned exactly the expected subset. Re-ran the same archive/restore/hard-delete/ledger-protection checks the prior two Contacts entries established, confirming no regression: archived a contact (disappeared from the default list, reappeared with `?includeArchived=true`), restored it, hard-deleted a contact with no ledger history (200, then a confirmed `404` on follow-up `GET`), and specifically re-tested the ledger-block path — inserted a **balanced** journal entry/lines pair directly via `psql` referencing a fresh contact (a first attempt with an intentionally unbalanced pair was correctly rejected by the pre-existing DB trigger, `check_journal_entry_balanced()`, itself reconfirming Phase 0's ledger-integrity constraint is intact), then confirmed `DELETE` on that contact returned exactly `400 {"message":"Contact has financial ledger history and cannot be deleted — archive it instead"}` (the same string the UI's `Alert` shows) and that `POST /contacts/:id/archive` still succeeds as the escape hatch. No browser-automation tooling is available in this environment; all of the above was code-reviewed and typechecked, and every underlying API call each of those interactions makes was curl-verified directly instead, but none of it was interactively verified in a real browser.

Pre-existing (present before this session), and this task's brief explicitly scoped `contacts.service.ts`'s existing logic as untouchable beyond the new fields/array filter, so it's flagged rather than fixed.

### 2026-08-06 — Contacts & CRM (F1) follow-up: full CRUD in the web UI, and a redesigned two-column detail page

- **Correction, not a new feature:** the "Contacts & CRM (F1)" entry immediately below shipped incomplete — the API (`apps/api/src/modules/contacts/contacts.controller.ts`) already had full CRUD (`GET`/`GET :id`/`POST`/`PUT :id`/archive/restore/`DELETE :id`), but the web UI only ever wired Create. There was no way to edit a contact's own fields after creation, no delete, no archive/restore, and the detail page was a single stacked column with no header, no primary actions, and no create/delete confirmation anywhere. This entry closes both gaps: complete CRUD wiring, and an Attio/Twenty-style redesign of the detail page.
- **`apiClient` gains `.delete()`** (`apps/web/src/lib/api-client.ts`) — the underlying `request()` already supported the DELETE verb; the exported `apiClient` object just never surfaced it.
- **Inline edit** on the detail page (`apps/web/src/app/contacts/contact-detail.tsx`): clicking "Edit" turns the fields panel (type, company/individual, name, email, phone) into an editable form in place with Save/Cancel, using `PUT /contacts/:id` — no separate route, per explicit direction. **Delete** is wired behind an `AlertDialog` confirmation and redirects to `/contacts` on success; the API's exact 400 message ("Contact has financial ledger history and cannot be deleted — archive it instead") is surfaced verbatim via an `Alert` rather than a generic failure, confirmed live (see Verified). **Archive**/**Restore** are header actions — Archive shown when active, Restore shown when `archivedAt` is set — using the existing `?includeArchived` list param (already supported API-side, still no list-page toggle exposed this pass, matching the original entry's stated scope) to confirm an archived contact stays reachable and clearly marked on its own detail page.
- **Detail page redesign**: a header row (name, type badge, "Company" badge, "Archived" badge when applicable, primary actions top-right — Edit is the one filled/primary action per `docs/DESIGN.md`, Archive/Restore secondary, Delete danger-styled behind its confirmation), then a two-column body — left holds the contact's own fields plus `ContactPersonsSection`/`AddressesSection` (who this is), right holds `LeadsSection`/`ActivitiesSection` (what's happening with them). Modeled on Mobbin references pulled this session for [Attio's contact detail](https://mobbin.com/screens/cf4f2b49-652f-4c76-8a7c-1ea4f57c10cf) (header row with name/badge/actions top-right, left-rail own-fields) and [Jobber's client page](https://mobbin.com/screens/4ee9338b-de48-4168-9069-38d3307446ff) (closest domain match, being also a service-business tool — properties/contacts left, work/billing right), with [Twenty's](https://mobbin.com/screens/1347da63-1157-4923-b196-46c42e6880ea) collapsible-fields panel as a secondary reference. Built entirely from existing plain-Tailwind flex/grid classes, matching this codebase's actual convention — checked `packages/ui/src/components/layout.tsx`'s `Box`/`Flex`/`Grid` primitives first and confirmed the rest of `apps/web` doesn't use them (Settings, Dashboard, the original Contacts pass all use raw Tailwind), so no new layout convention was introduced.
- **Toast on every create, `AlertDialog` on every delete**, across all five entities this module touches. New `apps/web/src/app/contacts/entity-toast.tsx` (`useEntityToast`) generalizes `apps/settings/saved-toast.tsx`'s fixed "Saved" composition (`Toast`/`ToastProvider`/`ToastTitle`/`ToastDescription`/`ToastViewport`) into a `show(title, description)` hook, since each of the five creates needs its own message ("Contact created," "Contact person added," "Address added," "Lead added," "Activity logged") rather than one fixed string — one `useEntityToast()` instance lives in `contact-detail.tsx` and is threaded down via `onCreated` callbacks rather than five separate toast instances. The contact-create flow is a special case: `contact-form.tsx` navigates straight to the new contact's detail page on success, so there's no moment on the form itself to show a toast — it sets a one-shot `sessionStorage` flag (`spine:contact-created`) that `contact-detail.tsx` reads and clears on mount instead. `AlertDialog` confirmation was added not just to the new top-level contact delete but retrofitted onto `contact-persons-section.tsx` and `addresses-section.tsx`'s existing `handleRemove` flows, which previously deleted immediately on icon click with zero confirmation.
- Verified against the live dev stack (`docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml` Postgres/MinIO already up; both `apps/api`/`apps/web` dev servers were running and were restarted after this task's own `pnpm --filter @spine/web build` clobbered the dev `.next` cache again — cleaned `apps/web/.next` and relaunched both dev servers proactively before curling, per this session's established pattern). `pnpm --filter @spine/web typecheck`, `lint`, and `build` each run sequentially — all clean. Signed up a fresh test user via curl (`POST /api/auth/sign-up/email`), captured the session cookie, and drove the full lifecycle directly against the API: created a contact (`POST /contacts`), updated its own fields (`PUT /contacts/:id`, confirmed the new name/phone in the response), archived it (confirmed `archivedAt` set, confirmed it disappeared from the default `GET /contacts` list and reappeared with `?includeArchived=true`), restored it (confirmed `archivedAt` back to `null`), then deleted it with no ledger history (`DELETE /contacts/:id` → 200, follow-up `GET` → 404, confirming a true hard delete). Also tested the ledger-history-blocks-delete path specifically: created a second contact, inserted a balanced `journal_entries`/`journal_lines` row referencing it directly via `psql` (checked `apps/api/src/db/schema/ledger.ts` for the table shape first), then confirmed `DELETE /contacts/:id` returned exactly `400 {"message":"Contact has financial ledger history and cannot be deleted — archive it instead"}` — the same string now shown verbatim in the UI's `Alert` — and confirmed `POST /contacts/:id/archive` still succeeds as the escape hatch for that same contact. **Not verified, stated plainly:** the actual click-through (Edit button turning the panel editable, the `AlertDialog` opening/cancelling, a `Toast` appearing after a create) — no browser-automation tooling is available in this environment; this was code-reviewed and typechecked but not interactively verified in a browser, same honesty pattern as every prior entry this session.
- Stories: closes the remaining CRUD/UX gap in S-01.1/S-01.2 (edit/archive/restore/delete for the contact itself) left open by the entry below; no new stories, no scope change.
